Student visa
Obtain a student visa
Before you come to study in Australia, you must obtain a student visa from the Department of Home Affairs (DHA)
You may not require a student visa to study in Australia if you hold another visa (other temporary visas) that allows you to enter and stay in Australia with no restrictions on study.
Student visas can only be granted for programs that are registered on the Commonwealth Register of Institutions for Courses for Overseas Students (CRICOS).
Information about how to apply for a student visa and options available can be found on DHA's student visa pages.
It can take several months for your visa application to be processed so it is important to begin the application process as soon as you have accepted your offer and received an electronic Confirmation of Enrolment from Western Sydney University.
department of home affairs
CRICOS Website
Simplified Student Visa Framework
Genuine student and genuine temporary student requirement and access to funds
You are required to apply for your visa online. The online student visa application will assess you against a range of criteria and determine the level of English and financial capacity required. You are still expected to meet other requirements such as
Genuine Student (GS)
, good character, and health criteria.
To be eligible for streamlined visa processing and to apply to Western Sydney University you must be a genuine student and fulfil the genuine student requirement and have sufficient funds to:
cover your
tuition fees
cover your
living expenses and travel costs
for the duration of your stay in Australia
secure
overseas student health cover (OSHC)
for the duration of your study in Australia
cover
student services amenities fees
About Simplified student visa framework (SSVF)
The Student Visa Application Process
Before you come to study in Australia, you must obtain a student visa from the Department of Home Affairs (DHA)
Students often apply for a student visa with the assistance from one of our
agent representatives
.
On receipt of your Acceptance to Study at Western Sydney University and fee payment, the University will create an electronic Confirmation of Enrolment (eCoE) which is recorded with DHA for student visa application purposes. A copy of the eCoE will be sent to you or your agent to include with your Australian student visa application.
Continuing and Commencing student
If you hold a current student visa, Western Sydney University will send you your eCoE upon receipt of your program acceptance. You must apply for a new student visa prior to the expiry of your current visa.
subclass 500 student visa
Bringing family
If you wish to bring children and/or your spouse (dependents) for the duration of your study in Australia, please refer to DHA's website for
Information on bringing family
.
You will also need to consider financial requirements to cover any family members travelling with you:
Health cover
School costs for any school-aged dependents
Living expenses
bringing your family
Visa conditions
When you are issued with a student visa, your visa conditions will be attached to the grant of the visa. See
Visa conditions for Student Visa holders
.
If you are in Australia on a student visa, you must maintain satisfactory academic progress at all times. The University is obliged to advise Department of Home Affairs when an International Student Visa holder is not maintaining satisfactory academic progress. This may have an impact on your student visa.
It is your responsibility as the student visa applicant or as a student visa holder to be aware of the conditions and requirements of your student visa.
If you experience any difficulties during your studies, please get in touch with your Academic Course Advisor (for academic related matters) and with
Student Welfare Officer
(for other extenuating circumstances).
To ensure you receive important information from the Department of Home Affairs and to satisfy your student visa conditions, you must notify the University within 7 days of any new Australian contact details, including address, phone number, email address and emergency contact details.
As a student visa holder, you are required to complete your study program within the duration specified in your Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE).
Working in Australia
Student visas automatically grant students permission to do paid work while studying. The Australian Government temporarily removed work restrictions for student visa holders in January 2022. This temporary arrangement will end on 30 June 2023.
From 1 July 2023, student visa holders will be permitted to work up to 48 hours per fortnight while your program is in session and unlimited hours during scheduled university breaks.
You and your family members must not breach the student visa work conditions. More information is available on the Australian Government’s ‘
Check Visa Details and Conditions
’ page
student visa conditions
Provide Biometrics
Applicants outside Australia
You will need to provide your biometrics at an Australian Visa Application Centre (AVAC) or an Australian Biometrics Collection Centre (ABCC) if you apply:
for a
visa that is part of the biometrics program
from a
country that is part of our biometrics program
.
You can:
submit your visa application online where possible or by post. If we send you a letter to let you know we want your biometrics you must arrange an appointment and come into the AVAC or ABCC so we can collect them.
For more information, including updates on AVACs or ABCCs, and opening times in your country, see:
Our Offices outside Australia
. For information regarding the current visa processing arrangements, see
I want to apply for a visa
.
Applicants within Australia
Department of Home Affairs will ask you if you need to provide biometrics.
You will need to
advise the relevant processing office
to let them know that you are onshore so that they can arrange the collection of your biometrics in Australia.
More information can be found
here

Education Services for Overseas Students Act 2000 (ESOS Act) and the National Code 2018
A Simple Guide for International Students
As an international student studying at an Australian university, there are special laws that help protect you and make sure you get a quality education and proper support. These laws are called the ESOS Act and the National Code 2018.
ESOS Act
National Code 2018
ESOS Act
ESOS stands for Education Services for Overseas Students. The Australian government has established this legislative framework to ensure quality education and consumer protection for all international students coming to Australia to study on a student visa. This law makes sure international students are provided with the education, support, and information they are promised.
It also protects your tuition fees if something unexpected happens and your course can’t be delivered.
National Code 2018
The National Code 2018 is a set of standards that works alongside the ESOS Act. It explains how universities should support and monitor compliance for international students throughout their studies.
The ESOS Act and the National Code 2018 also set out the rights and obligations on international students. International students must satisfy the conditions of their student visa and the University is required by the government to monitor and report on activities related to these conditions.
Your Rights
To receive quality education.
To receive access to academic and personal support services.
To receive clear information about your course and enrolment.
To receive clear information about how to lodge complaints or appeals if something isn’t right.
Your Obligations
Maintain your visa conditions.
Maintain your Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) for the period of your stay.
Maintain satisfactory academic progress.
Keep your contact details up to date.
Follow the University’s policies processes.
If you are under 18, maintain your approved accommodation, support and general welfare arrangements.

Life Beyond
Western's contribution to your success does not end at graduation. We have what it takes to support your continuous learning and professional development.
International Orientation
The Western Sydney International Orientation program will help you in your transition to university and to a new chapter of your life: a new environment, a new culture, and a new way of learning.
GET READY TO START
The commencement of your study at Western Sydney University is fast approaching!
Use our starting at Western checklist to ensure you get the best start to your studies with us!
1. Accept Your Offer
2. Activate Your Account
3. Enrol in Your Subjects
4. Finalise Your Class Registration
5. Attend Orientation
6. Apply for your Student ID Card
Looking for accommodation?
Travelling to Australia?
1. ACCEPT YOUR OFFER
The first step to becoming a student at Western is to accept your offer.
The Western Sydney International Admissions team work tirelessly processing applications, issuing offers and working with future students to help them realise their educational goals with Western Sydney University. If you still need to formally accept your offer to enrol and finalise your timetable before the start of session, watch the ‘How to accept your offer video’ now.
If you have a question regarding your offer, the acceptance process or about your visa, visit the below links for more information.
Note: You must accept your offer and pay required fees as stated on your Offer Admission letter to receive your Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE). When you receive your CoE you can progress to the following steps.
Contact us
More Info
2. ACTIVATE YOUR ACCOUNT
If you've accepted your offer and received your confirmation of enrolment (eCOE), the next step is to
activate your student account
(Western Account).
This will give you access to all our online services, including your student email account, My Student Records (MySR), the Library and more. You'll need your Western Student ID number.
You can find this number on your Offer of Admission letter.
If you have a question about activating your Western Account, please contact International Admissions via
email
or call +61 2 9685 9280 during 9:00am-5:00pm AEDT Mon to Fri.
Student Email
Email is the official communication channel at Western Sydney University. We send important information about your enrolment, exams, results etc to
your student email account
, not by post, so it's important that you check it regularly - every day if you can or at least twice a week. Your student email address is studentid@student.westernsydney.edu.au
3. ENROL IN YOUR SUBJECTS
Enrolling in your subjects is the most important thing you need to do when starting at Western Sydney University. You need to complete this in
My Student Records (MySR)
.
To select your subjects, you will first need to find your program on the
Academic Handbook page.
When you search for your program, click on 'sequence' for the current recommended subject selections for your session.
Enrol in your subjects Now
International Students
Before registering into subjects, International Students must accept their offer and activate their account. Please view the
How to Accept
page for step by step instructions.
How to accept
Accept your offer video
Enrolment and Class Registration Help
For enrolment and class registration support we recommend you attend one of our Enrolment and Class Registration Support Sessions online. Our dedicated team will walk you through the steps and answer questions to assist you in the process.
Session Dates & Times (AEDT Sydney Time):
1 July 2026, 6pm
8 July 2026, 6pm
15 July 2026, 6pm
22 July 2026, 6pm
Join via Zoom:
https://uws.zoom.us/j/85291268748
Meeting ID: 852 9126 8748
Password: 247196
You can also contact the Student Services Hub via phone on +61 2 9174 6905, via WhatsApp on +61482095590 during 9:00am - 4:30pm AEDT, or email
internationalstudy@westernsydney.edu.au
4. FINALISE YOUR CLASS REGISTRATION
Class Registration
is how you choose your tutorials (and other classes) and put together your timetable. Allocate+ is the online system used to complete this process.
You'll need to make sure you are enrolled in all of your subjects. After being allocated into your classes, you may be able to swap classes depending on availability.
If you have just completed your enrolment, it may take a couple of hours for your subjects to appear in Allocate+. Check back later if they do not show up in Allocate+ immediately after enrolment.
Important additional information to do with Class Registration can be viewed on our
Class Registration page.
Note: After your timetable is complete, if you have been allocated to an on-campus class and not able to attend due to an underlying health condition, please contact your First Year Experience Coordinator to discuss the options available to you.
step by step instructions
5. ATTEND ORIENTATION
Orientation is designed to help you transition smoothly into university life at Western Sydney University. Through our orientation activities and events, you will receive important information about enrolment, student support services, academic expectations, campus life, and resources available to international students.
We encourage all international students to participate in both the online webinar and the International Student Welcome Session to help you feel confident and prepared before classes begin.
International Student Welcome Session - Social Connections
Join us on Tuesday, 14 July 2026 for the International Student Welcome Session at the Parramatta South Campus.
This on-campus session provides an opportunity to meet fellow international students, form the first essential social connections to your time at Western and start building your Western community before classes commence.
International Orientation Webinar
Friday, 3 July 2026 (3pm – 5pm)
Your attendance to this webinar Orientation session is compulsory.
Join our online International Orientation Webinar to help you prepare before classes begin. This session will provide important information and guidance to support your transition to university life at Western Sydney University.
Topics will include:
Essential student services and support available to you
Enrolment and class registration guidance
Your responsibilities as an international student
Tips for settling in and making the most of university life
Important information to help you get started at Western
Watch the webinar live online and have your questions answered by our support team in the Q&A chat.
Your email invite will be sent to your inbox of the email address you supplied when applying. Registered students will receive the Zoom webinar link via email prior to the session.
6. APPLY FOR YOUR STUDENT ID CARD
Students can now apply for their Student ID card to be posted to them once they arrive in Australia by following these steps:
Go to
onlineid.westernsydney.edu.au
and upload a photo and identity documentation that meets our guidelines. New students must upload one file containing one identity document from list A and another from list B.
We will print your card and post it to your postal address recorded in MySR.
Please view the
getting your new Student ID Card document
for photo guidelines and acceptable documentation.
More Information
Travelling to Australia?
If you are planning to travel to Sydney, make sure you review the
Pre-departure and Arrival Checklist
from the NSW Government so you know what you need to do. Please also visit our
International Student Arrivals webpage
to help you navigate information for returning to Australia.

original_evidence.text:
Western Sydney University
16
STUDY ABROAD
At Western Sydney University, 
we provide a wide range of 
services to help you achieve 
academic success. These include 
advice on careers, employment, 
learning skills, counselling, 
religious support and support 
for students with disabilities.
westernsydney.edu.au/services
AIRPORT PICK-UP
The complimentary airport pick-up 
service is available to all new international 
students commencing at the University in 
undergraduate, postgraduate or research 
programs. Students can arrange to be 
collected from Sydney airport on arrival 
and taken to their home campus. Students 
studying a pathway program (English, 
Diploma or Foundation Studies) at The 
College, Western Sydney University will be 
able to access this service for a fee.
westernsydney.edu.au/airportpickup 
INTERNATIONAL ORIENTATION
The International Orientation program is 
specifically designed for international students 
to help you prepare for your studies at Western 
Sydney University. It takes place before classes 
commence and all international students are 
required to attend (check your offer letter 
for dates). Please make sure you arrive in 
Australia at least one or two days before the 
commencement of the Orientation program.
westernsydney.edu.au/international/
arriving/orientation
STUDENT SERVICES HUB
The Student Services Hub is your first point 
of contact for information, advice, forms 
and referral to other services. The Student 
Services Hub team can help you with most of 
your enquiries and they can put you in touch 
with the right services or area to resolve your 
issues. Each campus has a Student Services 
Hub, where you can get assistance with issues 
related to student visas, overseas student 
health cover, enrolment and admission issues.  
westernsydney.edu.au/studentcentral 
STUDENT WELFARE 
The Student Welfare Service provides 
welfare support to all international students, 
including advice on financial assistance, 
accommodation, health related issues 
and student advocacy needs. This service 
has professionally trained staff to help 
you work through unexpected problems 
and is available at all campuses.
Welfare officers can provide information 
and advice about your study options, 
such as reduced study load or leave of 
absence on compassionate grounds, and 
can help find the right services to talk to.
The Student Welfare Service also regularly 
organises information sessions and 
workshops for international students.
westernsydney.edu.au/
internationalstudentsupport 
westernsydney.edu.au/welfareservice
STUDY SUPPORT
The teaching styles you will encounter at 
Western Sydney University and the study skills 
required might be very different from what 
you have been used to in your home country. 
Western Sydney University offers a range 
of support programs including Academic 
Literacy Workshops and other services to  
help you succeed. 
westernsydney.edu.au/
internationalstudentsupport
ENGLISH CONVERSATION GROUPS
Improve your English speaking skills and build 
your confidence by participating in English 
conversation groups. These groups are run 
by trained volunteers and will provide an 
opportunity for participants to practice and 
improve their spoken English in a friendly and 
social environment. 
westernsydney.edu.au/englishconversation
PEER ASSISTED STUDY SESSIONS (PASS) 
Peer Assisted Study Sessions (PASS) is a 
free and voluntary student-centred learning 
program offered face to face and online. 
One-hour sessions run weekly throughout 
the teaching session. In PASS, you will meet 
and work collaboratively with other students 
from your subject to understand the subject 
content and develop study strategies to help 
improve your academic performance. Sessions 
are facilitated by senior students who have 
successfully completed the subject before. 
They guide students through the program 
material and facilitate students’ learning 
through planned activities and discussion.
Through actively working together with 
other students, you will find that you are 
more engaged and will develop a deeper 
understanding of the subject content. PASS 
is an informal and welcoming environment 
to study, where you can gain a deeper 
understanding of subject content and meet 
other students from your program.
PASS sessions run for a large range of 
subjects and on multiple campuses. 
westernsydney.edu.au/pass
MATES
MATES is a peer-mentoring program for 
students just starting their university study, 
or returning to study after some time. New 
students are matched with students in 
later years of study. This helps you make 
friends, network with other students and 
gain knowledge and skills to settle into life at 
university.
westernsydney.edu.au/mates
mates@westernsydney.edu.au
STUDENT  
SUPPORT

國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。

PARTNER INFORMATION SHEET 
 
  
Application Information 
Nomination and Application 
procedure 
1. The International Office sends an information email and an information package to 
partner institutions.  
2. Partners institutions send a list of nominees including the following details: 
• The student’s full name(s) 
• Current level of studies at the home institution 
• Type of Exchange - credit-seeking or dual degree 
• Email address 
• Name and email address of the person in charge of the study period (at the home 
institution) 
Required documents 
Online Application Form: (please choose the option ‘You are from a partner institution’) 
Join Clermont School of Business - Clermont School of Business 
Applicants are required to upload the following documents : 
1- Photo 
2- Copy of passport or ID 
3- Previous year’s transcripts/degree certificates 
4- Proof of language level (Minimum B2-level in the language of the study program) 
Language level certificates 
accepted for Degree-seeking 
students (Please note : a B1 
level-certificate can be 
accepted for non-degree-
seeking exchange students) 
 
Programmes in English 
Native Speaker or official scores : TOEFL iTP 550, 
TOEFL iBT 80, IELTS 6.0, TOEIC 750, Duolingo 115, 
PTE general Level 3, PTE academic 58, ITEP 
academic 3.9, ISE II, Cambridge B2 first or C1 
Advanced. 
 
Programme in French 
Native speaker or B2 level 
Housing  
Various solutions to finding accommodation – search before the start of term: 
- Our partner housing agent, Moversia, offers a fee-paying ‘welcome package’ 
helping students to find suitable accommodation in the private sector (includes a 
pick-up service and administrative formalities (lease, gas, electricity, bank, phone 
& internet) https://welcomeclermont.com/ 
- Private Student partner residences (full details available in the international 
student guide.) 
- Small Ads: www.lokaviz.fr /  https://www.leboncoin.fr /  www.mapiaule.com 
- Guarantee for International Students: (Visale)  https://www.visale.fr/visale-pour-
les-locataires/avantages/  or (Garantme)  https://garantme.fr/en 
Expenses 
Living expenses including rent, food, other bills, can be estimated at around 700- 800€ per 
month depending on the student’s lifestyle and the type of accommodation rented. 
During the first month students will need extra money for rent deposits, connecting 
electricity, gas, telephone, and various other extras. 
Orientation & Integration 
All exchange students will have access to an online orientation session and on-campus 
orientation sessions prior to commencing their studies. The international office staff are 
easily accessible for any queries or guidance required by international students. Students 
also have access to many societies providing activities and events in and outside the 
school.

國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。

orientation sessions prior to commencing their studies. The international office staff are 
easily accessible for any queries or guidance required by international students. Students 
also have access to many societies providing activities and events in and outside the 
school.

Insurance

student visa. For more information, please visit: https://administration-etrangers-en-
france.interieur.gouv.fr/particuliers/#/

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320

 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。 
 
 
 
□我已閱讀並同意上述所有內容。 
申請人簽名:___________________ 
簽名日期:_____________________

Formation Internationale
Vous avez envie d’étudier l’ingénierie en France dans une Grande École d’ingénieurs ?
Pour participer à nos programmes de formation, vous devrez avoir été sélectionné(e) par votre université d’origine et justifier d’un bon niveau de français.
Plusieurs possibilités vous sont proposées, que vous souhaitiez suivre un programme diplômant ou non diplômant.
Sommaire
Étudier à Centrale Méditerranée
Double diplôme
Un semestre ou une année d'échange
Masters et doctorats
Contenu des cours
Étudier à Centrale Méditerranée
Centrale Méditerranée compte
20 % d'étudiants internationaux
en formation, tous cycles confondus.
En venant effectuer une partie de vos études dans notre établissement, vous ferez partie des nombreux étudiants du monde entier qui viennent à l'École chaque année, tout comme tous les élèves ingénieurs de notre école font un séjour à l'étranger.
Pour participer à l’un de nos programmes, vous devrez avoir été
sélectionné(e) par votre université d’origine.
Plusieurs possibilités de formation
vous sont proposées selon que vous souhaitez suivre un programme diplômant ou non diplômant.
Double diplôme
Les étudiants des établissements partenaires, après avoir commencé leur formation dans leur université d'origine, suivent
2 années de formation à Centrale Méditerranée
.
Ensuite, ils retournent dans leur pays pour terminer
leurs études
et ainsi obtenir les diplômes des
2 établissements.
Admission des étudiants internationaux dans le cadre d’un programme d’échange, une seule adresse :
international@centrale-med.fr
Un semestre ou une année d'échange
Séjour d'études
de
six mois
à
un an
offre la possibilité aux étudiants provenant d'un établissement partenaire de suivre les cours de
niveau Master (S8, S9 - S10)
à Centrale Méditerranée (dernière année avant l'obtention du diplôme d'Ingénieur).
Pendant
le semestre 8 (Master 1, 2ème semestre)
, les élèves sont amenés à suivre un parcours thématique. Ces parcours portent sur des grands
enjeux de société
pour les temps qui viennent.
Ils associent des enseignements scientifiques, dans une perspective pluridisciplinaire, et des considérations relevant des sciences sociales (éthique, géopolitique...).
Projet de recherche ou travail de fin d'étude (TFE)
Les étudiants internationaux des universités partenaires peuvent aussi effectuer un projet de recherche (ou travail de fin d'études) au sein de notre établissement pendant
4 à 6 mois
.
Ils intègrent
un des laboratoires de recherche
de l'École.
Masters et doctorats
Centrale Méditerranée propose plusieurs Masters (en anglais et en français) qui allient formation théorique de haut niveau et compétences professionnelles reconnues.
Master Erasmus-Mundus
: l'excellence et la qualité de ces Masters ont été reconnues par l'Union européenne :
Master of Science in Europhotonics
et
WAVES
.
Les laboratoires de l'école accueillent également des
étudiants internationaux.
Contenu des cours
Pour tout savoir sur les contenus des cours,
consultez le Wiki →
.

En venant effectuer une partie de vos études dans notre établissement, vous ferez partie des nombreux étudiants du monde entier qui viennent à l'École chaque année, tout comme tous les élèves ingénieurs de notre école font un séjour à l'étranger.
Pour participer à l’un de nos programmes, vous devrez avoir été
sélectionné(e) par votre université d’origine.
Plusieurs possibilités de formation
vous sont proposées selon que vous souhaitez suivre un programme diplômant ou non diplômant.
Double diplôme
Les étudiants des établissements partenaires, après avoir commencé leur formation dans leur université d'origine, suivent
2 années de formation à Centrale Méditerranée
.
Ensuite, ils retournent dans leur pays pour terminer
leurs études
et ainsi obtenir les diplômes des
2 établissements.

international@centrale-med.fr

de
six mois
à
un an
offre la possibilité aux étudiants provenant d'un établissement partenaire de suivre les cours de
niveau Master (S8, S9 - S10)
à Centrale Méditerranée (dernière année avant l'obtention du diplôme d'Ingénieur).

le semestre 8 (Master 1, 2ème semestre)

enjeux de société
pour les temps qui viennent.

4 à 6 mois
.
Ils intègrent
un des laboratoires de recherche
de l'École.

et

.

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。 
 
 
 
□我已閱讀並同意上述所有內容。 
申請人簽名:___________________ 
簽名日期:_____________________

Formation Internationale
Vous avez envie d’étudier l’ingénierie en France dans une Grande École d’ingénieurs ?
Pour participer à nos programmes de formation, vous devrez avoir été sélectionné(e) par votre université d’origine et justifier d’un bon niveau de français.
Plusieurs possibilités vous sont proposées, que vous souhaitiez suivre un programme diplômant ou non diplômant.
Sommaire
Étudier à Centrale Méditerranée
Double diplôme
Un semestre ou une année d'échange
Masters et doctorats
Contenu des cours
Étudier à Centrale Méditerranée
Centrale Méditerranée compte
20 % d'étudiants internationaux
en formation, tous cycles confondus.
En venant effectuer une partie de vos études dans notre établissement, vous ferez partie des nombreux étudiants du monde entier qui viennent à l'École chaque année, tout comme tous les élèves ingénieurs de notre école font un séjour à l'étranger.
Pour participer à l’un de nos programmes, vous devrez avoir été
sélectionné(e) par votre université d’origine.
Plusieurs possibilités de formation
vous sont proposées selon que vous souhaitez suivre un programme diplômant ou non diplômant.
Double diplôme
Les étudiants des établissements partenaires, après avoir commencé leur formation dans leur université d'origine, suivent
2 années de formation à Centrale Méditerranée
.
Ensuite, ils retournent dans leur pays pour terminer
leurs études
et ainsi obtenir les diplômes des
2 établissements.
Admission des étudiants internationaux dans le cadre d’un programme d’échange, une seule adresse :
international@centrale-med.fr
Un semestre ou une année d'échange
Séjour d'études
de
six mois
à
un an
offre la possibilité aux étudiants provenant d'un établissement partenaire de suivre les cours de
niveau Master (S8, S9 - S10)
à Centrale Méditerranée (dernière année avant l'obtention du diplôme d'Ingénieur).
Pendant
le semestre 8 (Master 1, 2ème semestre)
, les élèves sont amenés à suivre un parcours thématique. Ces parcours portent sur des grands
enjeux de société
pour les temps qui viennent.
Ils associent des enseignements scientifiques, dans une perspective pluridisciplinaire, et des considérations relevant des sciences sociales (éthique, géopolitique...).
Projet de recherche ou travail de fin d'étude (TFE)
Les étudiants internationaux des universités partenaires peuvent aussi effectuer un projet de recherche (ou travail de fin d'études) au sein de notre établissement pendant
4 à 6 mois
.
Ils intègrent
un des laboratoires de recherche
de l'École.
Masters et doctorats
Centrale Méditerranée propose plusieurs Masters (en anglais et en français) qui allient formation théorique de haut niveau et compétences professionnelles reconnues.
Master Erasmus-Mundus
: l'excellence et la qualité de ces Masters ont été reconnues par l'Union européenne :
Master of Science in Europhotonics
et
WAVES
.
Les laboratoires de l'école accueillent également des
étudiants internationaux.
Contenu des cours
Pour tout savoir sur les contenus des cours,
consultez le Wiki →
.

Formation Internationale
Vous avez envie d’étudier l’ingénierie en France dans une Grande École d’ingénieurs ?
Pour participer à nos programmes de formation, vous devrez avoir été sélectionné(e) par votre université d’origine et justifier d’un bon niveau de français.
Plusieurs possibilités vous sont proposées, que vous souhaitiez suivre un programme diplômant ou non diplômant.
Sommaire
Étudier à Centrale Méditerranée
Double diplôme
Un semestre ou une année d'échange
Masters et doctorats
Contenu des cours
Étudier à Centrale Méditerranée
Centrale Méditerranée compte
20 % d'étudiants internationaux
en formation, tous cycles confondus.
En venant effectuer une partie de vos études dans notre établissement, vous ferez partie des nombreux étudiants du monde entier qui viennent à l'École chaque année, tout comme tous les élèves ingénieurs de notre école font un séjour à l'étranger.
Pour participer à l’un de nos programmes, vous devrez avoir été
sélectionné(e) par votre université d’origine.
Plusieurs possibilités de formation
vous sont proposées selon que vous souhaitez suivre un programme diplômant ou non diplômant.
Double diplôme
Les étudiants des établissements partenaires, après avoir commencé leur formation dans leur université d'origine, suivent
2 années de formation à Centrale Méditerranée
.
Ensuite, ils retournent dans leur pays pour terminer
leurs études
et ainsi obtenir les diplômes des
2 établissements.
Admission des étudiants internationaux dans le cadre d’un programme d’échange, une seule adresse :
international@centrale-med.fr
Un semestre ou une année d'échange
Séjour d'études
de
six mois
à
un an
offre la possibilité aux étudiants provenant d'un établissement partenaire de suivre les cours de
niveau Master (S8, S9 - S10)
à Centrale Méditerranée (dernière année avant l'obtention du diplôme d'Ingénieur).
Pendant
le semestre 8 (Master 1, 2ème semestre)
, les élèves sont amenés à suivre un parcours thématique. Ces parcours portent sur des grands
enjeux de société
pour les temps qui viennent.
Ils associent des enseignements scientifiques, dans une perspective pluridisciplinaire, et des considérations relevant des sciences sociales (éthique, géopolitique...).
Projet de recherche ou travail de fin d'étude (TFE)
Les étudiants internationaux des universités partenaires peuvent aussi effectuer un projet de recherche (ou travail de fin d'études) au sein de notre établissement pendant
4 à 6 mois
.
Ils intègrent
un des laboratoires de recherche
de l'École.
Masters et doctorats
Centrale Méditerranée propose plusieurs Masters (en anglais et en français) qui allient formation théorique de haut niveau et compétences professionnelles reconnues.
Master Erasmus-Mundus
: l'excellence et la qualité de ces Masters ont été reconnues par l'Union européenne :
Master of Science in Europhotonics
et
WAVES
.
Les laboratoires de l'école accueillent également des
étudiants internationaux.
Contenu des cours
Pour tout savoir sur les contenus des cours,
consultez le Wiki →
.

Vous souhaitez intégrer une école dynamique d’ingénieurs généralistes ?
En intégrant notre établissement vous ferez partie des nombreux étudiants du monde entier qui viennent chaque année en formation au sein de notre école.

Candidature et délais pour les étudiants internationaux en échange
Les étudiants en programme d’échange n’ont
aucun frais de scolarité à payer grâce aux accords bilatéraux
signés entre notre établissement et leur établissement d’origine.
Les étudiants souhaitant réaliser une mobilité au sein de notre établissement en cycle d’ingénieur généraliste doivent-être nominé par leur université d’origine à l’adresse :
international@centrale-marseille.fr
Une fois nommés, les étudiants recevront la procédure de candidature avec la liste des documents à déposer sur la plateforme
Mobility Online →
.
Plusieurs possibilités de formation seront accessibles :
Double diplôme
dans le cadre de nos partenariats et ainsi recevoir le diplôme de l’Ecole Centrale Méditerranée et celui de votre université d’origine. Vous suivrez les deux premières années du tronc commun, ou selon l'accord avec votre établissement la deuxième et dernière année.
Un ou deux semestres d’échange
au niveau Master, en 2
e
ou 3
e
année afin de valider des crédits  (ECTS : European Credit Transfer).
Pour plus d’informations, consultez la page du Programme ingénieur →

Pour les échanges débutant en septembre (semestre d'automne) :
deadline 1
er
mai

deadline 1
er
décembre

Relevés de notes
Contrat d’études
Photocopie carte d’identité ou copie du passeport pour étudiants internationaux hors Europe

.

Submit your application at a centre for visas for France in Taiwan
All visa applications for France in Taiwan are only processed by the French Office in Taipei.
We remind you that after filling the form on the France-visas website, you must print it, sign it and give it when submitting your visa application, along with all the required supporting documents.
What are the visa fees ?
Fees (pdf)
are collected by the French administration for processing your application.
The payment is made by cash or by Easy Card in New Taiwanese Dollars

.
The amount collected will be kept by the administration even if the visa is refused.

Additional information
Making an appointment and waiting time
Please make an appointment only when you are able to submit all of the required documents.
For visa application :
https://consulat.gouv.fr/en/bureau-francais-de-taipei/appointment?name=VISAS
For passport application :
https://consulat.gouv.fr/en/bureau-francais-de-taipei/appointment?name=Retrait%20de%20passeport%20-%20Visas
Waiting time for an appointment :
The average waiting time for an appointment for short and long-stay visas is
48 hours
This waiting time may be extended up to
20 working days
prior to and during summer time.
Likewise, an increase of applications is to be expected prior to winter school holidays. As getting an appointment may exceed the normal waiting time, applicants are encouraged to submit their visa application with sufficient anticipation to avoid having to postpone their departure.
This appointment procedure does not apply to students as their appointments are arranged directly by Campus France.
Security information
When visiting the French Office in Taipei, you must not possess any weapon or dangerous product. Security checks are carried out prior to admission into the premises.
The use of mobile phones, cameras or other audio or video recording devices is strictly prohibited. You will be asked to drop off your mobile phone in lockers provided for this purpose before entering the waiting room.
Public holidays / closures
Weekly closing on
Saturdays
and
Sundays
.
Holidays in 2026:
May 1st : Labour Day
June 19th : Dragon Boat Festival
September 25th : Mid-Autumn Festival
September 28th : Teacher's Day
October 9th : Compensatory leave for Taiwan National Day
October 26th : Compensatory leave for Retrocession Day
December 25th : Constitution Day
Practical informations on your appointment
Preparation
You must submit all the required documents on the day of your appointment. No document sent to the visa section by any other means will be accepted.
In order to prepare your visa application, please consult the list of documents required according to the purpose of your stay on the France-Visas website.
Please note that only visa service officers are authorized to request additional supporting documents and that no third party individual or organization is allowed in matters regarding visas.
Submitting your visa application
: visa applications must be submitted by the applicant itself at the visa section. The French Office in Taipei will not process any visa application received through mail or any other means.
Do not forget to bring with you :
Confirmation of your appointment (printed) ;
Your passport ;
Your photo which meets the ICAO standards and issued less than 6 months ago ;
The printed France-visas filled form ;
All the requested documents listed on the France-visas website.
Registration of biometric data
All visas delivered by France are biometric.
Visa applicants above the age of 12 years old must come to the visa section when submitting their first visa application. The following biometric identifiers will be collected: a photo (which must be less than 6 months old), will be scanned on the day of your appointment, and your fingerprints will be collected.
However, it is possible to recover your biometric data if a former Schengen visa has been issued within the preceding 59 months.
Children under the age of 12 are exempted from fingerprints collection. The visa application must be submitted by one of the child’s parents or by the person who holds parental authority. The child’s
ICAO-compliant photograph (pdf)
will then be scanned. The child must be present when submitting the visa application.
Track your application and collect your passport
You have to make an appointment to collect your passport on the following link :
https://consulat.gouv.fr/en/bureau-francais-de-taipei/appointment?name=Retrait%20de%20passeport%20-%20Visas
If you are unable to come to collect your passport, a third party with a power of attorney, your payment receipt, a copy of your ID and of his own ID may collect it for you.
Particular situations
Taiwanese passport holders
Holders of a Taiwanese passport
with their identity number written on it, who wish to travel to Europe to one or several Schengen member states are exempted from having a visa for touristic, family or business stays of less than 90 days.
France has extended this exemption for Taiwanese nationals traveling to France’s non-European territories : French overseas departments, and French overseas collectivities and territories.
Taiwanese nationals who hold of a Taiwanese passport which does not include their identity number must apply for a short stay visa.
People in possession of a passport which does not include their identity number must contact the French Office.
Official passports
Visas issued to holders of official passports in the course of their duties are free of charge.
Studying in France
Students wishing to study in France for a period exceeding 3 months are obliged to enroll on the website of Campus France beforehand and also complete the educational evaluation procedure (
Studies in France
) and only then may they submit their student visa application.
The mission of Campus France is to guide and advise Taiwanese students wishing to continue their studies in France. Campus France provides extensive information on all courses provided by French Higher education system as well as specific information regarding the different French establishments permitting students to build- with success, their journey of academic mobility.
Campus France allows you to construct a step-by-step project of your studies in France. Its website allows you to create an online personalized account as well as a place to discuss with
Campus France representatives
.
The visa section is in charge of processing visa applications according to the rules and regulations in force. It is not authorized to give any information regarding dossiers being processed by telephone.
Campus France procedure for studying in France is as follows:
Inscription
Create an
account
Online completion of your application
Payment of services charges via bank transfer
Interview and submitting Campus France application
Once the service charges have been validated, you may proceed by making an appointment online on the Campus France website. You simply need to choose the date and time which suits you amongst the time slots proposed on your personal online account.
During off-peak season, there are 3 working days waiting time. During high peak season, there might be up to 10 working days waiting time.
On the day of your appointment, you should come to the Campus France Office bringing with you all of the
documents required (pdf)
.
The educational interview consists of an oral presentation of your personal studies plan and answering questions from the counselors regarding your application file. The interview may be proceeded in French, English or Chinese depending on the course you have chosen.
Submitting your student visa application :
You may submit your visa application dossier the same day as your interview with Campus France - no appointment with the visa section is necessary in this case provided that your visa application dossier is complete. You must submit your dossier personally at one of the visa section counters where you biometric data will be registered.
Bring photocopies of all substantiating documents as there is no possibility of making photocopies on the premises.
Once your have paid the application fee (in cash or by Easy Card), you will receive a receipt and your visa application will be processed by the visa section.
Processing time:
Approximately three weeks. During the summer peak, the processing time is up to one month.
Help
In case of difficulties related to your visa application, consular services can be contacted
by email only
.

Visa, Residence permit
Depending on your nationality, your situation and the length of your stay, you may be able to obtain a visa to study or conduct research in France or to return here after you graduate.
France-Visas
France-Visas
is the official website for visa application to France.
Please connect to:
https://france-visas.gouv.fr/
You will find all information you need to prepare your stay in France.
Apply for a visa on France-Visas
France-Visas allows international students to submit digital copies of their supporting documents when they complete their online visa application. This new service is initially available to international students residing in countries where visa applications are outsourced and available online. It allows for an accelerated process at the external service provider.
Prerequisites for a digitalized visa application
To be eligible to submit a digitalized visa application, you must meet the following conditions:
Be an international student applying to study in France.
Be applying for a long-stay student visa only.
Reside in a country where an external service provider is available for visa application collection.
Steps for the online visa application
If you meet the prerequisites, you can complete your student visa application in 4 steps:
Fill out your online visa application on France-Visas and upload your documents.
Submit your passport and signed form in person at the collection center.
Track your application online on the service provider's website.
Collect your passport.

No visa obligation for European students
If you are a national of a European Economic Area country (European Union country (EU) and Iceland, Norway and Liechtenstein) or Switzerland,
you do not need a student visa to study or do an internship in France.
You may freely enter French territory regardless of the length of your stay or your studies.
On the other hand, you must have a sickness and maternity insurance and sufficient financial resources to meet your needs and those of any of your family you may be supporting.
Citizens of the EU/EEA/Switzerland may
work while studying in France
without a residency permit to a maximum of 964 hours per year.
The short stay student visa
If you are not a national of a European Economic Area country (European Union country and Iceland, Norway and Liechtenstein) or of Switzerland, and depending on your nationality, you must obtain a student visa to study in France
even if your stay is
less than 3 months
.
There are two types of short stay visa:
the "short stay for studies" (
court séjour pour études
) visa and the "student in competition"
(
étudiant concours
) visa, which should be requested if you are convoked by a French institute for an exam or interview.
Note that nationals from certain non-European countries are not required to have a visa if their stay does not exceed 90 days. Check the article "
The student visa short stay
"for more information on this subject.
The long stay student visa
If you are not a national of a European Economic Area country (European Union country and Iceland, Norway and Liechtenstein) or of Switzerland,
you must request a student long stay visa
to study, conduct research or do an internship in France
for more than 3 months
.
There are two types of long term visas:
1/ the Long Term Visa used as Residence Permit (VLS-TS)
This visa allows you to remain in France for one year without needing to request a residency permit. You will still have to have your visa approved on arrival. Depending on the nature of your stay,
there are three types of long stay visas
:
the
student VLS-TS
for studies at the Bachelor's and Master's level;
the
Talent passport VLS-TS
for a doctorate and beyond;
the
internship VLS-TS
to do an internship in France as part of the programme you are enrolled in in your country of residence.
2/ the Temporary Long Term Visa (VLS-T)
With the
VLS-T
, you can stay in France for 1 year, and you don’t need to validate it at your arrival. It cannot be renewed, and it doesn’t grant the rights than the VLS-TS.
The Working Holiday visa
In the framework of a reciprocal agreement with several countries,
France grants Working Holiday visas
(vacances-travail)
.
Reserved for young people aged 18 to 30, they let you spend one year in France to learn about the country without studying here. They let you work in France to round out your resources during the year.
Check the article "
Working Holiday visa
" to find out if you are eligible for this and for more information on the subject.
Provisional residency permit
If you are not a national of a European Economic Area country (European Union country and Iceland, Norway and Liechtenstein) or of Switzerland,
the
Autorisation Provisoire de Séjour
(APS - Provisional Residency Permit)
allows you to remain one year in France after you graduate.
It is reserved for holders of a professional Bachelor's, a Master's-level degree and all graduates who are starting a company.
The travel visa or Schengen visa
If you are not
a national of a European Economic Area country (European Union country and Iceland, Norway and Liechtenstein) or of Switzerland, you can request a
travel visa
at the end of your studies. Reserved for holders of a Master's-level degree from a French higher education institute, it allows you to regularly return to France if you reside in another country after your studies in France.
Student visa: Campus France answers your questions
Regardless of your situation or nationality, check the following articles to find the answers to your questions concerning student visas:

法國教育中心面試所需文件 
Documents à présenter à l’entretien Campus France 
 
1. 有效護照正本。護照的有效日期須於赴法學習計畫結束後仍至少有三個月的效期。 
Votre passeport en cours de validité. La date de fin de validité doit être postérieure d’au moins 
3 mois à la date de fin de validité du visa sollicité. 
 
2. 法國學校開立之具名（預）註冊證明。請依以下符合您的身份準備： 
A. 由本中心線上系統申請學校者：請直接從法國教育中心線上系統下載您的（預）註冊證明。 
B. 已自行取得入學資格者 ：請務必提供載明學程名稱與就學期限的(預)註冊證明紙本正本， 並附
上影本一份。原則上，法國學校(預)註冊證明必須要有校方的親手簽名與蓋章。如果您的文件之
簽章為印製上去 ， 請務必保留好文件的信封 ， 並於面試當天將文件與信封一併出示 。唯交換/雙聯
學生可以電子檔列印出之版本送件。 
Attestation de (pré)-inscription nominative établie par un établissement français :  
A. Pour ceux postulant via la plateforme « É tudes en France » : l’attestation de (pré)-inscription 
est à télécharger en ligne.  
B. Pour les autres étudiants, l’attestation ORIGINALE de l’établissement mentionnant le nom 
du diplôme préparé ainsi que la durée des études (photocopie acceptée uniquement pour les 
étudiants d’é change). Veuillez noter que la signature manuscrite  ainsi que le cachet de 
l’établissement sont deux éléments indispensables qui doivent être portés sur l’attestation 
présentée. À  défaut d’une signature manuscrite, merci de bien vouloir conserver l’enveloppe 
du courrier reçu lors de votre entretien. 
 
3. 英文或法文最高學歷（畢業證書或在學證明）正本，並附上影本一份。 
Dernier diplôme obtenu ou attestation d’inscription pour ceux qui sont en cours d’études. 
 
 
備註:學生辦理簽證統一透過法國教育中心線上系統預約時間。已自行取得入學資格者，請務必備妥辦理簽證所需資料，
以便於面試結束送件辦理簽證。 
NB : La prise de rendez-vous pour demande de visa pour études est gérée directement par Campus France. Le dépôt 
du dossier de demande de visa peut avoir lieu le même jour que l’entretien Campus Franc à condition que votre dossier 
de demande de visa soit complet. 
 
法國在台協會 – 法國教育中心 
台北市敦化北路205號10樓 (民生東路口) 
T：02 - 2712 1233 Email：taipei@campusfrance.org 
對外開放時間：周一至周五 下午2~4點 
Bureau Français de Taipei – Campus France Taiwan 
10F, 205 Tun Hwa North Road, Taipei 
T：02 - 2712 1233 Email：taipei@campusfrance.org 
Horaires d’ouverture : du lundi au vendredi de 14h à 16h

Hello future EIVP student!
Are you preparing to start your studies at our wonderful school and are struggling to find accommodation?  → This page is for you!
The École des Ingénieurs de la Ville de Paris is located at 80 rue Rébeval in the 19th arrondissement of Paris.
EIVP is close to the “Belleville” station, served by lines 2 and 11. Line 11 of the Paris metro has recently been extended to Rosny-Bois-Perrier! You can also search for accommodation in several of the capital's arrondissements: 19th, 20th, 18th and 11th, as well as in the nearby communes of Les Lilas, Bagnolet, Romainville, Montreuil, Rosny-sous-Bois, etc.
Access our
Google Sheet
specially designed to help you find accommodation within the student network and/or find a roommate for the start of the school year.
Here
you'll find some general advice on finding accommodation!
Here are some examples of student residence accommodation close to the school:
-
Les Estudines Paris-Rosny residence
-
Cardinal Campus Palladium
-
Les Estudines Arago 1 Montreuil
-
Studéa Buttes-Chaumont 1
We invite you to consult the following websites to help you in your search!
-
Crous
: provides housing for students on scholarship. Around thirty places are available at EIVP. To give students the best possible support, it is possible to combine different types of assistance. In particular,
the Crous and Action Logement programs
can complement each other in terms of housing assistance.
-
Lokaviz
: offers accommodation in private homes.
-
Adele
: offers accommodation in student residences.
-
Logement EIVP Facebook group
: a self-help group for finding an apartment or shared flat.
-
Le site national des étudiants
: provides all the information you need to find accommodation, a guarantor, websites, procedures and financial aid.
-
RIVP
and
Hénéo
are landlords with which EIVP has signed agreements. These partnerships enable us to house some of our students every year.
-
Visale guarantee
: this is a free guarantee offered to tenants by Action Logement. It covers the payment of rent and damage to the principal residence, in the event of default by the tenant. Thanks to this reliable, free guarantee, tenants can find accommodation more easily and quickly, while reassuring their future landlord!
- Visa and health insurance requirements;
For students from outside the EU, the issuance of your visa may be subject to proof of short- or long-term health insurance. You can visit the following websites for further information:
www.cleiss.fr
or
https://www.international-sante.com/healthforexpats/
.
→ To obtain accommodation via Le Crous, RIVP or Hénéo, you need to go through the housing referent at the school.
Contact the EIVP schooling department:
service-scolarite@eivp-paris.fr

Course related information
Course structure
Admissions
Course overview
The Programme trains students and professionals in
urban planning for socio ecological transitions
through a rich mix of lectures, workshops and fieldwork with leading scholars and urban professionals. This semester offers the opportunity to dive into the
fertile learning ground that is the Parisian Metropolis
.
Is this course for me ?
Each year, the programme welcomes a cohort of up to 20 attendees, including exchange students from our international partners and free-moving candidates, seeking further training after completion of their studies.
Course details
Paris has been the birthplace of major urban models since the 19th century - and still is today. Current policies combine international attractiveness with an ambitious commitment to tackling the environmental and social challenges of the 21st century in the context of a historic European city. This reflects upon the programme’s interdisciplinary approach to urban planning, drawing on social sciences, engineering, design and environmental science, thus providing tools to critically engage with urban transitions.
At the curriculum’s core is the urban planning studio, in which students develop
analyses and proposals for real life project areas in the Paris area
. Recent topics include the low-carbon redevelopment of the Porte de Montreuil district and the future of the Bièvre, a river which ran through Paris before being buried and channeled in the early 20th century.
272 hours | 30 ECTS
UE 1 : Urban planning knowledge and practice (158h ; 13 ECTS)
Urban planning theory and practice (18h ; 4 ECTS)
Urban planning studio (140h ; 9 ECTS)
UE 2 : Socio-ecological Transitions in Urban Planning (42h ; 6 ECTS)
Urban planning and transitions in Paris: visits (18h ; 2 ECTS)
Urban natures (12h ; 2 ECTS)
Urban mobilities (12h ; 2 ETCS)
UE 3 : Representing the City (36h ; 6 ECTS)
Models for urban ecodesign (18h ; 3 ECTS)
International video workshop (18h ; 3 ECTS)
UE 4 : Languages and culture (36h ; 5 ECTS)
French foreign language (18h ; 2 ECTS)
Cultural diversity and intercultural management (18h ; 3 ECTS)
Requirements
English Level: B1 (with teacher's certificate)
Open to candidates with BSc / BEng degree or the French equivalent “licence” preferably in Architecture, Civil Engineering, Landscape Architecture, Urban Planning and design
Having a visa (consult:
https://www.eivp-paris.fr/international/how-get-visa
)
Calendar
There are two admission sessions. Applications end on
March 31st, 2026 (session 1)
and
May 31st (session 2).
Programme starts on
September 7, 2026
.
Programme ends on
December 18, 2026
.
Fees
Free of charge for exchange students,
5.055 € for free-movers
.
How to apply
If your university is a partner of EIVP
(consult
https://www.eivp-paris.fr/international/international-partnerships
), you have the possibility to come and study for 1 semester (30 ECTS) or 1 year (60 ECTS). You will not obtain a diploma from EIVP except in dual degree in Uban Engineering. You must first have been selected by your university (according to its terms and criteria) and officially announced by it to our university. You will then receive by email the complete instructions to proceed with your online application and provide the required documents. If your application is accepted, you will receive an admission letter by email that you can use for your administrative procedures, including the visa application if you are concerned.
If you are a free-mover student
, please contact the International Relations department at EIVP 📧
relations.internationales@eivp-paris.fr

Course related information
Course structure
Admissions
Course overview
The Programme trains students and professionals in
urban planning for socio ecological transitions
through a rich mix of lectures, workshops and fieldwork with leading scholars and urban professionals. This semester offers the opportunity to dive into the
fertile learning ground that is the Parisian Metropolis
.
Is this course for me ?
Each year, the programme welcomes a cohort of up to 20 attendees, including exchange students from our international partners and free-moving candidates, seeking further training after completion of their studies.
Course details
Paris has been the birthplace of major urban models since the 19th century - and still is today. Current policies combine international attractiveness with an ambitious commitment to tackling the environmental and social challenges of the 21st century in the context of a historic European city. This reflects upon the programme’s interdisciplinary approach to urban planning, drawing on social sciences, engineering, design and environmental science, thus providing tools to critically engage with urban transitions.
At the curriculum’s core is the urban planning studio, in which students develop
analyses and proposals for real life project areas in the Paris area
. Recent topics include the low-carbon redevelopment of the Porte de Montreuil district and the future of the Bièvre, a river which ran through Paris before being buried and channeled in the early 20th century.
272 hours | 30 ECTS
UE 1 : Urban planning knowledge and practice (158h ; 13 ECTS)
Urban planning theory and practice (18h ; 4 ECTS)
Urban planning studio (140h ; 9 ECTS)
UE 2 : Socio-ecological Transitions in Urban Planning (42h ; 6 ECTS)
Urban planning and transitions in Paris: visits (18h ; 2 ECTS)
Urban natures (12h ; 2 ECTS)
Urban mobilities (12h ; 2 ETCS)
UE 3 : Representing the City (36h ; 6 ECTS)
Models for urban ecodesign (18h ; 3 ECTS)
International video workshop (18h ; 3 ECTS)
UE 4 : Languages and culture (36h ; 5 ECTS)
French foreign language (18h ; 2 ECTS)
Cultural diversity and intercultural management (18h ; 3 ECTS)
Requirements
English Level: B1 (with teacher's certificate)
Open to candidates with BSc / BEng degree or the French equivalent “licence” preferably in Architecture, Civil Engineering, Landscape Architecture, Urban Planning and design
Having a visa (consult:
https://www.eivp-paris.fr/international/how-get-visa
)

There are two admission sessions. Applications end on
March 31st, 2026 (session 1)
and
May 31st (session 2).
Programme starts on
September 7, 2026
.
Programme ends on
December 18, 2026
.
Fees
Free of charge for exchange students,
5.055 € for free-movers
.
How to apply
If your university is a partner of EIVP
(consult
https://www.eivp-paris.fr/international/international-partnerships
), you have the possibility to come and study for 1 semester (30 ECTS) or 1 year (60 ECTS). You will not obtain a diploma from EIVP except in dual degree in Uban Engineering. You must first have been selected by your university (according to its terms and criteria) and officially announced by it to our university. You will then receive by email the complete instructions to proceed with your online application and provide the required documents. If your application is accepted, you will receive an admission letter by email that you can use for your administrative procedures, including the visa application if you are concerned.
If you are a free-mover student

•    Languages requirements at EIVP
Students, in urban engineering formation, must take two languages during their 1 and 2nd years.
English is compulsory.
The other courses are
Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, German and Mandarin
. Beginners are accepted in Spanish, Portuguese, Madarin and Italian. The student announces his choice at the time of administrative registration. Level tests are organized at the beginning of the school year for all the languages offered at EIVP. Students may, at their own expense, validate another language in another institution if, at the beginning of the school year, he can show a proof of registration and the final grade obtained.
For languages not offered at EIVP, students can enroll for free in language courses offered by CAPLA, the Centre d'Action pédagogique en langues de l'Université Gustave Eiffel, located on the Campus of the Université Gustave Eiffel in Marne la Vallée (accessible by RER A, 30 minutes from Châtelet).
For more information, contact
capla@univ-eiffel.fr
Tel: 01 60 95 76 21 (Languages offered: Chinese, German, Italian, Japanese, Latin, Portuguese, Russian, Korean, English +, English Help).
•
TOEIC
Language instruction is mandatory to get the diploma.
A session of the TOEIC® Listening and Reading Test is offered to all engineering students (2sessions by year). The minimum score to obtain is 785. The certificate of achievement is valid for 2 years. The date of issue must be during your studies at EIVP. Its validity does not have to be active when you obtain your diploma.
Other certifications accepted by the school are : Cambridge LINGUASKILL (160/200), Cambridge FCE or CAE (160/230), TOEFL ibt (72/120), Bright Language (3.5/5.0), Duolingo (100/160) or IELTS (5/9) (Academic or General)

地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。

Course related information
Course structure
Admissions
Course overview
The Programme trains students and professionals in
urban planning for socio ecological transitions
through a rich mix of lectures, workshops and fieldwork with leading scholars and urban professionals. This semester offers the opportunity to dive into the
fertile learning ground that is the Parisian Metropolis
.
Is this course for me ?
Each year, the programme welcomes a cohort of up to 20 attendees, including exchange students from our international partners and free-moving candidates, seeking further training after completion of their studies.
Course details
Paris has been the birthplace of major urban models since the 19th century - and still is today. Current policies combine international attractiveness with an ambitious commitment to tackling the environmental and social challenges of the 21st century in the context of a historic European city. This reflects upon the programme’s interdisciplinary approach to urban planning, drawing on social sciences, engineering, design and environmental science, thus providing tools to critically engage with urban transitions.
At the curriculum’s core is the urban planning studio, in which students develop
analyses and proposals for real life project areas in the Paris area
. Recent topics include the low-carbon redevelopment of the Porte de Montreuil district and the future of the Bièvre, a river which ran through Paris before being buried and channeled in the early 20th century.
272 hours | 30 ECTS
UE 1 : Urban planning knowledge and practice (158h ; 13 ECTS)
Urban planning theory and practice (18h ; 4 ECTS)
Urban planning studio (140h ; 9 ECTS)
UE 2 : Socio-ecological Transitions in Urban Planning (42h ; 6 ECTS)
Urban planning and transitions in Paris: visits (18h ; 2 ECTS)
Urban natures (12h ; 2 ECTS)
Urban mobilities (12h ; 2 ETCS)
UE 3 : Representing the City (36h ; 6 ECTS)
Models for urban ecodesign (18h ; 3 ECTS)
International video workshop (18h ; 3 ECTS)
UE 4 : Languages and culture (36h ; 5 ECTS)
French foreign language (18h ; 2 ECTS)
Cultural diversity and intercultural management (18h ; 3 ECTS)
Requirements
English Level: B1 (with teacher's certificate)
Open to candidates with BSc / BEng degree or the French equivalent “licence” preferably in Architecture, Civil Engineering, Landscape Architecture, Urban Planning and design
Having a visa (consult:
https://www.eivp-paris.fr/international/how-get-visa
)
Calendar
There are two admission sessions. Applications end on
March 31st, 2026 (session 1)
and
May 31st (session 2).
Programme starts on
September 7, 2026
.
Programme ends on
December 18, 2026
.
Fees
Free of charge for exchange students,
5.055 € for free-movers
.
How to apply
If your university is a partner of EIVP
(consult
https://www.eivp-paris.fr/international/international-partnerships
), you have the possibility to come and study for 1 semester (30 ECTS) or 1 year (60 ECTS). You will not obtain a diploma from EIVP except in dual degree in Uban Engineering. You must first have been selected by your university (according to its terms and criteria) and officially announced by it to our university. You will then receive by email the complete instructions to proceed with your online application and provide the required documents. If your application is accepted, you will receive an admission letter by email that you can use for your administrative procedures, including the visa application if you are concerned.
If you are a free-mover student
, please contact the International Relations department at EIVP 📧

original_evidence.text:
COURSE NAME
 HOURS
 ECTS
Urban planning knowledge and practice
Urban planning theory and practice
Main lecturer : Pedro Gomes
The module’s objectives are to provide insight on the main urban planning instruments
and objectives in France and in the Paris region in particular ; to link existing planning
documents, policies and practices to theoretical debates ; to develop comparative
thought between France and other national contexts. 
The module is lecture-based and built around a weekly reading assignment. Students
are assessed through a comparative essay between France and their place of origin,
on a planning issue of their choosing. Two in-class tutoring sessions are included in the
semester. 
Urban planning studio
Main lecturers : Jennifer Buyck and Pedro Gomes
In groups combining different nationalities and educational backgrounds, students
develop an autonomous ecological foresight exercise, including analysis and overall
strategy and concrete proposals. The main project tool used is the urban transect. 
The studio’s current topic is the future of the Bièvre river as a catalyst for urban
transitions. Local stakeholders and planning professionals, through site visits, lectures
and project reviews, among others. 
The planning studio is the backbone of the curriculum. Two full days are dedicated to it,
with six weekly hours of in-class tutoring.
The studio includes a COIL module with the MA in Architecture at IUAV (Venice) on
futuring techniques and scenario building.

COURSE NAME
 HOURS
 ECTS
Socio-ecological Transitions in Urban Planning
Urban planning and transitions in Paris - workshop
Coordinating lecturer: John Bingham-Hall
During a whole week, students actively and critically engage with transition initiatives in
the Paris region. The week’s’ format varies, including workhsops built around site visits
with urban professionals, to fieldwork- or project-based ones. The workshop may be
jointly led with students and faculty from other institutions in France and abroad. In
2026, students will critically engage with the city’s bioclimatic urbanism), in partnership
with the Paris School of Archtecture.
Urban natures
Main lecturer: Lou Gomez
Effective urban transitions must rethink the place of nature in urban areas. This course
introduces students to the issue, providing a theoretical background and practical
examples in the Paris region. Course topics include i) the major conceptual approaches
to nature and natural processes in cities, including ecosystem services and urban
metabolism; ii) planning and design approaches to green, blue and brown infrastructure
for ecosystem preservation and risk management; iii) environmental justice, i.e.
unequal access and vulnerability to urban natures.
42h

Urban mobilities
Main lecturers: Abel Girard and Marie Hue
Decarbonizing urban mobilities is a key factor in fighting climate change, promoting
urban health and struggling for spatial justice. This course’s main objective is to
introduce students to the relationships between urban space, urban and transportation
planning and mobilities. Course topics are i) main concepts in transportation and
mobility planning; ii) the mobility-urban planning nexus at different scales; iii) low
carbon mobilities, cyclable and walkable cities; iv) urban mobilities and inequality.
Examples from the Paris region will be used, through visits and/or case studies.

Representing the City
Models for urban ecodesign
Main lecturer: Florence Jacquinod
In this course, students learn to collect and use 2D and 3D geodata to analyse some
aspects of an urban site and to represent them in a GIS tool. Each session is divided
into two parts: a short introduction with conceptual notions and then practical exercises
using GIS tools and real world data. In this second part, quizzes are used to outline key
aspects in assessing the relevance of geodata and GIS tools for specific urban site
analyses. The course assignment contributes to data analysis within the Urban
Planning Studio.  
International video workshop
Coordinating lecturer: Jennifer Buyck
The workshop unites planning, engineering, architecture and arts students from
institutions in Chile, France, Italy and in the USA. During one week, students shoot,
edit video and sound in small groups, to collectively create their own version of Etudes
sur Paris, a 1928 silent film by André Sauvage. The workshop begins with a ciné-
concert of Sauvage’s film and ends with a screening of the students’ work.

Course related information
Course structure
Admissions
Course overview
The Programme trains students and professionals in
urban planning for socio ecological transitions
through a rich mix of lectures, workshops and fieldwork with leading scholars and urban professionals. This semester offers the opportunity to dive into the
fertile learning ground that is the Parisian Metropolis
.
Is this course for me ?
Each year, the programme welcomes a cohort of up to 20 attendees, including exchange students from our international partners and free-moving candidates, seeking further training after completion of their studies.
Course details
Paris has been the birthplace of major urban models since the 19th century - and still is today. Current policies combine international attractiveness with an ambitious commitment to tackling the environmental and social challenges of the 21st century in the context of a historic European city. This reflects upon the programme’s interdisciplinary approach to urban planning, drawing on social sciences, engineering, design and environmental science, thus providing tools to critically engage with urban transitions.
At the curriculum’s core is the urban planning studio, in which students develop
analyses and proposals for real life project areas in the Paris area
. Recent topics include the low-carbon redevelopment of the Porte de Montreuil district and the future of the Bièvre, a river which ran through Paris before being buried and channeled in the early 20th century.
272 hours | 30 ECTS
UE 1 : Urban planning knowledge and practice (158h ; 13 ECTS)
Urban planning theory and practice (18h ; 4 ECTS)
Urban planning studio (140h ; 9 ECTS)
UE 2 : Socio-ecological Transitions in Urban Planning (42h ; 6 ECTS)
Urban planning and transitions in Paris: visits (18h ; 2 ECTS)
Urban natures (12h ; 2 ECTS)
Urban mobilities (12h ; 2 ETCS)
UE 3 : Representing the City (36h ; 6 ECTS)
Models for urban ecodesign (18h ; 3 ECTS)
International video workshop (18h ; 3 ECTS)
UE 4 : Languages and culture (36h ; 5 ECTS)
French foreign language (18h ; 2 ECTS)
Cultural diversity and intercultural management (18h ; 3 ECTS)
Requirements
English Level: B1 (with teacher's certificate)
Open to candidates with BSc / BEng degree or the French equivalent “licence” preferably in Architecture, Civil Engineering, Landscape Architecture, Urban Planning and design

https://www.eivp-paris.fr/international/how-get-visa
)

and
May 31st (session 2).
Programme starts on
September 7, 2026
.

December 18, 2026
.

Free of charge for exchange students,
5.055 € for free-movers
.
How to apply
If your university is a partner of EIVP
(consult
https://www.eivp-paris.fr/international/international-partnerships
), you have the possibility to come and study for 1 semester (30 ECTS) or 1 year (60 ECTS). You will not obtain a diploma from EIVP except in dual degree in Uban Engineering. You must first have been selected by your university (according to its terms and criteria) and officially announced by it to our university. You will then receive by email the complete instructions to proceed with your online application and provide the required documents. If your application is accepted, you will receive an admission letter by email that you can use for your administrative procedures, including the visa application if you are concerned.
If you are a free-mover student
, please contact the International Relations department at EIVP 📧
