Visas
A
visa
is an official document issued by the competent authorities of a country. It must be
presented by a foreign visitor when they enter the country for which the visa applies
. Depending on the country and its laws, visas are required either for all visitors from other countries, or according to the visitor’s nationality.
It is a
prerequisite for entering and staying in a country
for a set period of time. However, it is not a guarantee as border authorities in certain countries may refuse to give a foreign visitor permission to enter their country, even if the visitor has a valid visa.
For more information:
https://france-visas.gouv.fr/en_US/web/france-visas
International Students / Degree-seeking Students
Espace Monde
is an organisation that
helps international students
interested in studying at the University of Rouen Normandy but
not registered at another university or on a student exchange programme
. With the help of
Espace Monde
‘s friendly and supportive staff, students can prepare properly for their stay here in Rouen and settle smoothly into life at the University of Rouen Normandy. More specifically,
Espace Monde
helps students with
all aspects of the university application process
, like giving advice and information on passing French language exams, CROUS student housing, obtaining financial support from the CAF and finding your way around the city.
For more information:
https://mesdemarches.univ-rouen.fr/en/practical-information/international-mobility/
If you are on an exchange programme, please check out the
Exchange Students
section.
How to apply
To enrol on a Bachelor’s (Licence) or Master’s degree course at the University of Rouen Normandy,
potential applicants must have their French Baccalauréat or equivalent
(DAP – see below) and have a minimum level of B2 in French.
Students who do not have the French Baccalauréat and wish to enrol on a French Bachelor’s degree course must complete a
Demande d’Admission Préalable
– DAP (Preliminary Admission Request) exam before admission.
For more information:
http://www.enseignementsup-recherche.gouv.fr
For applicants who need French language competency certificates, the DELF/DALF exams can be taken in your home country.
For more information about the DELF exam:
https://www.france-education-international.fr/en/diplome/delf-tout-public?langue=enhttp://www.ciep.fr
For applicants who have little experience of the French language, have recently begun learning French, or would like to start learning the language, we offer
up to two years of preparatory language classes
. Students can register for intensive French language classes at the university’s
Maison des Langues
. This gives non-French speakers who would like to enrol at the University of Rouen Normandy an opportunity to get up to speed in terms of language, culture and university life before embarking on a Bachelor’s or Master’s course. Signing up to this preparatory option also gives international students
time to get to know the Normandy region
, explore the city, learn about its history, and join various societies and sports clubs.
Maison des Langues
Bâtiment 7C
17 rue Lavoisier
76821 MONT SAINT AIGNAN Cedex, France
Contact:
mdl@univ-rouen.fr
How to register
International students registering for the first time at the University of Rouen Normandy need to
go to Espace Monde’s one-stop office
(Building B4 – Michel Serres – entrance hall) on the Mont-Saint-Aignan campus.
Here are the different steps for completing your registration:
Before registering
at the University of Rouen Normandy, you need to provide a
receipt
proving that you have paid your
CVEC
(student and campus life contribution) fees, which is issued by the CROUS from 1 July.
You will find all the information you need by clicking on the following links:
http://www.crous-normandie.fr/crous/cvec-contribution-vie-etudiante-de-campus/
or
cvec.etudiant.gouv.fr
Register in person
at the Espace Monde one-stop office
Medical check-up (optional)
Enrol
on your course (via your personal online workspace (ENT))
Open a
Multipass account
(via your personal online workspace (ENT))
Create your student card:
Léocarte
(via your personal online workspace (ENT))
Exchange students
Over 300 students
are accepted on an
exchange programme
every year at the University of Rouen Normandy! URN has
partnerships with over 239 universities
, giving the student population a very international feel. Exchange programme agreements signed with other universities include:
Erasmus
BCI-PÉÉ – an exchange programme between France and Québec (Canada)
For first semester and/or full year exchanges, the application deadline is
1 June
. For students applying for the second semester, the application deadline is
1 November
.
For more information and to apply:
http://international.univ-rouen.fr/etudiants-en-echange-519277.kjsp
How to apply
Check that
your university is partnered with the University of Rouen Normandy
. To do this, contact the international office at your university and ask what the procedure is (form, prerequisites, application submission dates, study period, etc.).
Once you have completed all the formalities,
your university will let you know
if your request to study in Rouen has been accepted.
If it has, congratulations!
We will get in touch with you
and send you the
forms you need to fill in
, such as: your Learning Agreement, your student accommodation application, an information sheet.
A
letter of acceptance
will be sent to you as soon as your application has been confirmed.
Please note: we would like to remind all students wishing to come to the University of Rouen Normandy that most of the lectures and seminars are given in French.
Your French therefore needs to be relatively good for your studies to be a success
.
Below is a list of all the lecturers representing each department in the context of exchange programmes (Arts, Medicine, Law, Economics, etc.) You may contact them to receive the list of lectures and seminars given:
https://mesdemarches.univ-rouen.fr/en/inscriptions/eu-international-students-erasmus-and-icm-exchanges/
How to register
Before you arrive, you will be offered
an appointment to register at the university
. When you get here, you will need to go to the
Direction des Relations Internationales et de la Coopération
(international office) at the appointed date and time.
Espace Michel Serres, 2nd floor
Rue Thomas Becket
76821 MONT SAINT AIGNAN Cedex, France
service.international@univ-rouen.fr
Once you have registered at the university, you will need to go to
your faculty’s department office
to register for your course.

EU international students – Erasmus+ and ICM exchanges
Home
EU international students – Erasmus+ and ICM exchanges
Exchange students
Every year, the University of Rouen Normandie welcomes around 150 exchange students.
If your home university has selected you to come to the University of Rouen Normandie as part of an exchange program, you’ll find some useful information here.
APPLYING TO UNIVERSITY
Applications :
Application deadlines are as follows:
–
June 1 for 1st semester and full-year mobility
–
November 1 for 2nd semester mobility
Appointments :
Nominations must be sent by e-mail to the following address:
mobility.in@univ-rouen.fr
Nomination deadlines are as follows:
– May 15 for 1st semester and full-year mobility
– October 15 for 2nd semester mobility
An online application link will be sent to you once your university has selected you and informed the University of Rouen Normandy.
If the University of Rouen’s pedagogical coordinators approve your application, you can then send them your pedagogical/learning agreement, already signed by your university.
A final letter of acceptance will be sent to you once your teaching contract has been signed by both universities. Please note that no letter of acceptance will be sent until we have received your validated teaching contract.
We would like to remind all Erasmus+ students who wish to come to the University of Rouen Normandie that all courses are taught in French. A B2 level of the CEFR is therefore strongly recommended to ensure that your studies run smoothly. Examinations for Erasmus+ students are the same as those for students at the Université de Rouen, and no adaptation will be proposed.
RENTRÉE 2024 – GUICHET D’ACCUEIL DES ETUDIANTS EN ÉCHANGE
August 26 to September 23
Monday to Thursday, 9am to 12pm and 1:30pm to 4pm
Office 011, Espace Michel Serres
UNIVERSITY HOUSING
When you register, you can apply for a room in a public student residence managed by CROUS Normandie, an external partner of the University. For more information,
click here
.
Please note that the university does not manage accommodations and the mobility service only acts as a liaison; we have no information on accommodations or application files. The mobility department will forward your details to CROUS, who will contact you to allocate rooms.
Contact
Mobility department
Mont Saint Aignan site, Michel Serres building, first floor, office 11
mobility.in@univ-rouen.fr

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。 
 
 
 
□我已閱讀並同意上述所有內容。

Underage students

The procedure is closed for 2024-2025.

Exceptional requests for late registration
You can make an exceptional request for late registration according to the schedule on the form below.
First-semester application form available here
Second semester application form available here
File transfer
The “arrival” transfer is MANDATORY if you have already been registered at least once at a French university, whatever your discipline or degree.

Form available here

.

Visas
A
visa
is an official document issued by the competent authorities of a country. It must be
presented by a foreign visitor when they enter the country for which the visa applies
. Depending on the country and its laws, visas are required either for all visitors from other countries, or according to the visitor’s nationality.
It is a
prerequisite for entering and staying in a country
for a set period of time. However, it is not a guarantee as border authorities in certain countries may refuse to give a foreign visitor permission to enter their country, even if the visitor has a valid visa.
For more information:
https://france-visas.gouv.fr/en_US/web/france-visas
International Students / Degree-seeking Students
Espace Monde
is an organisation that
helps international students
interested in studying at the University of Rouen Normandy but
not registered at another university or on a student exchange programme
. With the help of
Espace Monde
‘s friendly and supportive staff, students can prepare properly for their stay here in Rouen and settle smoothly into life at the University of Rouen Normandy. More specifically,
Espace Monde
helps students with
all aspects of the university application process
, like giving advice and information on passing French language exams, CROUS student housing, obtaining financial support from the CAF and finding your way around the city.
For more information:
https://mesdemarches.univ-rouen.fr/en/practical-information/international-mobility/
If you are on an exchange programme, please check out the
Exchange Students
section.
How to apply
To enrol on a Bachelor’s (Licence) or Master’s degree course at the University of Rouen Normandy,
potential applicants must have their French Baccalauréat or equivalent
(DAP – see below) and have a minimum level of B2 in French.
Students who do not have the French Baccalauréat and wish to enrol on a French Bachelor’s degree course must complete a
Demande d’Admission Préalable
– DAP (Preliminary Admission Request) exam before admission.
For more information:
http://www.enseignementsup-recherche.gouv.fr
For applicants who need French language competency certificates, the DELF/DALF exams can be taken in your home country.
For more information about the DELF exam:
https://www.france-education-international.fr/en/diplome/delf-tout-public?langue=enhttp://www.ciep.fr
For applicants who have little experience of the French language, have recently begun learning French, or would like to start learning the language, we offer
up to two years of preparatory language classes
. Students can register for intensive French language classes at the university’s
Maison des Langues
. This gives non-French speakers who would like to enrol at the University of Rouen Normandy an opportunity to get up to speed in terms of language, culture and university life before embarking on a Bachelor’s or Master’s course. Signing up to this preparatory option also gives international students
time to get to know the Normandy region
, explore the city, learn about its history, and join various societies and sports clubs.
Maison des Langues
Bâtiment 7C
17 rue Lavoisier
76821 MONT SAINT AIGNAN Cedex, France
Contact:
mdl@univ-rouen.fr
How to register
International students registering for the first time at the University of Rouen Normandy need to
go to Espace Monde’s one-stop office
(Building B4 – Michel Serres – entrance hall) on the Mont-Saint-Aignan campus.
Here are the different steps for completing your registration:
Before registering
at the University of Rouen Normandy, you need to provide a
receipt
proving that you have paid your
CVEC
(student and campus life contribution) fees, which is issued by the CROUS from 1 July.
You will find all the information you need by clicking on the following links:
http://www.crous-normandie.fr/crous/cvec-contribution-vie-etudiante-de-campus/
or
cvec.etudiant.gouv.fr
Register in person
at the Espace Monde one-stop office
Medical check-up (optional)
Enrol
on your course (via your personal online workspace (ENT))
Open a
Multipass account
(via your personal online workspace (ENT))
Create your student card:
Léocarte
(via your personal online workspace (ENT))
Exchange students
Over 300 students
are accepted on an
exchange programme
every year at the University of Rouen Normandy! URN has
partnerships with over 239 universities
, giving the student population a very international feel. Exchange programme agreements signed with other universities include:
Erasmus
BCI-PÉÉ – an exchange programme between France and Québec (Canada)
For first semester and/or full year exchanges, the application deadline is
1 June
. For students applying for the second semester, the application deadline is
1 November
.
For more information and to apply:
http://international.univ-rouen.fr/etudiants-en-echange-519277.kjsp
How to apply
Check that
your university is partnered with the University of Rouen Normandy
. To do this, contact the international office at your university and ask what the procedure is (form, prerequisites, application submission dates, study period, etc.).
Once you have completed all the formalities,
your university will let you know
if your request to study in Rouen has been accepted.
If it has, congratulations!
We will get in touch with you
and send you the
forms you need to fill in
, such as: your Learning Agreement, your student accommodation application, an information sheet.
A
letter of acceptance
will be sent to you as soon as your application has been confirmed.
Please note: we would like to remind all students wishing to come to the University of Rouen Normandy that most of the lectures and seminars are given in French.
Your French therefore needs to be relatively good for your studies to be a success
.
Below is a list of all the lecturers representing each department in the context of exchange programmes (Arts, Medicine, Law, Economics, etc.) You may contact them to receive the list of lectures and seminars given:
https://mesdemarches.univ-rouen.fr/en/inscriptions/eu-international-students-erasmus-and-icm-exchanges/
How to register
Before you arrive, you will be offered
an appointment to register at the university
. When you get here, you will need to go to the
Direction des Relations Internationales et de la Coopération
(international office) at the appointed date and time.
Espace Michel Serres, 2nd floor
Rue Thomas Becket
76821 MONT SAINT AIGNAN Cedex, France
service.international@univ-rouen.fr
Once you have registered at the university, you will need to go to
your faculty’s department office
to register for your course.

Home
EU international students – Erasmus+ and ICM exchanges
Exchange students
Every year, the University of Rouen Normandie welcomes around 150 exchange students.
If your home university has selected you to come to the University of Rouen Normandie as part of an exchange program, you’ll find some useful information here.
APPLYING TO UNIVERSITY
Applications :
Application deadlines are as follows:
–
June 1 for 1st semester and full-year mobility
–
November 1 for 2nd semester mobility
Appointments :
Nominations must be sent by e-mail to the following address:
mobility.in@univ-rouen.fr
Nomination deadlines are as follows:
– May 15 for 1st semester and full-year mobility
– October 15 for 2nd semester mobility
An online application link will be sent to you once your university has selected you and informed the University of Rouen Normandy.
If the University of Rouen’s pedagogical coordinators approve your application, you can then send them your pedagogical/learning agreement, already signed by your university.
A final letter of acceptance will be sent to you once your teaching contract has been signed by both universities. Please note that no letter of acceptance will be sent until we have received your validated teaching contract.
We would like to remind all Erasmus+ students who wish to come to the University of Rouen Normandie that all courses are taught in French. A B2 level of the CEFR is therefore strongly recommended to ensure that your studies run smoothly. Examinations for Erasmus+ students are the same as those for students at the Université de Rouen, and no adaptation will be proposed.
RENTRÉE 2024 – GUICHET D’ACCUEIL DES ETUDIANTS EN ÉCHANGE
August 26 to September 23
Monday to Thursday, 9am to 12pm and 1:30pm to 4pm
Office 011, Espace Michel Serres
UNIVERSITY HOUSING
When you register, you can apply for a room in a public student residence managed by CROUS Normandie, an external partner of the University. For more information,
click here
.
Please note that the university does not manage accommodations and the mobility service only acts as a liaison; we have no information on accommodations or application files. The mobility department will forward your details to CROUS, who will contact you to allocate rooms.

Visas
A
visa
is an official document issued by the competent authorities of a country. It must be
presented by a foreign visitor when they enter the country for which the visa applies
. Depending on the country and its laws, visas are required either for all visitors from other countries, or according to the visitor’s nationality.
It is a
prerequisite for entering and staying in a country
for a set period of time. However, it is not a guarantee as border authorities in certain countries may refuse to give a foreign visitor permission to enter their country, even if the visitor has a valid visa.
For more information:
https://france-visas.gouv.fr/en_US/web/france-visas
International Students / Degree-seeking Students
Espace Monde
is an organisation that
helps international students
interested in studying at the University of Rouen Normandy but
not registered at another university or on a student exchange programme
. With the help of
Espace Monde
‘s friendly and supportive staff, students can prepare properly for their stay here in Rouen and settle smoothly into life at the University of Rouen Normandy. More specifically,
Espace Monde
helps students with
all aspects of the university application process
, like giving advice and information on passing French language exams, CROUS student housing, obtaining financial support from the CAF and finding your way around the city.
For more information:
https://mesdemarches.univ-rouen.fr/en/practical-information/international-mobility/
If you are on an exchange programme, please check out the
Exchange Students
section.
How to apply
To enrol on a Bachelor’s (Licence) or Master’s degree course at the University of Rouen Normandy,
potential applicants must have their French Baccalauréat or equivalent
(DAP – see below) and have a minimum level of B2 in French.
Students who do not have the French Baccalauréat and wish to enrol on a French Bachelor’s degree course must complete a
Demande d’Admission Préalable
– DAP (Preliminary Admission Request) exam before admission.
For more information:
http://www.enseignementsup-recherche.gouv.fr
For applicants who need French language competency certificates, the DELF/DALF exams can be taken in your home country.
For more information about the DELF exam:
https://www.france-education-international.fr/en/diplome/delf-tout-public?langue=enhttp://www.ciep.fr
For applicants who have little experience of the French language, have recently begun learning French, or would like to start learning the language, we offer
up to two years of preparatory language classes
. Students can register for intensive French language classes at the university’s
Maison des Langues
. This gives non-French speakers who would like to enrol at the University of Rouen Normandy an opportunity to get up to speed in terms of language, culture and university life before embarking on a Bachelor’s or Master’s course. Signing up to this preparatory option also gives international students
time to get to know the Normandy region
, explore the city, learn about its history, and join various societies and sports clubs.
Maison des Langues
Bâtiment 7C
17 rue Lavoisier
76821 MONT SAINT AIGNAN Cedex, France
Contact:
mdl@univ-rouen.fr
How to register
International students registering for the first time at the University of Rouen Normandy need to
go to Espace Monde’s one-stop office
(Building B4 – Michel Serres – entrance hall) on the Mont-Saint-Aignan campus.
Here are the different steps for completing your registration:
Before registering
at the University of Rouen Normandy, you need to provide a
receipt
proving that you have paid your
CVEC
(student and campus life contribution) fees, which is issued by the CROUS from 1 July.
You will find all the information you need by clicking on the following links:
http://www.crous-normandie.fr/crous/cvec-contribution-vie-etudiante-de-campus/
or
cvec.etudiant.gouv.fr
Register in person
at the Espace Monde one-stop office
Medical check-up (optional)
Enrol
on your course (via your personal online workspace (ENT))
Open a
Multipass account
(via your personal online workspace (ENT))
Create your student card:
Léocarte
(via your personal online workspace (ENT))
Exchange students
Over 300 students
are accepted on an
exchange programme
every year at the University of Rouen Normandy! URN has
partnerships with over 239 universities
, giving the student population a very international feel. Exchange programme agreements signed with other universities include:
Erasmus
BCI-PÉÉ – an exchange programme between France and Québec (Canada)
For first semester and/or full year exchanges, the application deadline is
1 June
. For students applying for the second semester, the application deadline is
1 November
.
For more information and to apply:
http://international.univ-rouen.fr/etudiants-en-echange-519277.kjsp
How to apply
Check that
your university is partnered with the University of Rouen Normandy
. To do this, contact the international office at your university and ask what the procedure is (form, prerequisites, application submission dates, study period, etc.).
Once you have completed all the formalities,
your university will let you know
if your request to study in Rouen has been accepted.
If it has, congratulations!
We will get in touch with you
and send you the
forms you need to fill in
, such as: your Learning Agreement, your student accommodation application, an information sheet.
A
letter of acceptance
will be sent to you as soon as your application has been confirmed.
Please note: we would like to remind all students wishing to come to the University of Rouen Normandy that most of the lectures and seminars are given in French.
Your French therefore needs to be relatively good for your studies to be a success
.
Below is a list of all the lecturers representing each department in the context of exchange programmes (Arts, Medicine, Law, Economics, etc.) You may contact them to receive the list of lectures and seminars given:
https://mesdemarches.univ-rouen.fr/en/inscriptions/eu-international-students-erasmus-and-icm-exchanges/
How to register
Before you arrive, you will be offered
an appointment to register at the university
. When you get here, you will need to go to the
Direction des Relations Internationales et de la Coopération
(international office) at the appointed date and time.
Espace Michel Serres, 2nd floor
Rue Thomas Becket
76821 MONT SAINT AIGNAN Cedex, France
service.international@univ-rouen.fr
Once you have registered at the university, you will need to go to
your faculty’s department office
to register for your course.

The CVEC
Pursuant to Law no. 2018-166 of March 8, 2018 on student orientation and success,
all students enrolled in initial training at a higher education institution must pay the Contribution de Vie Étudiante et de Campus (CVEC) before proceeding with their administrative registration.
This contribution, introduced by article L841-5 of the French Education Code, aims to strengthen social support, health services, cultural initiatives and sports activities for students.
Payment is made online via the Crous website.
Paying the CVEC
Tremplin Phénix Normandie – Event financed by the CVEC
At the end of this process, a certificate of payment or exemption will be issued.
Students receiving social grants, beneficiaries of subsidiary protection and refugees are exempt from payment, but must still log on to the platform to obtain their attestation, which is essential for administrative registration.
For further information, please consult the official Crous website or contact our administrative services.

EU international students – Erasmus+ and ICM exchanges
Home
EU international students – Erasmus+ and ICM exchanges
Exchange students
Every year, the University of Rouen Normandie welcomes around 150 exchange students.
If your home university has selected you to come to the University of Rouen Normandie as part of an exchange program, you’ll find some useful information here.
APPLYING TO UNIVERSITY
Applications :
Application deadlines are as follows:
–
June 1 for 1st semester and full-year mobility
–
November 1 for 2nd semester mobility
Appointments :
Nominations must be sent by e-mail to the following address:
mobility.in@univ-rouen.fr
Nomination deadlines are as follows:
– May 15 for 1st semester and full-year mobility
– October 15 for 2nd semester mobility
An online application link will be sent to you once your university has selected you and informed the University of Rouen Normandy.
If the University of Rouen’s pedagogical coordinators approve your application, you can then send them your pedagogical/learning agreement, already signed by your university.
A final letter of acceptance will be sent to you once your teaching contract has been signed by both universities. Please note that no letter of acceptance will be sent until we have received your validated teaching contract.
We would like to remind all Erasmus+ students who wish to come to the University of Rouen Normandie that all courses are taught in French. A B2 level of the CEFR is therefore strongly recommended to ensure that your studies run smoothly. Examinations for Erasmus+ students are the same as those for students at the Université de Rouen, and no adaptation will be proposed.
RENTRÉE 2024 – GUICHET D’ACCUEIL DES ETUDIANTS EN ÉCHANGE
August 26 to September 23
Monday to Thursday, 9am to 12pm and 1:30pm to 4pm
Office 011, Espace Michel Serres
UNIVERSITY HOUSING
When you register, you can apply for a room in a public student residence managed by CROUS Normandie, an external partner of the University. For more information,
click here
.
Please note that the university does not manage accommodations and the mobility service only acts as a liaison; we have no information on accommodations or application files. The mobility department will forward your details to CROUS, who will contact you to allocate rooms.
Contact
Mobility department
Mont Saint Aignan site, Michel Serres building, first floor, office 11
mobility.in@univ-rouen.fr

Social security
As of the start of the 2019-2020 academic year, the student social security system no longer exists.
As a new student, you remain affiliated to your current social security scheme (usually that of your parents or legal guardians).
If you are an international student from outside the European Union, you must apply for affiliation to the
Caisse Primaire d’Assurance Maladie
(CPAM).
You will also need to do this if you are a French national from New Caledonia or Wallis and Futuna, or if you were born abroad.
If you are an EU/EEA or Swiss national, you can apply for a European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) from the social security organization in your home country.
Find out more
Mutual insurance companies
Student mutual insurers continue to offer complementary health insurance specifically designed for students.

Additional information
Making an appointment and waiting time
Please make an appointment only when you are able to submit all of the required documents.
For visa application :
https://consulat.gouv.fr/en/bureau-francais-de-taipei/appointment?name=VISAS
For passport application :
https://consulat.gouv.fr/en/bureau-francais-de-taipei/appointment?name=Retrait%20de%20passeport%20-%20Visas
Waiting time for an appointment :
The average waiting time for an appointment for short and long-stay visas is
48 hours
This waiting time may be extended up to
20 working days
prior to and during summer time.
Likewise, an increase of applications is to be expected prior to winter school holidays. As getting an appointment may exceed the normal waiting time, applicants are encouraged to submit their visa application with sufficient anticipation to avoid having to postpone their departure.
This appointment procedure does not apply to students as their appointments are arranged directly by Campus France.
Security information
When visiting the French Office in Taipei, you must not possess any weapon or dangerous product. Security checks are carried out prior to admission into the premises.
The use of mobile phones, cameras or other audio or video recording devices is strictly prohibited. You will be asked to drop off your mobile phone in lockers provided for this purpose before entering the waiting room.
Public holidays / closures
Weekly closing on
Saturdays
and
Sundays
.
Holidays in 2026:
May 1st : Labour Day
June 19th : Dragon Boat Festival
September 25th : Mid-Autumn Festival
September 28th : Teacher's Day
October 9th : Compensatory leave for Taiwan National Day
October 26th : Compensatory leave for Retrocession Day
December 25th : Constitution Day
Practical informations on your appointment
Preparation
You must submit all the required documents on the day of your appointment. No document sent to the visa section by any other means will be accepted.
In order to prepare your visa application, please consult the list of documents required according to the purpose of your stay on the France-Visas website.
Please note that only visa service officers are authorized to request additional supporting documents and that no third party individual or organization is allowed in matters regarding visas.
Submitting your visa application
: visa applications must be submitted by the applicant itself at the visa section. The French Office in Taipei will not process any visa application received through mail or any other means.
Do not forget to bring with you :
Confirmation of your appointment (printed) ;
Your passport ;
Your photo which meets the ICAO standards and issued less than 6 months ago ;
The printed France-visas filled form ;
All the requested documents listed on the France-visas website.
Registration of biometric data
All visas delivered by France are biometric.
Visa applicants above the age of 12 years old must come to the visa section when submitting their first visa application. The following biometric identifiers will be collected: a photo (which must be less than 6 months old), will be scanned on the day of your appointment, and your fingerprints will be collected.
However, it is possible to recover your biometric data if a former Schengen visa has been issued within the preceding 59 months.
Children under the age of 12 are exempted from fingerprints collection. The visa application must be submitted by one of the child’s parents or by the person who holds parental authority. The child’s
ICAO-compliant photograph (pdf)
will then be scanned. The child must be present when submitting the visa application.
Track your application and collect your passport
You have to make an appointment to collect your passport on the following link :
https://consulat.gouv.fr/en/bureau-francais-de-taipei/appointment?name=Retrait%20de%20passeport%20-%20Visas
If you are unable to come to collect your passport, a third party with a power of attorney, your payment receipt, a copy of your ID and of his own ID may collect it for you.
Particular situations
Taiwanese passport holders
Holders of a Taiwanese passport
with their identity number written on it, who wish to travel to Europe to one or several Schengen member states are exempted from having a visa for touristic, family or business stays of less than 90 days.
France has extended this exemption for Taiwanese nationals traveling to France’s non-European territories : French overseas departments, and French overseas collectivities and territories.
Taiwanese nationals who hold of a Taiwanese passport which does not include their identity number must apply for a short stay visa.
People in possession of a passport which does not include their identity number must contact the French Office.
Official passports
Visas issued to holders of official passports in the course of their duties are free of charge.
Studying in France
Students wishing to study in France for a period exceeding 3 months are obliged to enroll on the website of Campus France beforehand and also complete the educational evaluation procedure (
Studies in France
) and only then may they submit their student visa application.
The mission of Campus France is to guide and advise Taiwanese students wishing to continue their studies in France. Campus France provides extensive information on all courses provided by French Higher education system as well as specific information regarding the different French establishments permitting students to build- with success, their journey of academic mobility.
Campus France allows you to construct a step-by-step project of your studies in France. Its website allows you to create an online personalized account as well as a place to discuss with
Campus France representatives
.
The visa section is in charge of processing visa applications according to the rules and regulations in force. It is not authorized to give any information regarding dossiers being processed by telephone.
Campus France procedure for studying in France is as follows:
Inscription
Create an
account
Online completion of your application
Payment of services charges via bank transfer
Interview and submitting Campus France application
Once the service charges have been validated, you may proceed by making an appointment online on the Campus France website. You simply need to choose the date and time which suits you amongst the time slots proposed on your personal online account.
During off-peak season, there are 3 working days waiting time. During high peak season, there might be up to 10 working days waiting time.
On the day of your appointment, you should come to the Campus France Office bringing with you all of the
documents required (pdf)
.
The educational interview consists of an oral presentation of your personal studies plan and answering questions from the counselors regarding your application file. The interview may be proceeded in French, English or Chinese depending on the course you have chosen.
Submitting your student visa application :
You may submit your visa application dossier the same day as your interview with Campus France - no appointment with the visa section is necessary in this case provided that your visa application dossier is complete. You must submit your dossier personally at one of the visa section counters where you biometric data will be registered.
Bring photocopies of all substantiating documents as there is no possibility of making photocopies on the premises.
Once your have paid the application fee (in cash or by Easy Card), you will receive a receipt and your visa application will be processed by the visa section.
Processing time:
Approximately three weeks. During the summer peak, the processing time is up to one month.
Help
In case of difficulties related to your visa application, consular services can be contacted
by email only
.

Visa, Residence permit
Depending on your nationality, your situation and the length of your stay, you may be able to obtain a visa to study or conduct research in France or to return here after you graduate.
France-Visas
France-Visas
is the official website for visa application to France.
Please connect to:
https://france-visas.gouv.fr/
You will find all information you need to prepare your stay in France.
Apply for a visa on France-Visas
France-Visas allows international students to submit digital copies of their supporting documents when they complete their online visa application. This new service is initially available to international students residing in countries where visa applications are outsourced and available online. It allows for an accelerated process at the external service provider.
Prerequisites for a digitalized visa application
To be eligible to submit a digitalized visa application, you must meet the following conditions:
Be an international student applying to study in France.
Be applying for a long-stay student visa only.
Reside in a country where an external service provider is available for visa application collection.
Steps for the online visa application
If you meet the prerequisites, you can complete your student visa application in 4 steps:
Fill out your online visa application on France-Visas and upload your documents.
Submit your passport and signed form in person at the collection center.
Track your application online on the service provider's website.
Collect your passport.

No visa obligation for European students
If you are a national of a European Economic Area country (European Union country (EU) and Iceland, Norway and Liechtenstein) or Switzerland,
you do not need a student visa to study or do an internship in France.
You may freely enter French territory regardless of the length of your stay or your studies.
On the other hand, you must have a sickness and maternity insurance and sufficient financial resources to meet your needs and those of any of your family you may be supporting.
Citizens of the EU/EEA/Switzerland may
work while studying in France
without a residency permit to a maximum of 964 hours per year.
The short stay student visa
If you are not a national of a European Economic Area country (European Union country and Iceland, Norway and Liechtenstein) or of Switzerland, and depending on your nationality, you must obtain a student visa to study in France
even if your stay is
less than 3 months
.
There are two types of short stay visa:
the "short stay for studies" (
court séjour pour études
) visa and the "student in competition"
(
étudiant concours
) visa, which should be requested if you are convoked by a French institute for an exam or interview.
Note that nationals from certain non-European countries are not required to have a visa if their stay does not exceed 90 days. Check the article "
The student visa short stay
"for more information on this subject.
The long stay student visa
If you are not a national of a European Economic Area country (European Union country and Iceland, Norway and Liechtenstein) or of Switzerland,
you must request a student long stay visa
to study, conduct research or do an internship in France
for more than 3 months
.
There are two types of long term visas:
1/ the Long Term Visa used as Residence Permit (VLS-TS)
This visa allows you to remain in France for one year without needing to request a residency permit. You will still have to have your visa approved on arrival. Depending on the nature of your stay,
there are three types of long stay visas
:
the
student VLS-TS
for studies at the Bachelor's and Master's level;
the
Talent passport VLS-TS
for a doctorate and beyond;
the
internship VLS-TS
to do an internship in France as part of the programme you are enrolled in in your country of residence.
2/ the Temporary Long Term Visa (VLS-T)
With the
VLS-T
, you can stay in France for 1 year, and you don’t need to validate it at your arrival. It cannot be renewed, and it doesn’t grant the rights than the VLS-TS.
The Working Holiday visa
In the framework of a reciprocal agreement with several countries,
France grants Working Holiday visas
(vacances-travail)
.
Reserved for young people aged 18 to 30, they let you spend one year in France to learn about the country without studying here. They let you work in France to round out your resources during the year.
Check the article "
Working Holiday visa
" to find out if you are eligible for this and for more information on the subject.
Provisional residency permit
If you are not a national of a European Economic Area country (European Union country and Iceland, Norway and Liechtenstein) or of Switzerland,
the
Autorisation Provisoire de Séjour
(APS - Provisional Residency Permit)
allows you to remain one year in France after you graduate.
It is reserved for holders of a professional Bachelor's, a Master's-level degree and all graduates who are starting a company.
The travel visa or Schengen visa
If you are not
a national of a European Economic Area country (European Union country and Iceland, Norway and Liechtenstein) or of Switzerland, you can request a
travel visa
at the end of your studies. Reserved for holders of a Master's-level degree from a French higher education institute, it allows you to regularly return to France if you reside in another country after your studies in France.
Student visa: Campus France answers your questions
Regardless of your situation or nationality, check the following articles to find the answers to your questions concerning student visas:

法國教育中心面試所需文件 
Documents à présenter à l’entretien Campus France 
 
1. 有效護照正本。護照的有效日期須於赴法學習計畫結束後仍至少有三個月的效期。 
Votre passeport en cours de validité. La date de fin de validité doit être postérieure d’au moins 
3 mois à la date de fin de validité du visa sollicité. 
 
2. 法國學校開立之具名（預）註冊證明。請依以下符合您的身份準備： 
A. 由本中心線上系統申請學校者：請直接從法國教育中心線上系統下載您的（預）註冊證明。 
B. 已自行取得入學資格者 ：請務必提供載明學程名稱與就學期限的(預)註冊證明紙本正本， 並附
上影本一份。原則上，法國學校(預)註冊證明必須要有校方的親手簽名與蓋章。如果您的文件之
簽章為印製上去 ， 請務必保留好文件的信封 ， 並於面試當天將文件與信封一併出示 。唯交換/雙聯
學生可以電子檔列印出之版本送件。 
Attestation de (pré)-inscription nominative établie par un établissement français :  
A. Pour ceux postulant via la plateforme « É tudes en France » : l’attestation de (pré)-inscription 
est à télécharger en ligne.  
B. Pour les autres étudiants, l’attestation ORIGINALE de l’établissement mentionnant le nom 
du diplôme préparé ainsi que la durée des études (photocopie acceptée uniquement pour les 
étudiants d’é change). Veuillez noter que la signature manuscrite  ainsi que le cachet de 
l’établissement sont deux éléments indispensables qui doivent être portés sur l’attestation 
présentée. À  défaut d’une signature manuscrite, merci de bien vouloir conserver l’enveloppe 
du courrier reçu lors de votre entretien. 
 
3. 英文或法文最高學歷（畢業證書或在學證明）正本，並附上影本一份。 
Dernier diplôme obtenu ou attestation d’inscription pour ceux qui sont en cours d’études. 
 
 
備註:學生辦理簽證統一透過法國教育中心線上系統預約時間。已自行取得入學資格者，請務必備妥辦理簽證所需資料，
以便於面試結束送件辦理簽證。 
NB : La prise de rendez-vous pour demande de visa pour études est gérée directement par Campus France. Le dépôt 
du dossier de demande de visa peut avoir lieu le même jour que l’entretien Campus Franc à condition que votre dossier 
de demande de visa soit complet.

A
visa
is an official document issued by the competent authorities of a country. It must be
presented by a foreign visitor when they enter the country for which the visa applies
. Depending on the country and its laws, visas are required either for all visitors from other countries, or according to the visitor’s nationality.
It is a
prerequisite for entering and staying in a country
for a set period of time. However, it is not a guarantee as border authorities in certain countries may refuse to give a foreign visitor permission to enter their country, even if the visitor has a valid visa.
For more information:
https://france-visas.gouv.fr/en_US/web/france-visas
International Students / Degree-seeking Students
Espace Monde
is an organisation that
helps international students
interested in studying at the University of Rouen Normandy but
not registered at another university or on a student exchange programme
. With the help of
Espace Monde
‘s friendly and supportive staff, students can prepare properly for their stay here in Rouen and settle smoothly into life at the University of Rouen Normandy. More specifically,
Espace Monde
helps students with
all aspects of the university application process
, like giving advice and information on passing French language exams, CROUS student housing, obtaining financial support from the CAF and finding your way around the city.
For more information:
https://mesdemarches.univ-rouen.fr/en/practical-information/international-mobility/
If you are on an exchange programme, please check out the
Exchange Students
section.
How to apply
To enrol on a Bachelor’s (Licence) or Master’s degree course at the University of Rouen Normandy,
potential applicants must have their French Baccalauréat or equivalent
(DAP – see below) and have a minimum level of B2 in French.
Students who do not have the French Baccalauréat and wish to enrol on a French Bachelor’s degree course must complete a
Demande d’Admission Préalable
– DAP (Preliminary Admission Request) exam before admission.
For more information:
http://www.enseignementsup-recherche.gouv.fr
For applicants who need French language competency certificates, the DELF/DALF exams can be taken in your home country.
For more information about the DELF exam:
https://www.france-education-international.fr/en/diplome/delf-tout-public?langue=enhttp://www.ciep.fr
For applicants who have little experience of the French language, have recently begun learning French, or would like to start learning the language, we offer
up to two years of preparatory language classes
. Students can register for intensive French language classes at the university’s
Maison des Langues
. This gives non-French speakers who would like to enrol at the University of Rouen Normandy an opportunity to get up to speed in terms of language, culture and university life before embarking on a Bachelor’s or Master’s course. Signing up to this preparatory option also gives international students
time to get to know the Normandy region
, explore the city, learn about its history, and join various societies and sports clubs.
Maison des Langues
Bâtiment 7C
17 rue Lavoisier
76821 MONT SAINT AIGNAN Cedex, France
Contact:
mdl@univ-rouen.fr
How to register
International students registering for the first time at the University of Rouen Normandy need to
go to Espace Monde’s one-stop office
(Building B4 – Michel Serres – entrance hall) on the Mont-Saint-Aignan campus.
Here are the different steps for completing your registration:
Before registering
at the University of Rouen Normandy, you need to provide a
receipt
proving that you have paid your
CVEC
(student and campus life contribution) fees, which is issued by the CROUS from 1 July.
You will find all the information you need by clicking on the following links:
http://www.crous-normandie.fr/crous/cvec-contribution-vie-etudiante-de-campus/
or
cvec.etudiant.gouv.fr
Register in person
at the Espace Monde one-stop office
Medical check-up (optional)
Enrol
on your course (via your personal online workspace (ENT))
Open a
Multipass account
(via your personal online workspace (ENT))
Create your student card:
Léocarte
(via your personal online workspace (ENT))
Exchange students
Over 300 students
are accepted on an
exchange programme
every year at the University of Rouen Normandy! URN has
partnerships with over 239 universities
, giving the student population a very international feel. Exchange programme agreements signed with other universities include:
Erasmus
BCI-PÉÉ – an exchange programme between France and Québec (Canada)
For first semester and/or full year exchanges, the application deadline is
1 June
. For students applying for the second semester, the application deadline is
1 November
.
For more information and to apply:
http://international.univ-rouen.fr/etudiants-en-echange-519277.kjsp
How to apply
Check that
your university is partnered with the University of Rouen Normandy
. To do this, contact the international office at your university and ask what the procedure is (form, prerequisites, application submission dates, study period, etc.).
Once you have completed all the formalities,
your university will let you know
if your request to study in Rouen has been accepted.
If it has, congratulations!
We will get in touch with you
and send you the
forms you need to fill in
, such as: your Learning Agreement, your student accommodation application, an information sheet.
A
letter of acceptance
will be sent to you as soon as your application has been confirmed.
Please note: we would like to remind all students wishing to come to the University of Rouen Normandy that most of the lectures and seminars are given in French.
Your French therefore needs to be relatively good for your studies to be a success
.
Below is a list of all the lecturers representing each department in the context of exchange programmes (Arts, Medicine, Law, Economics, etc.) You may contact them to receive the list of lectures and seminars given:
https://mesdemarches.univ-rouen.fr/en/inscriptions/eu-international-students-erasmus-and-icm-exchanges/
How to register
Before you arrive, you will be offered
an appointment to register at the university
. When you get here, you will need to go to the
Direction des Relations Internationales et de la Coopération
(international office) at the appointed date and time.
Espace Michel Serres, 2nd floor
Rue Thomas Becket
76821 MONT SAINT AIGNAN Cedex, France
service.international@univ-rouen.fr
Once you have registered at the university, you will need to go to
your faculty’s department office
to register for your course.

Exchange students
Every year, the University of Rouen Normandie welcomes around 150 exchange students.
If your home university has selected you to come to the University of Rouen Normandie as part of an exchange program, you’ll find some useful information here.
APPLYING TO UNIVERSITY
Applications :
Application deadlines are as follows:
–
June 1 for 1st semester and full-year mobility
–
November 1 for 2nd semester mobility
Appointments :
Nominations must be sent by e-mail to the following address:
mobility.in@univ-rouen.fr
Nomination deadlines are as follows:
– May 15 for 1st semester and full-year mobility
– October 15 for 2nd semester mobility
An online application link will be sent to you once your university has selected you and informed the University of Rouen Normandy.
If the University of Rouen’s pedagogical coordinators approve your application, you can then send them your pedagogical/learning agreement, already signed by your university.
A final letter of acceptance will be sent to you once your teaching contract has been signed by both universities. Please note that no letter of acceptance will be sent until we have received your validated teaching contract.
We would like to remind all Erasmus+ students who wish to come to the University of Rouen Normandie that all courses are taught in French. A B2 level of the CEFR is therefore strongly recommended to ensure that your studies run smoothly. Examinations for Erasmus+ students are the same as those for students at the Université de Rouen, and no adaptation will be proposed.

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320

國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。

original_evidence.text:
National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。 
 
 
 
□我已閱讀並同意上述所有內容。 
申請人簽名:___________________ 
簽名日期:_____________________

original_evidence.text:
National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。

FACT SHEET  
ACADEMIC YEAR 2024/25 
Page 3 of 3 
 
 
 
 
 
 
ACCOMMODATION 
Student Dormitory The university does not have its own accommodation. The International Office offers support in 
finding accommodation. However, the “Studierendenwerk Thüringen” is in charge for the 
allocation of places in student dormitories. The overall rent varies from about 250€ to 350€ per 
month.  
https://www.uni-weimar.de/en/university/international/to-weimar/exchange-studies/visa-
accommodation-preparation/accommodation/  
Private Residence Many students in Weimar live in shared flats and houses rented from private landlords. 
Depending on room size and comfort the prices range between 250€ and 450€ per month.  
Website 
Accommodation 
https://www.uni-weimar.de/en/university/international/to-weimar/exchange-studies/visa-
accommodation-preparation/accommodation/  
 
 
 
WELCOME EVENTS & SOCIAL ACTIVITIES 
Welcome Events The exchange programme starts with special “Welcome Events” offering an overview of the 
city of Weimar and its surroundings, of the university and its faculties, and enabling first 
contacts with other exchange students.  
The “Welcome Events” takes place at the same time as the free German intensive course in 
March (summer semester) or September (winter semester): 
https://www.uni-weimar.de/en/university/international/to-weimar/exchange-studies/info-
event-international-welcome/  
Summer School & 
Spring School (BIP) 
“Bauhaus Summer School” and “Bauhaus Spring School” are short-term exchange projects of 
the Bauhaus-Universität Weimar taking place every year in August and in March.  
It offers German language courses and academic projects for German and international 
students. 
https://www.uni-weimar.de/springschool/en/ 
https://www.uni-weimar.de/summerschool/en/  
Student Initiatives Exchange students are cordially invited to participate in initiatives like »Bauhaus Internationals«, 
»BeBuddy« and »Culture-Talk«. The central venue for students is »m18« - the Haus der 
Studierenden - the home of the Student Government, the Faculty Student Council, initiatives, 
and student “Café s140” 
https://www.uni-weimar.de/en/university/profile/student-initiatives/  
University Sports 
Centre 
The “University Sports Centre” offers different sport courses during the semester.  
Please mind the application deadlines for courses: 
https://www.uni-weimar.de/en/university/structure/central-university-
facilities/university-sports-centre/  
 
HEALTH INSURANCE 
Health 
Insurance 
Regulations 
Students from Non-EU countries need to take out an international health insurance which is 
valid in Germany. 
Students from EU countries need to have a European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) issued by a 
health insurance company in their home country.  
Website Insurance https://www.uni-weimar.de/en/university/international/to-weimar/exchange-studies/visa-
accommodation-preparation/health-insurance/

original_evidence.text:
FACT SHEET  
ACADEMIC YEAR 2024/25 
Page 3 of 3 
 
 
 
 
 
 
ACCOMMODATION 
Student Dormitory The university does not have its own accommodation. The International Office offers support in 
finding accommodation. However, the “Studierendenwerk Thüringen” is in charge for the 
allocation of places in student dormitories. The overall rent varies from about 250€ to 350€ per 
month.  
https://www.uni-weimar.de/en/university/international/to-weimar/exchange-studies/visa-
accommodation-preparation/accommodation/  
Private Residence Many students in Weimar live in shared flats and houses rented from private landlords. 
Depending on room size and comfort the prices range between 250€ and 450€ per month.  
Website 
Accommodation 
https://www.uni-weimar.de/en/university/international/to-weimar/exchange-studies/visa-
accommodation-preparation/accommodation/  
 
 
 
WELCOME EVENTS & SOCIAL ACTIVITIES 
Welcome Events The exchange programme starts with special “Welcome Events” offering an overview of the 
city of Weimar and its surroundings, of the university and its faculties, and enabling first 
contacts with other exchange students.  
The “Welcome Events” takes place at the same time as the free German intensive course in 
March (summer semester) or September (winter semester): 
https://www.uni-weimar.de/en/university/international/to-weimar/exchange-studies/info-
event-international-welcome/  
Summer School & 
Spring School (BIP) 
“Bauhaus Summer School” and “Bauhaus Spring School” are short-term exchange projects of 
the Bauhaus-Universität Weimar taking place every year in August and in March.  
It offers German language courses and academic projects for German and international 
students. 
https://www.uni-weimar.de/springschool/en/ 
https://www.uni-weimar.de/summerschool/en/  
Student Initiatives Exchange students are cordially invited to participate in initiatives like »Bauhaus Internationals«, 
»BeBuddy« and »Culture-Talk«. The central venue for students is »m18« - the Haus der 
Studierenden - the home of the Student Government, the Faculty Student Council, initiatives, 
and student “Café s140” 
https://www.uni-weimar.de/en/university/profile/student-initiatives/  
University Sports 
Centre 
The “University Sports Centre” offers different sport courses during the semester.  
Please mind the application deadlines for courses: 
https://www.uni-weimar.de/en/university/structure/central-university-
facilities/university-sports-centre/  
 
HEALTH INSURANCE 
Health 
Insurance 
Regulations 
Students from Non-EU countries need to take out an international health insurance which is 
valid in Germany. 
Students from EU countries need to have a European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) issued by a 
health insurance company in their home country.  
Website Insurance https://www.uni-weimar.de/en/university/international/to-weimar/exchange-studies/visa-
accommodation-preparation/health-insurance/

Bauhaus-Universitat Weimar 魏瑪包浩斯大學 
地點 Geschwister-Scholl-Straße 8, 99423 Weimar, Germany 
 
申請資格 
Undergraduate and Graduate(限申請姐妹校 Faculty of Civil Engineering 或 Faculty of 
Media- Media Studies 專業) 
語言要求 
(2022 update) 
Most classes are in German; some programs are available in English. 
Please note that the faculties of the Bauhaus-Universität Weimar require German language 
proficiency at level A1 to B1 depending on the study programs. 
交換期間 Fall Semester: October-March 
Spring Semester: April-September 
簽證 Students have to get a student visa prior to arrive in Germany. First students need to ask for 
appointment at the German embassy in Taipei after getting admission letter from 
Bauhaus-Universitat Weimar 
費用 Exchange students to BUW will need to pay a “Semester Charge” of about EURO 160. This is 
not a university fee, but a charge destined for a national student organization that includes 
the student ID, a train pass, the use of the sport complex, access to meals and housing 
discounts, and other social and cultural services. 
學校網址 https://www.uni-weimar.de/en/university/international/to-weimar/exchange-students/

Exchange students may find information on every step on the way to Weimar on our 
website for exchange students and in our “Checklist for exchange students” 
 
LANGUAGE REQUIREMENTS 
Language Requirements The recommendation for English and German language proficiency are depending on the 
study programme. Please visit our website for exchange students for detailed information. 
German Intensive Course The University’s Language Centre offers a three-week German intensive language course 
(60h) which takes place before the semester starts and is obligatory for exchange 
students with German language skills below B1 CEFR.  
The German Intensive Course is free of charge for exchange students. 
More information can be found on the website of the Language Center.

original_evidence.text:
Housing in Munich unfortunately is a major issue. We are only able to house 
about 50% to 60% of our incoming students in student residence halls (they 
are subsidized by the state and therefore only cost around 280 to 360 Euro). 
Since there is no fair way to distribute the rooms, we use a lottery system in 
order to assign them. Those who are not lucky need to find a room on the 
private market. Although we do assist students by handing out information 
on how to find affordable housing, it is up to the student to find 
accommodation. Private rooms are much more expensive (starting at around 
500 Euro in shared apartments) and students should also consider living in 
the suburbs or towns along the regional train lines.

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。 
 
 
 
□我已閱讀並同意上述所有內容。 
申請人簽名:___________________ 
簽名日期:_____________________

國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。

Aschaffenburg University of Applied Sciences www.th-ab.de/eng
Semester Fee
All students of Aschaffenburg UAS, including 
Erasmus+ and exchange students, have to 
pay a semester fee of 70 EUR. You will receive 
further information after your application. 
Arrival
Frankfurt am Main (FRA) airport is the closest 
major airport to Aschaffenburg (~ 50 km). From 
Terminal 1, it is easy to reach Aschaffenburg 
Hbf (main station) by train. From there, you 
can take a bus or train to get to the university 
(Hochschule, Aschaffenburg or Aschaffenburg 
Hochschule). We recommend using the  
DB Navigator app or the Deutsche Bahn website 
when planning and buying a ticket. 
Be careful: some slower travel options may 
require a different ticket. Also note that there 
are two different train stations at Terminal 1. 
ICE trains are the fastest option. They leave 
from “Frankfurt Flughafen Fernbahnhof“.
Grading System
Local Grade Definition
1,0 – 1,5 excellent / very good
1,6 – 2,5 good
2,6 – 3,5 satisfactory
3,6 – 4,0 sufficient
5,0 fail
Buddy Programme &  
Welcome Weeks
As an international student, you will be matched 
with a local “buddy“ who will help you get 
settled in Aschaffenburg. Your buddy, who is 
a student at Aschaffenburg UAS, will help you 
with all your administrative and social queries 
on arrival in Aschaffenburg and during the 
Welcome Weeks.
Health Insurance
All students studying in Germany must have 
health insurance that is accepted in Germany. 
If you are from an EU country, please check that 
your European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) is 
valid. You can then ask for an exemption from 
German health insurance. 
If you come from a non-EU country, you can buy 
German statutory health insurance (about €135 
per month) or ask for an exemption if you have 
private insurance.

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。 
 
 
 
□我已閱讀並同意上述所有內容。

original_evidence.text:
Application Guide
www.th-ab.de/eng  
✓ This handout will answer your first questions about applying to Aschaffenburg University of Applied 
Sciences as an exchange student. Check off each item once completed to help keep track of your progress.
Step 1: Nomination
We kindly ask all partner institutions to nominate their outgoing students by sending an email to incoming@
th-ab.de, stating the students‘ full name, gender, email address, field of studies and period of stay.
Step 2: Online Application
› Please go to www .th-ab.de/apply-online to access our online application. You will need to create a personal
account to access the application form.
› The following documents are to be uploaded during the online application:
Passport-style photo (i.e. digital portrait photo, coloured, JPG only) 
Scan of your passport / identity card
Current transcript of records from your home university
Erasmus+ or GJU students: learning agreement, signed by you and your home university 
EU-citizens: scan of your EU health insurance card (both sides).
› Once you submit the application online, a PDF document will be cr
eated. This may take a few minutes.
› Please print 
and sign the document on the last page under the “Declaration and Consent” section,
stating the date and place of the signature.
› Please email the signed application form to 
incoming@th-ab.de.
Step 3: Letter of Acceptance
The letter of acceptance is an electronic document issued by Aschaffenburg UAS, that contains your 
personal details as well as information about your exchange studies with us. If your application is 
successful, your letter of acceptance will be emailed to you after the application period.
Step 4: Semester Fee (“Studierendenwerksbeitrag”)
According to the Bavarian Higher Education Act, all students are to pay a small service fee for the adminis-
tration of certain services, such as the cafeteria or the halls of residence. Paying the semester fee is man-
datory for enrolment at Aschaffenburg UAS. Please note that the fee has to be paid before your arrival. Cur-
rently, the semester fee amounts to 70 EUR. Further information will be sent with the letter of acceptance.
Further Steps
Once you have been accepted and received your letter of acceptance, depending on where you are from, 
there are a few other formalities to take care of. We will send further information on applying for 
a visa, health insurance, and housing with your letter of acceptance. The halls of residence are run by 
Studierendenwerk Wuerzburg. We cannot guarantee a room in the halls and recommend looking for private 
accommodation as well. Please apply for the halls of residence by June 15 (for the winter semester) and 
January 15 (for the summer semester.)

original_evidence.text:
German as a Foreign Language
Learning German can be very useful to connect 
with the locals. Aschaffenburg UAS offers German 
language courses for all skill levels – whether 
you are starting out as a beginner or at a more 
advanced level. In addition to the courses offered 
during the semester, Aschaffenburg UAS offers 
four-week intensive German courses in August.
 www.th-ab.de/learngerman
Credit system and grading
A full-time workload is 30 ECTS credits per 
semester. Grades are awarded from 1,0 (highest) 
to 5,0 (lowest) with 4,0 as the minimum passing 
grade. Some courses are evaluated on a pass / 
fail grading system.
Erasmus+ and exchange students will receive 
credits for all successfully completed courses and 
all obtained credits will be listed on a transcript 
of records. Students can download the transcript 
of records themselves, and it will also be sent 
directly to the home institution.

While English-taught modules take place almost 
exclusively on the main campus in Aschaffenburg, 
there are also two smaller locations in town and 
a campus in Miltenberg, which is located about 
40 km from Aschaffenburg.
Aschaffenburg UAS is a research-intensive 
university of applied sciences with special focus 
on intelligent systems, materials, information 
management and structural transformation. 
Within international research consortia as well as 
in intensive cooperation with local partners, our 
scientists strive to foster innovation in business 
and society. 
Other campuses and facilities
In the Centre for Scientific Services and Transfer 
(ZeWiS) Aschaffenburg UAS strengthens its 
cooperation with the regional industry. Located in 
Obernburg – halfway between our main campus 
in Aschaffenburg and our campus in Miltenberg – 
ZeWiS maintains more than 1,000 square meters 
of laboratory space for application-oriented 
research and transfer. 
 www.th-ab.de/en/research/collaborate/students

Application Guide
www.th-ab.de/eng  
✓ This handout will answer your first questions about applying to Aschaffenburg University of Applied 
Sciences as an exchange student. Check off each item once completed to help keep track of your progress.
Step 1: Nomination
We kindly ask all partner institutions to nominate their outgoing students by sending an email to incoming@
th-ab.de, stating the students‘ full name, gender, email address, field of studies and period of stay.
Step 2: Online Application
› Please go to www .th-ab.de/apply-online to access our online application. You will need to create a personal
account to access the application form.
› The following documents are to be uploaded during the online application:
Passport-style photo (i.e. digital portrait photo, coloured, JPG only) 
Scan of your passport / identity card
Current transcript of records from your home university
Erasmus+ or GJU students: learning agreement, signed by you and your home university 
EU-citizens: scan of your EU health insurance card (both sides).
› Once you submit the application online, a PDF document will be cr
eated. This may take a few minutes.
› Please print 
and sign the document on the last page under the “Declaration and Consent” section,
stating the date and place of the signature.
› Please email the signed application form to 
incoming@th-ab.de.
Step 3: Letter of Acceptance
The letter of acceptance is an electronic document issued by Aschaffenburg UAS, that contains your 
personal details as well as information about your exchange studies with us. If your application is 
successful, your letter of acceptance will be emailed to you after the application period.
Step 4: Semester Fee (“Studierendenwerksbeitrag”)
According to the Bavarian Higher Education Act, all students are to pay a small service fee for the adminis-
tration of certain services, such as the cafeteria or the halls of residence. Paying the semester fee is man-
datory for enrolment at Aschaffenburg UAS. Please note that the fee has to be paid before your arrival. Cur-
rently, the semester fee amounts to 70 EUR. Further information will be sent with the letter of acceptance.
Further Steps
Once you have been accepted and received your letter of acceptance, depending on where you are from, 
there are a few other formalities to take care of. We will send further information on applying for 
a visa, health insurance, and housing with your letter of acceptance. The halls of residence are run by 
Studierendenwerk Wuerzburg. We cannot guarantee a room in the halls and recommend looking for private 
accommodation as well. Please apply for the halls of residence by June 15 (for the winter semester) and 
January 15 (for the summer semester.)

original_evidence.text:
Fee
No fees will be charged by Aschaffenburg UAS, 
but all students have to pay the semester fee. In 
Germany, the Studentenwerk maintains a range 
of services such as the campus dining hall, 
the halls of residence, or counselling services. 
According to the Bavarian Higher Education Act, 
all students are to pay a small service fee for 
the administration of these services – currently 
70 EUR (as of March 2025).
Nomination and application 
Exchange students are nominated by their home 
university before they apply at Aschaffenburg UAS 
using an online application form. 
 www.th-ab.de/apply-online
Nomination / application deadlines
Winter semester: 20 May / 1 June
Summer semester: 20 November / 1 December
Classes
Students are encouraged to organise their 
learning in a responsible and self-regulated way. 
Attendance is not compulsory for most classes. 
At the same time, active participation is expected. 
Please:
   do ask if you have questions,
   contribute whenever there is an opportunity,
    get in contact with your German classmates 
and do not be afraid of taking the initiative.
Often, so called Tutorien are offered – additional 
classes where students help you grasp the 
material. Tutorien are announced by your 
professors and on campus.

original_evidence.text:
Registration in town
All students have to register their place of 
residence within two weeks of their arrival at 
the town hall’s Residents’ Registration Office 
(Einwohnermeldeamt). After the registration 
you will receive a confirmation called 
Meldebescheinigung that is often required to open 
a German bank account. 
Please bring:
    your passport / ID card,
    your certificate of enrolment,
    your rental contract and documents 
(Wohnungsgeberbescheinigung).
Insurance
It is mandatory as a student to have health 
insurance cover for your entire stay in Germany. 
EU and EFTA nationals are entitled to medical 
treatment with their European Health Insurance 
Card. Students from outside EU/EFTA countries 
should sign up for statutory or private health 
insurance. We recommend taking out a policy 
with a German statutory health insurance 
company. These institutions offer special prices 
for students — approx. 130 EUR / month for 
health and long-term care insurance.
In addition, we recommend taking out personal 
liability insurance (Haftpflichtversicherung). 
Although it is not compulsory, it covers unintentional 
damage to a third party or a third party’s property.

original_evidence.text:
Buddy programme
As an international student, you will be matched 
with a local “buddy” who will help you get settled 
in Aschaffenburg. Your buddy is a full-time 
student at Aschaffenburg UAS and will meet you 
upon arrival, show you around and help you with 
practical matters, such as registration or opening 
a bank account. During the semester, the buddies 
will organise social events and trips, and answer 
social questions throughout your stay.
Welcome Weeks
Prior to the start of the semester, the International 
Office organises two (compulsory) Welcome 
Weeks. You will have the chance to learn some 
German, clear all administrative milestones, and 
participate in various events and activities. This is 
a great opportunity to settle in, meet new people 
and make some friends.
Cost of living
Prices in Germany are in line with the EU average. 
The German government estimates the average 
expenditure for students to be approx. EUR 934 
a month, which includes accommodation, food, 
study materials, leisure, and transport. There are 
many generous grant and scholarship schemes 
that can help to cover your cost of living during 
your stay. 
 www.daad.de/en 
Licence fee
Every household in Germany is required to pay 
a licence fee (Rundfunkbeitrag) of 18.36 EUR /
month for public service broadcasting. The fee is 
subject to the principle of solidarity. It is relatively 
small because everyone pays regardless of   
actual media use. 
 www.rundfunkbeitrag.de/welcome
