Frequently Asked Questions
Frequently Asked Questions
Practical arrangements
How can I look for housing in Belgium?
Remember to start on time!
Please consult our database to start looking for accommodation: indicate the campus of your choice and change the search date. You will receive an overview of the available student rooms as for that date and the information and contact details of the landlord.
You need to contact the landlord and arrange the contract yourself.
You can find more details about housing on
this page
.
Go to the database
How can I open a bank account in Belgium?
If you come from an
EEA country
, the bank card from your home country should work in Belgium. Please always check with your bank at home before traveling to Belgium.
If you wish to open a bank account:
You are free to choose your bank branch in Belgium, but we recommend using the
KBC bank
. If you choose this brand, please use
these instructions
to complete the bank account request
earliest one month before arrival.
What will my first days in Belgium look like?
At Thomas More, your first experience starts with the
Orientation Days
.
During the Orientation Days all international students come together to get to know the university, get lots of important information, get to know their peers and join social events!
The Orientation Days take place the week before the semester starts and are
compulsory
to attend.
Can’t make it to the Orientation Days? Let us know! We’ll give you a personal welcome upon arrival and make sure you get integrated smoothly.
Contact:
Degree students via
international.support@thomasmore.be
Exchange students via
incoming@thomasmore.be
Orientation Days
Where can I find an estimate of the cost of living in Belgium?
Here you can find an overview of the costs of living in Belgium.
Cost of living
Is it possible to combine work and studies?
It's possible to work as a student in Belgium. However, there are limits on how many hours per week you can work. Also, due to the workload required for you to be successful in your studies, financing your education through a student job is not advisable.
For details about working as a student, check the '
Student at work
' website. If you do not have the Belgian nationality and want to work in Belgium as a job student? Go to the section
Foreign students
. On the site you will find a nice overview of the limitations on and requirements for student work.
You will some extra information in our
student portal
(accessible once you are enrolled).
What does my academic year/semester look like?
At Thomas More the academic year runs from September until September.
You can start either in September (autumn semester) or in February (spring semester).
Curious to find out when your classes will take place? Or when the holiday periods are planned? Check it out here:
Academic Calendar 25/26
Academic Calendar 26/27
Where do I find my schedule?
All programmes publish their timetables on the same website.
You will only have access to your timetable once you have c
ompleted your Individual Study Programme
(ISP).
It's possible there are some changes to your original timetable during the semester. Please make sure to check your timetable regularly not to miss any changes.
Find your timetable here
Administration and enrolment
What is Thomas More's Erasmus Code?
Thomas More consists of two different official instances, each of which has a different Erasmus code. The Erasmus code you will need will depend on the campus you will be studying at:
Thomas More Mechelen-Antwerpen:
B MECHELE14
Campus Antwerp, De Nayer (Sint-Katelijne-Waver) and Mechelen
Thomas More Kempen:
B GEEL07
Campus Lier, Geel, Vorselaar and Turnhout
Do I have to pay tuition fees?
Students from partner universities where both schools have signed and Inter-Institutional Agreement (IIA) or Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) obtain a waiver of this tuition fee.
This means that if Thomas More has an agreement with your home university, you won’t have to pay tuition fees at Thomas More during your
exchange
, since you pay them at your home university.
Not sure if our universities have an agreement already? Please check with your home university first.
How can I get nominated and apply for my exchange?
In order to join our exchange programmes you need to first get nominated. If your nomination gets accepted, you will receive the application procedure via email.
Learn more
When are the nomination and application deadlines?
When is the nomination deadline?
Autumn semester (and whole academic year) - 1st of May
Spring semester - 15th of October
When is the application deadline?
Autumn semester (and whole academic year) - 15th of May
Spring semester - 31st of October
When do I know whether I've been accepted?
After you have submitted your application, the International Office will process it and contact you asap.
If you have been accepted into the exchange programme you applied for, you will get your acceptance letter by email.
If not, you will receive an email to inform you why.
Application deadline
Acceptance Letters
Autumn semester and whole academic year
15th of May
Begin June
Spring semester
31st of October
Mid-November
Autumn semester
= September to January
Spring semester
= February yo June
What about my (Online) Learning Agreement?
As an exchange student you must always submit your (Online) Learning Agreement before arrival:
What?
An (Online) Learning Agreement is a mandatory document in order to participate in an exchange programme. The purpose of the (Online) Learning Agreement is to provide a
transparent and efficient preparation
of the exchange to make sure that
students receive recognition
for the activities successfully completed abroad. It sets out the programme of the studies or the traineeship to be followed abroad.
Online Learning Agreement
Compulsory for all students coming from a European Higher Education Institution according to the Erasmus+ rules
You need to start the procedure at your home institution
It's very important to choose the correct Erasmus+ code in the system, since Thomas More has officially 2 different codes
Learning Agreement
The paper version of the Learning Agreement can be used by students studying outside of Europe
You can use our
Learning Agreement template
if your home institution doesn't provide one
When?
You need to submit your (Online) Learning Agreement ((O)LA) before arrival:
Exchange period
Deadline to submit (O)LA
Autumn semester and whole academic year
15 June
Spring semester
15 January
Where?
Online Learning Agreement
You need to start the procedure
online
at your home institution. Every institution uses another procedure, please check with your International Office for the correct procedure.
Learning Agreement
You should upload the
signed
Learning  Agreement in the system before the deadline. You will receive the instructions to do so by email.
This document needs to be signed by you and your international coordinator at home.
How do I activate my Thomas More account?
After your enrolment has been processed, you will receive an email from Thomas More’s Student Administration. It will contain a
personalized URL
for you to activate your account. You need this link and your student number to complete the activation.
Your username = your account number = your student number
(written as: r0123456). You will find this number in the same email. After activating your account, you will have access to the main information channel for your study programme and other services like
the student portal
.
You will need to set a
password
for your Thomas accounts. Please note that this password must comply with a number of conditions, which can also be found in the account activation email. everyone at Thomas More logs into their account with a password and an additional security method (usually an app on your smartphone). Read all about it
here
.
Is there a problem?
Then it’s best to request a new code from the service desk by going to
this website
and choosing 'I cannot log in'.
What do I use my account for?
You can use it to log into the
Thomas More applications
(Canvas, email, student portal…). In this case you need to use your full email address as your username and the password you chose.
You can also use it for the web-based applications from the
KU Leuven Association
(such as KU Loket), where you will need to use only your student number (not the full email address) as your user name. The password is always the same.
How can I request my certificates?
You can request certain certificates yourself via the application ‘
Selfservice certificates
’ in the ‘KU Loket’ system.  The application is available as a tile under ‘Study & Exams’.
When all fields are filled in, a button ‘send’ appears. If you press this button, a certificate is generated in the background. This certificate will be sent as an
attachment in pdf-format to your Thomas More email address
. You will receive a confirmation when the creation of the certificate and the preparation of the email have gone correctly. Sending the email make take some time.
Most certificates will have a QR-code on them. This unique code can be used to verify the authenticity of the certificate through a professional scanner or with QR-code apps on smartphones, tablets and PC.
KU Loket
I received some certificates via email, what are they for?
NMBS/De Lijn certificate:
If you come to school by train or bus and would like to purchase a campus card or season ticket with NMBS/SNCB (Belgian train companies) or De Lijn/STIB/MIVB (Belgian bus and tram companies), you can use this certificate to prove that you are indeed enrolled at Thomas More and thus entitled to the student discount.
Proof of enrolment (certificate called “inschrijvingsbewijs”):
You can use this certificate at any time to prove that you are enrolled at Thomas More (e.g., if your landlord asks, for the townhall registration, etc.).
What about my Thomas More email?
About 3 hours after you have activated your Thomas more account and chosen your password, you have access to your Thomas More mail.
How does my Thomas More mail look like?
Your Thomas More email address, looks like this:  <your r-number>@student.thomasmore.be (e.g.
r0123456@student.thomasmore.be
).
How can I check my Thomas More mail?
You can check your Thomas More mail if you login at
https://outlook.office356.com
with your
r-number@student.thomasmore.be
(e.g.
r0123456@thomasmore.be
) and the password you have set.
More information
What is Canvas?
Canvas is our digital learning environment for lessons, tests, exams, … Each professor has a corresponding Canvas course for his/her subject.  In this course on Canvas learning material such as slides, extra exercises, info about the exam, … will be posted.
Check it regularly!
How to log in into Canvas?
You can access Canvas via this webpage. Log in with your Thomas More email address (ex.
r0123456@student.thomasmore.be
) and your personal password.
As from when do I have access to Canvas?
After activating your account, it may take one to two days before your data is uploaded into the Thomas More digital learning environment.
What if I cannot see my courses in Canvas?
There could be different reasons for this:
If your Individual Study Programme (ISP) has not been arranged/approved yet, you won’t be able to see your courses.
The teacher might have not published the course yet (ex. At the beginning of the semester).
More information on Canvas in
the student portal
.
Go to Canvas
KU Loket: what is it and how to log in?
What is the KU Loket?
The KU Loket is your digital student file. Here you can:
compose your
individual study programme (ISP)
at the start of the academic year and send it to your study counsellor. Your ISP is your individual study contract. It determines the courses you are enrolled in and which exams you will take this year.
consult your
exam results
after each examination period
check your
registration information
and the
courses you're enrolled in
for the whole academic year
re-enrol
for the next academic year if you are a full degree student. You receive an invitation email to do so.
and much more!
How to log in to the KU Loket?
You'll have to log on using your Thomas More account. Your username is your r-number (r0123456) and your password is your Thomas More password.​
Please note it's only possible to access this platform once  you have officially enrolled in our system and activated your account.
Go to the KU Loket
ISP (Individual Study Programme)
What is an ISP?
With your
Individual Study Programme
(ISP) you determine the courses you will take in the coming academic year. Your ISP has to meet the requirements of the programme you're registered for.
When to fill in my ISP?
International students create and edit their ISPs during the Orientation Days:
Autumn semester
: your ISP is available from September 14 and has to be submitted before October 1 2026.
Spring semester
: your ISP is available from February 1 and had to be submitted before February 18 2027.
Where do I find my study material?
Via our services
You will be able to buy or order all new study material via Thomas More. Our different campuses work with different suppliers.
Second-hand study material
Both for buying and selling second hand books we refer our students to the website of
Stubooks
(Dutch only).  Here  you can create a profile as a student and put books for sale as well as buy books.  You can easily filter on Thomas More and even on education.
Some Thomas More campuses also organise sales days for second hand books.
Extra information about the education system at Thomas More
What are ECTS credits, and how many hours of work do they entail?
What are ECTS credits?
ECTS is short for European Credit Transfer and Accumulation System. It is a standard way to compare the credits associated with a certain amount of learning and the associated workload in higher education across the European Union.
Workload
ECTS is a credit system based on student workload. The credits are a value given to course units to describe the amount of work needed to complete them successfully.
1 ECTS corresponds to 25 to 30 hours of work
per semester (including time spent in class, meetings for group work, reading assignments, studying for exams, etc.).
ECTS credits express a relative value. Study hours are estimates because you may spend more time on a course you are not so familiar with and maybe less on another course that is exactly in your area of interest and expertise. That means that one of your 3 ECTS courses may involve more work than a 6 ECTS course.
A bachelor's degree consists of 180 ECTS credits. One year’s study is 60 credits, which is normally equivalent to 1500–1800 hours of total workload.
ECTS grading scale
ECTS also includes a standard grading scale, shown in addition to Flemish standard grades.
EXCELLENT - outstanding performance with only minor errors
A
17-20
VERY GOOD - above the average standard but with some errors
B
15-16
GOOD - generally sound work with a number of notable errors
C
13-14
SATISFACTORY - fair but with significant shortcomings
D
11-12
SUFFICIENT - performance meets the minimum criteria
E
10
FAIL - some more work required before the credit can be awarded
FX
8-9
FAIL - considerable further work is required
F
0-7
Visa application
Do I need a visa?
Country of origin
Requires a student visa
EEA + Monaco and Switzerland
No
NON EEA
Yes
NON EEA with a visa for another EEA country
No*
* If you are a non-EEA student who is already studying in another EEA country and, therefore, you already have a visa for that other EEA country, then you don't need to apply for a new visa to come to Belgium.
However,
the International Office will need to notify the authorities about this latest  days before your arrival in Belgium.
Is this your case?
You need to contact yourself the International Office via
incoming@thomasmore.be
asap to start this procedure.
Which type of visa do I need?
If you need a visa to study at Thomas More, you will need to apply for a long-stay visa (type D). This is also called an Authorisation for Provisional Sojourn (Machtiging tot Voorlopig Verblijf). It allows the holder to enter and remain in Belgium for a period longer than 90 days.
Students should not enter Belgium on a tourist visa if they intend to stay longer than 90 days. Thomas More will not support an application for a change of status or visa.
Where should I submit my visa application?
The visa application must be completed at the
Belgian Consulate or Embassy
in your home country or in the country where you legally reside. If there is no Belgian consulate or embassy in your country, you may submit your application to the
Belgian consulate or Embassy
in a neighbouring country.  In some countries, a visa application centre handles the visa procedures for Belgium, for example
VFS Global
and
TLS
.
Make sure that you inform Thomas More via email (Degree students:
admissions@thomasmore.be
. Exchange students:
incoming@thomasmore.be
) about the application number and/or contact person at the Belgian embassy or consulate where you are applying for your visa. This way, we can confirm your admission directly with them.
When should I start the visa application?
If you need a visa, we highly recommend starting this process as soon as you have received the necessary documents from Admissions (for Degree students) or International Office (for Exchange students). Student visa applications can often take 3 to 4 months to be processed so it is essential to start the process as soon as you received your documents.
Plan to be in Belgium at least two weeks before the start of the classes in order to attend
Orientation Days
.
It is important to refer to the Belgian Embassy or Belgian Consulate website in your home or neighbouring country. They will provide you with information about which documents are required to apply for a student visa. Please note that some embassies and consulates work with external agencies like VFS or TLS.
Which Thomas More address do I use in my student visa application?
If you are going to study Applied Computer Science then you may fill in the following details:
Name university: Thomas More Kempen
Organisation nr: 103581
Nr + Street: 2 Havenlaan
Postal code: 2440
City: Geel
If you are going to study any of our other English programmes then you may fill in the following details:
Name university: Thomas More Mechelen-Antwerpen
Organisation nr: 103598
Nr + Street: 60 Zandpoortvest
Postal code: 2800
City: Mechelen
How do I get my acceptance letter for my visa application?
If you are an exchange student, the international Office will automatically send you your acceptance letter by e-mail once you have been accepted to Thomas More. You will receive this letter after the application deadline has passed.
Important additional requirements for a student visa
Please take these additional tips & tricks into account when applying for your student visa:
The Belgian Embassy will ask you to fill out a questionnaire or they will have an interview. In this interview they will assess your
study choice, university choice, post-study plans
etc... It is of utmost importance that you prepare yourself for these questions and that you have thoroughly studied your programme and Thomas More. Attending our
webinars
can be a great start, but also checking out our website. The Embassy will expect you to know exact details of your programme and studies and well thought through answers (no general, vague answers).
Please make sure to not share your answers with fellow student visa applicants. The Embassy will notice and this will most likely have a negative effect on your visa decision.
Examples of questions that you could get asked:
What kind of studies do you want to follow in Belgium?
What motivated your choice for these kind of studies?
Give a brief survey of the programme of the studies you want to follow.
Which profession would you like to exercise?
Which are the professional outlets in your country of origin with the diploma you will have obtained in Belgium?
How does the blocked account procedure work for exchange students?
Thomas More offers exchange students who have been accepted to one of their programmes the option of a blocked account procedure.
What is a blocked account procedure?
It's a way for you to prove your financial solvency, i.e. sufficient means of subsistence, when applying for a student visa.
How does it work?
You make an
advance payment
of your monthly living expenses into a blocked account managed by Thomas More. The minimum amount to cover your living expenses is €1062 per month and is set by the Belgian government*. There is an administrative fee of €250.
Blocked account 26/27:  €1062 x 5 months + 250€ administrative fee =  €5560
When you arrive in Belgium you
open a Belgian bank account
in your name into which you receive monthly payments during your stay with us.  At the end of your stay you are fully reimbursed, apart from the €250 administrative fee.
* Be aware that the monthly amount is set by the Belgian Government and is subject to change at any given time. If any changes should occur we will notify our students.
How can I apply for a blocked account?
If you want to apply for a blocked account as an exchange student, you need to contact the International Office yourself asap via
incoming@thomasmore.be
. They will send you the procedure via email.
Please note you should do this as soon as possible, since it takes some time to set it up.
Should your visa be refused, the blocked account will be fully refunded (€-250 administrative fee 26/27) onto the account where the money originally was transferred from.
Didn't find the answer to your question(s) above?
Help! I’m stuck!
Questions about your registration, the activation code, your account, mail, Canvas, ICT, libraries, … can be reported via our Helpdesk for students.
General questions?
Degree students: please reach out to our
International Support Team
Exchange students: please reach out to our
International Office Team

Frequently Asked Questions
Frequently Asked Questions
Practical arrangements
How can I look for housing in Belgium?
Remember to start on time!
Please consult our database to start looking for accommodation: indicate the campus of your choice and change the search date. You will receive an overview of the available student rooms as for that date and the information and contact details of the landlord.
You need to contact the landlord and arrange the contract yourself.
You can find more details about housing on
this page
.
Go to the database
How can I open a bank account in Belgium?
If you come from an
EEA country
, the bank card from your home country should work in Belgium. Please always check with your bank at home before traveling to Belgium.
If you wish to open a bank account:
You are free to choose your bank branch in Belgium, but we recommend using the
KBC bank
. If you choose this brand, please use
these instructions
to complete the bank account request
earliest one month before arrival.
What will my first days in Belgium look like?
At Thomas More, your first experience starts with the
Orientation Days
.
During the Orientation Days all international students come together to get to know the university, get lots of important information, get to know their peers and join social events!
The Orientation Days take place the week before the semester starts and are
compulsory
to attend.
Can’t make it to the Orientation Days? Let us know! We’ll give you a personal welcome upon arrival and make sure you get integrated smoothly.
Contact:
Degree students via
international.support@thomasmore.be
Exchange students via
incoming@thomasmore.be
Orientation Days
Where can I find an estimate of the cost of living in Belgium?
Here you can find an overview of the costs of living in Belgium.
Cost of living
Is it possible to combine work and studies?
It's possible to work as a student in Belgium. However, there are limits on how many hours per week you can work. Also, due to the workload required for you to be successful in your studies, financing your education through a student job is not advisable.
For details about working as a student, check the '
Student at work
' website. If you do not have the Belgian nationality and want to work in Belgium as a job student? Go to the section
Foreign students
. On the site you will find a nice overview of the limitations on and requirements for student work.
You will some extra information in our
student portal
(accessible once you are enrolled).
What does my academic year/semester look like?
At Thomas More the academic year runs from September until September.
You can start either in September (autumn semester) or in February (spring semester).
Curious to find out when your classes will take place? Or when the holiday periods are planned? Check it out here:
Academic Calendar 25/26
Academic Calendar 26/27
Where do I find my schedule?
All programmes publish their timetables on the same website.
You will only have access to your timetable once you have c
ompleted your Individual Study Programme
(ISP).
It's possible there are some changes to your original timetable during the semester. Please make sure to check your timetable regularly not to miss any changes.
Find your timetable here
Administration and enrolment
What is Thomas More's Erasmus Code?
Thomas More consists of two different official instances, each of which has a different Erasmus code. The Erasmus code you will need will depend on the campus you will be studying at:
Thomas More Mechelen-Antwerpen:
B MECHELE14
Campus Antwerp, De Nayer (Sint-Katelijne-Waver) and Mechelen
Thomas More Kempen:
B GEEL07
Campus Lier, Geel, Vorselaar and Turnhout
Do I have to pay tuition fees?
Students from partner universities where both schools have signed and Inter-Institutional Agreement (IIA) or Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) obtain a waiver of this tuition fee.
This means that if Thomas More has an agreement with your home university, you won’t have to pay tuition fees at Thomas More during your
exchange
, since you pay them at your home university.
Not sure if our universities have an agreement already? Please check with your home university first.
How can I get nominated and apply for my exchange?
In order to join our exchange programmes you need to first get nominated. If your nomination gets accepted, you will receive the application procedure via email.
Learn more
When are the nomination and application deadlines?
When is the nomination deadline?
Autumn semester (and whole academic year) - 1st of May
Spring semester - 15th of October
When is the application deadline?
Autumn semester (and whole academic year) - 15th of May
Spring semester - 31st of October
When do I know whether I've been accepted?
After you have submitted your application, the International Office will process it and contact you asap.
If you have been accepted into the exchange programme you applied for, you will get your acceptance letter by email.
If not, you will receive an email to inform you why.
Application deadline
Acceptance Letters

What about my (Online) Learning Agreement?
As an exchange student you must always submit your (Online) Learning Agreement before arrival:
What?
An (Online) Learning Agreement is a mandatory document in order to participate in an exchange programme. The purpose of the (Online) Learning Agreement is to provide a
transparent and efficient preparation
of the exchange to make sure that
students receive recognition
for the activities successfully completed abroad. It sets out the programme of the studies or the traineeship to be followed abroad.
Online Learning Agreement
Compulsory for all students coming from a European Higher Education Institution according to the Erasmus+ rules
You need to start the procedure at your home institution
It's very important to choose the correct Erasmus+ code in the system, since Thomas More has officially 2 different codes
Learning Agreement
The paper version of the Learning Agreement can be used by students studying outside of Europe
You can use our
Learning Agreement template
if your home institution doesn't provide one
When?
You need to submit your (Online) Learning Agreement ((O)LA) before arrival:
Exchange period
Deadline to submit (O)LA
Autumn semester and whole academic year
15 June
Spring semester
15 January
Where?
Online Learning Agreement
You need to start the procedure
online
at your home institution. Every institution uses another procedure, please check with your International Office for the correct procedure.
Learning Agreement
You should upload the
signed
Learning  Agreement in the system before the deadline. You will receive the instructions to do so by email.
This document needs to be signed by you and your international coordinator at home.
How do I activate my Thomas More account?
After your enrolment has been processed, you will receive an email from Thomas More’s Student Administration. It will contain a
personalized URL
for you to activate your account. You need this link and your student number to complete the activation.
Your username = your account number = your student number
(written as: r0123456). You will find this number in the same email. After activating your account, you will have access to the main information channel for your study programme and other services like
the student portal
.
You will need to set a
password
for your Thomas accounts. Please note that this password must comply with a number of conditions, which can also be found in the account activation email. everyone at Thomas More logs into their account with a password and an additional security method (usually an app on your smartphone). Read all about it
here
.
Is there a problem?
Then it’s best to request a new code from the service desk by going to
this website
and choosing 'I cannot log in'.
What do I use my account for?
You can use it to log into the
Thomas More applications
(Canvas, email, student portal…). In this case you need to use your full email address as your username and the password you chose.
You can also use it for the web-based applications from the
KU Leuven Association
(such as KU Loket), where you will need to use only your student number (not the full email address) as your user name. The password is always the same.
How can I request my certificates?
You can request certain certificates yourself via the application ‘
Selfservice certificates
’ in the ‘KU Loket’ system.  The application is available as a tile under ‘Study & Exams’.
When all fields are filled in, a button ‘send’ appears. If you press this button, a certificate is generated in the background. This certificate will be sent as an
attachment in pdf-format to your Thomas More email address
. You will receive a confirmation when the creation of the certificate and the preparation of the email have gone correctly. Sending the email make take some time.
Most certificates will have a QR-code on them. This unique code can be used to verify the authenticity of the certificate through a professional scanner or with QR-code apps on smartphones, tablets and PC.
KU Loket
I received some certificates via email, what are they for?
NMBS/De Lijn certificate:
If you come to school by train or bus and would like to purchase a campus card or season ticket with NMBS/SNCB (Belgian train companies) or De Lijn/STIB/MIVB (Belgian bus and tram companies), you can use this certificate to prove that you are indeed enrolled at Thomas More and thus entitled to the student discount.
Proof of enrolment (certificate called “inschrijvingsbewijs”):
You can use this certificate at any time to prove that you are enrolled at Thomas More (e.g., if your landlord asks, for the townhall registration, etc.).
What about my Thomas More email?
About 3 hours after you have activated your Thomas more account and chosen your password, you have access to your Thomas More mail.
How does my Thomas More mail look like?
Your Thomas More email address, looks like this:  <your r-number>@student.thomasmore.be (e.g.
r0123456@student.thomasmore.be
).
How can I check my Thomas More mail?
You can check your Thomas More mail if you login at
https://outlook.office356.com
with your
r-number@student.thomasmore.be
(e.g.
r0123456@thomasmore.be
) and the password you have set.
More information
What is Canvas?
Canvas is our digital learning environment for lessons, tests, exams, … Each professor has a corresponding Canvas course for his/her subject.  In this course on Canvas learning material such as slides, extra exercises, info about the exam, … will be posted.
Check it regularly!
How to log in into Canvas?
You can access Canvas via this webpage. Log in with your Thomas More email address (ex.
r0123456@student.thomasmore.be
) and your personal password.
As from when do I have access to Canvas?
After activating your account, it may take one to two days before your data is uploaded into the Thomas More digital learning environment.
What if I cannot see my courses in Canvas?
There could be different reasons for this:
If your Individual Study Programme (ISP) has not been arranged/approved yet, you won’t be able to see your courses.
The teacher might have not published the course yet (ex. At the beginning of the semester).
More information on Canvas in
the student portal
.
Go to Canvas
KU Loket: what is it and how to log in?
What is the KU Loket?
The KU Loket is your digital student file. Here you can:
compose your
individual study programme (ISP)
at the start of the academic year and send it to your study counsellor. Your ISP is your individual study contract. It determines the courses you are enrolled in and which exams you will take this year.
consult your
exam results
after each examination period
check your
registration information
and the
courses you're enrolled in
for the whole academic year
re-enrol
for the next academic year if you are a full degree student. You receive an invitation email to do so.
and much more!
How to log in to the KU Loket?
You'll have to log on using your Thomas More account. Your username is your r-number (r0123456) and your password is your Thomas More password.​
Please note it's only possible to access this platform once  you have officially enrolled in our system and activated your account.
Go to the KU Loket
ISP (Individual Study Programme)
What is an ISP?
With your
Individual Study Programme
(ISP) you determine the courses you will take in the coming academic year. Your ISP has to meet the requirements of the programme you're registered for.
When to fill in my ISP?
International students create and edit their ISPs during the Orientation Days:
Autumn semester
: your ISP is available from September 14 and has to be submitted before October 1 2026.
Spring semester
: your ISP is available from February 1 and had to be submitted before February 18 2027.
Where do I find my study material?
Via our services
You will be able to buy or order all new study material via Thomas More. Our different campuses work with different suppliers.
Second-hand study material
Both for buying and selling second hand books we refer our students to the website of
Stubooks
(Dutch only).  Here  you can create a profile as a student and put books for sale as well as buy books.  You can easily filter on Thomas More and even on education.
Some Thomas More campuses also organise sales days for second hand books.
Extra information about the education system at Thomas More
What are ECTS credits, and how many hours of work do they entail?
What are ECTS credits?
ECTS is short for European Credit Transfer and Accumulation System. It is a standard way to compare the credits associated with a certain amount of learning and the associated workload in higher education across the European Union.
Workload
ECTS is a credit system based on student workload. The credits are a value given to course units to describe the amount of work needed to complete them successfully.
1 ECTS corresponds to 25 to 30 hours of work
per semester (including time spent in class, meetings for group work, reading assignments, studying for exams, etc.).
ECTS credits express a relative value. Study hours are estimates because you may spend more time on a course you are not so familiar with and maybe less on another course that is exactly in your area of interest and expertise. That means that one of your 3 ECTS courses may involve more work than a 6 ECTS course.
A bachelor's degree consists of 180 ECTS credits. One year’s study is 60 credits, which is normally equivalent to 1500–1800 hours of total workload.
ECTS grading scale
ECTS also includes a standard grading scale, shown in addition to Flemish standard grades.
EXCELLENT - outstanding performance with only minor errors
A
17-20
VERY GOOD - above the average standard but with some errors
B
15-16
GOOD - generally sound work with a number of notable errors
C
13-14
SATISFACTORY - fair but with significant shortcomings
D
11-12
SUFFICIENT - performance meets the minimum criteria
E
10
FAIL - some more work required before the credit can be awarded
FX
8-9
FAIL - considerable further work is required
F
0-7
Visa application
Do I need a visa?
Country of origin
Requires a student visa
EEA + Monaco and Switzerland
No
NON EEA
Yes
NON EEA with a visa for another EEA country
No*
* If you are a non-EEA student who is already studying in another EEA country and, therefore, you already have a visa for that other EEA country, then you don't need to apply for a new visa to come to Belgium.
However,
the International Office will need to notify the authorities about this latest  days before your arrival in Belgium.
Is this your case?
You need to contact yourself the International Office via
incoming@thomasmore.be
asap to start this procedure.
Which type of visa do I need?
If you need a visa to study at Thomas More, you will need to apply for a long-stay visa (type D). This is also called an Authorisation for Provisional Sojourn (Machtiging tot Voorlopig Verblijf). It allows the holder to enter and remain in Belgium for a period longer than 90 days.
Students should not enter Belgium on a tourist visa if they intend to stay longer than 90 days. Thomas More will not support an application for a change of status or visa.
Where should I submit my visa application?
The visa application must be completed at the
Belgian Consulate or Embassy
in your home country or in the country where you legally reside. If there is no Belgian consulate or embassy in your country, you may submit your application to the
Belgian consulate or Embassy
in a neighbouring country.  In some countries, a visa application centre handles the visa procedures for Belgium, for example
VFS Global
and
TLS
.
Make sure that you inform Thomas More via email (Degree students:
admissions@thomasmore.be
. Exchange students:
incoming@thomasmore.be
) about the application number and/or contact person at the Belgian embassy or consulate where you are applying for your visa. This way, we can confirm your admission directly with them.
When should I start the visa application?
If you need a visa, we highly recommend starting this process as soon as you have received the necessary documents from Admissions (for Degree students) or International Office (for Exchange students). Student visa applications can often take 3 to 4 months to be processed so it is essential to start the process as soon as you received your documents.
Plan to be in Belgium at least two weeks before the start of the classes in order to attend
Orientation Days
.
It is important to refer to the Belgian Embassy or Belgian Consulate website in your home or neighbouring country. They will provide you with information about which documents are required to apply for a student visa. Please note that some embassies and consulates work with external agencies like VFS or TLS.
Which Thomas More address do I use in my student visa application?
If you are going to study Applied Computer Science then you may fill in the following details:
Name university: Thomas More Kempen
Organisation nr: 103581
Nr + Street: 2 Havenlaan
Postal code: 2440
City: Geel
If you are going to study any of our other English programmes then you may fill in the following details:
Name university: Thomas More Mechelen-Antwerpen
Organisation nr: 103598
Nr + Street: 60 Zandpoortvest
Postal code: 2800
City: Mechelen
How do I get my acceptance letter for my visa application?
If you are an exchange student, the international Office will automatically send you your acceptance letter by e-mail once you have been accepted to Thomas More. You will receive this letter after the application deadline has passed.
Important additional requirements for a student visa
Please take these additional tips & tricks into account when applying for your student visa:
The Belgian Embassy will ask you to fill out a questionnaire or they will have an interview. In this interview they will assess your
study choice, university choice, post-study plans
etc... It is of utmost importance that you prepare yourself for these questions and that you have thoroughly studied your programme and Thomas More. Attending our
webinars
can be a great start, but also checking out our website. The Embassy will expect you to know exact details of your programme and studies and well thought through answers (no general, vague answers).
Please make sure to not share your answers with fellow student visa applicants. The Embassy will notice and this will most likely have a negative effect on your visa decision.
Examples of questions that you could get asked:
What kind of studies do you want to follow in Belgium?
What motivated your choice for these kind of studies?
Give a brief survey of the programme of the studies you want to follow.
Which profession would you like to exercise?
Which are the professional outlets in your country of origin with the diploma you will have obtained in Belgium?
How does the blocked account procedure work for exchange students?
Thomas More offers exchange students who have been accepted to one of their programmes the option of a blocked account procedure.
What is a blocked account procedure?
It's a way for you to prove your financial solvency, i.e. sufficient means of subsistence, when applying for a student visa.
How does it work?
You make an
advance payment
of your monthly living expenses into a blocked account managed by Thomas More. The minimum amount to cover your living expenses is €1062 per month and is set by the Belgian government*. There is an administrative fee of €250.
Blocked account 26/27:  €1062 x 5 months + 250€ administrative fee =  €5560
When you arrive in Belgium you
open a Belgian bank account
in your name into which you receive monthly payments during your stay with us.  At the end of your stay you are fully reimbursed, apart from the €250 administrative fee.
* Be aware that the monthly amount is set by the Belgian Government and is subject to change at any given time. If any changes should occur we will notify our students.
How can I apply for a blocked account?
If you want to apply for a blocked account as an exchange student, you need to contact the International Office yourself asap via
incoming@thomasmore.be
. They will send you the procedure via email.
Please note you should do this as soon as possible, since it takes some time to set it up.
Should your visa be refused, the blocked account will be fully refunded (€-250 administrative fee 26/27) onto the account where the money originally was transferred from.
Didn't find the answer to your question(s) above?
Help! I’m stuck!
Questions about your registration, the activation code, your account, mail, Canvas, ICT, libraries, … can be reported via our Helpdesk for students.
General questions?
Degree students: please reach out to our
International Support Team
Exchange students: please reach out to our
International Office Team

Frequently Asked Questions
Practical arrangements
How can I look for housing in Belgium?
Remember to start on time!
Please consult our database to start looking for accommodation: indicate the campus of your choice and change the search date. You will receive an overview of the available student rooms as for that date and the information and contact details of the landlord.
You need to contact the landlord and arrange the contract yourself.
You can find more details about housing on
this page
.
Go to the database
How can I open a bank account in Belgium?
If you come from an
EEA country
, the bank card from your home country should work in Belgium. Please always check with your bank at home before traveling to Belgium.
If you wish to open a bank account:
You are free to choose your bank branch in Belgium, but we recommend using the
KBC bank
. If you choose this brand, please use
these instructions
to complete the bank account request
earliest one month before arrival.
What will my first days in Belgium look like?
At Thomas More, your first experience starts with the
Orientation Days
.
During the Orientation Days all international students come together to get to know the university, get lots of important information, get to know their peers and join social events!
The Orientation Days take place the week before the semester starts and are
compulsory
to attend.
Can’t make it to the Orientation Days? Let us know! We’ll give you a personal welcome upon arrival and make sure you get integrated smoothly.
Contact:
Degree students via
international.support@thomasmore.be
Exchange students via
incoming@thomasmore.be
Orientation Days
Where can I find an estimate of the cost of living in Belgium?
Here you can find an overview of the costs of living in Belgium.
Cost of living
Is it possible to combine work and studies?
It's possible to work as a student in Belgium. However, there are limits on how many hours per week you can work. Also, due to the workload required for you to be successful in your studies, financing your education through a student job is not advisable.
For details about working as a student, check the '
Student at work
' website. If you do not have the Belgian nationality and want to work in Belgium as a job student? Go to the section
Foreign students
. On the site you will find a nice overview of the limitations on and requirements for student work.
You will some extra information in our
student portal
(accessible once you are enrolled).
What does my academic year/semester look like?
At Thomas More the academic year runs from September until September.
You can start either in September (autumn semester) or in February (spring semester).
Curious to find out when your classes will take place? Or when the holiday periods are planned? Check it out here:
Academic Calendar 25/26
Academic Calendar 26/27
Where do I find my schedule?
All programmes publish their timetables on the same website.
You will only have access to your timetable once you have c
ompleted your Individual Study Programme
(ISP).
It's possible there are some changes to your original timetable during the semester. Please make sure to check your timetable regularly not to miss any changes.
Find your timetable here
Administration and enrolment
What is Thomas More's Erasmus Code?
Thomas More consists of two different official instances, each of which has a different Erasmus code. The Erasmus code you will need will depend on the campus you will be studying at:
Thomas More Mechelen-Antwerpen:
B MECHELE14
Campus Antwerp, De Nayer (Sint-Katelijne-Waver) and Mechelen
Thomas More Kempen:
B GEEL07
Campus Lier, Geel, Vorselaar and Turnhout
Do I have to pay tuition fees?
Students from partner universities where both schools have signed and Inter-Institutional Agreement (IIA) or Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) obtain a waiver of this tuition fee.
This means that if Thomas More has an agreement with your home university, you won’t have to pay tuition fees at Thomas More during your
exchange
, since you pay them at your home university.
Not sure if our universities have an agreement already? Please check with your home university first.
How can I get nominated and apply for my exchange?
In order to join our exchange programmes you need to first get nominated. If your nomination gets accepted, you will receive the application procedure via email.
Learn more
When are the nomination and application deadlines?
When is the nomination deadline?
Autumn semester (and whole academic year) - 1st of May
Spring semester - 15th of October
When is the application deadline?
Autumn semester (and whole academic year) - 15th of May
Spring semester - 31st of October
When do I know whether I've been accepted?
After you have submitted your application, the International Office will process it and contact you asap.
If you have been accepted into the exchange programme you applied for, you will get your acceptance letter by email.
If not, you will receive an email to inform you why.
Application deadline
Acceptance Letters
Autumn semester and whole academic year
15th of May
Begin June

Mid-November
Autumn semester
= September to January

What about my (Online) Learning Agreement?
As an exchange student you must always submit your (Online) Learning Agreement before arrival:
What?
An (Online) Learning Agreement is a mandatory document in order to participate in an exchange programme. The purpose of the (Online) Learning Agreement is to provide a
transparent and efficient preparation
of the exchange to make sure that
students receive recognition
for the activities successfully completed abroad. It sets out the programme of the studies or the traineeship to be followed abroad.
Online Learning Agreement
Compulsory for all students coming from a European Higher Education Institution according to the Erasmus+ rules
You need to start the procedure at your home institution
It's very important to choose the correct Erasmus+ code in the system, since Thomas More has officially 2 different codes
Learning Agreement
The paper version of the Learning Agreement can be used by students studying outside of Europe
You can use our
Learning Agreement template
if your home institution doesn't provide one
When?
You need to submit your (Online) Learning Agreement ((O)LA) before arrival:
Exchange period
Deadline to submit (O)LA
Autumn semester and whole academic year
15 June
Spring semester
15 January
Where?
Online Learning Agreement
You need to start the procedure
online
at your home institution. Every institution uses another procedure, please check with your International Office for the correct procedure.
Learning Agreement
You should upload the
signed
Learning  Agreement in the system before the deadline. You will receive the instructions to do so by email.
This document needs to be signed by you and your international coordinator at home.
How do I activate my Thomas More account?
After your enrolment has been processed, you will receive an email from Thomas More’s Student Administration. It will contain a
personalized URL
for you to activate your account. You need this link and your student number to complete the activation.
Your username = your account number = your student number
(written as: r0123456). You will find this number in the same email. After activating your account, you will have access to the main information channel for your study programme and other services like
the student portal
.
You will need to set a
password
for your Thomas accounts. Please note that this password must comply with a number of conditions, which can also be found in the account activation email. everyone at Thomas More logs into their account with a password and an additional security method (usually an app on your smartphone). Read all about it
here
.
Is there a problem?
Then it’s best to request a new code from the service desk by going to
this website
and choosing 'I cannot log in'.
What do I use my account for?
You can use it to log into the
Thomas More applications
(Canvas, email, student portal…). In this case you need to use your full email address as your username and the password you chose.
You can also use it for the web-based applications from the
KU Leuven Association
(such as KU Loket), where you will need to use only your student number (not the full email address) as your user name. The password is always the same.
How can I request my certificates?
You can request certain certificates yourself via the application ‘
Selfservice certificates
’ in the ‘KU Loket’ system.  The application is available as a tile under ‘Study & Exams’.
When all fields are filled in, a button ‘send’ appears. If you press this button, a certificate is generated in the background. This certificate will be sent as an
attachment in pdf-format to your Thomas More email address
. You will receive a confirmation when the creation of the certificate and the preparation of the email have gone correctly. Sending the email make take some time.
Most certificates will have a QR-code on them. This unique code can be used to verify the authenticity of the certificate through a professional scanner or with QR-code apps on smartphones, tablets and PC.
KU Loket
I received some certificates via email, what are they for?
NMBS/De Lijn certificate:
If you come to school by train or bus and would like to purchase a campus card or season ticket with NMBS/SNCB (Belgian train companies) or De Lijn/STIB/MIVB (Belgian bus and tram companies), you can use this certificate to prove that you are indeed enrolled at Thomas More and thus entitled to the student discount.
Proof of enrolment (certificate called “inschrijvingsbewijs”):
You can use this certificate at any time to prove that you are enrolled at Thomas More (e.g., if your landlord asks, for the townhall registration, etc.).
What about my Thomas More email?
About 3 hours after you have activated your Thomas more account and chosen your password, you have access to your Thomas More mail.
How does my Thomas More mail look like?
Your Thomas More email address, looks like this:  <your r-number>@student.thomasmore.be (e.g.
r0123456@student.thomasmore.be
).
How can I check my Thomas More mail?
You can check your Thomas More mail if you login at
https://outlook.office356.com
with your
r-number@student.thomasmore.be
(e.g.
r0123456@thomasmore.be
) and the password you have set.
More information
What is Canvas?
Canvas is our digital learning environment for lessons, tests, exams, … Each professor has a corresponding Canvas course for his/her subject.  In this course on Canvas learning material such as slides, extra exercises, info about the exam, … will be posted.
Check it regularly!
How to log in into Canvas?
You can access Canvas via this webpage. Log in with your Thomas More email address (ex.
r0123456@student.thomasmore.be
) and your personal password.
As from when do I have access to Canvas?
After activating your account, it may take one to two days before your data is uploaded into the Thomas More digital learning environment.
What if I cannot see my courses in Canvas?
There could be different reasons for this:
If your Individual Study Programme (ISP) has not been arranged/approved yet, you won’t be able to see your courses.
The teacher might have not published the course yet (ex. At the beginning of the semester).
More information on Canvas in
the student portal
.
Go to Canvas
KU Loket: what is it and how to log in?
What is the KU Loket?
The KU Loket is your digital student file. Here you can:
compose your
individual study programme (ISP)
at the start of the academic year and send it to your study counsellor. Your ISP is your individual study contract. It determines the courses you are enrolled in and which exams you will take this year.
consult your
exam results
after each examination period
check your
registration information
and the
courses you're enrolled in
for the whole academic year
re-enrol
for the next academic year if you are a full degree student. You receive an invitation email to do so.
and much more!
How to log in to the KU Loket?
You'll have to log on using your Thomas More account. Your username is your r-number (r0123456) and your password is your Thomas More password.​
Please note it's only possible to access this platform once  you have officially enrolled in our system and activated your account.
Go to the KU Loket
ISP (Individual Study Programme)
What is an ISP?
With your
Individual Study Programme
(ISP) you determine the courses you will take in the coming academic year. Your ISP has to meet the requirements of the programme you're registered for.
When to fill in my ISP?
International students create and edit their ISPs during the Orientation Days:
Autumn semester
: your ISP is available from September 14 and has to be submitted before October 1 2026.
Spring semester
: your ISP is available from February 1 and had to be submitted before February 18 2027.
Where do I find my study material?
Via our services
You will be able to buy or order all new study material via Thomas More. Our different campuses work with different suppliers.
Second-hand study material
Both for buying and selling second hand books we refer our students to the website of
Stubooks
(Dutch only).  Here  you can create a profile as a student and put books for sale as well as buy books.  You can easily filter on Thomas More and even on education.
Some Thomas More campuses also organise sales days for second hand books.
Extra information about the education system at Thomas More
What are ECTS credits, and how many hours of work do they entail?
What are ECTS credits?
ECTS is short for European Credit Transfer and Accumulation System. It is a standard way to compare the credits associated with a certain amount of learning and the associated workload in higher education across the European Union.
Workload
ECTS is a credit system based on student workload. The credits are a value given to course units to describe the amount of work needed to complete them successfully.
1 ECTS corresponds to 25 to 30 hours of work
per semester (including time spent in class, meetings for group work, reading assignments, studying for exams, etc.).
ECTS credits express a relative value. Study hours are estimates because you may spend more time on a course you are not so familiar with and maybe less on another course that is exactly in your area of interest and expertise. That means that one of your 3 ECTS courses may involve more work than a 6 ECTS course.
A bachelor's degree consists of 180 ECTS credits. One year’s study is 60 credits, which is normally equivalent to 1500–1800 hours of total workload.
ECTS grading scale
ECTS also includes a standard grading scale, shown in addition to Flemish standard grades.
EXCELLENT - outstanding performance with only minor errors
A
17-20
VERY GOOD - above the average standard but with some errors
B
15-16
GOOD - generally sound work with a number of notable errors
C
13-14
SATISFACTORY - fair but with significant shortcomings
D
11-12
SUFFICIENT - performance meets the minimum criteria
E
10
FAIL - some more work required before the credit can be awarded
FX
8-9
FAIL - considerable further work is required
F
0-7
Visa application
Do I need a visa?
Country of origin
Requires a student visa
EEA + Monaco and Switzerland
No
NON EEA
Yes
NON EEA with a visa for another EEA country
No*
* If you are a non-EEA student who is already studying in another EEA country and, therefore, you already have a visa for that other EEA country, then you don't need to apply for a new visa to come to Belgium.
However,
the International Office will need to notify the authorities about this latest  days before your arrival in Belgium.
Is this your case?
You need to contact yourself the International Office via
incoming@thomasmore.be
asap to start this procedure.
Which type of visa do I need?
If you need a visa to study at Thomas More, you will need to apply for a long-stay visa (type D). This is also called an Authorisation for Provisional Sojourn (Machtiging tot Voorlopig Verblijf). It allows the holder to enter and remain in Belgium for a period longer than 90 days.
Students should not enter Belgium on a tourist visa if they intend to stay longer than 90 days. Thomas More will not support an application for a change of status or visa.
Where should I submit my visa application?
The visa application must be completed at the
Belgian Consulate or Embassy
in your home country or in the country where you legally reside. If there is no Belgian consulate or embassy in your country, you may submit your application to the
Belgian consulate or Embassy
in a neighbouring country.  In some countries, a visa application centre handles the visa procedures for Belgium, for example
VFS Global
and
TLS
.
Make sure that you inform Thomas More via email (Degree students:
admissions@thomasmore.be
. Exchange students:
incoming@thomasmore.be
) about the application number and/or contact person at the Belgian embassy or consulate where you are applying for your visa. This way, we can confirm your admission directly with them.
When should I start the visa application?
If you need a visa, we highly recommend starting this process as soon as you have received the necessary documents from Admissions (for Degree students) or International Office (for Exchange students). Student visa applications can often take 3 to 4 months to be processed so it is essential to start the process as soon as you received your documents.
Plan to be in Belgium at least two weeks before the start of the classes in order to attend
Orientation Days
.
It is important to refer to the Belgian Embassy or Belgian Consulate website in your home or neighbouring country. They will provide you with information about which documents are required to apply for a student visa. Please note that some embassies and consulates work with external agencies like VFS or TLS.
Which Thomas More address do I use in my student visa application?
If you are going to study Applied Computer Science then you may fill in the following details:
Name university: Thomas More Kempen
Organisation nr: 103581
Nr + Street: 2 Havenlaan
Postal code: 2440
City: Geel
If you are going to study any of our other English programmes then you may fill in the following details:
Name university: Thomas More Mechelen-Antwerpen
Organisation nr: 103598
Nr + Street: 60 Zandpoortvest
Postal code: 2800
City: Mechelen
How do I get my acceptance letter for my visa application?
If you are an exchange student, the international Office will automatically send you your acceptance letter by e-mail once you have been accepted to Thomas More. You will receive this letter after the application deadline has passed.
Important additional requirements for a student visa
Please take these additional tips & tricks into account when applying for your student visa:
The Belgian Embassy will ask you to fill out a questionnaire or they will have an interview. In this interview they will assess your
study choice, university choice, post-study plans
etc... It is of utmost importance that you prepare yourself for these questions and that you have thoroughly studied your programme and Thomas More. Attending our
webinars
can be a great start, but also checking out our website. The Embassy will expect you to know exact details of your programme and studies and well thought through answers (no general, vague answers).
Please make sure to not share your answers with fellow student visa applicants. The Embassy will notice and this will most likely have a negative effect on your visa decision.
Examples of questions that you could get asked:
What kind of studies do you want to follow in Belgium?
What motivated your choice for these kind of studies?
Give a brief survey of the programme of the studies you want to follow.
Which profession would you like to exercise?
Which are the professional outlets in your country of origin with the diploma you will have obtained in Belgium?
How does the blocked account procedure work for exchange students?
Thomas More offers exchange students who have been accepted to one of their programmes the option of a blocked account procedure.
What is a blocked account procedure?
It's a way for you to prove your financial solvency, i.e. sufficient means of subsistence, when applying for a student visa.
How does it work?
You make an
advance payment
of your monthly living expenses into a blocked account managed by Thomas More. The minimum amount to cover your living expenses is €1062 per month and is set by the Belgian government*. There is an administrative fee of €250.
Blocked account 26/27:  €1062 x 5 months + 250€ administrative fee =  €5560
When you arrive in Belgium you
open a Belgian bank account
in your name into which you receive monthly payments during your stay with us.  At the end of your stay you are fully reimbursed, apart from the €250 administrative fee.
* Be aware that the monthly amount is set by the Belgian Government and is subject to change at any given time. If any changes should occur we will notify our students.
How can I apply for a blocked account?
If you want to apply for a blocked account as an exchange student, you need to contact the International Office yourself asap via
incoming@thomasmore.be
. They will send you the procedure via email.
Please note you should do this as soon as possible, since it takes some time to set it up.
Should your visa be refused, the blocked account will be fully refunded (€-250 administrative fee 26/27) onto the account where the money originally was transferred from.
Didn't find the answer to your question(s) above?
Help! I’m stuck!
Questions about your registration, the activation code, your account, mail, Canvas, ICT, libraries, … can be reported via our Helpdesk for students.
General questions?
Degree students: please reach out to our
International Support Team
Exchange students: please reach out to our
International Office Team

In order to join our exchange programmes you need to first get nominated. If your nomination gets accepted, you will receive the application procedure via email.

What?

transparent and efficient preparation
of the exchange to make sure that
students receive recognition
for the activities successfully completed abroad. It sets out the programme of the studies or the traineeship to be followed abroad.
Online Learning Agreement
Compulsory for all students coming from a European Higher Education Institution according to the Erasmus+ rules
You need to start the procedure at your home institution

How do I activate my Thomas More account?
After your enrolment has been processed, you will receive an email from Thomas More’s Student Administration. It will contain a
personalized URL
for you to activate your account. You need this link and your student number to complete the activation.
Your username = your account number = your student number
(written as: r0123456). You will find this number in the same email. After activating your account, you will have access to the main information channel for your study programme and other services like
the student portal
.
You will need to set a
password
for your Thomas accounts. Please note that this password must comply with a number of conditions, which can also be found in the account activation email. everyone at Thomas More logs into their account with a password and an additional security method (usually an app on your smartphone). Read all about it
here
.
Is there a problem?
Then it’s best to request a new code from the service desk by going to
this website
and choosing 'I cannot log in'.
What do I use my account for?
You can use it to log into the
Thomas More applications
(Canvas, email, student portal…). In this case you need to use your full email address as your username and the password you chose.
You can also use it for the web-based applications from the
KU Leuven Association
(such as KU Loket), where you will need to use only your student number (not the full email address) as your user name. The password is always the same.
How can I request my certificates?
You can request certain certificates yourself via the application ‘
Selfservice certificates
’ in the ‘KU Loket’ system.  The application is available as a tile under ‘Study & Exams’.
When all fields are filled in, a button ‘send’ appears. If you press this button, a certificate is generated in the background. This certificate will be sent as an
attachment in pdf-format to your Thomas More email address
. You will receive a confirmation when the creation of the certificate and the preparation of the email have gone correctly. Sending the email make take some time.
Most certificates will have a QR-code on them. This unique code can be used to verify the authenticity of the certificate through a professional scanner or with QR-code apps on smartphones, tablets and PC.

I received some certificates via email, what are they for?
NMBS/De Lijn certificate:
If you come to school by train or bus and would like to purchase a campus card or season ticket with NMBS/SNCB (Belgian train companies) or De Lijn/STIB/MIVB (Belgian bus and tram companies), you can use this certificate to prove that you are indeed enrolled at Thomas More and thus entitled to the student discount.
Proof of enrolment (certificate called “inschrijvingsbewijs”):
You can use this certificate at any time to prove that you are enrolled at Thomas More (e.g., if your landlord asks, for the townhall registration, etc.).
What about my Thomas More email?

How does my Thomas More mail look like?

with your

What is Canvas?

Check it regularly!
How to log in into Canvas?
You can access Canvas via this webpage. Log in with your Thomas More email address (ex.
r0123456@student.thomasmore.be
) and your personal password.
As from when do I have access to Canvas?
After activating your account, it may take one to two days before your data is uploaded into the Thomas More digital learning environment.
What if I cannot see my courses in Canvas?
There could be different reasons for this:
If your Individual Study Programme (ISP) has not been arranged/approved yet, you won’t be able to see your courses.
The teacher might have not published the course yet (ex. At the beginning of the semester).
More information on Canvas in
the student portal
.

What is the KU Loket?
The KU Loket is your digital student file. Here you can:
compose your

for the whole academic year

and much more!
How to log in to the KU Loket?
You'll have to log on using your Thomas More account. Your username is your r-number (r0123456) and your password is your Thomas More password.​
Please note it's only possible to access this platform once  you have officially enrolled in our system and activated your account.
Go to the KU Loket
ISP (Individual Study Programme)
What is an ISP?
With your
Individual Study Programme
(ISP) you determine the courses you will take in the coming academic year. Your ISP has to meet the requirements of the programme you're registered for.
When to fill in my ISP?
International students create and edit their ISPs during the Orientation Days:
Autumn semester
: your ISP is available from September 14 and has to be submitted before October 1 2026.
Spring semester
: your ISP is available from February 1 and had to be submitted before February 18 2027.
Where do I find my study material?
Via our services
You will be able to buy or order all new study material via Thomas More. Our different campuses work with different suppliers.
Second-hand study material
Both for buying and selling second hand books we refer our students to the website of
Stubooks
(Dutch only).  Here  you can create a profile as a student and put books for sale as well as buy books.  You can easily filter on Thomas More and even on education.
Some Thomas More campuses also organise sales days for second hand books.
Extra information about the education system at Thomas More
What are ECTS credits, and how many hours of work do they entail?
What are ECTS credits?
ECTS is short for European Credit Transfer and Accumulation System. It is a standard way to compare the credits associated with a certain amount of learning and the associated workload in higher education across the European Union.
Workload
ECTS is a credit system based on student workload. The credits are a value given to course units to describe the amount of work needed to complete them successfully.
1 ECTS corresponds to 25 to 30 hours of work
per semester (including time spent in class, meetings for group work, reading assignments, studying for exams, etc.).
ECTS credits express a relative value. Study hours are estimates because you may spend more time on a course you are not so familiar with and maybe less on another course that is exactly in your area of interest and expertise. That means that one of your 3 ECTS courses may involve more work than a 6 ECTS course.
A bachelor's degree consists of 180 ECTS credits. One year’s study is 60 credits, which is normally equivalent to 1500–1800 hours of total workload.
ECTS grading scale
ECTS also includes a standard grading scale, shown in addition to Flemish standard grades.

A

VERY GOOD - above the average standard but with some errors

D
11-12
SUFFICIENT - performance meets the minimum criteria
E
10
FAIL - some more work required before the credit can be awarded
FX
8-9
FAIL - considerable further work is required
F
