Essential Facts about Exchange Studies at the Faculty of Science and Engineering  
General information The Faculty of Science and Engineering is with more than 14.000 students 
one of Sweden’s major faculties of engineering and science offering 
education at all levels in five main disciplines: (1) Computer Science, 
Information Technology, Media Technology and Visualisation, (2) 
Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics and Computational Sciences, (3) 
Mechanical Engineering and Design, (4) Industrial Engineering and 
Logistics, (5) Biology, Chemistry, Biotechnology and Biomedical 
Engineering. 
Website for exchange 
students 
https://liu.se/en/education/exchange-studies 
Application process 
and course offer 
 
For our course catalogue as well as all necessary application information, 
see the links below. Students can select courses within different subject 
areas offered by different departments at LiU, provided they meet the 
prerequisites. 
https://liu.se/en/article/application-procedure-faculty-of-science-and-
engineering  
https://liu.se/en/article/exchange-courses?faculty=3  
Nomination Students need to be nominated by their home university for exchange 
studies at LiU. Please consult with a student exchange coordinator at 
your home university regarding the options available to you. 
Nomination deadlines April 15: Autumn Semester as well as coming Academic Year 
October 15: Spring Semester 
Application deadlines April 15: Autumn Semester as well as coming Academic Year 
October 15: Spring Semester 
Credit and application 
requirements 
Non-EU students must apply for and be admitted to at least 30 ECTS 
credits per semester as this is a requirement by the Swedish Migration 
Agency to be granted a residence permit: 
https://www.migrationsverket.se/English/Private-individuals/Studying-
in-Sweden.html   
Language 
requirements 
No proof of language is required. Students should, however, show a good 
command of English to follow the technical courses properly.  
Decision on admission Decision on admission of nominated students will be sent within 10 
weeks.  
Housing assistance Students outside the EU will be prioritized when allocating 
accommodation through LiU. European students will be offered 
accommodation if available.  
More information: https://liu.se/en/article/accommodation  
Insurances and visa 
/residence permits 
Please see: https://liu.se/en/article/residence-permit-visa-and-insurance 
Student life in 
Linköping 
Linköping University has a vibrant and dynamic student life with a wide 
range of associations active in different fields. Linköping is a multiple-
time winner of the annual ranking of Sweden’s most student-friendly 
cities. https://liu.se/en/education/student-life  
LiU on social media Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/linkopingsuniversitet  
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/linkopings_universitet 
Youtube: https://www.youtube.com/user/LinkopingUniversity 
Questions? Please contact via incoming@lith.liu.se

original_evidence.text:
Essential Facts about Exchange Studies at the Faculty of Science and Engineering  
General information The Faculty of Science and Engineering is with more than 14.000 students 
one of Sweden’s major faculties of engineering and science offering 
education at all levels in five main disciplines: (1) Computer Science, 
Information Technology, Media Technology and Visualisation, (2) 
Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics and Computational Sciences, (3) 
Mechanical Engineering and Design, (4) Industrial Engineering and 
Logistics, (5) Biology, Chemistry, Biotechnology and Biomedical 
Engineering. 
Website for exchange 
students 
https://liu.se/en/education/exchange-studies 
Application process 
and course offer 
 
For our course catalogue as well as all necessary application information, 
see the links below. Students can select courses within different subject 
areas offered by different departments at LiU, provided they meet the 
prerequisites. 
https://liu.se/en/article/application-procedure-faculty-of-science-and-
engineering  
https://liu.se/en/article/exchange-courses?faculty=3  
Nomination Students need to be nominated by their home university for exchange 
studies at LiU. Please consult with a student exchange coordinator at 
your home university regarding the options available to you. 
Nomination deadlines April 15: Autumn Semester as well as coming Academic Year 
October 15: Spring Semester 
Application deadlines April 15: Autumn Semester as well as coming Academic Year 
October 15: Spring Semester 
Credit and application 
requirements 
Non-EU students must apply for and be admitted to at least 30 ECTS 
credits per semester as this is a requirement by the Swedish Migration 
Agency to be granted a residence permit: 
https://www.migrationsverket.se/English/Private-individuals/Studying-
in-Sweden.html   
Language 
requirements 
No proof of language is required. Students should, however, show a good 
command of English to follow the technical courses properly.  
Decision on admission Decision on admission of nominated students will be sent within 10 
weeks.  
Housing assistance Students outside the EU will be prioritized when allocating 
accommodation through LiU. European students will be offered 
accommodation if available.  
More information: https://liu.se/en/article/accommodation  
Insurances and visa 
/residence permits 
Please see: https://liu.se/en/article/residence-permit-visa-and-insurance 
Student life in 
Linköping 
Linköping University has a vibrant and dynamic student life with a wide 
range of associations active in different fields. Linköping is a multiple-
time winner of the annual ranking of Sweden’s most student-friendly 
cities. https://liu.se/en/education/student-life  
LiU on social media Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/linkopingsuniversitet  
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/linkopings_universitet 
Youtube: https://www.youtube.com/user/LinkopingUniversity 
Questions? Please contact via incoming@lith.liu.se

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。 
 
 
 
□我已閱讀並同意上述所有內容。

簽名日期:_____________________

Incoming exchange students
The Stockholm School of Economics welcomes around 180 exchange students each year. The Global Initiatives Team within the Education Office coordinates the student exchange program and supports students and partner institutions before, during, and after the exchange period.
On this page, you will find useful information about studying at SSE and living in Stockholm.
Please note that SSE does not accept free movers.
About the Stockholm School of Economics
The Stockholm School of Economics (SSE) is an internationally recognized business school in the Nordic and Baltic region. Since 1909, SSE has educated people for leading roles in business, government, civil society and the public sector.
SSE’s education is grounded in current research and strengthened by close collaboration with Swedish and international organizations. SSE is accredited by EQUIS, the European Quality Improvement System.
>>> A guide to life in Stockholm and Sweden
Nomination and application
SSE accepts nominations only through its official online form. Partner universities receive the nomination link when the nomination period opens. Students who have not been nominated through the form cannot be enrolled in the exchange program.
Nomination deadlines
April 1
for the fall semester and
October 1
for the spring semester.
After the nomination period closes, nominated students are invited to complete an online registration form.
Students nominated for the spring semester will receive access to the registration form in October. Students nominated for the fall semester will receive access in April.
Student application and account
Once the registration form has been completed and approved, the student will be issued an acceptance letter. They will also receive further information about the housing application and SSE student account.
Prior to their arrival, a mandatory online meeting will be held for all incoming exchange students where they will receive more information about course registration and practical information for their stay at SSE.
Documents needed for the student application
Photo
Completed Student Pledge
Completed Online Registration Form
Academic calendar
The academic year at SSE is divided into two semesters: a fall semester and a spring semester. Each semester is further divided into two teaching periods, with periods one and two in the fall semester and periods three and four in the spring semester.
While most exchange students attend SSE for a full semester, partner universities are welcome to nominate their students for only one teaching period or for the full academic year if preferred. This can be indicated in the nomination form.
Before the start of each semester, we welcome all exchange students to SSE with an Orientation Day to get acquainted with the university and to get to know other students and the SSE community.
See the
Academic Calendar 2026-2027
for semester, teaching-period and examination dates.
Courses
Students may register for up to two courses per teaching period, or three courses if one of them is a language course. To take a third non-language course, students must obtain approval from their home university.
Check the course lists linked below for a list of courses open to exchange students. Bachelor’s students may in some cases enroll in Master’s-level courses, provided they meet the course prerequisites and have approval from their home university.
Students should check each course’s exam schedule and the language of instruction, as a select number of courses from the Bachelor’s program are taught in Sweden.
Exchange BSc in Business and Economics - courses offered
Exchange MSc in Business and Economics - courses offered
CEMS accredited course list
Teaching and assessment
The educational programs at SSE are based on research and stress a theoretical and analytical approach. Since the School’s foundation, Economics has occupied a stronger position in the curriculum than at most business schools.
The teaching methodology is a mixture of American and European teaching methods and theories. Some courses are characterized by more traditional teaching, with lectures, written course assignments and seminars.
In other courses the teaching is to a great extent based on cases; active participation in class is expected and contributes to the final grade. Many of the courses require substantial preparatory reading.
The contacts between students and faculty members are rather informal at SSE. Feel free to contact your professors if you have any questions regarding the courses you are taking.
As an exchange student you study under the same conditions as the Swedish students. You may find that the structure of the SSE exams differs from those at your home university and therefore it is advisable to review past papers before taking your first exam.
>>> Exam Regulations (login)
Academic information
English language requirements
Students must demonstrate English proficiency at CEFR level B2 or above. The home university is responsible for confirming that nominated students meet this requirement.
Course format
Courses are typically conducted on site and in person. Exchange students are expected to remain until the end of their scheduled examinations. No special arrangements for early exams can be made.
Workload
A full-semester workload is 30 ECTS credits, normally 15 ECTS credits or two courses per teaching period.
Transcripts
Transcripts are available approximately two months after the final examinations. Students are invited to download their transcript directly from the internal portal. An original copy can be sent by post upon request.
Practical matters
Housing
At SSE, we have a small housing office that offers rooms and apartments to some of our international students. There is no guarantee of housing, so we recommend that you also explore other accommodation options. You can find more information
here
.
Cost of living
The following is a feasible monthly budget:
Housing: SEK 6,000 – 10,000
Food: SEK 3,000
Insurance: SEK 500
Hobbies: SEK 2,000
Local Transportation: SEK 650
Total: SEK 12,150 - 16,150
Exchange students have so far been exempt from the otherwise compulsory student association fees. Please note that you will need to pay for course literature, i.e. books, compendiums, etc.
Resident permit for studies
Depending on their citizenship and length of stay, students may need a residence permit to study in Sweden. Check the
Swedish Migration Agency website
for the requirements that apply to you.
Insurance
It is important that you purchase travel insurance covering your journey to Sweden and ensure that you have valid health insurance for the duration of your stay in Sweden.
Students from EU/EEA countries should bring a
European Health Insurance Card
from their home country or documentation confirming comprehensive private health insurance coverage.
Students with specific needs
Our Guidance and Wellbeing Office provides support to students with special needs, access to a certified counsellor, and assistance from the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Manager.
>>> Student health and support
Would you like to learn Swedish?
Although all programs at SSE are taught entirely in English - and English is widely spoken throughout Sweden - many international students choose to learn some Swedish to feel more connected to everyday life in Stockholm and Swedish society.
The
Swedish Institute
offers a range of helpful resources, language tools, and study tips for students who would like to begin learning Swedish before arriving in Sweden or continue improving their skills during their studies.
SSE also offers Swedish language courses at different levels for students who would like to learn the language while studying at the School.
Even a basic understanding of Swedish can make it easier to navigate daily life, meet new people, and gain additional insights into Swedish culture and society.
In addition, feel free to check out the following Swedish courses as well:

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。

Incoming exchange students
Incoming exchange students
The Stockholm School of Economics welcomes around 180 exchange students each year. The Global Initiatives Team within the Education Office coordinates the student exchange program and supports students and partner institutions before, during, and after the exchange period.
On this page, you will find useful information about studying at SSE and living in Stockholm.
Please note that SSE does not accept free movers.
About the Stockholm School of Economics
The Stockholm School of Economics (SSE) is an internationally recognized business school in the Nordic and Baltic region. Since 1909, SSE has educated people for leading roles in business, government, civil society and the public sector.
SSE’s education is grounded in current research and strengthened by close collaboration with Swedish and international organizations. SSE is accredited by EQUIS, the European Quality Improvement System.
>>> A guide to life in Stockholm and Sweden
Nomination and application
SSE accepts nominations only through its official online form. Partner universities receive the nomination link when the nomination period opens. Students who have not been nominated through the form cannot be enrolled in the exchange program.
Nomination deadlines
April 1
for the fall semester and
October 1
for the spring semester.
After the nomination period closes, nominated students are invited to complete an online registration form.
Students nominated for the spring semester will receive access to the registration form in October. Students nominated for the fall semester will receive access in April.
Student application and account
Once the registration form has been completed and approved, the student will be issued an acceptance letter. They will also receive further information about the housing application and SSE student account.
Prior to their arrival, a mandatory online meeting will be held for all incoming exchange students where they will receive more information about course registration and practical information for their stay at SSE.
Documents needed for the student application
Photo
Completed Student Pledge
Completed Online Registration Form
Academic calendar
The academic year at SSE is divided into two semesters: a fall semester and a spring semester. Each semester is further divided into two teaching periods, with periods one and two in the fall semester and periods three and four in the spring semester.
While most exchange students attend SSE for a full semester, partner universities are welcome to nominate their students for only one teaching period or for the full academic year if preferred. This can be indicated in the nomination form.
Before the start of each semester, we welcome all exchange students to SSE with an Orientation Day to get acquainted with the university and to get to know other students and the SSE community.
See the
Academic Calendar 2026-2027
for semester, teaching-period and examination dates.
Courses
Students may register for up to two courses per teaching period, or three courses if one of them is a language course. To take a third non-language course, students must obtain approval from their home university.
Check the course lists linked below for a list of courses open to exchange students. Bachelor’s students may in some cases enroll in Master’s-level courses, provided they meet the course prerequisites and have approval from their home university.
Students should check each course’s exam schedule and the language of instruction, as a select number of courses from the Bachelor’s program are taught in Sweden.
Exchange BSc in Business and Economics - courses offered
Exchange MSc in Business and Economics - courses offered
CEMS accredited course list
Teaching and assessment
The educational programs at SSE are based on research and stress a theoretical and analytical approach. Since the School’s foundation, Economics has occupied a stronger position in the curriculum than at most business schools.
The teaching methodology is a mixture of American and European teaching methods and theories. Some courses are characterized by more traditional teaching, with lectures, written course assignments and seminars.
In other courses the teaching is to a great extent based on cases; active participation in class is expected and contributes to the final grade. Many of the courses require substantial preparatory reading.
The contacts between students and faculty members are rather informal at SSE. Feel free to contact your professors if you have any questions regarding the courses you are taking.
As an exchange student you study under the same conditions as the Swedish students. You may find that the structure of the SSE exams differs from those at your home university and therefore it is advisable to review past papers before taking your first exam.
>>> Exam Regulations (login)
Academic information
English language requirements
Students must demonstrate English proficiency at CEFR level B2 or above. The home university is responsible for confirming that nominated students meet this requirement.
Course format
Courses are typically conducted on site and in person. Exchange students are expected to remain until the end of their scheduled examinations. No special arrangements for early exams can be made.
Workload
A full-semester workload is 30 ECTS credits, normally 15 ECTS credits or two courses per teaching period.
Transcripts
Transcripts are available approximately two months after the final examinations. Students are invited to download their transcript directly from the internal portal. An original copy can be sent by post upon request.
Practical matters
Housing
At SSE, we have a small housing office that offers rooms and apartments to some of our international students. There is no guarantee of housing, so we recommend that you also explore other accommodation options. You can find more information
here
.
Cost of living
The following is a feasible monthly budget:
Housing: SEK 6,000 – 10,000
Food: SEK 3,000
Insurance: SEK 500
Hobbies: SEK 2,000
Local Transportation: SEK 650
Total: SEK 12,150 - 16,150
Exchange students have so far been exempt from the otherwise compulsory student association fees. Please note that you will need to pay for course literature, i.e. books, compendiums, etc.
Resident permit for studies
Depending on their citizenship and length of stay, students may need a residence permit to study in Sweden. Check the
Swedish Migration Agency website
for the requirements that apply to you.
Insurance
It is important that you purchase travel insurance covering your journey to Sweden and ensure that you have valid health insurance for the duration of your stay in Sweden.
Students from EU/EEA countries should bring a
European Health Insurance Card
from their home country or documentation confirming comprehensive private health insurance coverage.
Students with specific needs
Our Guidance and Wellbeing Office provides support to students with special needs, access to a certified counsellor, and assistance from the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Manager.
>>> Student health and support
Would you like to learn Swedish?
Although all programs at SSE are taught entirely in English - and English is widely spoken throughout Sweden - many international students choose to learn some Swedish to feel more connected to everyday life in Stockholm and Swedish society.
The
Swedish Institute
offers a range of helpful resources, language tools, and study tips for students who would like to begin learning Swedish before arriving in Sweden or continue improving their skills during their studies.
SSE also offers Swedish language courses at different levels for students who would like to learn the language while studying at the School.
Even a basic understanding of Swedish can make it easier to navigate daily life, meet new people, and gain additional insights into Swedish culture and society.
In addition, feel free to check out the following Swedish courses as well:
Folkuniversitet: Swedish Course - Online
Hermods: Swedish Online Courses
Udemy: Swedish Language Courses
Alison: Free Online Swedish Courses
Study in Sweden: Learn Swedish Online
LanguaTalk: Become Fluent in Swedish
Learning Swedish: A Free Language Course
Get in touch with us
Do you have questions about our student exchange program, bilateral agreements, the MBA Short Program, the Wallenberg International Fellows Program, GNAM, or our double degree programs with Sciences Po? Feel free to contact our team:

here

Insurance: SEK 500
Hobbies: SEK 2,000

Incoming exchange students
The Stockholm School of Economics welcomes around 180 exchange students each year. The Global Initiatives Team within the Education Office coordinates the student exchange program and supports students and partner institutions before, during, and after the exchange period.
On this page, you will find useful information about studying at SSE and living in Stockholm.
Please note that SSE does not accept free movers.
About the Stockholm School of Economics
The Stockholm School of Economics (SSE) is an internationally recognized business school in the Nordic and Baltic region. Since 1909, SSE has educated people for leading roles in business, government, civil society and the public sector.
SSE’s education is grounded in current research and strengthened by close collaboration with Swedish and international organizations. SSE is accredited by EQUIS, the European Quality Improvement System.
>>> A guide to life in Stockholm and Sweden
Nomination and application
SSE accepts nominations only through its official online form. Partner universities receive the nomination link when the nomination period opens. Students who have not been nominated through the form cannot be enrolled in the exchange program.
Nomination deadlines
April 1
for the fall semester and
October 1
for the spring semester.
After the nomination period closes, nominated students are invited to complete an online registration form.
Students nominated for the spring semester will receive access to the registration form in October. Students nominated for the fall semester will receive access in April.
Student application and account
Once the registration form has been completed and approved, the student will be issued an acceptance letter. They will also receive further information about the housing application and SSE student account.
Prior to their arrival, a mandatory online meeting will be held for all incoming exchange students where they will receive more information about course registration and practical information for their stay at SSE.
Documents needed for the student application
Photo
Completed Student Pledge
Completed Online Registration Form
Academic calendar
The academic year at SSE is divided into two semesters: a fall semester and a spring semester. Each semester is further divided into two teaching periods, with periods one and two in the fall semester and periods three and four in the spring semester.
While most exchange students attend SSE for a full semester, partner universities are welcome to nominate their students for only one teaching period or for the full academic year if preferred. This can be indicated in the nomination form.
Before the start of each semester, we welcome all exchange students to SSE with an Orientation Day to get acquainted with the university and to get to know other students and the SSE community.
See the
Academic Calendar 2026-2027
for semester, teaching-period and examination dates.
Courses
Students may register for up to two courses per teaching period, or three courses if one of them is a language course. To take a third non-language course, students must obtain approval from their home university.
Check the course lists linked below for a list of courses open to exchange students. Bachelor’s students may in some cases enroll in Master’s-level courses, provided they meet the course prerequisites and have approval from their home university.
Students should check each course’s exam schedule and the language of instruction, as a select number of courses from the Bachelor’s program are taught in Sweden.
Exchange BSc in Business and Economics - courses offered
Exchange MSc in Business and Economics - courses offered
CEMS accredited course list
Teaching and assessment
The educational programs at SSE are based on research and stress a theoretical and analytical approach. Since the School’s foundation, Economics has occupied a stronger position in the curriculum than at most business schools.
The teaching methodology is a mixture of American and European teaching methods and theories. Some courses are characterized by more traditional teaching, with lectures, written course assignments and seminars.
In other courses the teaching is to a great extent based on cases; active participation in class is expected and contributes to the final grade. Many of the courses require substantial preparatory reading.
The contacts between students and faculty members are rather informal at SSE. Feel free to contact your professors if you have any questions regarding the courses you are taking.
As an exchange student you study under the same conditions as the Swedish students. You may find that the structure of the SSE exams differs from those at your home university and therefore it is advisable to review past papers before taking your first exam.
>>> Exam Regulations (login)
Academic information
English language requirements
Students must demonstrate English proficiency at CEFR level B2 or above. The home university is responsible for confirming that nominated students meet this requirement.
Course format
Courses are typically conducted on site and in person. Exchange students are expected to remain until the end of their scheduled examinations. No special arrangements for early exams can be made.
Workload
A full-semester workload is 30 ECTS credits, normally 15 ECTS credits or two courses per teaching period.
Transcripts
Transcripts are available approximately two months after the final examinations. Students are invited to download their transcript directly from the internal portal. An original copy can be sent by post upon request.
Practical matters
Housing
At SSE, we have a small housing office that offers rooms and apartments to some of our international students. There is no guarantee of housing, so we recommend that you also explore other accommodation options. You can find more information
here
.
Cost of living
The following is a feasible monthly budget:
Housing: SEK 6,000 – 10,000
Food: SEK 3,000
Insurance: SEK 500
Hobbies: SEK 2,000
Local Transportation: SEK 650
Total: SEK 12,150 - 16,150
Exchange students have so far been exempt from the otherwise compulsory student association fees. Please note that you will need to pay for course literature, i.e. books, compendiums, etc.
Resident permit for studies
Depending on their citizenship and length of stay, students may need a residence permit to study in Sweden. Check the
Swedish Migration Agency website
for the requirements that apply to you.
Insurance
It is important that you purchase travel insurance covering your journey to Sweden and ensure that you have valid health insurance for the duration of your stay in Sweden.
Students from EU/EEA countries should bring a
European Health Insurance Card
from their home country or documentation confirming comprehensive private health insurance coverage.
Students with specific needs
Our Guidance and Wellbeing Office provides support to students with special needs, access to a certified counsellor, and assistance from the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Manager.
>>> Student health and support
Would you like to learn Swedish?
Although all programs at SSE are taught entirely in English - and English is widely spoken throughout Sweden - many international students choose to learn some Swedish to feel more connected to everyday life in Stockholm and Swedish society.
The
Swedish Institute
offers a range of helpful resources, language tools, and study tips for students who would like to begin learning Swedish before arriving in Sweden or continue improving their skills during their studies.
SSE also offers Swedish language courses at different levels for students who would like to learn the language while studying at the School.
Even a basic understanding of Swedish can make it easier to navigate daily life, meet new people, and gain additional insights into Swedish culture and society.

Incoming exchange students
The Stockholm School of Economics welcomes around 180 exchange students each year. The Global Initiatives Team within the Education Office coordinates the student exchange program and supports students and partner institutions before, during, and after the exchange period.
On this page, you will find useful information about studying at SSE and living in Stockholm.
Please note that SSE does not accept free movers.
About the Stockholm School of Economics
The Stockholm School of Economics (SSE) is an internationally recognized business school in the Nordic and Baltic region. Since 1909, SSE has educated people for leading roles in business, government, civil society and the public sector.
SSE’s education is grounded in current research and strengthened by close collaboration with Swedish and international organizations. SSE is accredited by EQUIS, the European Quality Improvement System.
>>> A guide to life in Stockholm and Sweden
Nomination and application
SSE accepts nominations only through its official online form. Partner universities receive the nomination link when the nomination period opens. Students who have not been nominated through the form cannot be enrolled in the exchange program.
Nomination deadlines
April 1
for the fall semester and
October 1
for the spring semester.
After the nomination period closes, nominated students are invited to complete an online registration form.
Students nominated for the spring semester will receive access to the registration form in October. Students nominated for the fall semester will receive access in April.
Student application and account
Once the registration form has been completed and approved, the student will be issued an acceptance letter. They will also receive further information about the housing application and SSE student account.
Prior to their arrival, a mandatory online meeting will be held for all incoming exchange students where they will receive more information about course registration and practical information for their stay at SSE.
Documents needed for the student application
Photo
Completed Student Pledge
Completed Online Registration Form
Academic calendar
The academic year at SSE is divided into two semesters: a fall semester and a spring semester. Each semester is further divided into two teaching periods, with periods one and two in the fall semester and periods three and four in the spring semester.
While most exchange students attend SSE for a full semester, partner universities are welcome to nominate their students for only one teaching period or for the full academic year if preferred. This can be indicated in the nomination form.
Before the start of each semester, we welcome all exchange students to SSE with an Orientation Day to get acquainted with the university and to get to know other students and the SSE community.
See the
Academic Calendar 2026-2027
for semester, teaching-period and examination dates.
Courses
Students may register for up to two courses per teaching period, or three courses if one of them is a language course. To take a third non-language course, students must obtain approval from their home university.
Check the course lists linked below for a list of courses open to exchange students. Bachelor’s students may in some cases enroll in Master’s-level courses, provided they meet the course prerequisites and have approval from their home university.
Students should check each course’s exam schedule and the language of instruction, as a select number of courses from the Bachelor’s program are taught in Sweden.
Exchange BSc in Business and Economics - courses offered
Exchange MSc in Business and Economics - courses offered
CEMS accredited course list
Teaching and assessment
The educational programs at SSE are based on research and stress a theoretical and analytical approach. Since the School’s foundation, Economics has occupied a stronger position in the curriculum than at most business schools.
The teaching methodology is a mixture of American and European teaching methods and theories. Some courses are characterized by more traditional teaching, with lectures, written course assignments and seminars.
In other courses the teaching is to a great extent based on cases; active participation in class is expected and contributes to the final grade. Many of the courses require substantial preparatory reading.
The contacts between students and faculty members are rather informal at SSE. Feel free to contact your professors if you have any questions regarding the courses you are taking.
As an exchange student you study under the same conditions as the Swedish students. You may find that the structure of the SSE exams differs from those at your home university and therefore it is advisable to review past papers before taking your first exam.
>>> Exam Regulations (login)
Academic information
English language requirements
Students must demonstrate English proficiency at CEFR level B2 or above. The home university is responsible for confirming that nominated students meet this requirement.
Course format
Courses are typically conducted on site and in person. Exchange students are expected to remain until the end of their scheduled examinations. No special arrangements for early exams can be made.
Workload
A full-semester workload is 30 ECTS credits, normally 15 ECTS credits or two courses per teaching period.
Transcripts
Transcripts are available approximately two months after the final examinations. Students are invited to download their transcript directly from the internal portal. An original copy can be sent by post upon request.
Practical matters
Housing
At SSE, we have a small housing office that offers rooms and apartments to some of our international students. There is no guarantee of housing, so we recommend that you also explore other accommodation options. You can find more information
here
.
Cost of living
The following is a feasible monthly budget:
Housing: SEK 6,000 – 10,000
Food: SEK 3,000
Insurance: SEK 500
Hobbies: SEK 2,000
Local Transportation: SEK 650
Total: SEK 12,150 - 16,150
Exchange students have so far been exempt from the otherwise compulsory student association fees. Please note that you will need to pay for course literature, i.e. books, compendiums, etc.
Resident permit for studies
Depending on their citizenship and length of stay, students may need a residence permit to study in Sweden. Check the
Swedish Migration Agency website
for the requirements that apply to you.
Insurance
It is important that you purchase travel insurance covering your journey to Sweden and ensure that you have valid health insurance for the duration of your stay in Sweden.
Students from EU/EEA countries should bring a
European Health Insurance Card
from their home country or documentation confirming comprehensive private health insurance coverage.
Students with specific needs
Our Guidance and Wellbeing Office provides support to students with special needs, access to a certified counsellor, and assistance from the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Manager.
>>> Student health and support

Although all programs at SSE are taught entirely in English - and English is widely spoken throughout Sweden - many international students choose to learn some Swedish to feel more connected to everyday life in Stockholm and Swedish society.

Swedish Institute
offers a range of helpful resources, language tools, and study tips for students who would like to begin learning Swedish before arriving in Sweden or continue improving their skills during their studies.

Even a basic understanding of Swedish can make it easier to navigate daily life, meet new people, and gain additional insights into Swedish culture and society.

Incoming exchange students
Incoming exchange students
The Stockholm School of Economics welcomes around 180 exchange students each year. The Global Initiatives Team within the Education Office coordinates the student exchange program and supports students and partner institutions before, during, and after the exchange period.
On this page, you will find useful information about studying at SSE and living in Stockholm.
Please note that SSE does not accept free movers.
About the Stockholm School of Economics
The Stockholm School of Economics (SSE) is an internationally recognized business school in the Nordic and Baltic region. Since 1909, SSE has educated people for leading roles in business, government, civil society and the public sector.
SSE’s education is grounded in current research and strengthened by close collaboration with Swedish and international organizations. SSE is accredited by EQUIS, the European Quality Improvement System.
>>> A guide to life in Stockholm and Sweden
Nomination and application
SSE accepts nominations only through its official online form. Partner universities receive the nomination link when the nomination period opens. Students who have not been nominated through the form cannot be enrolled in the exchange program.
Nomination deadlines
April 1
for the fall semester and
October 1
for the spring semester.
After the nomination period closes, nominated students are invited to complete an online registration form.
Students nominated for the spring semester will receive access to the registration form in October. Students nominated for the fall semester will receive access in April.
Student application and account
Once the registration form has been completed and approved, the student will be issued an acceptance letter. They will also receive further information about the housing application and SSE student account.
Prior to their arrival, a mandatory online meeting will be held for all incoming exchange students where they will receive more information about course registration and practical information for their stay at SSE.
Documents needed for the student application
Photo
Completed Student Pledge
Completed Online Registration Form
Academic calendar
The academic year at SSE is divided into two semesters: a fall semester and a spring semester. Each semester is further divided into two teaching periods, with periods one and two in the fall semester and periods three and four in the spring semester.
While most exchange students attend SSE for a full semester, partner universities are welcome to nominate their students for only one teaching period or for the full academic year if preferred. This can be indicated in the nomination form.
Before the start of each semester, we welcome all exchange students to SSE with an Orientation Day to get acquainted with the university and to get to know other students and the SSE community.
See the
Academic Calendar 2026-2027
for semester, teaching-period and examination dates.
Courses
Students may register for up to two courses per teaching period, or three courses if one of them is a language course. To take a third non-language course, students must obtain approval from their home university.
Check the course lists linked below for a list of courses open to exchange students. Bachelor’s students may in some cases enroll in Master’s-level courses, provided they meet the course prerequisites and have approval from their home university.
Students should check each course’s exam schedule and the language of instruction, as a select number of courses from the Bachelor’s program are taught in Sweden.
Exchange BSc in Business and Economics - courses offered
Exchange MSc in Business and Economics - courses offered
CEMS accredited course list
Teaching and assessment
The educational programs at SSE are based on research and stress a theoretical and analytical approach. Since the School’s foundation, Economics has occupied a stronger position in the curriculum than at most business schools.
The teaching methodology is a mixture of American and European teaching methods and theories. Some courses are characterized by more traditional teaching, with lectures, written course assignments and seminars.
In other courses the teaching is to a great extent based on cases; active participation in class is expected and contributes to the final grade. Many of the courses require substantial preparatory reading.
The contacts between students and faculty members are rather informal at SSE. Feel free to contact your professors if you have any questions regarding the courses you are taking.
As an exchange student you study under the same conditions as the Swedish students. You may find that the structure of the SSE exams differs from those at your home university and therefore it is advisable to review past papers before taking your first exam.
>>> Exam Regulations (login)
Academic information
English language requirements
Students must demonstrate English proficiency at CEFR level B2 or above. The home university is responsible for confirming that nominated students meet this requirement.
Course format
Courses are typically conducted on site and in person. Exchange students are expected to remain until the end of their scheduled examinations. No special arrangements for early exams can be made.
Workload
A full-semester workload is 30 ECTS credits, normally 15 ECTS credits or two courses per teaching period.
Transcripts
Transcripts are available approximately two months after the final examinations. Students are invited to download their transcript directly from the internal portal. An original copy can be sent by post upon request.
Practical matters
Housing
At SSE, we have a small housing office that offers rooms and apartments to some of our international students. There is no guarantee of housing, so we recommend that you also explore other accommodation options. You can find more information
here
.
Cost of living
The following is a feasible monthly budget:
Housing: SEK 6,000 – 10,000
Food: SEK 3,000
Insurance: SEK 500
Hobbies: SEK 2,000
Local Transportation: SEK 650
Total: SEK 12,150 - 16,150
Exchange students have so far been exempt from the otherwise compulsory student association fees. Please note that you will need to pay for course literature, i.e. books, compendiums, etc.
Resident permit for studies
Depending on their citizenship and length of stay, students may need a residence permit to study in Sweden. Check the
Swedish Migration Agency website
for the requirements that apply to you.
Insurance
It is important that you purchase travel insurance covering your journey to Sweden and ensure that you have valid health insurance for the duration of your stay in Sweden.
Students from EU/EEA countries should bring a
European Health Insurance Card
from their home country or documentation confirming comprehensive private health insurance coverage.
Students with specific needs
Our Guidance and Wellbeing Office provides support to students with special needs, access to a certified counsellor, and assistance from the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Manager.
>>> Student health and support
Would you like to learn Swedish?
Although all programs at SSE are taught entirely in English - and English is widely spoken throughout Sweden - many international students choose to learn some Swedish to feel more connected to everyday life in Stockholm and Swedish society.
The
Swedish Institute
offers a range of helpful resources, language tools, and study tips for students who would like to begin learning Swedish before arriving in Sweden or continue improving their skills during their studies.
SSE also offers Swedish language courses at different levels for students who would like to learn the language while studying at the School.
Even a basic understanding of Swedish can make it easier to navigate daily life, meet new people, and gain additional insights into Swedish culture and society.
In addition, feel free to check out the following Swedish courses as well:

Incoming exchange students
Incoming exchange students
The Stockholm School of Economics welcomes around 180 exchange students each year. The Global Initiatives Team within the Education Office coordinates the student exchange program and supports students and partner institutions before, during, and after the exchange period.
On this page, you will find useful information about studying at SSE and living in Stockholm.
Please note that SSE does not accept free movers.
About the Stockholm School of Economics
The Stockholm School of Economics (SSE) is an internationally recognized business school in the Nordic and Baltic region. Since 1909, SSE has educated people for leading roles in business, government, civil society and the public sector.
SSE’s education is grounded in current research and strengthened by close collaboration with Swedish and international organizations. SSE is accredited by EQUIS, the European Quality Improvement System.
>>> A guide to life in Stockholm and Sweden
Nomination and application
SSE accepts nominations only through its official online form. Partner universities receive the nomination link when the nomination period opens. Students who have not been nominated through the form cannot be enrolled in the exchange program.
Nomination deadlines
April 1
for the fall semester and
October 1
for the spring semester.
After the nomination period closes, nominated students are invited to complete an online registration form.
Students nominated for the spring semester will receive access to the registration form in October. Students nominated for the fall semester will receive access in April.
Student application and account
Once the registration form has been completed and approved, the student will be issued an acceptance letter. They will also receive further information about the housing application and SSE student account.
Prior to their arrival, a mandatory online meeting will be held for all incoming exchange students where they will receive more information about course registration and practical information for their stay at SSE.
Documents needed for the student application
Photo
Completed Student Pledge
Completed Online Registration Form
Academic calendar
The academic year at SSE is divided into two semesters: a fall semester and a spring semester. Each semester is further divided into two teaching periods, with periods one and two in the fall semester and periods three and four in the spring semester.
While most exchange students attend SSE for a full semester, partner universities are welcome to nominate their students for only one teaching period or for the full academic year if preferred. This can be indicated in the nomination form.
Before the start of each semester, we welcome all exchange students to SSE with an Orientation Day to get acquainted with the university and to get to know other students and the SSE community.
See the
Academic Calendar 2026-2027
for semester, teaching-period and examination dates.
Courses
Students may register for up to two courses per teaching period, or three courses if one of them is a language course. To take a third non-language course, students must obtain approval from their home university.
Check the course lists linked below for a list of courses open to exchange students. Bachelor’s students may in some cases enroll in Master’s-level courses, provided they meet the course prerequisites and have approval from their home university.
Students should check each course’s exam schedule and the language of instruction, as a select number of courses from the Bachelor’s program are taught in Sweden.
Exchange BSc in Business and Economics - courses offered
Exchange MSc in Business and Economics - courses offered
CEMS accredited course list
Teaching and assessment
The educational programs at SSE are based on research and stress a theoretical and analytical approach. Since the School’s foundation, Economics has occupied a stronger position in the curriculum than at most business schools.
The teaching methodology is a mixture of American and European teaching methods and theories. Some courses are characterized by more traditional teaching, with lectures, written course assignments and seminars.
In other courses the teaching is to a great extent based on cases; active participation in class is expected and contributes to the final grade. Many of the courses require substantial preparatory reading.
The contacts between students and faculty members are rather informal at SSE. Feel free to contact your professors if you have any questions regarding the courses you are taking.
As an exchange student you study under the same conditions as the Swedish students. You may find that the structure of the SSE exams differs from those at your home university and therefore it is advisable to review past papers before taking your first exam.
>>> Exam Regulations (login)
Academic information
English language requirements
Students must demonstrate English proficiency at CEFR level B2 or above. The home university is responsible for confirming that nominated students meet this requirement.
Course format
Courses are typically conducted on site and in person. Exchange students are expected to remain until the end of their scheduled examinations. No special arrangements for early exams can be made.
Workload
A full-semester workload is 30 ECTS credits, normally 15 ECTS credits or two courses per teaching period.
Transcripts
Transcripts are available approximately two months after the final examinations. Students are invited to download their transcript directly from the internal portal. An original copy can be sent by post upon request.
Practical matters
Housing
At SSE, we have a small housing office that offers rooms and apartments to some of our international students. There is no guarantee of housing, so we recommend that you also explore other accommodation options. You can find more information
here
.
Cost of living
The following is a feasible monthly budget:
Housing: SEK 6,000 – 10,000
Food: SEK 3,000
Insurance: SEK 500
Hobbies: SEK 2,000
Local Transportation: SEK 650
Total: SEK 12,150 - 16,150
Exchange students have so far been exempt from the otherwise compulsory student association fees. Please note that you will need to pay for course literature, i.e. books, compendiums, etc.
Resident permit for studies
Depending on their citizenship and length of stay, students may need a residence permit to study in Sweden. Check the
Swedish Migration Agency website
for the requirements that apply to you.
Insurance
It is important that you purchase travel insurance covering your journey to Sweden and ensure that you have valid health insurance for the duration of your stay in Sweden.
Students from EU/EEA countries should bring a
European Health Insurance Card
from their home country or documentation confirming comprehensive private health insurance coverage.
Students with specific needs
Our Guidance and Wellbeing Office provides support to students with special needs, access to a certified counsellor, and assistance from the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Manager.
>>> Student health and support
Would you like to learn Swedish?
Although all programs at SSE are taught entirely in English - and English is widely spoken throughout Sweden - many international students choose to learn some Swedish to feel more connected to everyday life in Stockholm and Swedish society.
The
Swedish Institute
offers a range of helpful resources, language tools, and study tips for students who would like to begin learning Swedish before arriving in Sweden or continue improving their skills during their studies.
SSE also offers Swedish language courses at different levels for students who would like to learn the language while studying at the School.
Even a basic understanding of Swedish can make it easier to navigate daily life, meet new people, and gain additional insights into Swedish culture and society.
In addition, feel free to check out the following Swedish courses as well:
Folkuniversitet: Swedish Course - Online
Hermods: Swedish Online Courses
Udemy: Swedish Language Courses
Alison: Free Online Swedish Courses
Study in Sweden: Learn Swedish Online

original_evidence.text:
PRACTICAL MATTERS 
General semester dates Autumn Semester: 1 September – 1 February 
Spring Semester: 1 February – 1 July 
The academic calendar can be found online. 
Online nomination Partner universities fill out our online nomination form.   
**Please nominate within our nomination period** 
Nomination period Autumn semester: 15 March – 15 May 
Spring semester: 15 September - 15 October 
Online application Students need to apply online and upload the required 
documents.  Check out our application procedure 
Application period Autumn semester: 15 April – 1 June 
Spring semester: 1 October- 1 November  
Exchange programmes Find our exchange programmes online.   
We offer fixed programmes.  
It is not possible to mix and match courses from different 
programmes due to timetable constraints. 
Possibility of attending courses 
from different departments  
Students can apply for an exchange programme  with a Hanze 
School as stated in our agreement.    
Language of instruction English 
Language requirement Exchange students are not required to submit proof of their 
English proficiency, but we ask partner institutions to select 
students who have a good standard of English (minimum of 
B2/CEFR). 
Learning Agreements Learning Agreements are approved and signed by the Hanze 
School. The School can answer questions about courses. 
ECTS Grading Tabels More information about the Dutch Grading System. 
Immigration & visa Students with a non-European nationality need a 
visa/permit to study in The Netherlands.  
Team Immigration will apply for the visa/permit and will 
contact students with the immigraton procedure once they 
have received their acceptance letter.   
As part of this procedure students need to transfer 
a financial guarantee to the bank account of Hanze.   
Welcome Day At the start of each semester Hanze organises a Welcome Day 
for all new international students.  
Housing 
 
 
 
Check out our housing page and the housing page of the city 
of Groningen At Home in Groningen.  Students need to find 
a room themselves, but can contact Team Housing for 
advice, questions or problems: housing@org.hanze.nl. 
It is important that students start looking in time. 
Moving to the Netherlands Check out practical information about moving to the 
Netherlands such as opening a bank account, cost of living. 
Insurance We strongly advise students to be fully insured for their time 
abroad.  
Team Immigration will take out insurance with AON for Non 
EU students.  
Language Courses Students have the possibility to follow a language course at 
the Hanze Language Centre.  
Available places are limited, and costs vary.  
Traveling to Groningen & Pick up 
Service 
Check out how you can best travel to Groningen or apply for 
our pick up service. 
 
PROGRAMME RELATED INFORMATION 
Programme specific questions (transcript of records, course information, learning 
agreements) will be dealt with by the international coordinator of the Hanze School (Faculty). 
You can find their details when you click on the applicable exchange programme link.

項目 說明 
申請表 請務必完成簽核 
家長同意書(必繳) 請務必由家長親筆簽名 
個資同意書(必繳)  
語言測驗成績單影本(必繳) 1. 線上申請截止日前需備妥此資料之正式
成績單影本，不接受網路截圖成績單或
補繳 
2. 赴國外或大陸港澳地區交換者，無論姐
妹校是否有規定，均應於校內申請時具
備並繳交外語檢定考試成績（不限成績
級數） ：《英文檢定成績需為二年內效
期》 
⚫ 托福 TOEFL iBT/ITP 
⚫ 雅思 IELTS（學術組） 
⚫ 全民英檢 GEPT（複試通過） 
⚫ 多益 TOEIC（包含聽讀） 
⚫ 領思（實用組） 
⚫ 培力英檢 
3. 或志願校接受之第三外語檢定成績
（如：德檢、法檢、日檢 JLPT、韓檢
TOPIK 等） 。 
中文版歷年成績單(必繳) 1. 請至註冊組申請

印出來並簽名掃瞄為證明，或先欠繳。惟需
要在姐妹校申請截止日前補繳正式成績單，
無法出具者視同未獲校內錄取資格。 
其他能力證明或個人作品(選繳)  
以上兩步驟皆需完成才算完成整個申請程序，請注意繳件時間，逾期或資料不
全，於申請截止日後將不予受理!

學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。

PRACTICAL MATTERS 
General semester dates Autumn Semester: 1 September – 1 February 
Spring Semester: 1 February – 1 July 
The academic calendar can be found online. 
Online nomination Partner universities fill out our online nomination form.   
**Please nominate within our nomination period** 
Nomination period Autumn semester: 15 March – 15 May 
Spring semester: 15 September - 15 October 
Online application Students need to apply online and upload the required 
documents.  Check out our application procedure 
Application period Autumn semester: 15 April – 1 June 
Spring semester: 1 October- 1 November  
Exchange programmes Find our exchange programmes online.   
We offer fixed programmes.  
It is not possible to mix and match courses from different 
programmes due to timetable constraints. 
Possibility of attending courses 
from different departments  
Students can apply for an exchange programme  with a Hanze 
School as stated in our agreement.    
Language of instruction English 
Language requirement Exchange students are not required to submit proof of their 
English proficiency, but we ask partner institutions to select 
students who have a good standard of English (minimum of 
B2/CEFR). 
Learning Agreements Learning Agreements are approved and signed by the Hanze 
School. The School can answer questions about courses. 
ECTS Grading Tabels More information about the Dutch Grading System. 
Immigration & visa Students with a non-European nationality need a 
visa/permit to study in The Netherlands.  
Team Immigration will apply for the visa/permit and will 
contact students with the immigraton procedure once they 
have received their acceptance letter.   
As part of this procedure students need to transfer 
a financial guarantee to the bank account of Hanze.   
Welcome Day At the start of each semester Hanze organises a Welcome Day 
for all new international students.  
Housing 
 
 
 
Check out our housing page and the housing page of the city 
of Groningen At Home in Groningen.  Students need to find 
a room themselves, but can contact Team Housing for 
advice, questions or problems: housing@org.hanze.nl. 
It is important that students start looking in time. 
Moving to the Netherlands Check out practical information about moving to the 
Netherlands such as opening a bank account, cost of living. 
Insurance We strongly advise students to be fully insured for their time 
abroad.  
Team Immigration will take out insurance with AON for Non 
EU students.  
Language Courses Students have the possibility to follow a language course at 
the Hanze Language Centre.  
Available places are limited, and costs vary.  
Traveling to Groningen & Pick up 
Service 
Check out how you can best travel to Groningen or apply for 
our pick up service. 
 
PROGRAMME RELATED INFORMATION 
Programme specific questions (transcript of records, course information, learning 
agreements) will be dealt with by the international coordinator of the Hanze School (Faculty). 
You can find their details when you click on the applicable exchange programme link.

PRACTICAL MATTERS 
General semester dates Autumn Semester: 1 September – 1 February 
Spring Semester: 1 February – 1 July 
The academic calendar can be found online. 
Online nomination Partner universities fill out our online nomination form.   
**Please nominate within our nomination period** 
Nomination period Autumn semester: 15 March – 15 May 
Spring semester: 15 September - 15 October 
Online application Students need to apply online and upload the required 
documents.  Check out our application procedure 
Application period Autumn semester: 15 April – 1 June 
Spring semester: 1 October- 1 November  
Exchange programmes Find our exchange programmes online.   
We offer fixed programmes.  
It is not possible to mix and match courses from different 
programmes due to timetable constraints. 
Possibility of attending courses 
from different departments  
Students can apply for an exchange programme  with a Hanze 
School as stated in our agreement.    
Language of instruction English 
Language requirement Exchange students are not required to submit proof of their 
English proficiency, but we ask partner institutions to select 
students who have a good standard of English (minimum of 
B2/CEFR). 
Learning Agreements Learning Agreements are approved and signed by the Hanze 
School. The School can answer questions about courses. 
ECTS Grading Tabels More information about the Dutch Grading System. 
Immigration & visa Students with a non-European nationality need a 
visa/permit to study in The Netherlands.  
Team Immigration will apply for the visa/permit and will 
contact students with the immigraton procedure once they 
have received their acceptance letter.   
As part of this procedure students need to transfer 
a financial guarantee to the bank account of Hanze.   
Welcome Day At the start of each semester Hanze organises a Welcome Day 
for all new international students.  
Housing 
 
 
 
Check out our housing page and the housing page of the city 
of Groningen At Home in Groningen.  Students need to find 
a room themselves, but can contact Team Housing for 
advice, questions or problems: housing@org.hanze.nl. 
It is important that students start looking in time. 
Moving to the Netherlands Check out practical information about moving to the 
Netherlands such as opening a bank account, cost of living. 
Insurance We strongly advise students to be fully insured for their time 
abroad.  
Team Immigration will take out insurance with AON for Non 
EU students.  
Language Courses Students have the possibility to follow a language course at 
the Hanze Language Centre.  
Available places are limited, and costs vary.  
Traveling to Groningen & Pick up 
Service 
Check out how you can best travel to Groningen or apply for 
our pick up service. 
 
PROGRAMME RELATED INFORMATION 
Programme specific questions (transcript of records, course information, learning 
agreements) will be dealt with by the international coordinator of the Hanze School (Faculty). 
You can find their details when you click on the applicable exchange programme link.

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。 
 
 
 
□我已閱讀並同意上述所有內容。

簽名日期:_____________________

original_evidence.text:
University of Deusto 德烏斯托大學 
地點 Unibertsitate Etorb., 24, 48007 Bilbo, Bizkaia, Spain 
 
 
 
申請資格 Undergraduate/Graduate 
語言要求 
 
 

【同頁視覺核對選定原文；非全文轉錄】
UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS
No official certificate is required. Students should have enough knowledge of either Spanish or English to follow lessons and sit exams.
In general, minimum B1, although a B2 is strongly recommended.
A B2 in either language is compulsory for Engineering degrees.
A B2 or C1 is compulsory for some courses from the Modern Language degree.
Both courses are free of charge (except learning materials).
MASTER & PhD STUDENTS
Each master or PhD programme might have a different language requirement, but a C1 in the language of tuition is usually required.
Permission for acceptance must be forwarded to the director of the programme who might also require further documents such as the Transcript of Records to decide on the acceptance of the exchange student.

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。 
 
 
 
□我已閱讀並同意上述所有內容。

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。

Academic information
Subjects catalogue
Subjects belonging to official degrees are generally taught in Spanish.
Erasmus+ students must choose subjects from the study area for which they have been selected according to the bilateral agreement between both universities.
Official Degrees
Official subjects taught in English
List of courses in English
Class groups and availability
Depending on the number of students, some courses are divided into different groups, usually taught by different teachers and with different timetables, and in some cases offered in several languages (Spanish, Valencian, English).
However, class groups have a limited number of students and, for this reason, enrollment depends on the established limit. Being able to study the subjects included in the
Learning Agreement
depends on the availability of places in the groups.
Spanish course
A Spanish course is offered to international exchange students. No registration fee is paid, but it has a cost of €60 for the materials. Its duration is 60 hours and, once passed, 6 ECTS are obtained.
Additional courses can be taken by paying the corresponding registration fee.
More information on the Spanish course
Usual workload
30 ECTS per semester.
The recommendation for international students is 3-5 subjects (18-30 credits) per semester.
Credits System
6 ECTS per subject.
1 credit (ECTS) is equivalent to 25 hours of workload, where a 40% are face-to-face hours in class and 60% correspond to autonomous student work.
Qualification system
The scale is over 10, where 5 is the minimum to pass a subject.
Matrícula de Honor (9-10): the most outstanding performance → A
Sobresaliente: (9-10): excellent performance → A
Notable (7-8.9): very good performance → B
Aprobado (5-6.9): average performance → C
Suspenso (0-4.9): insufficient performance → F
No presentado: exam not done by the student → no grade
Language Requirement
Spanish B1 is recommended to take subjects in Spanish.
English B2 is recommended to take subjects in English.

Cost of living
Accommodation: ~ €450/month in a shared flat, plus water, gas and electricity.
Transport: ~ €40/month (tram or bus).
Living expenses and other personal expenses: ~ €450/month.
Visas
Those students who do not have the nationality of a member state of the European Union must apply for a
study visa
at the corresponding embassy or consular office.
When applying for a visa, it is necessary to select the category:
Authorization to stay for the purpose of higher education. Art. 52.1.A.
During the orientation sessions, international students are advised on immigration procedures required upon arrival.
Health care insurance
All exchange students must be covered by
medical insurance
during their stay, which includes medical assistance and repatriation. In the case of internships, it must also include civil liability.
Sports facilities

15 or 30 use pass
allows access to the following facilities: gym, paddle tennis, tennis, squash, table tennis, athletics track, climbing wall (with federation license), tatami, and locker rooms. The pool is no longer included as it has been closed for renovations.
Transport
Due to its location, next to exit 70 of the A-70 motorway, the University of Alicante has good accessibility by road. The same A-70 motorway connects the university with the Alicante-Elche airport (exit 72), allowing the visitor to travel quickly and comfortably to the airport. It can be accessed by bus, bicycle and tram (TRAM line 2) that connects Alicante with the campus.

Academic information
Subjects catalogue
Subjects belonging to official degrees are generally taught in Spanish.
Erasmus+ students must choose subjects from the study area for which they have been selected according to the bilateral agreement between both universities.
Official Degrees
Official subjects taught in English
List of courses in English
Class groups and availability
Depending on the number of students, some courses are divided into different groups, usually taught by different teachers and with different timetables, and in some cases offered in several languages (Spanish, Valencian, English).
However, class groups have a limited number of students and, for this reason, enrollment depends on the established limit. Being able to study the subjects included in the
Learning Agreement
depends on the availability of places in the groups.
Spanish course
A Spanish course is offered to international exchange students. No registration fee is paid, but it has a cost of €60 for the materials. Its duration is 60 hours and, once passed, 6 ECTS are obtained.
Additional courses can be taken by paying the corresponding registration fee.
More information on the Spanish course
Usual workload
30 ECTS per semester.
The recommendation for international students is 3-5 subjects (18-30 credits) per semester.
Credits System
6 ECTS per subject.
1 credit (ECTS) is equivalent to 25 hours of workload, where a 40% are face-to-face hours in class and 60% correspond to autonomous student work.
Qualification system
The scale is over 10, where 5 is the minimum to pass a subject.
Matrícula de Honor (9-10): the most outstanding performance → A
Sobresaliente: (9-10): excellent performance → A
Notable (7-8.9): very good performance → B
Aprobado (5-6.9): average performance → C
Suspenso (0-4.9): insufficient performance → F
No presentado: exam not done by the student → no grade
Language Requirement
Spanish B1 is recommended to take subjects in Spanish.
English B2 is recommended to take subjects in English.

桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。 
 
 
 
□我已閱讀並同意上述所有內容。 
申請人簽名:___________________ 
簽名日期:_____________________

出國研修獎助辦法」前往合作協議之學校進修。於合作協議學校期間，保證
敝子弟遵守兩校之規定及該計畫之規範。結束時，按時返國絕無滯留當地不
返國等現象，如有違反以上之情，本人願負法律上一切責任，且不殃及他人
與學校，更不以法律行為進行抗辯，恐口說無憑，特立此具結保證書以資為
