Douglas College Overview

Douglas College is a public post-secondary institution located in British Columbia, Canada, known for offering a high-quality education in a welcoming and diverse environment. For exchange students studying for one or two semesters, the college provides an excellent opportunity to experience Canadian academic life while earning credits toward your home institution’s program.

The college has two main campuses in New Westminster and Coquitlam, both easily accessible by public transit and situated within the vibrant Metro Vancouver region. Students will find modern facilities, a friendly atmosphere, and a community that values global perspectives.

Douglas College offers a wide variety of courses across disciplines such as business, humanities, sciences, health, and the arts. Exchange students can select from a broad range of classes to suit their academic goals, with most courses designed to blend theory with practical learning. Many classes include hands-on projects, case studies, or applied assignments that reflect real-world situations, which enrich the academic experience beyond the classroom.

A major benefit of studying at Douglas is its smaller class sizes. With fewer students per class than many larger institutions, exchange students are more likely to receive individualized attention from instructors, participate in discussions, and engage directly in the learning process.

Campus life at Douglas is active and inclusive. Exchange students can take part in student clubs, cultural events, and activities that help them connect with peers and feel part of the community. The college also offers a range of support services, including orientation for new international students, academic advising, and assistance with housing and adapting to life in Canada.

Overall, spending a semester or two at Douglas College gives exchange students the chance to study in a supportive academic environment, experience Canadian culture, and gain valuable international experience — all while enjoying the natural beauty and urban amenities of the surrounding region.

We look forward to welcoming you!

Exchange students are able to take almost all the courses offered at Douglas College as long as they have proper English language proficiency (for English language requirements see the 'application process' tab). Students who do not meet the English language requirements, or fall below the minimum in one or two areas, can register for Douglas College's English Language and Learning Acquisition (ELLA) program.

There are some departments that require special permission for exchange students to take courses. The following areas require special permission from the department in order for exchange students to register.

Contemporary Arts (Music and Visual Arts)
Sports Science

Exchange students cannot take courses in the following departments: 

Applied Community Studies
Health Sciences

In general, not all courses are offered every semester. So, it is a good idea to check what courses will be available during the semester you will be on exchange. You can find Douglas College courses listed online. If the semester you will be on exchange is not available yet, try checking what courses were offered during the same semester the previous year. Upper-level courses (3000-4000 level) are often difficult to register for as there are few course sections and many students that need to take these courses. It is advised that exchange students try tof fulfill any general elective requirements they may need while on exchange.

English Language and Learning Acquisition (ELLA) program

Student who enrol in ELLA courses are still considered exchange students, meaning they do not need to pay Douglas College tuition in addition to their home institution tuition. Exchange students can also combine ELLA courses with academic courses if they meet the English proficiency requirements in some areas but not others. For example, if you meet the minimum IELTS requirements for reading and writing, but not listening and speaking, you may take two academic courses and the two ELLA courses in the areas you need to improve.

Full-time Status

Exchange students are expected to register for and maintain a full-time course schedule during their exchange semester. At Douglas College full-time study means taking 9-15 credits, which is the same a 3-5 classes in most cases. 15 credits is the equivalent of 30 ECTS.

ELIGIBILITY

Students at our partner institutions may apply to study here as an exchange student for one or two semesters (4 or 8 months). To be eligible, you must be enrolled at a partner institution for at least the semester before applying for the exchange, have the equivalent of a 2.5 (C) Grade Point Average, and be nominated by your learning institution. 

The language of instruction at Douglas College is English and students enrolling in academic courses will be expected to meet the college language proficiency requirement. If you are not proficient in English at the academic level, you can take our English Language Learning and Acquisition (ELLA) courses to improve your language skills. To take academic courses students must have a IELTS overall score of at least 6.5 or an overall TOEFL score of at least 83.

If you are not an English speaker, or are not taking your studies in English at your home institution, you should submit a copy of your IELTS or TOEFL scores.

BEFORE YOU APPLY

Your first step is to contact the International Exchange Coordinator at your home institution to determine if you are eligible to apply for an exchange at Douglas College, and to discuss the application process. All incoming exchange students must first be nominated by their home University or college. Only students from partners of Douglas College will be accepted to the Douglas College exchange program. Students from institutions without partnerships with Douglas College may be able to study as fee-paying visiting students. For more information you contact Douglas College Global Engagement.

Next, explore our programs and courses to choose the courses that best fit your existing study program and your educational goals.  Check to see if each course you are choosing has pre-requisites. If it does, make sure you meet the pre-requisites; otherwise you won't be able to take that course. Once you've finalized your course selection and ensured you have the pre-requisites, review your choices with your home institution coordinator to see if the credit from the courses you've chosen transfer to your program.  Students typically study between 12 and 15 credits per semester. 

Once you have determined that Douglas College has the courses appropriate for your studies and have secured the financial resources necessary to participate in an exchange, complete your institution’s exchange application process.

After your home institution approves you for the exchange, you can complete and submit the Douglas College exchange application package per the steps below.

1) Online application questionnaire

2) Upload a copy of your passport photo page

3) Upload a copy of your latest transcript

4) Upoload a copy of your English language certificate

This program is not currently accepting applications.

VISA AND STUDY PERMIT

For stays less than 6 months (1 semester)

Students do not need a study permit to study in Canada for less than 6 months.
Most students will either need an eTA or visa to enter Canada. More information can be found here: Find out if you need a visa to travel to Canada

For stays more than 6 months (2 semesters or more)

Students will need to obtain a Study Permit before arriving in Canada.
Visas and study permits | Douglas College
Once Douglas College approves your application, we will provide you with a Letter of Acceptance which you will use to apply for a study permit if necessary.  
Regarding the designated learning institutions list, Douglas College will appear on the designated learning institutions list after you choose “British Columbia” in the “View list by province or territory drop-down box, and type “Douglas College” in the “Filter items” box.
If you have any questions regarding your study permit application, please reach out to one of our International Advisors.
MEDICAL INSURANCE

For stays less than 6 months (1 semester)

All incoming exchange students must have adequate medical insurance coverage.
Students are responsible for purchasing their insurance before entering Canada.

For stays more than 6 months (2 semesters or more)

Students who will stay for more than 1 semester must register for the government health plan (MSP) in addition to their private insurance.
Medical insurance for international students | Douglas College - PLEASE NOTE - exchange students are NOT covered under "guard.me", and will need to buy private health insurance to cover their waiting period. 
MSP costs CAD $75 per month. More information can be found here Apply for MSP - Province of British Columbia. It is recommended students apply as soon as they arrive.

ACCOMMODATION 

Douglas College is located in a suburb of the Greater Vancouver area. Exchange students have many choices for accommodations. While Douglas College does not have student residences, we do work with First Choice International Placement who offers homestay accommodation to students.  

Living in Vancouver | Douglas College

TRANSPORTATION

Getting around the Vancouver area is easy with our efficient public transportation system, known as TransLink. As part of your exchange, youwill be eligible for the U-Pass, a transit discounted passes for post-secondary students which is loaded on a Compass Card each month.

Your U-Pass provides unlimited access to bus, SeaBus, and SkyTrain services within the Vancouver area. To begin accessing the public transportation system, purchase a Compass Card at any SkyTrain station or one of these retailers and load your U-Pass BC onto it.

Step-by-Step: How to load your U-Pass onto a Compass Card (download PDF)

Exchange students arriving at Vancouver International Airport can easily access a taxi, uber/Lyft or take skytrain / transit.  

COSTS

As an exchange student, you will continue to pay tuition and student fees to your home institution. Douglas College does not charge our incoming exchange students any tuition or student fees.  You will also get your monthly U-Passes (public transit pass) free of charge.  However, you are responsible for covering the costs of your basic medical insurance coverage, textbooks, course materials, food, accommodation and personal spending expenses.

Vancouver is one of the most beautiful, and expensive, cities in the world! It is important that students keep this in mind while saving up or budgeting for their exchange semester. The amount of money you will need varies greatly depending on what you would like to do while you are in Canada. Travelling on the weekends or study breaks can make your semester abroad much more expensive than if you like to stay around your neighborhood or city. Also, if you prefer to eat out you will spend much more than someone who prefers to cook at home. The best person to consult about your budget is always yourself. But, here are some cost estimates to guide your planning.

Monthly rent and utilities (private room in a shared house) ~ $800-$1000
One bedroom or studio apartment ~ $1500- $2400
Dinner out (one person) ~ $25 ($30 with tip) ~ $45 with alcoholic drinks
Basic groceries $100-150 per week
Approximate taxi or Uber ~ $3.25 flate rate + $1.84/km
Student Season Ski Pass (Cypress Mountain) ~ $400

A great place to find more tips and resources for students is on the Douglas Student Union (DSU) website.

RESOURCES

Exchange students are able to take almost all the courses offered at Douglas College as long as they have proper English language proficiency (for English language requirements see the 'application process' tab). Students who do not meet the English language requirements, or fall below the minimum in one or two areas, can register for Douglas College's English Language and Learning Acquisition (ELLA) program.

There are some departments that require special permission for exchange students to take courses. The following areas require special permission from the department in order for exchange students to register.

Contemporary Arts (Music and Visual Arts)
Sports Science

Exchange students cannot take courses in the following departments: 

Applied Community Studies
Health Sciences

In general, not all courses are offered every semester. So, it is a good idea to check what courses will be available during the semester you will be on exchange. You can find Douglas College courses listed online. If the semester you will be on exchange is not available yet, try checking what courses were offered during the same semester the previous year. Upper-level courses (3000-4000 level) are often difficult to register for as there are few course sections and many students that need to take these courses. It is advised that exchange students try tof fulfill any general elective requirements they may need while on exchange.

English Language and Learning Acquisition (ELLA) program

Student who enrol in ELLA courses are still considered exchange students, meaning they do not need to pay Douglas College tuition in addition to their home institution tuition. Exchange students can also combine ELLA courses with academic courses if they meet the English proficiency requirements in some areas but not others. For example, if you meet the minimum IELTS requirements for reading and writing, but not listening and speaking, you may take two academic courses and the two ELLA courses in the areas you need to improve.

Full-time Status

Exchange students are expected to register for and maintain a full-time course schedule during their exchange semester. At Douglas College full-time study means taking 9-15 credits, which is the same a 3-5 classes in most cases. 15 credits is the equivalent of 30 ECTS.

ELIGIBILITY

Students at our partner institutions may apply to study here as an exchange student for one or two semesters (4 or 8 months). To be eligible, you must be enrolled at a partner institution for at least the semester before applying for the exchange, have the equivalent of a 2.5 (C) Grade Point Average, and be nominated by your learning institution. 

The language of instruction at Douglas College is English and students enrolling in academic courses will be expected to meet the college language proficiency requirement. If you are not proficient in English at the academic level, you can take our English Language Learning and Acquisition (ELLA) courses to improve your language skills. To take academic courses students must have a IELTS overall score of at least 6.5 or an overall TOEFL score of at least 83.

If you are not an English speaker, or are not taking your studies in English at your home institution, you should submit a copy of your IELTS or TOEFL scores.

BEFORE YOU APPLY

Your first step is to contact the International Exchange Coordinator at your home institution to determine if you are eligible to apply for an exchange at Douglas College, and to discuss the application process. All incoming exchange students must first be nominated by their home University or college. Only students from partners of Douglas College will be accepted to the Douglas College exchange program. Students from institutions without partnerships with Douglas College may be able to study as fee-paying visiting students. For more information you contact Douglas College Global Engagement.

Next, explore our programs and courses to choose the courses that best fit your existing study program and your educational goals.  Check to see if each course you are choosing has pre-requisites. If it does, make sure you meet the pre-requisites; otherwise you won't be able to take that course. Once you've finalized your course selection and ensured you have the pre-requisites, review your choices with your home institution coordinator to see if the credit from the courses you've chosen transfer to your program.  Students typically study between 12 and 15 credits per semester. 

Once you have determined that Douglas College has the courses appropriate for your studies and have secured the financial resources necessary to participate in an exchange, complete your institution’s exchange application process.

After your home institution approves you for the exchange, you can complete and submit the Douglas College exchange application package per the steps below.

1) Online application questionnaire

2) Upload a copy of your passport photo page

3) Upload a copy of your latest transcript

4) Upoload a copy of your English language certificate

This program is not currently accepting applications.

VISA AND STUDY PERMIT

For stays less than 6 months (1 semester)

Students do not need a study permit to study in Canada for less than 6 months.
Most students will either need an eTA or visa to enter Canada. More information can be found here: Find out if you need a visa to travel to Canada

For stays more than 6 months (2 semesters or more)

Students will need to obtain a Study Permit before arriving in Canada.
Visas and study permits | Douglas College
Once Douglas College approves your application, we will provide you with a Letter of Acceptance which you will use to apply for a study permit if necessary.  
Regarding the designated learning institutions list, Douglas College will appear on the designated learning institutions list after you choose “British Columbia” in the “View list by province or territory drop-down box, and type “Douglas College” in the “Filter items” box.
If you have any questions regarding your study permit application, please reach out to one of our International Advisors.
MEDICAL INSURANCE

For stays less than 6 months (1 semester)

All incoming exchange students must have adequate medical insurance coverage.
Students are responsible for purchasing their insurance before entering Canada.

For stays more than 6 months (2 semesters or more)

Students who will stay for more than 1 semester must register for the government health plan (MSP) in addition to their private insurance.
Medical insurance for international students | Douglas College - PLEASE NOTE - exchange students are NOT covered under "guard.me", and will need to buy private health insurance to cover their waiting period. 
MSP costs CAD $75 per month. More information can be found here Apply for MSP - Province of British Columbia. It is recommended students apply as soon as they arrive.

ACCOMMODATION 

Douglas College is located in a suburb of the Greater Vancouver area. Exchange students have many choices for accommodations. While Douglas College does not have student residences, we do work with First Choice International Placement who offers homestay accommodation to students.  

Living in Vancouver | Douglas College

TRANSPORTATION

Getting around the Vancouver area is easy with our efficient public transportation system, known as TransLink. As part of your exchange, youwill be eligible for the U-Pass, a transit discounted passes for post-secondary students which is loaded on a Compass Card each month.

Your U-Pass provides unlimited access to bus, SeaBus, and SkyTrain services within the Vancouver area. To begin accessing the public transportation system, purchase a Compass Card at any SkyTrain station or one of these retailers and load your U-Pass BC onto it.

Step-by-Step: How to load your U-Pass onto a Compass Card (download PDF)

Exchange students arriving at Vancouver International Airport can easily access a taxi, uber/Lyft or take skytrain / transit.  

COSTS

As an exchange student, you will continue to pay tuition and student fees to your home institution. Douglas College does not charge our incoming exchange students any tuition or student fees.  You will also get your monthly U-Passes (public transit pass) free of charge.  However, you are responsible for covering the costs of your basic medical insurance coverage, textbooks, course materials, food, accommodation and personal spending expenses.

Vancouver is one of the most beautiful, and expensive, cities in the world! It is important that students keep this in mind while saving up or budgeting for their exchange semester. The amount of money you will need varies greatly depending on what you would like to do while you are in Canada. Travelling on the weekends or study breaks can make your semester abroad much more expensive than if you like to stay around your neighborhood or city. Also, if you prefer to eat out you will spend much more than someone who prefers to cook at home. The best person to consult about your budget is always yourself. But, here are some cost estimates to guide your planning.

Monthly rent and utilities (private room in a shared house) ~ $800-$1000
One bedroom or studio apartment ~ $1500- $2400
Dinner out (one person) ~ $25 ($30 with tip) ~ $45 with alcoholic drinks
Basic groceries $100-150 per week
Approximate taxi or Uber ~ $3.25 flate rate + $1.84/km
Student Season Ski Pass (Cypress Mountain) ~ $400

A great place to find more tips and resources for students is on the Douglas Student Union (DSU) website.

Living in Vancouver
Living in Vancouver is a rewarding experience. However, rentals and accommodation can be difficult to secure. There are many options for students, but be sure to go through a reputable housing management company to protect yourself from fraud or mistreatment from landlords.
Douglas College does not endorse any of the companies on the list. It is solely up to students to choose any service that is appropriate for them or meets their needs.
Accommodation and housing
Homestay
Many international students at Douglas College choose to live in homestay for their first few months of living in Canada.
FCI
,
Cypress Accommodations
and
CanBeHome Canada Homestay
will help to place you with a homestay family depending on your interests and individual requirements. Homestay families are all carefully screened and selected to ensure the best possible experience.
Student residences
Global Education City
offers different locations and options for student housing.
Renting your own place
Reputable placement services will help to provide quality housing, management, and placement for students looking to rent your own place. Here are a few reliable companies:
https://www.vancouverrentit.com/
https://www.caprent.com/apartments-for-rent/
Be cautious when searching and remember to view the inside of a property before you sign a lease or pay any money. Ensure you know your rights and responsibilities as a tenant (renter).
To learn more, visit the following websites:
Tenant Resource & Advisory Centre
Tenants Rights - Province of British Columbia
Safety
Crime happens everywhere. Thefts, pick-pocketing and small crimes occur from time to time. For your information, Vancouver Police Department has provided the following website with
tips and helpful information
to stay safe in Vancouver.
Transportation
Getting around the Vancouver area is easy with our efficient public transportation system, known as
TransLink
. As part of your student fees, you have paid for a U-Pass, a transit discounted passes for post-secondary students which is loaded on a Compass Card (the image on the right) each month.
Your U-Pass provides unlimited access to bus, SeaBus, and SkyTrain services within the Vancouver area. To begin accessing the public transportation system, purchase a Compass Card at any SkyTrain station or
one of these retailers
and
load your U-Pass BC
onto it.

Douglas College Overview

Douglas College is a public post-secondary institution located in British Columbia, Canada, known for offering a high-quality education in a welcoming and diverse environment. For exchange students studying for one or two semesters, the college provides an excellent opportunity to experience Canadian academic life while earning credits toward your home institution’s program.

The college has two main campuses in New Westminster and Coquitlam, both easily accessible by public transit and situated within the vibrant Metro Vancouver region. Students will find modern facilities, a friendly atmosphere, and a community that values global perspectives.

Douglas College offers a wide variety of courses across disciplines such as business, humanities, sciences, health, and the arts. Exchange students can select from a broad range of classes to suit their academic goals, with most courses designed to blend theory with practical learning. Many classes include hands-on projects, case studies, or applied assignments that reflect real-world situations, which enrich the academic experience beyond the classroom.

A major benefit of studying at Douglas is its smaller class sizes. With fewer students per class than many larger institutions, exchange students are more likely to receive individualized attention from instructors, participate in discussions, and engage directly in the learning process.

Campus life at Douglas is active and inclusive. Exchange students can take part in student clubs, cultural events, and activities that help them connect with peers and feel part of the community. The college also offers a range of support services, including orientation for new international students, academic advising, and assistance with housing and adapting to life in Canada.

Overall, spending a semester or two at Douglas College gives exchange students the chance to study in a supportive academic environment, experience Canadian culture, and gain valuable international experience — all while enjoying the natural beauty and urban amenities of the surrounding region.

We look forward to welcoming you!

Exchange students are able to take almost all the courses offered at Douglas College as long as they have proper English language proficiency (for English language requirements see the 'application process' tab). Students who do not meet the English language requirements, or fall below the minimum in one or two areas, can register for Douglas College's English Language and Learning Acquisition (ELLA) program.

There are some departments that require special permission for exchange students to take courses. The following areas require special permission from the department in order for exchange students to register.

Contemporary Arts (Music and Visual Arts)
Sports Science

Exchange students cannot take courses in the following departments: 

Applied Community Studies
Health Sciences

In general, not all courses are offered every semester. So, it is a good idea to check what courses will be available during the semester you will be on exchange. You can find Douglas College courses listed online. If the semester you will be on exchange is not available yet, try checking what courses were offered during the same semester the previous year. Upper-level courses (3000-4000 level) are often difficult to register for as there are few course sections and many students that need to take these courses. It is advised that exchange students try tof fulfill any general elective requirements they may need while on exchange.

English Language and Learning Acquisition (ELLA) program

Student who enrol in ELLA courses are still considered exchange students, meaning they do not need to pay Douglas College tuition in addition to their home institution tuition. Exchange students can also combine ELLA courses with academic courses if they meet the English proficiency requirements in some areas but not others. For example, if you meet the minimum IELTS requirements for reading and writing, but not listening and speaking, you may take two academic courses and the two ELLA courses in the areas you need to improve.

Full-time Status

Exchange students are expected to register for and maintain a full-time course schedule during their exchange semester. At Douglas College full-time study means taking 9-15 credits, which is the same a 3-5 classes in most cases. 15 credits is the equivalent of 30 ECTS.

ELIGIBILITY

Students at our partner institutions may apply to study here as an exchange student for one or two semesters (4 or 8 months). To be eligible, you must be enrolled at a partner institution for at least the semester before applying for the exchange, have the equivalent of a 2.5 (C) Grade Point Average, and be nominated by your learning institution. 

The language of instruction at Douglas College is English and students enrolling in academic courses will be expected to meet the college language proficiency requirement. If you are not proficient in English at the academic level, you can take our English Language Learning and Acquisition (ELLA) courses to improve your language skills. To take academic courses students must have a IELTS overall score of at least 6.5 or an overall TOEFL score of at least 83.

If you are not an English speaker, or are not taking your studies in English at your home institution, you should submit a copy of your IELTS or TOEFL scores.

BEFORE YOU APPLY

Your first step is to contact the International Exchange Coordinator at your home institution to determine if you are eligible to apply for an exchange at Douglas College, and to discuss the application process. All incoming exchange students must first be nominated by their home University or college. Only students from partners of Douglas College will be accepted to the Douglas College exchange program. Students from institutions without partnerships with Douglas College may be able to study as fee-paying visiting students. For more information you contact Douglas College Global Engagement.

Next, explore our programs and courses to choose the courses that best fit your existing study program and your educational goals.  Check to see if each course you are choosing has pre-requisites. If it does, make sure you meet the pre-requisites; otherwise you won't be able to take that course. Once you've finalized your course selection and ensured you have the pre-requisites, review your choices with your home institution coordinator to see if the credit from the courses you've chosen transfer to your program.  Students typically study between 12 and 15 credits per semester. 

Once you have determined that Douglas College has the courses appropriate for your studies and have secured the financial resources necessary to participate in an exchange, complete your institution’s exchange application process.

After your home institution approves you for the exchange, you can complete and submit the Douglas College exchange application package per the steps below.

1) Online application questionnaire

2) Upload a copy of your passport photo page

3) Upload a copy of your latest transcript

4) Upoload a copy of your English language certificate

This program is not currently accepting applications.

VISA AND STUDY PERMIT

For stays less than 6 months (1 semester)

Students do not need a study permit to study in Canada for less than 6 months.
Most students will either need an eTA or visa to enter Canada. More information can be found here: Find out if you need a visa to travel to Canada

For stays more than 6 months (2 semesters or more)

Students will need to obtain a Study Permit before arriving in Canada.
Visas and study permits | Douglas College
Once Douglas College approves your application, we will provide you with a Letter of Acceptance which you will use to apply for a study permit if necessary.  
Regarding the designated learning institutions list, Douglas College will appear on the designated learning institutions list after you choose “British Columbia” in the “View list by province or territory drop-down box, and type “Douglas College” in the “Filter items” box.
If you have any questions regarding your study permit application, please reach out to one of our International Advisors.
MEDICAL INSURANCE

For stays less than 6 months (1 semester)

All incoming exchange students must have adequate medical insurance coverage.
Students are responsible for purchasing their insurance before entering Canada.

For stays more than 6 months (2 semesters or more)

Students who will stay for more than 1 semester must register for the government health plan (MSP) in addition to their private insurance.
Medical insurance for international students | Douglas College - PLEASE NOTE - exchange students are NOT covered under "guard.me", and will need to buy private health insurance to cover their waiting period. 
MSP costs CAD $75 per month. More information can be found here Apply for MSP - Province of British Columbia. It is recommended students apply as soon as they arrive.

ACCOMMODATION 

Douglas College is located in a suburb of the Greater Vancouver area. Exchange students have many choices for accommodations. While Douglas College does not have student residences, we do work with First Choice International Placement who offers homestay accommodation to students.  

Living in Vancouver | Douglas College

TRANSPORTATION

Getting around the Vancouver area is easy with our efficient public transportation system, known as TransLink. As part of your exchange, youwill be eligible for the U-Pass, a transit discounted passes for post-secondary students which is loaded on a Compass Card each month.

Your U-Pass provides unlimited access to bus, SeaBus, and SkyTrain services within the Vancouver area. To begin accessing the public transportation system, purchase a Compass Card at any SkyTrain station or one of these retailers and load your U-Pass BC onto it.

Step-by-Step: How to load your U-Pass onto a Compass Card (download PDF)

Exchange students arriving at Vancouver International Airport can easily access a taxi, uber/Lyft or take skytrain / transit.  

COSTS

As an exchange student, you will continue to pay tuition and student fees to your home institution. Douglas College does not charge our incoming exchange students any tuition or student fees.  You will also get your monthly U-Passes (public transit pass) free of charge.  However, you are responsible for covering the costs of your basic medical insurance coverage, textbooks, course materials, food, accommodation and personal spending expenses.

Vancouver is one of the most beautiful, and expensive, cities in the world! It is important that students keep this in mind while saving up or budgeting for their exchange semester. The amount of money you will need varies greatly depending on what you would like to do while you are in Canada. Travelling on the weekends or study breaks can make your semester abroad much more expensive than if you like to stay around your neighborhood or city. Also, if you prefer to eat out you will spend much more than someone who prefers to cook at home. The best person to consult about your budget is always yourself. But, here are some cost estimates to guide your planning.

Monthly rent and utilities (private room in a shared house) ~ $800-$1000
One bedroom or studio apartment ~ $1500- $2400
Dinner out (one person) ~ $25 ($30 with tip) ~ $45 with alcoholic drinks
Basic groceries $100-150 per week
Approximate taxi or Uber ~ $3.25 flate rate + $1.84/km
Student Season Ski Pass (Cypress Mountain) ~ $400

A great place to find more tips and resources for students is on the Douglas Student Union (DSU) website.

Medical insurance for international students
All international students have a variety of medical coverages depending on your date of arrival, length of stay, and current coverage. Most students who arrive in Canada for their first semester of study will be automatically enrolled in a temporary policy (Guard Me) for 3 months while waiting for BC MSP to begin.
Types of medical insurance
BC Medical Services Plan (mandatory government insurance)
All international students studying for more than 6 months in BC are required to have basic medical coverage. This medical coverage is issued through the government of British Columbia and is called the
Medical Services Plan (MSP)
.
MSP covers the cost of any medically required service provided by a physician enrolled with MSP. There is a monthly fee for this coverage and it is billed to you directly by the government. The total cost of MSP is $75 per month, per student. You can
apply for MSP coverage online or by mail
. You will be required to submit a scan of your study permit for the MSP application.
For students under Maintained Status (previously called Implied Status), please visit
Visas and Study Permits
page for more information.
If you plan to leave Canada for more than 6 months, you may need to reapply for MSP on return.
Click here
for more information regarding leaving BC.
Guard Me (temporary medical insurance)
First semester international students at Douglas College are charged $148.50 for private basic medical insurance coverage provided by Guard Me during the 90 day mandatory BC Medical Services Plan wait period.
This coverage starts on their first day of class.
Coverage for the Fall 2026 semester begins on September 8, 2026 and will end on December 6, 2026
. Additional coverage may be purchased for early arrivals or family members.
Guard Me temporary medical insurance for Douglas College students
Guard Me medical insurance cards
New international students will receive their digital insurance cards after the add/drop date of each semester. Don't worry, new international students are covered starting the first day of the semester or the day you purchase Guard Me medical insurance if you arrive early before the semester begins.
If you require your policy in advance due to falling ill or as a requirement to purchase insurance for dependents, please contact us at
dci@douglascollege.ca
.
Opting Out of Guard Me
If you already have valid coverage through BC Medical Services Plan (MSP), you may be eligible to
opt out of Guard.Me
health insurance plan.
The opt out period for the Fall 2026 semester will be September 22 - October 21, 2026.
DSU Health & Dental Plan (extended health insurance)
This extended coverage plan covers things that are not covered by the MSP, such as ambulance fee, vision care, dental care and prescription drugs. Students registered in 6 credits or more in a Fall semester are automatically enrolled in the Student Health and Dental plan for $276.95 per year, charged as part of the tuition fees. The insurance period begins on September 1 and ends on August 31 of the following year.
If you start your studies in a Winter semester, you can opt-in to the coverage during the last two weeks of January.
For more details about this insurance plan and what it covers, visit the
DSU website.
Accessing medical services
Seeking medical support in a new country can be challenging. Generally, international students go to either a walk-in clinic or a hospital (Emergency Room) when they require a medical attention. See the chart below to find out when you should go to a clinic or a hospital.
Bring your
MSP card or Private Insurance Card
. If you have a private insurance, you may need to pay any fees in advance and submit a claim for reimbursement. If you do not have a medical insurance coverage, you will be required to pay for medical services in FULL out of pocket.
Walk-in Clinics
You should visit a clinic if you need to see a doctor, but the situation is not urgent or does not require immediate attention.
Examples:
Colds and flus
Minor injuries (cuts, sprains etc.)
Routine check-up
Most clinics are by walk-in basis and do not require an appointment. It is on a first come, first serve basis.
Find a Clinic
near you
Hospital Emergency Room
For immediate medical attention, go to the Emergency Room at a hospital.
The closest hospital to Douglas College New Westminster Campus is:
Royal Columbian Hospital
330 E Columbia St
New Westminster, BC V3L 3W7
Phone: 604-520-4253
The closest hospital to Douglas College David Lam Campus is:
Eagle Ridge Hospital
475 Guildford Way
Port Moody, BC V3H 3W9
Tel: 604-461-2022
Babylon by Telus Health (online appointments)
Babylon by TELUS Health lets you see a doctor*, mental health counsellor or dietitian from your phone, where and when it’s convenient for you.
*Doctor consultations for BC residents are covered under the Medical Services Plan (MSP).
https://www.telus.com/en/health/personal/babylon
TELUS Health MyCare App
Talk to a Doctor
Book a video-appointment with a Family Doctor or Mental Health Counsellor, even on evenings and weekends.
Get a prescription or referral
After your consultation, get prescriptions and referrals for diagnostic tests or specialists as needed, directly through the app.
Check your symptoms
Powered by Artificial Intelligence, our Symptom Checker asks you questions about your symptoms to suggest possible courses of action.
Digitally monitor your health
With the Healthcheck and Monitor features, get practical insights about your physical and mental health to make positive lifestyle changes.
mobileDOCTOR by Guard.me (online appointment)
mobileDOCTOR by guard.me
allows you to connect with Canadian doctors on Maple, a telemedicine company, as a part of your health benefits. Maple provides access to doctors, Canada wide, on your phone, tablet or computer anytime, anywhere.
Seeing a doctor on Maple is safe and reliable, and can help prevent the need to go to a walk-in clinic or Emergency Room.
When outside of Canada the mobileDOCTOR service connecting you to a Canadian doctor in real time remains available 24/7 for advice purposes only.
HealthLink BC | (Call 8-1-1)
8-1-1
is a free-of-charge provincial health information and advice phone line available in British Columbia. The
8-1-1
phone line is operated by HealthLink BC, which is part of the Ministry of Health. By calling
8-1-1
, you can speak to a health service navigator, who can help you find health information and services; or connect you directly with a registered nurse, a registered dietitian, a qualified exercise professional, or a pharmacist. Any one of these healthcare professionals will help you get the information you need to manage your health concerns, or those of your family.
HealthLink BC 8-1-1
BC Services Card app
Use this app to prove who you are when you log in to
online services
. The BC Services Card app is available for Android™ and iOS (iPhone® and iPad®).
BC Services Card Login
Find a Canadian Clinic (guard.me)
https://www.guard.me/douglascollege/clinicSearch/
New to Canada?
Be sure to apply for MSP as soon as you arrive. This is mandatory for all BC residents and students staying longer than 6 months. Note: there is a 3 months processing time. Please see 'Guard Me (temporary medical insurance)'.

Last updated on July 7, 2026
You can apply for MSP online, in person or by mail. Use the option that works best for you.
On this page
Why you need to enrol in MSP

I need help
Why you need to enrol in MSP
All people residing in B.C. must enrol in the Medical Services Plan (MSP).
This makes sure you can access provincial health care benefits like visits to a doctor.
New residents or persons re-establishing residence in B.C. may be eligible for coverage after
completing a wait period
that consists of the balance of the month in which residence is established, plus two months.
Expand All
|
Collapse All
New to Canada
Apply as soon as you arrive. Your coverage may start three months after your arrival date in British Columbia. You should get private health care insurance while you wait.
Moving to B.C. from another province
You should arrange for coverage with your former medical plan during the wait period. If your family is not here yet, they need to keep their existing provincial health care. Once they arrive, you can apply to add them to your plan. The wait period for each family member will begin on their individual arrival date.
Arriving from Ukraine
The 3-month wait period for MSP coverage is waived for returning Canadians, permanent residents and people arriving in Canada through CUEAT.
My coverage will be under a employer, pension plan or union group plan
Contact your group administrator for more information on applying.
Coverage is always dependent on residency
If you leave B.C. within 6 months of enrolling for MSP, you may have to repay your medical expenses.
How to apply
Apply online
Applying online is the easiest and fastest way to enrol. Before you start, make sure:
Use the latest version of Firefox, Chrome or Safari.
You have
identification
for everyone on your application. You will be asked to upload digital images of documents that support the name and Canadian citizenship or immigration status for all persons
You have your marriage certificate, divorce decree or legal name change certificate if your current legal name doesn’t match the name on your ID
Apply for MSP
It takes about 15 minutes to complete.
Apply by mail
Apply by mail using a paper application form.
Application for Enrolment, HLTH 101 (PDF, 1.4MB)
Mail the completed application form to:
Health Insurance BC
Medical Services Plan

Douglas College Overview

Douglas College is a public post-secondary institution located in British Columbia, Canada, known for offering a high-quality education in a welcoming and diverse environment. For exchange students studying for one or two semesters, the college provides an excellent opportunity to experience Canadian academic life while earning credits toward your home institution’s program.

The college has two main campuses in New Westminster and Coquitlam, both easily accessible by public transit and situated within the vibrant Metro Vancouver region. Students will find modern facilities, a friendly atmosphere, and a community that values global perspectives.

Douglas College offers a wide variety of courses across disciplines such as business, humanities, sciences, health, and the arts. Exchange students can select from a broad range of classes to suit their academic goals, with most courses designed to blend theory with practical learning. Many classes include hands-on projects, case studies, or applied assignments that reflect real-world situations, which enrich the academic experience beyond the classroom.

A major benefit of studying at Douglas is its smaller class sizes. With fewer students per class than many larger institutions, exchange students are more likely to receive individualized attention from instructors, participate in discussions, and engage directly in the learning process.

Campus life at Douglas is active and inclusive. Exchange students can take part in student clubs, cultural events, and activities that help them connect with peers and feel part of the community. The college also offers a range of support services, including orientation for new international students, academic advising, and assistance with housing and adapting to life in Canada.

Overall, spending a semester or two at Douglas College gives exchange students the chance to study in a supportive academic environment, experience Canadian culture, and gain valuable international experience — all while enjoying the natural beauty and urban amenities of the surrounding region.

We look forward to welcoming you!

Exchange students are able to take almost all the courses offered at Douglas College as long as they have proper English language proficiency (for English language requirements see the 'application process' tab). Students who do not meet the English language requirements, or fall below the minimum in one or two areas, can register for Douglas College's English Language and Learning Acquisition (ELLA) program.

There are some departments that require special permission for exchange students to take courses. The following areas require special permission from the department in order for exchange students to register.

Contemporary Arts (Music and Visual Arts)
Sports Science

Exchange students cannot take courses in the following departments: 

Applied Community Studies
Health Sciences

In general, not all courses are offered every semester. So, it is a good idea to check what courses will be available during the semester you will be on exchange. You can find Douglas College courses listed online. If the semester you will be on exchange is not available yet, try checking what courses were offered during the same semester the previous year. Upper-level courses (3000-4000 level) are often difficult to register for as there are few course sections and many students that need to take these courses. It is advised that exchange students try tof fulfill any general elective requirements they may need while on exchange.

English Language and Learning Acquisition (ELLA) program

Student who enrol in ELLA courses are still considered exchange students, meaning they do not need to pay Douglas College tuition in addition to their home institution tuition. Exchange students can also combine ELLA courses with academic courses if they meet the English proficiency requirements in some areas but not others. For example, if you meet the minimum IELTS requirements for reading and writing, but not listening and speaking, you may take two academic courses and the two ELLA courses in the areas you need to improve.

Full-time Status

Exchange students are expected to register for and maintain a full-time course schedule during their exchange semester. At Douglas College full-time study means taking 9-15 credits, which is the same a 3-5 classes in most cases. 15 credits is the equivalent of 30 ECTS.

ELIGIBILITY

Students at our partner institutions may apply to study here as an exchange student for one or two semesters (4 or 8 months). To be eligible, you must be enrolled at a partner institution for at least the semester before applying for the exchange, have the equivalent of a 2.5 (C) Grade Point Average, and be nominated by your learning institution. 

The language of instruction at Douglas College is English and students enrolling in academic courses will be expected to meet the college language proficiency requirement. If you are not proficient in English at the academic level, you can take our English Language Learning and Acquisition (ELLA) courses to improve your language skills. To take academic courses students must have a IELTS overall score of at least 6.5 or an overall TOEFL score of at least 83.

If you are not an English speaker, or are not taking your studies in English at your home institution, you should submit a copy of your IELTS or TOEFL scores.

BEFORE YOU APPLY

Your first step is to contact the International Exchange Coordinator at your home institution to determine if you are eligible to apply for an exchange at Douglas College, and to discuss the application process. All incoming exchange students must first be nominated by their home University or college. Only students from partners of Douglas College will be accepted to the Douglas College exchange program. Students from institutions without partnerships with Douglas College may be able to study as fee-paying visiting students. For more information you contact Douglas College Global Engagement.

Next, explore our programs and courses to choose the courses that best fit your existing study program and your educational goals.  Check to see if each course you are choosing has pre-requisites. If it does, make sure you meet the pre-requisites; otherwise you won't be able to take that course. Once you've finalized your course selection and ensured you have the pre-requisites, review your choices with your home institution coordinator to see if the credit from the courses you've chosen transfer to your program.  Students typically study between 12 and 15 credits per semester. 

Once you have determined that Douglas College has the courses appropriate for your studies and have secured the financial resources necessary to participate in an exchange, complete your institution’s exchange application process.

After your home institution approves you for the exchange, you can complete and submit the Douglas College exchange application package per the steps below.

1) Online application questionnaire

2) Upload a copy of your passport photo page

3) Upload a copy of your latest transcript

4) Upoload a copy of your English language certificate

This program is not currently accepting applications.

VISA AND STUDY PERMIT

For stays less than 6 months (1 semester)

Students do not need a study permit to study in Canada for less than 6 months.
Most students will either need an eTA or visa to enter Canada. More information can be found here: Find out if you need a visa to travel to Canada

For stays more than 6 months (2 semesters or more)

Students will need to obtain a Study Permit before arriving in Canada.
Visas and study permits | Douglas College
Once Douglas College approves your application, we will provide you with a Letter of Acceptance which you will use to apply for a study permit if necessary.  
Regarding the designated learning institutions list, Douglas College will appear on the designated learning institutions list after you choose “British Columbia” in the “View list by province or territory drop-down box, and type “Douglas College” in the “Filter items” box.
If you have any questions regarding your study permit application, please reach out to one of our International Advisors.
MEDICAL INSURANCE

For stays less than 6 months (1 semester)

All incoming exchange students must have adequate medical insurance coverage.
Students are responsible for purchasing their insurance before entering Canada.

For stays more than 6 months (2 semesters or more)

Students who will stay for more than 1 semester must register for the government health plan (MSP) in addition to their private insurance.
Medical insurance for international students | Douglas College - PLEASE NOTE - exchange students are NOT covered under "guard.me", and will need to buy private health insurance to cover their waiting period. 
MSP costs CAD $75 per month. More information can be found here Apply for MSP - Province of British Columbia. It is recommended students apply as soon as they arrive.

ACCOMMODATION 

Douglas College is located in a suburb of the Greater Vancouver area. Exchange students have many choices for accommodations. While Douglas College does not have student residences, we do work with First Choice International Placement who offers homestay accommodation to students.  

Living in Vancouver | Douglas College

TRANSPORTATION

Getting around the Vancouver area is easy with our efficient public transportation system, known as TransLink. As part of your exchange, youwill be eligible for the U-Pass, a transit discounted passes for post-secondary students which is loaded on a Compass Card each month.

Your U-Pass provides unlimited access to bus, SeaBus, and SkyTrain services within the Vancouver area. To begin accessing the public transportation system, purchase a Compass Card at any SkyTrain station or one of these retailers and load your U-Pass BC onto it.

Step-by-Step: How to load your U-Pass onto a Compass Card (download PDF)

Exchange students arriving at Vancouver International Airport can easily access a taxi, uber/Lyft or take skytrain / transit.  

COSTS

As an exchange student, you will continue to pay tuition and student fees to your home institution. Douglas College does not charge our incoming exchange students any tuition or student fees.  You will also get your monthly U-Passes (public transit pass) free of charge.  However, you are responsible for covering the costs of your basic medical insurance coverage, textbooks, course materials, food, accommodation and personal spending expenses.

Vancouver is one of the most beautiful, and expensive, cities in the world! It is important that students keep this in mind while saving up or budgeting for their exchange semester. The amount of money you will need varies greatly depending on what you would like to do while you are in Canada. Travelling on the weekends or study breaks can make your semester abroad much more expensive than if you like to stay around your neighborhood or city. Also, if you prefer to eat out you will spend much more than someone who prefers to cook at home. The best person to consult about your budget is always yourself. But, here are some cost estimates to guide your planning.

Monthly rent and utilities (private room in a shared house) ~ $800-$1000
One bedroom or studio apartment ~ $1500- $2400
Dinner out (one person) ~ $25 ($30 with tip) ~ $45 with alcoholic drinks
Basic groceries $100-150 per week
Approximate taxi or Uber ~ $3.25 flate rate + $1.84/km
Student Season Ski Pass (Cypress Mountain) ~ $400

A great place to find more tips and resources for students is on the Douglas Student Union (DSU) website.

Getting and submitting your PAL/TAL
Find out how to get your PAL/TAL and when you should submit it.
Who issues my PAL/TAL?
The province or territory where you plan to study issues your PAL/TAL. It confirms that you’ve been assigned one of the available spaces to study in that province or territory.
How do I apply for a PAL/TAL?
You should contact your school (DLI) to find out how to apply for a PAL/TAL. Once you have one, you can apply for a study permit.

Douglas College Overview

Douglas College is a public post-secondary institution located in British Columbia, Canada, known for offering a high-quality education in a welcoming and diverse environment. For exchange students studying for one or two semesters, the college provides an excellent opportunity to experience Canadian academic life while earning credits toward your home institution’s program.

The college has two main campuses in New Westminster and Coquitlam, both easily accessible by public transit and situated within the vibrant Metro Vancouver region. Students will find modern facilities, a friendly atmosphere, and a community that values global perspectives.

Douglas College offers a wide variety of courses across disciplines such as business, humanities, sciences, health, and the arts. Exchange students can select from a broad range of classes to suit their academic goals, with most courses designed to blend theory with practical learning. Many classes include hands-on projects, case studies, or applied assignments that reflect real-world situations, which enrich the academic experience beyond the classroom.

A major benefit of studying at Douglas is its smaller class sizes. With fewer students per class than many larger institutions, exchange students are more likely to receive individualized attention from instructors, participate in discussions, and engage directly in the learning process.

Campus life at Douglas is active and inclusive. Exchange students can take part in student clubs, cultural events, and activities that help them connect with peers and feel part of the community. The college also offers a range of support services, including orientation for new international students, academic advising, and assistance with housing and adapting to life in Canada.

Overall, spending a semester or two at Douglas College gives exchange students the chance to study in a supportive academic environment, experience Canadian culture, and gain valuable international experience — all while enjoying the natural beauty and urban amenities of the surrounding region.

We look forward to welcoming you!

Exchange students are able to take almost all the courses offered at Douglas College as long as they have proper English language proficiency (for English language requirements see the 'application process' tab). Students who do not meet the English language requirements, or fall below the minimum in one or two areas, can register for Douglas College's English Language and Learning Acquisition (ELLA) program.

There are some departments that require special permission for exchange students to take courses. The following areas require special permission from the department in order for exchange students to register.

Contemporary Arts (Music and Visual Arts)
Sports Science

Exchange students cannot take courses in the following departments: 

Applied Community Studies
Health Sciences

In general, not all courses are offered every semester. So, it is a good idea to check what courses will be available during the semester you will be on exchange. You can find Douglas College courses listed online. If the semester you will be on exchange is not available yet, try checking what courses were offered during the same semester the previous year. Upper-level courses (3000-4000 level) are often difficult to register for as there are few course sections and many students that need to take these courses. It is advised that exchange students try tof fulfill any general elective requirements they may need while on exchange.

English Language and Learning Acquisition (ELLA) program

Student who enrol in ELLA courses are still considered exchange students, meaning they do not need to pay Douglas College tuition in addition to their home institution tuition. Exchange students can also combine ELLA courses with academic courses if they meet the English proficiency requirements in some areas but not others. For example, if you meet the minimum IELTS requirements for reading and writing, but not listening and speaking, you may take two academic courses and the two ELLA courses in the areas you need to improve.

Full-time Status

Exchange students are expected to register for and maintain a full-time course schedule during their exchange semester. At Douglas College full-time study means taking 9-15 credits, which is the same a 3-5 classes in most cases. 15 credits is the equivalent of 30 ECTS.

ELIGIBILITY

Students at our partner institutions may apply to study here as an exchange student for one or two semesters (4 or 8 months). To be eligible, you must be enrolled at a partner institution for at least the semester before applying for the exchange, have the equivalent of a 2.5 (C) Grade Point Average, and be nominated by your learning institution. 

The language of instruction at Douglas College is English and students enrolling in academic courses will be expected to meet the college language proficiency requirement. If you are not proficient in English at the academic level, you can take our English Language Learning and Acquisition (ELLA) courses to improve your language skills. To take academic courses students must have a IELTS overall score of at least 6.5 or an overall TOEFL score of at least 83.

If you are not an English speaker, or are not taking your studies in English at your home institution, you should submit a copy of your IELTS or TOEFL scores.

BEFORE YOU APPLY

Your first step is to contact the International Exchange Coordinator at your home institution to determine if you are eligible to apply for an exchange at Douglas College, and to discuss the application process. All incoming exchange students must first be nominated by their home University or college. Only students from partners of Douglas College will be accepted to the Douglas College exchange program. Students from institutions without partnerships with Douglas College may be able to study as fee-paying visiting students. For more information you contact Douglas College Global Engagement.

Next, explore our programs and courses to choose the courses that best fit your existing study program and your educational goals.  Check to see if each course you are choosing has pre-requisites. If it does, make sure you meet the pre-requisites; otherwise you won't be able to take that course. Once you've finalized your course selection and ensured you have the pre-requisites, review your choices with your home institution coordinator to see if the credit from the courses you've chosen transfer to your program.  Students typically study between 12 and 15 credits per semester. 

Once you have determined that Douglas College has the courses appropriate for your studies and have secured the financial resources necessary to participate in an exchange, complete your institution’s exchange application process.

After your home institution approves you for the exchange, you can complete and submit the Douglas College exchange application package per the steps below.

1) Online application questionnaire

2) Upload a copy of your passport photo page

3) Upload a copy of your latest transcript

4) Upoload a copy of your English language certificate

This program is not currently accepting applications.

VISA AND STUDY PERMIT

For stays less than 6 months (1 semester)

Students do not need a study permit to study in Canada for less than 6 months.
Most students will either need an eTA or visa to enter Canada. More information can be found here: Find out if you need a visa to travel to Canada

For stays more than 6 months (2 semesters or more)

Students will need to obtain a Study Permit before arriving in Canada.
Visas and study permits | Douglas College
Once Douglas College approves your application, we will provide you with a Letter of Acceptance which you will use to apply for a study permit if necessary.  
Regarding the designated learning institutions list, Douglas College will appear on the designated learning institutions list after you choose “British Columbia” in the “View list by province or territory drop-down box, and type “Douglas College” in the “Filter items” box.
If you have any questions regarding your study permit application, please reach out to one of our International Advisors.
MEDICAL INSURANCE

For stays less than 6 months (1 semester)

All incoming exchange students must have adequate medical insurance coverage.
Students are responsible for purchasing their insurance before entering Canada.

For stays more than 6 months (2 semesters or more)

Students who will stay for more than 1 semester must register for the government health plan (MSP) in addition to their private insurance.
Medical insurance for international students | Douglas College - PLEASE NOTE - exchange students are NOT covered under "guard.me", and will need to buy private health insurance to cover their waiting period. 
MSP costs CAD $75 per month. More information can be found here Apply for MSP - Province of British Columbia. It is recommended students apply as soon as they arrive.

ACCOMMODATION 

Douglas College is located in a suburb of the Greater Vancouver area. Exchange students have many choices for accommodations. While Douglas College does not have student residences, we do work with First Choice International Placement who offers homestay accommodation to students.  

Living in Vancouver | Douglas College

TRANSPORTATION

Getting around the Vancouver area is easy with our efficient public transportation system, known as TransLink. As part of your exchange, youwill be eligible for the U-Pass, a transit discounted passes for post-secondary students which is loaded on a Compass Card each month.

Your U-Pass provides unlimited access to bus, SeaBus, and SkyTrain services within the Vancouver area. To begin accessing the public transportation system, purchase a Compass Card at any SkyTrain station or one of these retailers and load your U-Pass BC onto it.

Step-by-Step: How to load your U-Pass onto a Compass Card (download PDF)

Exchange students arriving at Vancouver International Airport can easily access a taxi, uber/Lyft or take skytrain / transit.  

COSTS

As an exchange student, you will continue to pay tuition and student fees to your home institution. Douglas College does not charge our incoming exchange students any tuition or student fees.  You will also get your monthly U-Passes (public transit pass) free of charge.  However, you are responsible for covering the costs of your basic medical insurance coverage, textbooks, course materials, food, accommodation and personal spending expenses.

Vancouver is one of the most beautiful, and expensive, cities in the world! It is important that students keep this in mind while saving up or budgeting for their exchange semester. The amount of money you will need varies greatly depending on what you would like to do while you are in Canada. Travelling on the weekends or study breaks can make your semester abroad much more expensive than if you like to stay around your neighborhood or city. Also, if you prefer to eat out you will spend much more than someone who prefers to cook at home. The best person to consult about your budget is always yourself. But, here are some cost estimates to guide your planning.

Monthly rent and utilities (private room in a shared house) ~ $800-$1000
One bedroom or studio apartment ~ $1500- $2400
Dinner out (one person) ~ $25 ($30 with tip) ~ $45 with alcoholic drinks
Basic groceries $100-150 per week
Approximate taxi or Uber ~ $3.25 flate rate + $1.84/km
Student Season Ski Pass (Cypress Mountain) ~ $400

A great place to find more tips and resources for students is on the Douglas Student Union (DSU) website.

Why you should choose University of Manitoba
Located on original lands of Anishinaabeg, Cree, Oji-Cree, Dakota, and Dene peoples, and on the homeland of the Métis Nation, Manitoba is known for its pristine nature, beautiful landscape, vibrant culture and friendly people. With two main campuses in Winnipeg and over 100 programs, the University of Manitoba offers a chance to learn and explore in a unique and supportive environment.
Member of Canada's
U15
and is Manitoba’s research-intensive (medical-doctoral) university.
More than
31,000
students at two main campuses and satellite campuses throughout the province
More than
6000
international students from over 122 countries around the world
Nearly
3000
First Nations, Metis and Inuit students
Discover UM
The University of Manitoba is the oldest university in Western Canada and one of the country’s top research institutions. We have more than 29,000 undergraduate and graduate students, and more than 145,000 alumni living in 140 countries.
Historic buildings have defined our campuses for more than a century, while modern facilities enrich learning experiences and provide opportunities for research and discovery.
Cradled in a box of the Red River, the Fort Garry campus is home to over 90 major buildings with a range of state-of-the-art facilities
Host to the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation (NCTR) – a place where Survivors, scholars and the public can explore the legacy of Canada’s residential school system through an extensive collection of sacred materials that help foster healing and understanding.
Your future starts here!
Explore our campus through the 360° Campus Tour
Discover key locations on campus right from your own device.
Take the 360° Campus Tour
Winnipeg and Manitoba Tourism
Winnipeg is the capital city of Manitoba, located in the centre of Canada. Home to a diverse population of more than 850,000 people, the city and metropolitan area is a vibrant hub of industry and culture.
Living and learning in Winnipeg
With international students from over 120 different countries, UM is part Winnipeg’s unique and diverse cultural community.
Living in Winnipeg provides opportunities to experience Canada’s great outdoors with unique activities in all four seasons.
Located in the heart of Canada, the province of Manitoba is known for its pristine nature, beautiful landscape, vibrant culture and friendly people.
Events like UM Bisons games are a fun and exciting way to get involved and feel the energy on campus.

Health and Wellness
Student health and mental well-being are very important. Visit our health and wellness page for the resources and supports available for all students, including exchange students.
IC Exchange Buddy Program
The IC Exchange Buddy Program connects exchange students with UM students who have previously completed an outbound exchange through the IC. This program is an opportunity to build meaningful connections and support the transition and integration into life in Winnipeg.

The University of Manitoba is the oldest university in Western Canada and one of the country’s top research institutions. We have more than 29,000 undergraduate and graduate students, and more than 145,000 alumni living in 140 countries.
Historic buildings have defined our campuses for more than a century, while modern facilities enrich learning experiences and provide opportunities for research and discovery.
Cradled in a box of the Red River, the Fort Garry campus is home to over 90 major buildings with a range of state-of-the-art facilities
Host to the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation (NCTR) – a place where Survivors, scholars and the public can explore the legacy of Canada’s residential school system through an extensive collection of sacred materials that help foster healing and understanding.
Your future starts here!
Explore our campus through the 360° Campus Tour

Winnipeg and Manitoba Tourism
Winnipeg is the capital city of Manitoba, located in the centre of Canada. Home to a diverse population of more than 850,000 people, the city and metropolitan area is a vibrant hub of industry and culture.
Living and learning in Winnipeg
With international students from over 120 different countries, UM is part Winnipeg’s unique and diverse cultural community.
Living in Winnipeg provides opportunities to experience Canada’s great outdoors with unique activities in all four seasons.
Located in the heart of Canada, the province of Manitoba is known for its pristine nature, beautiful landscape, vibrant culture and friendly people.
Events like UM Bisons games are a fun and exciting way to get involved and feel the energy on campus.
