FAQ
Q1
What are the reasons for starting pre-entry TB screening?
A
In recent years, the number of foreign-born TB cases has been increasing in Japan.  In 2025, 23.8% of the newly notified TB cases were foreign-born.
In addition, several countries other than Japan have introduced TB screening for foreign nationals as a TB control measure for those entering the country. In view of the situation of TB cases in Japan, Pre-Entry TB screening will be introduced to nationals of countries with a particularly large number of TB cases in Japan, and who intend to enter Japan and stay for a medium- to long-term period, to ensure that they do not have active TB before traveling to Japan.
Q2
Which are the countries and people subject to pre-entry TB screening?
A
Countries subject to screening shall be countries with a large proportion of foreign-born cases diagnosed with TB during their stay in Japan (the Philippines, Viet Nam, Indonesia, Nepal, Myanmar, and China (hereafter collectively referred to as the “target countries”)). As for the people subject to screening, they shall be nationals of target countries who intend to enter and stay in Japan as mid- to long-term residents (*) (excluding re-entry permits holders) or under the provisions of Notifications No. 53 (Digital Nomad) or No. 54 (Spouse or Child of Digital Nomad) on Designated Activities.
However, if the residence permit or other documentation issued by the government of the applicant’s place of residence confirms that their current place of residence is outside the target countries or region, the applicant will be exempted from the TB screening.
JET Programme participants, JICA trainees (both long-term and short-term ),  international students of JICA’s Project for Human Resource Development Scholarship (JDS), participants to the long-term and mid-term invitation programs of Japan Foundation, Japanese Government Scholarship students with an embassy recommendation, foreign students who enter Japan under commissioned education and training programs, nurses and care workers accepted under Economic Partnership Agreements (EPAs) with applicable countries, specified skilled workers, foreign nationals who enter Japan under the provision of Notification No. 55 (specified motor vehicle transportation business preparation) on Designated Activities, and foreign nationals who enter Japan under the Project to Accept Foreigners Conducting Housekeeping Services in National Strategic Special Zones (pursuant to the Act on National Strategic Special Zones, Article 16-4) will be temporarily exempted from screening.
(*) “Mid- to long-term residents” refers to individuals specified in Article 19-3 of the Immigration Control and Refugee Recognition Act (foreign nationals who are residing in Japan with a status of residence, excluding those who fall into one of the following categories: (1) a person who has been granted a period of stay of not exceeding three months; (2) a person who has been granted the status of residence “Temporary Visitor”; (3) a person who has been granted the status of residence of “Diplomat” or “Official”; and (4) a person prescribed by Ministry of Justice Order as being equivalent to a person mentioned in (1) through (3)).
Q3
What is the screening process?
A
Applicants will undergo a medical examination and chest X-ray (or sputum test at the doctor’s discretion if there are concerns) at designated medical facility (hereafter referred as Panel Clinic) located in the target countries for screening (see below).
TB Clearance Certificate will be issued by the Panel Clinic when the applicant does not have active tuberculosis
Applicants will be required to submit the TB Clearance Certificate when applying for a Certificate of Eligibility (or when applying for a visa at a Japanese diplomatic mission abroad in cases where they apply for a visa without obtaining a Certificate of Eligibility).
* People who are diagnosed with active TB must undergo another TB examination at a Panel Clinic after completing treatment.
Q4
What is the legal grounds for JPETS?
A
Tuberculosis is defined as a Class II infectious disease under Article 6, paragraph (3), item (ii) of the Act on the Prevention of Infectious Diseases and Medical Care for Patients with Infectious Diseases (Act No. 114 of 1998).
Article 5, paragraph (1), item (i) of the Immigration Control and Refugee Recognition Act (Cabinet Order No. 319 of 1951; hereinafter, "Immigration Control Act") stipulates that suffering from a Class II infectious disease constitutes grounds for being denied entry into Japan. In principle, foreign nationals who have active TB do not meet the conditions for landing in Japan set forth under Article 7, paragraph (1), item (i) of the Immigration Control Act and will thus not be admitted entry into Japan.
In addition, based on the provisions of Article 7-2 of the Immigration Control Act, the examination process of the Application for the Certificate of Eligibility requires verification that the individual has conformed to the entry conditions set forth under Article 7, paragraph (1), item (ii) of the same Act.
Moreover, based on the provisions of Article 6-2, paragraph (5) of the Regulation for Enforcement of the Immigration Control Act, authorities may refuse to issue the Certificate of Eligibility when the applicant evidently does not conform to the conditions set forth in Article 7, paragraph (1), items (i), (iii) or (iv) of the Immigration Control Act.
Thus, in the application process for Certificate of Eligibility, Immigration Services Agency shall require the TB Clearance Certificate as a means of confirming that he/she satisfies the entry conditions set forth under Article 7, paragraph (1), item (ii) of the Immigration Control Act.
In the visa application process, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (and its diplomatic missions abroad), based upon the Criteria of Visa Issuance, shall require the TB Clearance Certificate from the applicant to confirm that the applicant does not fall under any of the items of Article 5, paragraph (1) of the Immigration Control Act.
Q5
What is a Panel Clinic?
A
Panel Clinics are medical facilities designated by the Japanese government to ensure the quality of pre-entry TB screening. Japanese diplomatic missions in target countries recommend local medical facilities that meet the requirements set by the Japanese government, and the Centre for Japan-Pre-entry TB Screening Quality Assessment, commissioned by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) of Japan, inspects these facilities. The facilities that meet the criteria are designated as Panel Clinics by the Japanese government.
Q6
When will the screening commence?
A
The screening will commence gradually starting with target countries for which coordination has been completed.
As of September 25 2026, the dates for the start of reception for medical examination at Panel Clinics and introduction of the mandatory requirement for submission of the TB Clearance Certificate when applying for a Certificate of Eligibility or a visa are outlined below.

Can the “chest X-ray examination” required for the Pre-Entry Tuberculosis (TB) Screening Program and the “health status assessment” required under the Employment for Skill Development Program be undertaken at the same time?
A
JPETS is intended to confirm, prior to entry into Japan, that the applicant does not have active tuberculosis, thereby contributing to infectious disease control measures. This purpose differs from the health condition verification required when applying for approval of an Employment for Skill Development Plan under the Employment for Skill Development Program, and the respective requirements are also different.
However, because the results of a chest X-ray examination conducted by a Panel Clinic may be regarded as satisfying the chest X-ray examination requirement within the comprehensive medical examination required for the acceptance of foreign nationals under the Employment for Skill Development Program, some applicants may wish to undergo both JPETS and the comprehensive medical examination simultaneously at a Panel Clinic.
For information on designated panel clinics where both examinations may be undertaken concurrently, please refer to the list below.

Notification to mid- to long-term residents in Japan
Mid- to long-term residents in Japan who originate from or have stayed in countries on the
World Health Organization’s list of high TB burden countries
, or who have been identified as being at risk of developing TB during their pre-entry TB screening, should seek medical examination in a medical facility if they have any TB symptoms (cough, sputum expectoration, mild fever, or body lethargy lasting more than two weeks). Those who are eligible for medical examinations provided by schools, workplaces, or local governments, should strive to undergo regular medical examinations.
If you develop TB in Japan, make sure you get the treatment you need. The public health center in your area of residence handles procedures related to provision of public funds to partially cover medical expenses involved in treating TB and provides assistance with taking medication.

Enroll in Pension System
All residents of Japan between age 20 and 59, regardless of nationality, must be covered by National Pension by law. There are three types of insured persons of National Pension according to their status as follows:
Category Ⅰ insured persons (self-employed persons, students, agricultural, forestry and fishery workers, unemployed persons)
Category Ⅱ insured persons (company workers and public sector workers)
Category Ⅲ insured persons (economically-dependent spouses of category Ⅱ insured persons)
Category Ⅰ Insured Persons
All residents of Japan between age 20 and 59 who are not Category Ⅱ or Ⅲ insured persons (e.g. self-employed persons, students, agricultural, forestry and fishery workers, unemployed persons.)
When you become subject to Category Ⅰ insured person, you need to submit, by yourself, application to enroll in as Category I insured person to the municipal office of your place of residence within 14 days.
Enrollment in National Pension
Note:Foreign nationals with specific visa (i.e. medical stay/long stay for sightseeing) are not subject to coverage of National Pension as Category Ⅰ insured persons.
Category Ⅱ Insured Persons
Company workers and public sector workers under 70 who are covered in Employees’ Pension Insurance  (except for persons age 65 or older who are eligible for old-age pension.)
When you become subject to the Category Ⅱ insured person, your employer needs to submit “Application to Enroll in EPI / EHI.”
Enrollment in Employees' Pension Insurance
Notes:
You must be covered as Category Ⅰ insured person for the period from your entry to Japan until you become Category Ⅱ insured person.
Mariners shall be covered by Seamen’s Insurance system.
Enrollment in Seamen's Insurance
Category Ⅲ Insured Persons
Category Ⅱ insured persons’ economically-dependent spouses between age 20 and 59, residing in Japan (excluding spouse of Category Ⅱ insured person who reached age 65 and eligible for Old-age Basic Pension.)
When you become subject to the Category Ⅲ insured person, employer of your spouse needs to submit “National Pension: Application to Enroll in as Category Ⅲ Insured Person.”
Report of Dependents
Notes:
You must be covered as Category Ⅰ insured person for the period from your entry to Japan until you become Category Ⅲ insured person.
Foreign nationals with specific visa (i.e. medical stay/long stay for sightseeing) are not subject to coverage of National Pension as the Category Ⅲ insured person.

International Exchange/Overseas Program
To all international students
Campus Life
About enrollment confirmation
Enrollment confirmation is to confirm that you are attending university. Enrollment confirmation must be carried out during semester periods (April and October).
15 days
Please come to the Center for Global Education (International Exchange Division) on your campus by the deadline and sign the enrollment confirmation book.A proxy signature by a friend or the like is not acceptable.
In addition, recipients of external scholarships are required to sign a confirmation of enrollment form by a specified deadline each month.
International students who do not confirm their enrollment will have their Asia Pacific Scholarships suspended and will be reported to the Immigration Bureau and Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology as a missing person.If the Immigration Bureau recognizes that there is a problem, the status of residence will be revoked and the person will be declared an "illegal stay" and will be forced to return to their home country.
Temporary departure/return
Before leaving Japan, be sure to fill out the "Overseas Travel Notification" and submit it to the Center for Global Education (International Exchange Division). Please come and pick up the form at the Center for Global Education (International Exchange Division).
In principle, students are not permitted to travel outside of Japan during classes.
Deemed re-entry
If you return to Japan within one year of leaving Japan, you do not need to obtain a re-entry permit if you present your residence card when you leave Japan.However, if you do not re-enter Japan within 1 year of your departure (if your period of stay is less than 1 year after your departure, until your period of stay expires), your status of residence will be lost and you will not be able to continue your studies in Japan. So please be careful.In the unlikely event that you leave Japan for more than one year, please apply for a re-entry permit.
For details, please see “Notices from the Career Support Office” on
Ministry of Justice homepage
Please check at
Notes

http://www.immi-moj.go.jp/re-ed/
when working part-time
Once you have decided on a part-time job, please fill out the "Part-time Job Report" and be sure to submit it to the Global Education Center (International Exchange Division). Please come to the Global Education Center (International Exchange Division) to pick up the form.
Permitting activities outside the status of qualification
The “Student” status of residence does not allow you to engage in remunerative activities in Japan.However, working part-time while studying abroad (excluding some occupations such as amusement business) is permitted if permission is obtained from the Minister of Justice to engage in activity other than that permitted under the status of residence previously granted (immigration control and Article 19 of the Refugee Recognition Act).If you work part-time without obtaining permission to engage in activities other than those permitted under the status of residence previously granted, engage in prohibited work, or engage in part-time work that exceeds the time limit, you may be subject to deportation.

About long vacation period proof
If you are an international student working part-time during long vacations and need to inform your employer of the university's long vacation periods, please check Web Class and submit the "Kansai International University Long Vacation Periods (Notice)" to your employer.
If you have not yet submitted the "Part-time Job Report", please make sure to submit it to the Global Education Center before completing the issuance procedure on Web Class.
If you would like to submit a paper version, please contact the Center for Global Education.It will be handed over two days after the request.
Graduation/Completion
Returning to Japan after Graduation
If you plan to return to your home country after graduating from university, please return to your home country as soon as possible, even if your period of stay for "Student" remains.When you return to Japan, you will be asked to return your residence card at the time of immigration inspection at the airport. It is illegal to stay in Japan with a “Student” status of residence.
When returning to your home country, do not forget to do the following:
Procedures for canceling/moving out of an apartment
Suspension of electricity, gas, and water services and settlement procedures
Handling of oversized garbage
Notification of moving out
Withdrawal from National Health Insurance and Liquidation
Cancellation of bank accounts, mobile phones, and the Internet
If you plan to stay in Japan after graduation
If you want to find a job in Japan, please consult with your employer and change your visa from a "Student" visa to a visa that matches the content of your new job.
If you plan to continue job hunting after graduation, please change your "Student" visa to a "Designated Activities" visa (please do so within two weeks of graduation). The period of stay on a "Designated Activities" visa is six months and can be extended only once. To apply for a "Designated Activities" visa, you will need a letter of recommendation from Kansai University of International Studies. Please contact the Career Support Office.
Documents, etc. that prove that you have been looking for a job continuously since you were in school
to request the issuance of a letter of recommendation.
To stay in Japan after graduation, whether you are finding employment or continuing your job search, you must notify the Immigration Services Agency of your "withdrawal" (graduation, completion, withdrawal, expulsion) from the institution you were currently working in within 14 days (those who continue their studies in Japan must notify the Immigration Services Agency of their "transfer"). Notification can be made online, by mail, or in person at the Immigration Services Bureau counter. Failure to notify may result in penalties.
For more information,
Ministry of Justice homepage
Please check with.
When taking a leave of absence or withdrawing from school
After consulting with your advisor, the Center for Global Education (International Exchange Division), etc. in advance, an interview will be held by the dean.After the interview, you will need to submit a “Request for Leave of Absence” and “Request for Withdrawal”.
take a leave of absence
According to the Immigration Control and Refugee Recognition Act, if you do not continue activities related to the status of residence "Student" for more than 3 months, your status of residence may be revoked.Therefore, if an international student does not continue to study or conduct research activities for more than 3 months due to reasons such as leave of absence, unless there is a legitimate reason for staying in Japan (hospitalization, etc.), he or she must promptly leave Japan or change to another status of residence. Must be changed.
quit school
If you leave the university, you cannot continue to stay in Japan with the status of residence of "Student".You must notify the Immigration Bureau within 14 days of leaving the university.Even if your period of stay is still valid, you must leave Japan promptly, or change your status of residence if you wish to continue staying in Japan.It is illegal to stay in Japan with a status of residence of “Student” or to engage in part-time work.

original_evidence.text:
Student Life
We are here to provide support so that each of you can lead a full university life.
The Careers Center
The Careers Center makes time to meet with you individually, and provides tailor-made careers advice. The Careers Center provides students with not only support in applying for various qualifications courses, internship programs and joint company information sessions, but also with practical lectures on how to join in group discussions and how to prepare for job interviews.
Welfare
The Health Care Center
The Health Care Center provides not only first-aid treatment for sudden illness and injury but also medical care and counseling for physical and mental concerns. Whether you have a condition upon entering university or develop a condition after entering university which may affect your studies, you can consult doctors who specialize in internal medicine, surgery, orthopedics, and psychosomatic internal medicine. This center also offers health guidance about first-aid treatment and the prevention of illness.
The Student Counseling Room
It is natural for students to have various concerns and worries during their time at university. Dealing with such concerns and worries one at a time by yourself means you will be strong enough to enter society after graduation. However, it is no good allowing these worries to build up inside so that the situation worsens. At these times, the Student Counseling Room comes into play. Here you can consult our professional counselors, advisors and lawyers in total confidentiality about your concerns no matter how small or big they may be.
The International Center
The International Center, established in May, 1988, is the office for the international exchange of students and scholars. The center promotes the internationalization of the University. One of its main activities is to teach Japanese language and culture to international students and to the Japanese returnee students who have lived extensively in foreign countries. The center also provides English language instruction for Komazawa University students.
Dormitory
International Exchange House
Komazawa University has a dormitory with 18 private rooms and three rooms with two bed rooms. This accommodation is available only for official exchange students, visiting scholars and researchers. The International Center assigns the rooms to official exchange students as its first priority, and secondly to visiting scholars and researchers.
room202 (sample)
Clubs and Activities
Sports Association
The members of the Sports Association are the stars who take part in official matches to uphold the honour of the University and the club. All groups which are members of the Komazawa University Sports Association are affiliated members of the various sports federations. If you have the motivation, even complete beginners can become active members.
Cultural and Arts Clubs
These groups were established half a century ago and have a long tradition. You can really make the most of your time at university by joining one of these cultural, arts, study or performance clubs, where you will be able to make new friends and meet new challenges.

國際交流中心
國際交流中心成立於1988年5月，是學生與學者之國際交流的主管單位，促進了本大學的國際化。主要的活動之一是教授留學生及長期生活於海外的日裔歸國學生日語與日本文化。本中心也為駒澤大學的學生提供英語課程。
國際交流中心委員會由各學院與行政單位之成員組成，委員會進行國際交流中心的現狀探討並承擔所推行之政策的責任。
國際交流中心提供的主要服務如下：
駒澤大學在正式協議的基礎上促進與外國大學的國際交流。協議為有意留學的交換學生建立規則架構。地圖上顯示與本校締結有國際交換協議之大學：卑詩大學（加拿大）；昆士蘭大學（澳洲）；格里菲斯大学（澳洲）；加州大學爾灣分校（美國）；加州大學洛杉磯分校（美國）；阿肯色理工大學（美國）；夏威夷大學瑪諾亞分校（美國）；艾希特大學（英國）；東國大學（韓國）；淡江大學（台灣）；華東師範大學（中國）；普羅旺斯大學（法國）；金斯頓大學（英國）；北京大學（中國）；開羅大學（埃及）。
國際交流中心為駒澤大學學生提供英語、中文與法文之海外短期密集課程。這些密集課程由與本校締結有正式協議的海外大學贊助。學生可透過寄宿家庭環境與當地學生的友誼，學到實用的英文、中文與法文。參加密集課程的學生在寄宿環境中過上一個月或更長之積極忙碌的生活。每項海外密集課程約有30名駒澤大學學生參與：艾希特大學、卑詩大學、加州大學爾灣分校、華東師範大學（整個暑假的密集課程）；昆士蘭大學、普羅旺斯大學（春季密集課程）。
駒澤大學為澳洲昆士蘭大學的學生提供短期密集課程。每年十一月及十二月國際交流中心會為約十五名澳洲學生舉辦日本語言、文化、自然與歷史講座。這個課程包含為期兩周的寄宿家庭生活。
對於想透過學校的計畫或自行出國留學的學生，國際交流中心將提供建議與協助。
國際交流中心為正式交換學生與其他留學生提供課程，諸如8堂課的日語課程以及10堂課的日本概況。
國際交流中心接待來自海外的訪問教授與學者。
國際交流中心為準備TOEFL®和TOEIC®測驗的本校學生舉辦密集課程。
國際交流會館
駒澤大學為留學生提供擁有14間個人房的宿舍。國際交流中心將這些宿舍優先分配給正式交換學生，其次是訪問學者與研究者人員。每個房間均備有空調、迷你廚房、冰箱、淋浴間與高速網路等舒適設施。

國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。

外国人留学生の方へ
外国人留学生試験・入学については、受験生向けのホームページ（こちら）をご覧ください。
2026年4月に入学する外国人留学生の皆さんへ
以下のとおり、外国人留学生向けオリエンテーションを実施しますので、該当者は必ず参加してください。
１．外国人留学生スタートガイダンス
【対象者】

（2）外国人留学生に対する大学のサポートや連絡方法について知りたい人

kyo2sec-in（a）komazawa-u.ac.jp

出入国在留管理局への申請書類の提出や在留カードの受領は、学生本人に代わって駒澤大学が業務委託にて行っています。
日本政府により外国人政策が厳格化される中、在留資格の更新に関する重要な事項について説明します。
在留資格の更新ができなくなることもあるので、必ず参加してください。

2026年4月1日（水）
15：00～

kokusaicenter（a）komazawa-u.ac.jp

登録のやり方がわからない人は、必ずこの期間内に教務部窓口へ相談に来てください。
４.在留資格認定証明書（ＣＯＥ）交付申請について
大学で教育を受けるために必要な在留資格（「留学」など）を有していない方は、出入国在留管理局への申請手続が必要なため2次手続（学費納入）後、3月７日（土）までに国際センターへ申し出てください。

kokusaicenter（a）komazawa-u.ac.jp

問い合わせ窓口について
問い合わせ内容によって窓口が変わります。詳細は以下画像でご確認ください。
外国人留学生の皆さんへ（在留資格等申請に関するお知らせ）
本学に在籍する外国人留学生（在留資格「留学」）の方に、以下の項目の学内申請手続きについてご案内しております。
在留期間更新許可申請（留学）
資格外活動（アルバイト）許可申請
みなし再入国許可申請（日本から一時出国する人）
【よくある質問】
在留資格申請でよくいただく質問について、Q&Aにまとめていますので参考にしてください。
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1NQ5i19sSO7NgLkbkUK4x0tL-Oc10eBXDSS_wkByxsY8/edit?usp=sharing
在留期間更新許可申請（留学）の更新申請と必要書類
出入国在留管理局への申請書類の提出や在留カードの受領について、駒澤大学が業務委託にて行っております。
つきましては、在留資格が「留学」の留学生は以下手順に従って、在留資格更新手続きを行ってください。
※留学生（申請者）本人が、出入国在留管理局へ赴く必要はありません。
【在留資格更新手続き手順】
ステップ１
在留期限の３か月前の月末（※）までに、国際センターから対象留学生に更新案内のメールを送信します。
※（例）在留期限が６月１２日の場合、３月３１日までに案内メールを送信
※案内メールが届かない方は、国際センターに問い合わせてください。
ステップ２
委託先の行政書士より、対象留学生に更新手続きについての詳細メールが送信されます。
ステップ３
対象留学生は「ステップ2」に従って、手続きをすすめてください。
なお、基本的な必要資料は以下の通りです。（詳細内容はSETP2の案内に従ってください。）
・申込書（指定書式）
・在留資格更新許可申請書（本人用、指定書式）
・資格外活動許可申請書（指定書式）
（※アルバイトをする場合のみ提出必要）
・アルバイトの給与明細書
（※アルバイトをしている場合のみ）
・銀行の通帳コピー
・在学証明書原本
・成績証明書原本
・パスポート原本
・在留カード原本
・入学前の学校の「卒業（修了）証明書」、「成績・出席証明書」
→新入生および入学後初めての更新の場合のみ提出必要
ステップ４
委託先が出入国在留管理局への取次申請を行います。
ステップ５
審査終了後、出入国管理局から対象留学生宛てに
在留許可期間に応じた在留許可手数料支払いに
ついての
メール連絡が入ります。　速やかに
コンビニ決済または銀行決済を済ませてください。
→在留許可手数料については、
出入国在留管理局のHP
で確認することができます。
ステップ６
新しい在留カードの交付後、委託先から対象留学生宛てにメール連絡が入ります。
国際センター窓口で、新・旧在留カードとパスポートを受け取ってください。
その際は学生証をご提示ください。
資格外活動の注意事項
アルバイトをする場合は、
「資格外活動許可申請書」
を同時に提出してください。在留資格「留学」は、「資格外許可申請」を取得しないとアルバイトはできません。
アルバイトは週 28 時間以内と入管法で定められています。
夏休み・冬休みは 8 時間以内/1 日可能（１週間４０時間を超えないこと）となります。ただし、春休みについては本学では学則に定められていないため、1月の定期試験終了時から 3月末までも週 28 時間以内となります。
風俗営業（スナック・キャバレー・パチンコ・ゲームセンターなど）や性風俗特殊営業店でのアル バイトは禁じられています。このような場所での受付やビラ配り、皿洗いや掃除をすることも禁止されています。
在留資格更新申請中の場合、在留期限（資格外活動許可期限）が切れた日より、アルバイトはできなくなります。
※定められた規則を守らない場合は、資格外活動違反となり、処罰や強制送還の対象となり、日本での留学生活ができなくなりますので十分に注意してください。
みなし再入国許可について（日本から一時出国する人）
日本を出国し、1年以内に再入国する場合は「みなし再入国制度により出国」できます。
出国時に「再入国EDカード」の「□一時的な出国であり、再入国する予定です」にレ点(チェック)をし、みなし再入国許可を得てから出国してください。
再入国の期限は出国後1年以内、在留期限が1年未満の場合は在留期限までに日本に入国してください。
（在留資格更新申請中の場合は、もとの在留期間の満了日から2カ月を経過する日までの間、再入国が可能です。）
詳細は
出入国管理局のHP
を参照してください。
一時帰国や海外旅行等で日本を離れる場合は、日本を出国する1週間前までを目途に、大学へ帰国届を提出する必要があります。
出国届
（
Googleフォーム
）
Googleフォームで提出できない方は、国際センター窓口か教務部⑤番窓口に相談してください。
お問い合わせ先
国際センター事務室

For the admission to exchange program, please complete and submit the application documents by

*Please apply for student visa at Japanese Embassy or 
Consulate nearby  immediately after receiving C.O.E  and 
Acceptance Letter. 
2026 Spring: Between February to Beginning of March 2026 
 
5: Class information 
Some general education courses and certain specialized courses in the Faculty of Global Media 
Studies are conducted in English; however, the majority of courses across other faculties are primarily 
conducted in Japanese. 
Japanese language courses and Japanese culture courses are also available for international 
students with beginner to intermediate Japanese proficiency. 
For specialized and general education courses conducted in Japanese, it is desirable to have a 
Japanese proficiency level equivalent to JLPT N2 (no certification submission is required). Even if 
you do not have N2 proficiency at the time of application, you can still apply for the exchange program, 
but the selection of your courses will be determined in consultat ion with an academic advisor after 
your acceptance is officially confirmed.

國際交流中心
國際交流中心成立於1988年5月，是學生與學者之國際交流的主管單位，促進了本大學的國際化。主要的活動之一是教授留學生及長期生活於海外的日裔歸國學生日語與日本文化。本中心也為駒澤大學的學生提供英語課程。
國際交流中心委員會由各學院與行政單位之成員組成，委員會進行國際交流中心的現狀探討並承擔所推行之政策的責任。
國際交流中心提供的主要服務如下：
駒澤大學在正式協議的基礎上促進與外國大學的國際交流。協議為有意留學的交換學生建立規則架構。地圖上顯示與本校締結有國際交換協議之大學：卑詩大學（加拿大）；昆士蘭大學（澳洲）；格里菲斯大学（澳洲）；加州大學爾灣分校（美國）；加州大學洛杉磯分校（美國）；阿肯色理工大學（美國）；夏威夷大學瑪諾亞分校（美國）；艾希特大學（英國）；東國大學（韓國）；淡江大學（台灣）；華東師範大學（中國）；普羅旺斯大學（法國）；金斯頓大學（英國）；北京大學（中國）；開羅大學（埃及）。
國際交流中心為駒澤大學學生提供英語、中文與法文之海外短期密集課程。這些密集課程由與本校締結有正式協議的海外大學贊助。學生可透過寄宿家庭環境與當地學生的友誼，學到實用的英文、中文與法文。參加密集課程的學生在寄宿環境中過上一個月或更長之積極忙碌的生活。每項海外密集課程約有30名駒澤大學學生參與：艾希特大學、卑詩大學、加州大學爾灣分校、華東師範大學（整個暑假的密集課程）；昆士蘭大學、普羅旺斯大學（春季密集課程）。
駒澤大學為澳洲昆士蘭大學的學生提供短期密集課程。每年十一月及十二月國際交流中心會為約十五名澳洲學生舉辦日本語言、文化、自然與歷史講座。這個課程包含為期兩周的寄宿家庭生活。
對於想透過學校的計畫或自行出國留學的學生，國際交流中心將提供建議與協助。
國際交流中心為正式交換學生與其他留學生提供課程，諸如8堂課的日語課程以及10堂課的日本概況。
國際交流中心接待來自海外的訪問教授與學者。
國際交流中心為準備TOEFL®和TOEIC®測驗的本校學生舉辦密集課程。
國際交流會館
駒澤大學為留學生提供擁有14間個人房的宿舍。國際交流中心將這些宿舍優先分配給正式交換學生，其次是訪問學者與研究者人員。每個房間均備有空調、迷你廚房、冰箱、淋浴間與高速網路等舒適設施。

外国人留学生の方へ
外国人留学生試験・入学については、受験生向けのホームページ（こちら）をご覧ください。
2026年4月に入学する外国人留学生の皆さんへ
以下のとおり、外国人留学生向けオリエンテーションを実施しますので、該当者は必ず参加してください。
１．外国人留学生スタートガイダンス
【対象者】
（1）在留資格（ビザ）「留学」で在学する予定の人
（2）外国人留学生に対する大学のサポートや連絡方法について知りたい人
（3）学生証が自宅に届いていない、持っていない人
【日　時】2026年4月1日（水）
以下の時間から、好きな時間を1つ選んで参加してください。
所要時間は約30分を予定しています。
（1）13:00〜
（2）14:00〜
（3）16:00〜
（4）17:00〜
【場　所】教務部④番窓口（駒沢キャンパス本部棟1階）
【持ち物】
（1）筆記用具
（2）学生証（持っている人のみ）
（3）スマートフォン、タブレット、またはノートパソコン
【内　容】
（1）学生証の受け渡し
（2）大学のネットワーク（KOMAnet）の登録
（3）学内Wifi、Google Classroomの登録
（4）留学生向けの支援制度を紹介
【問い合わせ】教務部教務課教務2係（教務部④番窓口）
kyo2sec-in（a）komazawa-u.ac.jp
※（a）を@に変更してください。
２．在留資格（ビザ）オリエンテーション
出入国在留管理局への申請書類の提出や在留カードの受領は、学生本人に代わって駒澤大学が業務委託にて行っています。
日本政府により外国人政策が厳格化される中、在留資格の更新に関する重要な事項について説明します。
在留資格の更新ができなくなることもあるので、必ず参加してください。
【対象者】在留資格（ビザ）「留学」で在学する予定の人
【日　時】
2026年4月1日（水）
15：00～
【場　所】駒沢キャンパス　1号館　1-204教場
【持ち物】
（1）筆記用具
（2）学生証（持っている人のみ）
（3）パスポート
（4）在留カード（交付されている人のみ）
（5）スマートフォン、タブレット、またはノートパソコン
【問い合わせ】国際センター事務室
（駒沢キャンパス本部棟1階）
kokusaicenter（a）komazawa-u.ac.jp
※（a）を@に変更してください。
３. 授業の履修登録の相談
4月3日（金）から4月6日（月）までの間に、1年間の授業を登録します。
登録のやり方がわからない人は、必ずこの期間内に教務部窓口へ相談に来てください。
４.在留資格認定証明書（ＣＯＥ）交付申請について
大学で教育を受けるために必要な在留資格（「留学」など）を有していない方は、出入国在留管理局への申請手続が必要なため2次手続（学費納入）後、3月７日（土）までに国際センターへ申し出てください。
５．入学許可証について
本学では、「入学許可証」の発行はしておりません。在学中の日本語学校等で提出を求められている場合でも、対応しかねますので、ご了承ください。
国際センター事務室
kokusaicenter（a）komazawa-u.ac.jp
※（a）を@に変更してください。
問い合わせ窓口について
問い合わせ内容によって窓口が変わります。詳細は以下画像でご確認ください。
外国人留学生の皆さんへ（在留資格等申請に関するお知らせ）
本学に在籍する外国人留学生（在留資格「留学」）の方に、以下の項目の学内申請手続きについてご案内しております。
在留期間更新許可申請（留学）
資格外活動（アルバイト）許可申請
みなし再入国許可申請（日本から一時出国する人）
【よくある質問】
在留資格申請でよくいただく質問について、Q&Aにまとめていますので参考にしてください。
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1NQ5i19sSO7NgLkbkUK4x0tL-Oc10eBXDSS_wkByxsY8/edit?usp=sharing
在留期間更新許可申請（留学）の更新申請と必要書類
出入国在留管理局への申請書類の提出や在留カードの受領について、駒澤大学が業務委託にて行っております。
つきましては、在留資格が「留学」の留学生は以下手順に従って、在留資格更新手続きを行ってください。
※留学生（申請者）本人が、出入国在留管理局へ赴く必要はありません。
【在留資格更新手続き手順】
ステップ１
在留期限の３か月前の月末（※）までに、国際センターから対象留学生に更新案内のメールを送信します。
※（例）在留期限が６月１２日の場合、３月３１日までに案内メールを送信
※案内メールが届かない方は、国際センターに問い合わせてください。
ステップ２
委託先の行政書士より、対象留学生に更新手続きについての詳細メールが送信されます。
ステップ３
対象留学生は「ステップ2」に従って、手続きをすすめてください。
なお、基本的な必要資料は以下の通りです。（詳細内容はSETP2の案内に従ってください。）
・申込書（指定書式）
・在留資格更新許可申請書（本人用、指定書式）
・資格外活動許可申請書（指定書式）
（※アルバイトをする場合のみ提出必要）
・アルバイトの給与明細書
（※アルバイトをしている場合のみ）
・銀行の通帳コピー
・在学証明書原本
・成績証明書原本
・パスポート原本
・在留カード原本
・入学前の学校の「卒業（修了）証明書」、「成績・出席証明書」
→新入生および入学後初めての更新の場合のみ提出必要
ステップ４
委託先が出入国在留管理局への取次申請を行います。
ステップ５
審査終了後、出入国管理局から対象留学生宛てに
在留許可期間に応じた在留許可手数料支払いに
ついての
メール連絡が入ります。　速やかに
コンビニ決済または銀行決済を済ませてください。
→在留許可手数料については、
出入国在留管理局のHP
で確認することができます。
ステップ６
新しい在留カードの交付後、委託先から対象留学生宛てにメール連絡が入ります。
国際センター窓口で、新・旧在留カードとパスポートを受け取ってください。
その際は学生証をご提示ください。
資格外活動の注意事項
アルバイトをする場合は、
「資格外活動許可申請書」
を同時に提出してください。在留資格「留学」は、「資格外許可申請」を取得しないとアルバイトはできません。
アルバイトは週 28 時間以内と入管法で定められています。
夏休み・冬休みは 8 時間以内/1 日可能（１週間４０時間を超えないこと）となります。ただし、春休みについては本学では学則に定められていないため、1月の定期試験終了時から 3月末までも週 28 時間以内となります。
風俗営業（スナック・キャバレー・パチンコ・ゲームセンターなど）や性風俗特殊営業店でのアル バイトは禁じられています。このような場所での受付やビラ配り、皿洗いや掃除をすることも禁止されています。
在留資格更新申請中の場合、在留期限（資格外活動許可期限）が切れた日より、アルバイトはできなくなります。
※定められた規則を守らない場合は、資格外活動違反となり、処罰や強制送還の対象となり、日本での留学生活ができなくなりますので十分に注意してください。
みなし再入国許可について（日本から一時出国する人）
日本を出国し、1年以内に再入国する場合は「みなし再入国制度により出国」できます。
出国時に「再入国EDカード」の「□一時的な出国であり、再入国する予定です」にレ点(チェック)をし、みなし再入国許可を得てから出国してください。
再入国の期限は出国後1年以内、在留期限が1年未満の場合は在留期限までに日本に入国してください。
（在留資格更新申請中の場合は、もとの在留期間の満了日から2カ月を経過する日までの間、再入国が可能です。）
詳細は
出入国管理局のHP
を参照してください。
一時帰国や海外旅行等で日本を離れる場合は、日本を出国する1週間前までを目途に、大学へ帰国届を提出する必要があります。
出国届
（
Googleフォーム
）
Googleフォームで提出できない方は、国際センター窓口か教務部⑤番窓口に相談してください。
お問い合わせ先
国際センター事務室
kokusaicenter（a）komazawa-u.ac.jp
※（a）を@に変更してください。

Student Life
We are here to provide support so that each of you can lead a full university life.
The Careers Center
The Careers Center makes time to meet with you individually, and provides tailor-made careers advice. The Careers Center provides students with not only support in applying for various qualifications courses, internship programs and joint company information sessions, but also with practical lectures on how to join in group discussions and how to prepare for job interviews.
Welfare
The Health Care Center
The Health Care Center provides not only first-aid treatment for sudden illness and injury but also medical care and counseling for physical and mental concerns. Whether you have a condition upon entering university or develop a condition after entering university which may affect your studies, you can consult doctors who specialize in internal medicine, surgery, orthopedics, and psychosomatic internal medicine. This center also offers health guidance about first-aid treatment and the prevention of illness.
The Student Counseling Room
It is natural for students to have various concerns and worries during their time at university. Dealing with such concerns and worries one at a time by yourself means you will be strong enough to enter society after graduation. However, it is no good allowing these worries to build up inside so that the situation worsens. At these times, the Student Counseling Room comes into play. Here you can consult our professional counselors, advisors and lawyers in total confidentiality about your concerns no matter how small or big they may be.
The International Center
The International Center, established in May, 1988, is the office for the international exchange of students and scholars. The center promotes the internationalization of the University. One of its main activities is to teach Japanese language and culture to international students and to the Japanese returnee students who have lived extensively in foreign countries. The center also provides English language instruction for Komazawa University students.
Dormitory
International Exchange House
Komazawa University has a dormitory with 18 private rooms and three rooms with two bed rooms. This accommodation is available only for official exchange students, visiting scholars and researchers. The International Center assigns the rooms to official exchange students as its first priority, and secondly to visiting scholars and researchers.
room202 (sample)
Clubs and Activities
Sports Association
The members of the Sports Association are the stars who take part in official matches to uphold the honour of the University and the club. All groups which are members of the Komazawa University Sports Association are affiliated members of the various sports federations. If you have the motivation, even complete beginners can become active members.
Cultural and Arts Clubs
These groups were established half a century ago and have a long tradition. You can really make the most of your time at university by joining one of these cultural, arts, study or performance clubs, where you will be able to make new friends and meet new challenges.

original_evidence.text:
The International Center
The International Center, established in May, 1988, is the office for the international exchange of students and scholars. It endeavors to promote the internationalization of the university. One of its main activities is to teach Japanese language and culture to foreign students and to Japanese returnee students who have lived extensively in foreign countries. It also provides English language instruction for Komazawa students.
The International Center Committee is composed of members from each faculty and administrative organization of the University. The Committee discusses the current affairs of the International Center and is responsible for its policies.
The main services offered by the International Center are as follows.
Komazawa University promotes international relations with foreign universities on the basis of official agreements. The agreements establish a framework of rules for exchanging students who wish to study abroad. The map which follows exhibits the universities which have international exchange agreements with Komazawa University: The University of British Columbia (Canada); The University of Queensland (Australia); Griffith University (Australia); The University of California, Irvine (U.S.A); California State University, Los Angeles (U.S.A.); Arkansas Tech University (U.S.A.); The University of Hawaii, Manoa (U.S.A.); The University of Exeter (Great Britain); Dongguk University (The Republic of Korea); Tamkang University (Taiwan); East China Normal University (China);Université de Provence (France); Peking University (China); I-Shou University（Taiwan）.
The International Center conducts short-term intensive English, Chinese and French courses abroad for Komazawa University students. The programs for these intensive courses are sponsored by foreign universities that have an official agreement with Komazawa University. The students can learn practical English, Chinese and French from their home-stay environments and from friendships with students of the host university. The students in the intensive program lead very active lives for a month or more in the home stay environment. Groups of roughly thirty students from Komazawa University per program participate in these overseas intensive courses: The University of Exeter, The University of British Columbia, The University of California, Irvine, East China Normal University (all summer intensive courses); The University of Queensland, Université de Provence (spring intensive courses).
Komazawa University provides intensive short-term courses for students from the University of Queensland of Australia. Every year in the months of November and December the International Center hosts about fifteen Australian students for a program of lectures on the language, culture, nature, and history of Japan. The program includes two weeks of home stay.
The International Center provides advice and assistance to students who want to study abroad in a university either through a University program or on their own.
The International Center provides official exchange students as well as other students from abroad such programs as an eight-course curriculum in the Japanese language and a ten-course curriculum in Japanese affairs.
The International Center hosts visiting professors and scholars from abroad.
The International Center conducts intensive courses for Komazawa University students preparing for the TOEFL® and TOEIC® examinations.
The International Exchange House
Komazawa University has a dormitory with 14 private rooms for accommodation of students from abroad. The International Center assigns the rooms to official exchange students as its first priority, and secondly to visiting scholars and researchers. Each room has very comfortable facilities including air-conditioning, a mini-kitchen, a refrigerator, a bath and shower, and an hi-speed Internet.

original_evidence.text:
國際交流中心
國際交流中心成立於1988年5月，是學生與學者之國際交流的主管單位，促進了本大學的國際化。主要的活動之一是教授留學生及長期生活於海外的日裔歸國學生日語與日本文化。本中心也為駒澤大學的學生提供英語課程。
國際交流中心委員會由各學院與行政單位之成員組成，委員會進行國際交流中心的現狀探討並承擔所推行之政策的責任。
國際交流中心提供的主要服務如下：
駒澤大學在正式協議的基礎上促進與外國大學的國際交流。協議為有意留學的交換學生建立規則架構。地圖上顯示與本校締結有國際交換協議之大學：卑詩大學（加拿大）；昆士蘭大學（澳洲）；格里菲斯大学（澳洲）；加州大學爾灣分校（美國）；加州大學洛杉磯分校（美國）；阿肯色理工大學（美國）；夏威夷大學瑪諾亞分校（美國）；艾希特大學（英國）；東國大學（韓國）；淡江大學（台灣）；華東師範大學（中國）；普羅旺斯大學（法國）；金斯頓大學（英國）；北京大學（中國）；開羅大學（埃及）。
國際交流中心為駒澤大學學生提供英語、中文與法文之海外短期密集課程。這些密集課程由與本校締結有正式協議的海外大學贊助。學生可透過寄宿家庭環境與當地學生的友誼，學到實用的英文、中文與法文。參加密集課程的學生在寄宿環境中過上一個月或更長之積極忙碌的生活。每項海外密集課程約有30名駒澤大學學生參與：艾希特大學、卑詩大學、加州大學爾灣分校、華東師範大學（整個暑假的密集課程）；昆士蘭大學、普羅旺斯大學（春季密集課程）。
駒澤大學為澳洲昆士蘭大學的學生提供短期密集課程。每年十一月及十二月國際交流中心會為約十五名澳洲學生舉辦日本語言、文化、自然與歷史講座。這個課程包含為期兩周的寄宿家庭生活。
對於想透過學校的計畫或自行出國留學的學生，國際交流中心將提供建議與協助。
國際交流中心為正式交換學生與其他留學生提供課程，諸如8堂課的日語課程以及10堂課的日本概況。
國際交流中心接待來自海外的訪問教授與學者。
國際交流中心為準備TOEFL®和TOEIC®測驗的本校學生舉辦密集課程。
國際交流會館
駒澤大學為留學生提供擁有14間個人房的宿舍。國際交流中心將這些宿舍優先分配給正式交換學生，其次是訪問學者與研究者人員。每個房間均備有空調、迷你廚房、冰箱、淋浴間與高速網路等舒適設施。

4: Admission Procedure 
For the admission to exchange program, please complete and submit the application documents by 
the deadline. Prescribed forms(#1、5、6) are sent by email to your home institution. All documents 
(see below) must be sent from your home institution by email. 
Once your admission has been approved, we will send the copies of your Certificate of Eligibility , 
your acceptance letter and “Pre-Departure Information” to you and your exchange coordinator  by 
email.  
 
Number of Accepting Students *Please check with exchange coordinator at home institution 
Application Documents #1 Exchange Program Application for Admission 
#2 Letter of Recommendation (written in Japanese or English) 
#3 Original Copy of Official Transcript (written in English) 
#4 Soft copy of your face picture(color, 4x3cm, face to shoulder, 
no hats, plain (white) back ground) 
#5 Certificate of Health Examination 
#6 Application for Certificate of Eligibility (do no post picture) 
  *See sample and input your personal data on Excel sheet 
#7 Scanned Data of Biographical Page of Passport 
#8 Supporting Financial Document (¥700,000 or more /year) 
  *Submit certificate of bank balance or scholarship 
Grant Notification for Admission 
(to be sent via email  including 
Certificate of Eligibility  and 
Acceptance Letter) 
2025 Fall: Between End of July to Mid-August 2025 
*Please apply for student visa at Japanese Embassy or 
Consulate nearby  immediately after receiving C.O.E  and 
Acceptance Letter. 
2026 Spring: Between February to Beginning of March 2026 
 
5: Class information 
Some general education courses and certain specialized courses in the Faculty of Global Media 
Studies are conducted in English; however, the majority of courses across other faculties are primarily 
conducted in Japanese. 
Japanese language courses and Japanese culture courses are also available for international 
students with beginner to intermediate Japanese proficiency. 
For specialized and general education courses conducted in Japanese, it is desirable to have a 
Japanese proficiency level equivalent to JLPT N2 (no certification submission is required). Even if 
you do not have N2 proficiency at the time of application, you can still apply for the exchange program, 
but the selection of your courses will be determined in consultat ion with an academic advisor after 
your acceptance is officially confirmed.

外国人留学生の方へ
外国人留学生試験・入学については、受験生向けのホームページ（こちら）をご覧ください。
2026年4月に入学する外国人留学生の皆さんへ
以下のとおり、外国人留学生向けオリエンテーションを実施しますので、該当者は必ず参加してください。
１．外国人留学生スタートガイダンス
【対象者】
（1）在留資格（ビザ）「留学」で在学する予定の人
（2）外国人留学生に対する大学のサポートや連絡方法について知りたい人
（3）学生証が自宅に届いていない、持っていない人
【日　時】2026年4月1日（水）
以下の時間から、好きな時間を1つ選んで参加してください。
所要時間は約30分を予定しています。
（1）13:00〜
（2）14:00〜
（3）16:00〜
（4）17:00〜
【場　所】教務部④番窓口（駒沢キャンパス本部棟1階）
【持ち物】
（1）筆記用具
（2）学生証（持っている人のみ）
（3）スマートフォン、タブレット、またはノートパソコン
【内　容】
（1）学生証の受け渡し
（2）大学のネットワーク（KOMAnet）の登録
（3）学内Wifi、Google Classroomの登録
（4）留学生向けの支援制度を紹介
【問い合わせ】教務部教務課教務2係（教務部④番窓口）
kyo2sec-in（a）komazawa-u.ac.jp
※（a）を@に変更してください。
２．在留資格（ビザ）オリエンテーション
出入国在留管理局への申請書類の提出や在留カードの受領は、学生本人に代わって駒澤大学が業務委託にて行っています。
日本政府により外国人政策が厳格化される中、在留資格の更新に関する重要な事項について説明します。
在留資格の更新ができなくなることもあるので、必ず参加してください。
【対象者】在留資格（ビザ）「留学」で在学する予定の人
【日　時】
2026年4月1日（水）
15：00～
【場　所】駒沢キャンパス　1号館　1-204教場
【持ち物】
（1）筆記用具
（2）学生証（持っている人のみ）
（3）パスポート
（4）在留カード（交付されている人のみ）
（5）スマートフォン、タブレット、またはノートパソコン
【問い合わせ】国際センター事務室
（駒沢キャンパス本部棟1階）
kokusaicenter（a）komazawa-u.ac.jp
※（a）を@に変更してください。
３. 授業の履修登録の相談
4月3日（金）から4月6日（月）までの間に、1年間の授業を登録します。
登録のやり方がわからない人は、必ずこの期間内に教務部窓口へ相談に来てください。
４.在留資格認定証明書（ＣＯＥ）交付申請について
大学で教育を受けるために必要な在留資格（「留学」など）を有していない方は、出入国在留管理局への申請手続が必要なため2次手続（学費納入）後、3月７日（土）までに国際センターへ申し出てください。
５．入学許可証について
本学では、「入学許可証」の発行はしておりません。在学中の日本語学校等で提出を求められている場合でも、対応しかねますので、ご了承ください。
国際センター事務室
kokusaicenter（a）komazawa-u.ac.jp
※（a）を@に変更してください。
問い合わせ窓口について
問い合わせ内容によって窓口が変わります。詳細は以下画像でご確認ください。
外国人留学生の皆さんへ（在留資格等申請に関するお知らせ）
本学に在籍する外国人留学生（在留資格「留学」）の方に、以下の項目の学内申請手続きについてご案内しております。
在留期間更新許可申請（留学）
資格外活動（アルバイト）許可申請
みなし再入国許可申請（日本から一時出国する人）
【よくある質問】
在留資格申請でよくいただく質問について、Q&Aにまとめていますので参考にしてください。
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1NQ5i19sSO7NgLkbkUK4x0tL-Oc10eBXDSS_wkByxsY8/edit?usp=sharing
在留期間更新許可申請（留学）の更新申請と必要書類
出入国在留管理局への申請書類の提出や在留カードの受領について、駒澤大学が業務委託にて行っております。
つきましては、在留資格が「留学」の留学生は以下手順に従って、在留資格更新手続きを行ってください。
※留学生（申請者）本人が、出入国在留管理局へ赴く必要はありません。
【在留資格更新手続き手順】
ステップ１
在留期限の３か月前の月末（※）までに、国際センターから対象留学生に更新案内のメールを送信します。
※（例）在留期限が６月１２日の場合、３月３１日までに案内メールを送信
※案内メールが届かない方は、国際センターに問い合わせてください。
ステップ２
委託先の行政書士より、対象留学生に更新手続きについての詳細メールが送信されます。
ステップ３
対象留学生は「ステップ2」に従って、手続きをすすめてください。
なお、基本的な必要資料は以下の通りです。（詳細内容はSETP2の案内に従ってください。）
・申込書（指定書式）
・在留資格更新許可申請書（本人用、指定書式）
・資格外活動許可申請書（指定書式）
（※アルバイトをする場合のみ提出必要）
・アルバイトの給与明細書
（※アルバイトをしている場合のみ）
・銀行の通帳コピー
・在学証明書原本
・成績証明書原本
・パスポート原本
・在留カード原本
・入学前の学校の「卒業（修了）証明書」、「成績・出席証明書」
→新入生および入学後初めての更新の場合のみ提出必要
ステップ４
委託先が出入国在留管理局への取次申請を行います。
ステップ５
審査終了後、出入国管理局から対象留学生宛てに
在留許可期間に応じた在留許可手数料支払いに
ついての
メール連絡が入ります。　速やかに
コンビニ決済または銀行決済を済ませてください。
→在留許可手数料については、
出入国在留管理局のHP
で確認することができます。
ステップ６
新しい在留カードの交付後、委託先から対象留学生宛てにメール連絡が入ります。
国際センター窓口で、新・旧在留カードとパスポートを受け取ってください。
その際は学生証をご提示ください。
資格外活動の注意事項
アルバイトをする場合は、
「資格外活動許可申請書」
を同時に提出してください。在留資格「留学」は、「資格外許可申請」を取得しないとアルバイトはできません。
アルバイトは週 28 時間以内と入管法で定められています。
夏休み・冬休みは 8 時間以内/1 日可能（１週間４０時間を超えないこと）となります。ただし、春休みについては本学では学則に定められていないため、1月の定期試験終了時から 3月末までも週 28 時間以内となります。
風俗営業（スナック・キャバレー・パチンコ・ゲームセンターなど）や性風俗特殊営業店でのアル バイトは禁じられています。このような場所での受付やビラ配り、皿洗いや掃除をすることも禁止されています。
在留資格更新申請中の場合、在留期限（資格外活動許可期限）が切れた日より、アルバイトはできなくなります。
※定められた規則を守らない場合は、資格外活動違反となり、処罰や強制送還の対象となり、日本での留学生活ができなくなりますので十分に注意してください。
みなし再入国許可について（日本から一時出国する人）
日本を出国し、1年以内に再入国する場合は「みなし再入国制度により出国」できます。
出国時に「再入国EDカード」の「□一時的な出国であり、再入国する予定です」にレ点(チェック)をし、みなし再入国許可を得てから出国してください。
再入国の期限は出国後1年以内、在留期限が1年未満の場合は在留期限までに日本に入国してください。
（在留資格更新申請中の場合は、もとの在留期間の満了日から2カ月を経過する日までの間、再入国が可能です。）
詳細は
出入国管理局のHP
を参照してください。
一時帰国や海外旅行等で日本を離れる場合は、日本を出国する1週間前までを目途に、大学へ帰国届を提出する必要があります。
出国届
（
Googleフォーム
）
Googleフォームで提出できない方は、国際センター窓口か教務部⑤番窓口に相談してください。
お問い合わせ先
国際センター事務室
kokusaicenter（a）komazawa-u.ac.jp
※（a）を@に変更してください。

Enroll in Pension System
All residents of Japan between age 20 and 59, regardless of nationality, must be covered by National Pension by law. There are three types of insured persons of National Pension according to their status as follows:
Category Ⅰ insured persons (self-employed persons, students, agricultural, forestry and fishery workers, unemployed persons)
Category Ⅱ insured persons (company workers and public sector workers)
Category Ⅲ insured persons (economically-dependent spouses of category Ⅱ insured persons)
Category Ⅰ Insured Persons
All residents of Japan between age 20 and 59 who are not Category Ⅱ or Ⅲ insured persons (e.g. self-employed persons, students, agricultural, forestry and fishery workers, unemployed persons.)
When you become subject to Category Ⅰ insured person, you need to submit, by yourself, application to enroll in as Category I insured person to the municipal office of your place of residence within 14 days.
Enrollment in National Pension
Note:Foreign nationals with specific visa (i.e. medical stay/long stay for sightseeing) are not subject to coverage of National Pension as Category Ⅰ insured persons.
Category Ⅱ Insured Persons
Company workers and public sector workers under 70 who are covered in Employees’ Pension Insurance  (except for persons age 65 or older who are eligible for old-age pension.)
When you become subject to the Category Ⅱ insured person, your employer needs to submit “Application to Enroll in EPI / EHI.”
Enrollment in Employees' Pension Insurance
Notes:
You must be covered as Category Ⅰ insured person for the period from your entry to Japan until you become Category Ⅱ insured person.
Mariners shall be covered by Seamen’s Insurance system.
Enrollment in Seamen's Insurance
Category Ⅲ Insured Persons
Category Ⅱ insured persons’ economically-dependent spouses between age 20 and 59, residing in Japan (excluding spouse of Category Ⅱ insured person who reached age 65 and eligible for Old-age Basic Pension.)
When you become subject to the Category Ⅲ insured person, employer of your spouse needs to submit “National Pension: Application to Enroll in as Category Ⅲ Insured Person.”
Report of Dependents
Notes:
You must be covered as Category Ⅰ insured person for the period from your entry to Japan until you become Category Ⅲ insured person.
Foreign nationals with specific visa (i.e. medical stay/long stay for sightseeing) are not subject to coverage of National Pension as the Category Ⅲ insured person.

visa.label: 簽證／居留
visa.note: 2025交換錄取後email COE及Acceptance Letter，持兩件申請student visa；最新版COE Excel／財力表未取得。與2026degree付款／不發LoA不同。JPETS僅個人適用按政府核，不全設臺灣學生檢查。 現在外國學生頁延簽通常在期限三月前開始，由校方委任行政書士处理；學位新生首次延簽前校證明、part-time許可／薪資只對有工作者，銀行與在學／成績／護照／在留卡原件按該程序，不当incoming初次八件。費用要查ISA當期，未造6000新價格。 臨時離日約一周前交校方表，再入境不得超過個人在留期限；打工須個人許可，host春假仍28h週的文字不是自行核發許可。年金減免需申請，不套自動免繳。

大学で教育を受けるために必要な在留資格（「留学」など）を有していない方は、出入国在留管理局への申請手続が必要なため2次手続（学費納入）後、3月７日（土）までに国際センターへ申し出てください。
５．入学許可証について
本学では、「入学許可証」の発行はしておりません。在学中の日本語学校等で提出を求められている場合でも、対応しかねますので、ご了承ください。

問い合わせ窓口について
問い合わせ内容によって窓口が変わります。詳細は以下画像でご確認ください。
外国人留学生の皆さんへ（在留資格等申請に関するお知らせ）
本学に在籍する外国人留学生（在留資格「留学」）の方に、以下の項目の学内申請手続きについてご案内しております。
在留期間更新許可申請（留学）

【よくある質問】
在留資格申請でよくいただく質問について、Q&Aにまとめていますので参考にしてください。
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1NQ5i19sSO7NgLkbkUK4x0tL-Oc10eBXDSS_wkByxsY8/edit?usp=sharing
在留期間更新許可申請（留学）の更新申請と必要書類
出入国在留管理局への申請書類の提出や在留カードの受領について、駒澤大学が業務委託にて行っております。
つきましては、在留資格が「留学」の留学生は以下手順に従って、在留資格更新手続きを行ってください。
※留学生（申請者）本人が、出入国在留管理局へ赴く必要はありません。
【在留資格更新手続き手順】
ステップ１
在留期限の３か月前の月末（※）までに、国際センターから対象留学生に更新案内のメールを送信します。
※（例）在留期限が６月１２日の場合、３月３１日までに案内メールを送信
※案内メールが届かない方は、国際センターに問い合わせてください。
ステップ２
委託先の行政書士より、対象留学生に更新手続きについての詳細メールが送信されます。
ステップ３
対象留学生は「ステップ2」に従って、手続きをすすめてください。
なお、基本的な必要資料は以下の通りです。（詳細内容はSETP2の案内に従ってください。）
・申込書（指定書式）
・在留資格更新許可申請書（本人用、指定書式）
・資格外活動許可申請書（指定書式）
（※アルバイトをする場合のみ提出必要）
・アルバイトの給与明細書
（※アルバイトをしている場合のみ）
・銀行の通帳コピー
・在学証明書原本
・成績証明書原本
・パスポート原本
・在留カード原本
・入学前の学校の「卒業（修了）証明書」、「成績・出席証明書」
→新入生および入学後初めての更新の場合のみ提出必要
ステップ４
委託先が出入国在留管理局への取次申請を行います。
ステップ５
審査終了後、出入国管理局から対象留学生宛てに
在留許可期間に応じた在留許可手数料支払いに
ついての
メール連絡が入ります。　速やかに
コンビニ決済または銀行決済を済ませてください。
→在留許可手数料については、
出入国在留管理局のHP
で確認することができます。
ステップ６
新しい在留カードの交付後、委託先から対象留学生宛てにメール連絡が入ります。
国際センター窓口で、新・旧在留カードとパスポートを受け取ってください。
その際は学生証をご提示ください。
資格外活動の注意事項
アルバイトをする場合は、
「資格外活動許可申請書」
を同時に提出してください。在留資格「留学」は、「資格外許可申請」を取得しないとアルバイトはできません。
アルバイトは週 28 時間以内と入管法で定められています。
夏休み・冬休みは 8 時間以内/1 日可能（１週間４０時間を超えないこと）となります。ただし、春休みについては本学では学則に定められていないため、1月の定期試験終了時から 3月末までも週 28 時間以内となります。
風俗営業（スナック・キャバレー・パチンコ・ゲームセンターなど）や性風俗特殊営業店でのアル バイトは禁じられています。このような場所での受付やビラ配り、皿洗いや掃除をすることも禁止されています。
在留資格更新申請中の場合、在留期限（資格外活動許可期限）が切れた日より、アルバイトはできなくなります。
※定められた規則を守らない場合は、資格外活動違反となり、処罰や強制送還の対象となり、日本での留学生活ができなくなりますので十分に注意してください。
みなし再入国許可について（日本から一時出国する人）
日本を出国し、1年以内に再入国する場合は「みなし再入国制度により出国」できます。
出国時に「再入国EDカード」の「□一時的な出国であり、再入国する予定です」にレ点(チェック)をし、みなし再入国許可を得てから出国してください。
再入国の期限は出国後1年以内、在留期限が1年未満の場合は在留期限までに日本に入国してください。
（在留資格更新申請中の場合は、もとの在留期間の満了日から2カ月を経過する日までの間、再入国が可能です。）
詳細は
出入国管理局のHP
を参照してください。
一時帰国や海外旅行等で日本を離れる場合は、日本を出国する1週間前までを目途に、大学へ帰国届を提出する必要があります。

25/Sep/2026
Pre-Entry Tuberculosis Screening to Be Launched in Indonesia.
26/Dec/2025
To apply for a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) or a visa,
applicants must undergo tuberculosis (TB) screening at a designated Panel Clinic
and submit an official JPETS Clearance Certificate issued by that clinic.
Please note:
- Only certificates issued by a designated Panel Clinic will be accepted as the official one.
- Any fraudulent act, including the falsification of certificates, may cause a significant result on your COE/visa application.
What's JPETS ?
Japan Pre-Entry Tuberculosis Screening (JPETS) is a TB test to certify with the TB Clearance Certificate that foreign nationals who intend to enter Japan from target countries and stay for a medium- to long-term do not have active tuberculosis by undergoing a chest x-ray examination, etc. at a Panel Clinic before traveling to Japan.
Applicants subject to JPETS
TB screening will apply to nationals of the Philippines, Viet Nam, Indonesia, Nepal, Myanmar, and China (*1) who intend to enter and stay in Japan as “mid- to long-term residents” (*2) (excluding re-entry permit holders) or under the provisions of Notifications No. 53 (Digital Nomad) or No. 54 (Spouse or Child of Digital Nomad) on Designated Activities.
(*1) Regarding Myanmar, and China, procedures are being coordinated and the commencing date is yet to be determined.
(*2) “Mid- to long-term residents” refers to individuals specified in Article 19-3 of the Immigration Control and Refugee Recognition Act (foreign nationals who are residing in Japan with a status of residence, excluding those who fall into one of the following categories: (1) a person who has been granted a period of stay of not exceeding three months; (2) a person who has been granted the status of residence of “Temporary Visitor”; (3) a person who has been granted the status of residence of “Diplomat” or “Official”; and (4) a person prescribed by Ministry of Justice Order as being equivalent to a person mentioned in (1) through (3)).
[Supplementary information]
If the residence permit or other documentation issued by the government of the applicant’s place of residence confirms that their current place of residence is outside the target countries or regions, the applicant will be exempt from the TB screening.
In addition, among nationals of the target countries, the following categories of persons will be temporarily exempt from this screening:
(*) JET Programme participants, JICA trainees (both long-term and short-term), international students of JICA’s Project for Human Resource Development Scholarship (JDS), participants
to the long-term and mid-term invitation programs of Japan Foundation, Japanese Government Scholarship students with an embassy recommendation, foreign students who enter Japan under commissioned education and training programs, nurses and care workers accepted under Economic Partnership Agreements (EPAs) with applicable countries, specified skilled workers, foreign nationals who enter Japan under the provision of Notification No. 55 (specified  motor  vehicle  transportation  business  preparation)  on  Designated  Activities, and foreign nationals who enter Japan under the Project to Accept Foreigners Conducting Housekeeping Services in National Strategic Special Zones (pursuant to the Act on National Strategic Special Zones, Article 16-4)
The screening process
Applicants will undergo a medical examination and chest X-ray (or sputum test at the doctor’s discretion if there are concerns) at Panel Clinics located in the target countries for screening (see below).
TB Clearance Certificate will be issued by the Panel Clinic when the applicant does not have active tuberculosis.
Applicants will be required to submit the TB Clearance Certificate when applying for a Certificate of Eligibility (or when applying for a visa at a Japanese diplomatic mission abroad in cases where they apply for a visa without obtaining a Certificate of Eligibility).
[Supplementary information]
Applicants will be required to present a valid passport for verifying their identity.
The cost of the TB screening will be borne by the applicant.
The number of days expected for issuance of the TB Clearance Certificate and the cost may vary depending on the medical facility.
The validity of the TB Clearance Certificate will be valid for 180 days from the date of the chest X-ray, in principle. (The validity period of the Certificate may be reduced to 90 days depending on conditions. Please contact the Panel Clinic for further details.)
Applicants must keep their personal copy of the TB Clearance Certificate, as they may be required to present it even after entering Japan.
[The screening flow]
(＊1)Those who stay for more than 3 months  for study, work, etc.
(＊2)Designated by the Government of Japan
The designated Panel Clinic :
・Conducts medical interview, physical examination, chest X-ray, and sputum examinations (If active TB is suspected).
・Uploads examination results on JPETS Information Management System (Online system for Japan Pre-Entry TB Screening).
・Issues a Tuberculosis Clearance Certificate if active TB is not suggested.

FAQ
Q1
What are the reasons for starting pre-entry TB screening?
A
In recent years, the number of foreign-born TB cases has been increasing in Japan.  In 2025, 23.8% of the newly notified TB cases were foreign-born.
In addition, several countries other than Japan have introduced TB screening for foreign nationals as a TB control measure for those entering the country. In view of the situation of TB cases in Japan, Pre-Entry TB screening will be introduced to nationals of countries with a particularly large number of TB cases in Japan, and who intend to enter Japan and stay for a medium- to long-term period, to ensure that they do not have active TB before traveling to Japan.
Q2
Which are the countries and people subject to pre-entry TB screening?
A
Countries subject to screening shall be countries with a large proportion of foreign-born cases diagnosed with TB during their stay in Japan (the Philippines, Viet Nam, Indonesia, Nepal, Myanmar, and China (hereafter collectively referred to as the “target countries”)). As for the people subject to screening, they shall be nationals of target countries who intend to enter and stay in Japan as mid- to long-term residents (*) (excluding re-entry permits holders) or under the provisions of Notifications No. 53 (Digital Nomad) or No. 54 (Spouse or Child of Digital Nomad) on Designated Activities.
However, if the residence permit or other documentation issued by the government of the applicant’s place of residence confirms that their current place of residence is outside the target countries or region, the applicant will be exempted from the TB screening.
JET Programme participants, JICA trainees (both long-term and short-term ),  international students of JICA’s Project for Human Resource Development Scholarship (JDS), participants to the long-term and mid-term invitation programs of Japan Foundation, Japanese Government Scholarship students with an embassy recommendation, foreign students who enter Japan under commissioned education and training programs, nurses and care workers accepted under Economic Partnership Agreements (EPAs) with applicable countries, specified skilled workers, foreign nationals who enter Japan under the provision of Notification No. 55 (specified motor vehicle transportation business preparation) on Designated Activities, and foreign nationals who enter Japan under the Project to Accept Foreigners Conducting Housekeeping Services in National Strategic Special Zones (pursuant to the Act on National Strategic Special Zones, Article 16-4) will be temporarily exempted from screening.
(*) “Mid- to long-term residents” refers to individuals specified in Article 19-3 of the Immigration Control and Refugee Recognition Act (foreign nationals who are residing in Japan with a status of residence, excluding those who fall into one of the following categories: (1) a person who has been granted a period of stay of not exceeding three months; (2) a person who has been granted the status of residence “Temporary Visitor”; (3) a person who has been granted the status of residence of “Diplomat” or “Official”; and (4) a person prescribed by Ministry of Justice Order as being equivalent to a person mentioned in (1) through (3)).
Q3
What is the screening process?
A
Applicants will undergo a medical examination and chest X-ray (or sputum test at the doctor’s discretion if there are concerns) at designated medical facility (hereafter referred as Panel Clinic) located in the target countries for screening (see below).
TB Clearance Certificate will be issued by the Panel Clinic when the applicant does not have active tuberculosis
Applicants will be required to submit the TB Clearance Certificate when applying for a Certificate of Eligibility (or when applying for a visa at a Japanese diplomatic mission abroad in cases where they apply for a visa without obtaining a Certificate of Eligibility).
* People who are diagnosed with active TB must undergo another TB examination at a Panel Clinic after completing treatment.
Q4
What is the legal grounds for JPETS?
A
Tuberculosis is defined as a Class II infectious disease under Article 6, paragraph (3), item (ii) of the Act on the Prevention of Infectious Diseases and Medical Care for Patients with Infectious Diseases (Act No. 114 of 1998).
Article 5, paragraph (1), item (i) of the Immigration Control and Refugee Recognition Act (Cabinet Order No. 319 of 1951; hereinafter, "Immigration Control Act") stipulates that suffering from a Class II infectious disease constitutes grounds for being denied entry into Japan. In principle, foreign nationals who have active TB do not meet the conditions for landing in Japan set forth under Article 7, paragraph (1), item (i) of the Immigration Control Act and will thus not be admitted entry into Japan.
In addition, based on the provisions of Article 7-2 of the Immigration Control Act, the examination process of the Application for the Certificate of Eligibility requires verification that the individual has conformed to the entry conditions set forth under Article 7, paragraph (1), item (ii) of the same Act.
Moreover, based on the provisions of Article 6-2, paragraph (5) of the Regulation for Enforcement of the Immigration Control Act, authorities may refuse to issue the Certificate of Eligibility when the applicant evidently does not conform to the conditions set forth in Article 7, paragraph (1), items (i), (iii) or (iv) of the Immigration Control Act.
Thus, in the application process for Certificate of Eligibility, Immigration Services Agency shall require the TB Clearance Certificate as a means of confirming that he/she satisfies the entry conditions set forth under Article 7, paragraph (1), item (ii) of the Immigration Control Act.
In the visa application process, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (and its diplomatic missions abroad), based upon the Criteria of Visa Issuance, shall require the TB Clearance Certificate from the applicant to confirm that the applicant does not fall under any of the items of Article 5, paragraph (1) of the Immigration Control Act.
Q5
What is a Panel Clinic?
A
Panel Clinics are medical facilities designated by the Japanese government to ensure the quality of pre-entry TB screening. Japanese diplomatic missions in target countries recommend local medical facilities that meet the requirements set by the Japanese government, and the Centre for Japan-Pre-entry TB Screening Quality Assessment, commissioned by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) of Japan, inspects these facilities. The facilities that meet the criteria are designated as Panel Clinics by the Japanese government.
Q6
When will the screening commence?
A
The screening will commence gradually starting with target countries for which coordination has been completed.
As of September 25 2026, the dates for the start of reception for medical examination at Panel Clinics and introduction of the mandatory requirement for submission of the TB Clearance Certificate when applying for a Certificate of Eligibility or a visa are outlined below.

Can the “chest X-ray examination” required for the Pre-Entry Tuberculosis (TB) Screening Program and the “health status assessment” required under the Employment for Skill Development Program be undertaken at the same time?
A
JPETS is intended to confirm, prior to entry into Japan, that the applicant does not have active tuberculosis, thereby contributing to infectious disease control measures. This purpose differs from the health condition verification required when applying for approval of an Employment for Skill Development Plan under the Employment for Skill Development Program, and the respective requirements are also different.
However, because the results of a chest X-ray examination conducted by a Panel Clinic may be regarded as satisfying the chest X-ray examination requirement within the comprehensive medical examination required for the acceptance of foreign nationals under the Employment for Skill Development Program, some applicants may wish to undergo both JPETS and the comprehensive medical examination simultaneously at a Panel Clinic.
For information on designated panel clinics where both examinations may be undertaken concurrently, please refer to the list below.
◇Designated Panel Clinics Offering Same-Day Examinations◇ (PDF)
See ｍore FAQ
Notification to mid- to long-term residents in Japan
Mid- to long-term residents in Japan who originate from or have stayed in countries on the
World Health Organization’s list of high TB burden countries
, or who have been identified as being at risk of developing TB during their pre-entry TB screening, should seek medical examination in a medical facility if they have any TB symptoms (cough, sputum expectoration, mild fever, or body lethargy lasting more than two weeks). Those who are eligible for medical examinations provided by schools, workplaces, or local governments, should strive to undergo regular medical examinations.
If you develop TB in Japan, make sure you get the treatment you need. The public health center in your area of residence handles procedures related to provision of public funds to partially cover medical expenses involved in treating TB and provides assistance with taking medication.

Enroll in Pension System
All residents of Japan between age 20 and 59, regardless of nationality, must be covered by National Pension by law. There are three types of insured persons of National Pension according to their status as follows:
Category Ⅰ insured persons (self-employed persons, students, agricultural, forestry and fishery workers, unemployed persons)
Category Ⅱ insured persons (company workers and public sector workers)
Category Ⅲ insured persons (economically-dependent spouses of category Ⅱ insured persons)
Category Ⅰ Insured Persons
All residents of Japan between age 20 and 59 who are not Category Ⅱ or Ⅲ insured persons (e.g. self-employed persons, students, agricultural, forestry and fishery workers, unemployed persons.)
When you become subject to Category Ⅰ insured person, you need to submit, by yourself, application to enroll in as Category I insured person to the municipal office of your place of residence within 14 days.
Enrollment in National Pension
Note:Foreign nationals with specific visa (i.e. medical stay/long stay for sightseeing) are not subject to coverage of National Pension as Category Ⅰ insured persons.
Category Ⅱ Insured Persons
Company workers and public sector workers under 70 who are covered in Employees’ Pension Insurance  (except for persons age 65 or older who are eligible for old-age pension.)
When you become subject to the Category Ⅱ insured person, your employer needs to submit “Application to Enroll in EPI / EHI.”
Enrollment in Employees' Pension Insurance
Notes:
You must be covered as Category Ⅰ insured person for the period from your entry to Japan until you become Category Ⅱ insured person.
Mariners shall be covered by Seamen’s Insurance system.
Enrollment in Seamen's Insurance
Category Ⅲ Insured Persons
Category Ⅱ insured persons’ economically-dependent spouses between age 20 and 59, residing in Japan (excluding spouse of Category Ⅱ insured person who reached age 65 and eligible for Old-age Basic Pension.)
When you become subject to the Category Ⅲ insured person, employer of your spouse needs to submit “National Pension: Application to Enroll in as Category Ⅲ Insured Person.”
Report of Dependents
Notes:
You must be covered as Category Ⅰ insured person for the period from your entry to Japan until you become Category Ⅲ insured person.
Foreign nationals with specific visa (i.e. medical stay/long stay for sightseeing) are not subject to coverage of National Pension as the Category Ⅲ insured person.

Student Life
We are here to provide support so that each of you can lead a full university life.
The Careers Center
The Careers Center makes time to meet with you individually, and provides tailor-made careers advice. The Careers Center provides students with not only support in applying for various qualifications courses, internship programs and joint company information sessions, but also with practical lectures on how to join in group discussions and how to prepare for job interviews.
Welfare
The Health Care Center
The Health Care Center provides not only first-aid treatment for sudden illness and injury but also medical care and counseling for physical and mental concerns. Whether you have a condition upon entering university or develop a condition after entering university which may affect your studies, you can consult doctors who specialize in internal medicine, surgery, orthopedics, and psychosomatic internal medicine. This center also offers health guidance about first-aid treatment and the prevention of illness.
The Student Counseling Room
It is natural for students to have various concerns and worries during their time at university. Dealing with such concerns and worries one at a time by yourself means you will be strong enough to enter society after graduation. However, it is no good allowing these worries to build up inside so that the situation worsens. At these times, the Student Counseling Room comes into play. Here you can consult our professional counselors, advisors and lawyers in total confidentiality about your concerns no matter how small or big they may be.
The International Center
The International Center, established in May, 1988, is the office for the international exchange of students and scholars. The center promotes the internationalization of the University. One of its main activities is to teach Japanese language and culture to international students and to the Japanese returnee students who have lived extensively in foreign countries. The center also provides English language instruction for Komazawa University students.
Dormitory
International Exchange House
Komazawa University has a dormitory with 18 private rooms and three rooms with two bed rooms. This accommodation is available only for official exchange students, visiting scholars and researchers. The International Center assigns the rooms to official exchange students as its first priority, and secondly to visiting scholars and researchers.
room202 (sample)
Clubs and Activities
Sports Association
The members of the Sports Association are the stars who take part in official matches to uphold the honour of the University and the club. All groups which are members of the Komazawa University Sports Association are affiliated members of the various sports federations. If you have the motivation, even complete beginners can become active members.
Cultural and Arts Clubs
These groups were established half a century ago and have a long tradition. You can really make the most of your time at university by joining one of these cultural, arts, study or performance clubs, where you will be able to make new friends and meet new challenges.

委託先の行政書士より、対象留学生に更新手続きについての詳細メールが送信されます。
ステップ３
対象留学生は「ステップ2」に従って、手続きをすすめてください。
なお、基本的な必要資料は以下の通りです。（詳細内容はSETP2の案内に従ってください。）
・申込書（指定書式）
・在留資格更新許可申請書（本人用、指定書式）
・資格外活動許可申請書（指定書式）
（※アルバイトをする場合のみ提出必要）
・アルバイトの給与明細書
（※アルバイトをしている場合のみ）
・銀行の通帳コピー
・在学証明書原本
・成績証明書原本
・パスポート原本
・在留カード原本
・入学前の学校の「卒業（修了）証明書」、「成績・出席証明書」
→新入生および入学後初めての更新の場合のみ提出必要
ステップ４
委託先が出入国在留管理局への取次申請を行います。
ステップ５
審査終了後、出入国管理局から対象留学生宛てに
在留許可期間に応じた在留許可手数料支払いに
ついての
メール連絡が入ります。　速やかに
コンビニ決済または銀行決済を済ませてください。
→在留許可手数料については、
出入国在留管理局のHP
で確認することができます。
ステップ６
新しい在留カードの交付後、委託先から対象留学生宛てにメール連絡が入ります。
国際センター窓口で、新・旧在留カードとパスポートを受け取ってください。
その際は学生証をご提示ください。
資格外活動の注意事項
アルバイトをする場合は、
「資格外活動許可申請書」
を同時に提出してください。在留資格「留学」は、「資格外許可申請」を取得しないとアルバイトはできません。
アルバイトは週 28 時間以内と入管法で定められています。
夏休み・冬休みは 8 時間以内/1 日可能（１週間４０時間を超えないこと）となります。ただし、春休みについては本学では学則に定められていないため、1月の定期試験終了時から 3月末までも週 28 時間以内となります。
風俗営業（スナック・キャバレー・パチンコ・ゲームセンターなど）や性風俗特殊営業店でのアル バイトは禁じられています。このような場所での受付やビラ配り、皿洗いや掃除をすることも禁止されています。
在留資格更新申請中の場合、在留期限（資格外活動許可期限）が切れた日より、アルバイトはできなくなります。
※定められた規則を守らない場合は、資格外活動違反となり、処罰や強制送還の対象となり、日本での留学生活ができなくなりますので十分に注意してください。
みなし再入国許可について（日本から一時出国する人）
日本を出国し、1年以内に再入国する場合は「みなし再入国制度により出国」できます。
出国時に「再入国EDカード」の「□一時的な出国であり、再入国する予定です」にレ点(チェック)をし、みなし再入国許可を得てから出国してください。
再入国の期限は出国後1年以内、在留期限が1年未満の場合は在留期限までに日本に入国してください。
（在留資格更新申請中の場合は、もとの在留期間の満了日から2カ月を経過する日までの間、再入国が可能です。）
詳細は
出入国管理局のHP
を参照してください。
一時帰国や海外旅行等で日本を離れる場合は、日本を出国する1週間前までを目途に、大学へ帰国届を提出する必要があります。
出国届
（
Googleフォーム
）
Googleフォームで提出できない方は、国際センター窓口か教務部⑤番窓口に相談してください。

original_evidence.text:
Important Changes and Notes Regarding the SDW : Sandwich 
Program (Coursework-Based Exchange) 
     NEW / Important Changes 
1. Graduate-Level Course Enrollment Restriction (Effective Spring 2027)   
 From Spring Semester 2027, undergraduate students participating in the SDW Program will 
no longer be allowed to enroll in graduate-level courses.  
 Students should consider this change when preparing study plans and discussing credit 
transfer arrangements with their home institution.  
 Until the Spring 2027 course list is published, students should refer to the current 
timetable for reference. 
 
2026 Grade 1 Exchange Program Exchange Program Student (Undergraduate) | Shibaura 
Institute of Technology Timetable Search 
 
 
2. Special Provision for Students from Five-Year Integrated Degree Programs 
 Students enrolled in integrated five-year degree programs may be considered academically 
equivalent to master's students during their senior years.  
 Eligible students may continue to enroll in graduate-level courses.  
 Partner institutions must explain which year(s) of their program are considered master's-
level equivalent.  
 Supporting documentation must be submitted through the TAO application system by the 
nominator. 
 
3. Mandatory Submission of Financial Support Documentation  
 Due to stricter immigration screening procedures, all student visa applicants must provide 
proof of financial capability.  
 Applicants must demonstrate sufficient financial resources to cover their living expenses 
during their stay. Details regarding the estimated monthly living expenses will be provided in 
the application system.  
 Supporting documents must be uploaded through the TAO application system.

original_evidence.text:
4. Research Activities for SDW Participants 
Eligibility 
 Only students enrolled in the SDW Program for two semesters (one academic year) are 
eligible. 
 
Requirements 
Students wishing to conduct research activities must: 
 Apply during the same application period as the REP (Research Exchange Program). 
 Obtain prior approval from the prospective academic supervisor (laboratory faculty 
member). 
 Submit the same application documents required for the REP Program, including:  
o Curriculum Vitae (CV) 
o Research Proposal 
o Any other required supporting documents 
 Pay the facility usage fee specified in the REP Program application guidelines. 
 
Important Notes 
 Research activities will only be permitted after all required application procedures have 
been completed and approved. 
 Final approval is subject to review by both the University and the prospective academic 
supervisor. 
 
 
5. No Extension of the SDW Program During Enrollment  
 
 Effective from Fall 2026, students who enroll for one semester are not permitted to extend 
their participation in the Sandwich Program during their period of enrollment. Applicants 
must carefully decide at the time of application whether to register for one semester or 
two semesters. 
 Please note that students who enroll for one semester are not permitted to switch from the 
Sandwich Program to the REP Program, as stated in Item 4 above.

original_evidence.text:
Important Changes and Notes Regarding the REP 
(Research Exchange Program) 
Please ensure that the following important information is communicated to students prior to 
nomination and application for the REP Program. 
 
     NEW / Important Changes 
 
1. Simultaneous Participation in the SDW Program (Coursework -Based Exchange Program) Is 
Not Permitted （NEW） 
 
Due to the increasing number of SDW participants, SIT expects that available course capacity 
will need to be prioritized for students officially enrolled in the SDW Program. As a result, it has 
become difficult to accommodate requests from REP students who wish to enroll in courses in 
addition to their research activities. Although REP students staying for one semester were 
previously allowed to take courses upon request, this arrangement will no longer be available. 
Accordingly: 
• Students participating in the REP (Research Exchange Program) are not eligible to 
participate in the SDW Program (coursework -based exchange program) at the same 
time. 
• Students admitted to the REP Program will engage exclusively in research activities . 
• Course enrollment will not be permitted  for REP students. 
 
 
2. Mandatory Submission of Financial Support Documentation  
Beginning in July 2026, the Immigration Services Agency of Japan will implement stricter 
screening procedures for student visa applications. As a result, all students applying for a 
student visa will be required to provide documentation demonstrating sufficient financial 
resources to support themselves during their stay in Japan. 
Accordingly: 
• All student visa applicants must submit financial support documentation. 
• Applicants must demonstrate sufficient financial resources to cover their living expenses 
during their stay. Details regarding the estimated monthly living expenses will be 
provided in the application system. 
• Detailed instructions regarding the required documents will be provided through the TAO 
Online Application System. Applicants will be required to upload the designated 
supporting documents through TAO.

■ A: Applicants Who Have Obtained Preliminary Acceptance from a Prospective Academic 
Supervisor 
 
The applicant must submit either one of the following: 
• An official English-language proficiency test score listed in the application guidelines; or 
• An email from the prospective academic supervisor confirming:  
o their preliminary acceptance of the applicant; and 
o that the applicant possesses sufficient English proficiency to conduct research 
activities. 
 
 
■ B: Applicants Without a Designated Prospective Academic Supervisor  
The applicant must submit: 
• An official English proficiency test score demonstrating CEFR B2 level or above (e.g., 
TOEIC, TOEFL, IELTS, or another test specified in the application guidelines). 
 
 
Notes  
• English proficiency certificates issued independently by universities or other educational 
institutions (e.g., CEFR B2 certification letters) will not be accepted. 
• Please note that this requirement differs from the English proficiency requirements for 
the SDW Program. 
• Applicants whose native language is English or who are enrolled in a degree program taught 
entirely in English must submit:  
Letter issued by their home institution confirming this status 
This requirement applies regardless of whether the applicant falls under Category A or 
Category B.
