Enroll in Pension System
All residents of Japan between age 20 and 59, regardless of nationality, must be covered by National Pension by law. There are three types of insured persons of National Pension according to their status as follows:
Category Ⅰ insured persons (self-employed persons, students, agricultural, forestry and fishery workers, unemployed persons)
Category Ⅱ insured persons (company workers and public sector workers)
Category Ⅲ insured persons (economically-dependent spouses of category Ⅱ insured persons)
Category Ⅰ Insured Persons
All residents of Japan between age 20 and 59 who are not Category Ⅱ or Ⅲ insured persons (e.g. self-employed persons, students, agricultural, forestry and fishery workers, unemployed persons.)
When you become subject to Category Ⅰ insured person, you need to submit, by yourself, application to enroll in as Category I insured person to the municipal office of your place of residence within 14 days.
Enrollment in National Pension
Note:Foreign nationals with specific visa (i.e. medical stay/long stay for sightseeing) are not subject to coverage of National Pension as Category Ⅰ insured persons.
Category Ⅱ Insured Persons
Company workers and public sector workers under 70 who are covered in Employees’ Pension Insurance  (except for persons age 65 or older who are eligible for old-age pension.)
When you become subject to the Category Ⅱ insured person, your employer needs to submit “Application to Enroll in EPI / EHI.”
Enrollment in Employees' Pension Insurance
Notes:
You must be covered as Category Ⅰ insured person for the period from your entry to Japan until you become Category Ⅱ insured person.
Mariners shall be covered by Seamen’s Insurance system.
Enrollment in Seamen's Insurance
Category Ⅲ Insured Persons
Category Ⅱ insured persons’ economically-dependent spouses between age 20 and 59, residing in Japan (excluding spouse of Category Ⅱ insured person who reached age 65 and eligible for Old-age Basic Pension.)
When you become subject to the Category Ⅲ insured person, employer of your spouse needs to submit “National Pension: Application to Enroll in as Category Ⅲ Insured Person.”
Report of Dependents
Notes:
You must be covered as Category Ⅰ insured person for the period from your entry to Japan until you become Category Ⅲ insured person.
Foreign nationals with specific visa (i.e. medical stay/long stay for sightseeing) are not subject to coverage of National Pension as the Category Ⅲ insured person.

Exemption of National Pension Contributions
Page ID：150010-891-528-929
Last updated date：4 1 2026
Print
You may apply for exemption or postponement of contribution payments if you have temporarily financial difficulties. Student may apply for "Special Payment system for Students“ (payment postponement.)
Your future Old-age Basic Pension amount will be, however, lower than that with fully paid periods, if you have such contribution-exempted or postponed period. To avoid that, you may make retroactive payments to recover the past contribution-exempted periods for up to the past 10 years.
Index
Special Payment System for Students
Exemption / Postponement of the Contributions by Application
Statutory Exemption (e.g. beneficiary of Disability Basic Pension)
Recovery of the Past Exempted-Contribution
Special Payment System for Students
If you are a student and your income is less than a certain amount, you may be allowed to postpone contribution payments if your application is approved.
The period which the postponement was granted is considered as valid periods, not as non-payment period. So, if you become disabled or die during such periods, Disability / Survivors' Basic Pensions will be provided if you meet the following conditions;
(1) By the second month preceding the month of incident causing disability or death, you have filled at least two-thirds of your insured periods (months) with contribution paid periods and contribution-exempted periods.
(2) You have paid your contributions or you were exempted from contribution payments for the last 12 months up to the second month preceding the month of incident causing disability or death.
The granted periods count as qualifying periods for Old-age Basic Pension, however, unless you recover contribution payments afterwards, the periods will not be reflected to the amount of old-age benefits.
How to apply
You need to apply for it at the municipal office of your place of residence. One application covers up to one year, so you need to apply for it every year, if needed.
Exemption / Postponement of the Contributions by Application
Contribution Exemption
You may be exempt from contribution payments if the previous year's income of you, your spouse, or head of your household is limited, and if your application for exemption is granted.
The type of exemption and monthly contribution amount for the fiscal year 2026 are as follows;
full-amount-exemption
3/4-amount-exemption (you pay remaining \4,480)
half-amount-exemption (you pay remaining \8,960)
1/4-amount-exemption (you pay remaining \13,440)
If you fail to pay the due remaining contribution amount during the granted period, however, it will be considered to be non-payment rather than partial exemption.
For the purpose of calculation of your pension benefits, your periods of full-amount-exemption for March 2009 and earlier will count as one-third of full-contribution-paid periods (the 3/4-amount-exemption periods will count as half, the half-amount-exemption periods as two-thirds and the 1/4-amount-exemption periods as five-sixths.) Your periods of full-amount-exemption for April 2009 and later will count as half of full-contribution-paid periods (the 3/4-amount-exemption periods will count as five-eighths, the half-amount exemption periods as six-eighths and the 1/4-amount-exemption periods as seven-eighths.)
How to apply
You need to apply for it at the municipal office of your place of residence. One application covers up to one year, so you need to apply for it every year, if needed.
Statutory Exemption (e.g. beneficiary of Disability Basic Pension)
If you meet certain conditions specified by National Pension Act, e.g. beneficiary of the Disability Basic Pension, your contribution shall be exempted.
How to report
To establish exemption, you must report at the municipal office of your place of residence.
Recovery of the Past Exempted-Contribution
You may retroactively make payments to recover past contribution-exempted periods for up to the past 10 years. In that case, a specific index shall be imposed on your past contribution amount when you recover the old payments. That is, if you were granted the contribution exemption in a certain fiscal year (April to March) and if you wish to recover the contribution three or more fiscal years later, your old contribution amount is indexed by certain rate according to the age of the due contribution.
Note: Apply for the retroactive payments well in advance. If applied just before the deadline, your payments may not be technically accepted in time.
How to pay for exempted / postponed contribution in the past
For retroactive payments, contact your
nearest JPS branch office.

・2027 年 4 月には、杉本キャンパス内に国際交流宿舎 OMU I-Dorm Sugimoto（https://dormy-ac.com/page/omu-
ac/properties/kokusai-kouryu/）がオープンする予定です。宿舎についての詳細は、受入決定通知送付時に案内します。 
 
履修 ※現時点の情報であり内容は変更になる場合があります。

・学部生は『基幹教育科目』を履修します。原則専門科目の履修はできません。修士学生は『専門科目』を履修します。

半期ごとの成績は本人が在籍中に学生ポータルにて確認できます。 
 
在留資格認定証明書（以下、COE） 
・COE の取得については、 申請時に申告された内容に基づき、大阪公立大学が出入国在留管理庁へ代理で申請します。  
※申請に必要な書類については大学担当者宛に別途案内します。 
※COE の発行は出入国在留管理庁の審査によるものです。大阪公立大学では、 COE の発行および発行時期について保証
できません。出入国在留管理庁の COE 発行に係る審査が⾧引いた場合は、送付が遅れる場合があります。  
・日本国籍をお持ちの方（二重国籍を含む）は、日本国籍で入国いただくため COE 申請の対象外となります。入国後の手
続きに関しては、別途案内します。 
 
受入許可証（Letter of Acceptance）の発行 
本学での受入許可の準備ができ次第、受入許可証（PDF）を発行します。 
なお、選考内容に関するお問い合わせにはお答えできませんので、ご了承ください。  
※受入許可証発行後であっても、申請内容の虚偽が発覚した場合、受け入れを取り消すことがあります。  
 
査証（ビザ）申請 
受入許可証（Letter of Acceptance）を印刷の上、電子在留資格認定証明書（COE）とともに在外公館へ査証申請をしてく
ださい。 
※ 査証（ビザ）申請に時間を要する場合がありますので、余裕を持って申請してください。 
※ 在外公館によっては、査証申請に予約が必要な場合がありますので、ご自身でご確認ください。 
※ 査証（ビザ）を取得した後に、航空券を購入してください。

*If you use only the subway OSAKA METRO, you will need to pay about 340 yen for one-way transportation. In case of

*Depending on the route used, a one-way ticket may cost about 500 yen, while a commuter pass may require 16,000 
to 18,000 yen.

insurance.note: 2027春I-wing初期含保費4000–5000JPY，但簡章未列完整保障／投保品名／期限；同批Excel舊1340Gakkensai＋Gakkenbai／2400六月份或3420年Comprehensive不可當116保費。NHI、學生事故／責任、宿舍保障與母校海外全期保障各不同，沒有把它們合為全醫療或初次保單upload。 堺市2026/3英頁：符合居住／年齡且無其他公醫療等排除才申請NHI，年青成人承保就醫自負30%、依上一年所得與資格計费，不是所有醫療70%免。英頁舊hokensho仍在；2026/9/28日頁改MyNumber保險卡／無者資格確認書，資格資訊通知書單獨不能看診，更新有等待，按在留／年龄可縮短有效期。此為實際住所堺市才適用，不能套住杉本大阪市。

*As a rule, the deposit is applied to the payment of the final month's dormitory fees if there is no outstanding

【Initial cost】 
・Information regarding dormitory application will be provided when the letter of acceptance is sent, so please do 
not apply for the dormitory on your own. 
 ・Applicants for I-wing Nakamozu must submit a health certificate. Early preparation is highly recommended. 
【NOTE】 
・As a rule, exchange students are expected to stay at the International House I-wing Nakamozu on the Nakamozu 
Campus. 
*Due to the limited number of rooms, we cannot guarantee occupancy. We may also guide you to other dormitories.  
*We do not provide support for off-campus housing. 
・If the Sugimoto Campus or Morinomiya Campus is your main campus, please use the campus shuttle bus or public 
transportation. 
*The travel time from I-wing Nakamozu to Morinomiya Campus is about 1 hour. 
*If you use only the subway OSAKA METRO, you will need to pay about 340 yen for one-way transportation. In case of 
a commuter pass, about 12,000 yen per month is needed. 
*Depending on the route used, a one-way ticket may cost about 500 yen, while a commuter pass may require 16,000 
to 18,000 yen. 
*Exchange students are not eligible to purchase a “student commuter pass”. When purchasing a commuter pass, it 
must be a “regular commuter pass. 
・A new international student residence, OMU I-Dorm Sugimoto ( https://dormy-ac.com/page/omu-
ac/properties/kokusai-kouryu/), is expected to open on the Sugimoto Campus in April 2027. Detailed information

Overview of Sakai City National Health Insurance
Update：2026/3/11
For those unfamiliar with Japan’s medical insurance system, please read this overview of Sakai City’s National Health Insurance, including differences from systems in other countries, so that you can understand and use it properly to stay in good health. Detailed explanations of each system are omitted here. For more information, please contact the Health Insurance and Pension Division in the ward where you currently live or previously lived.
1. What is National Health Insurance (NHI)?
2. Benefits Available
3. Insurance Premiums
4. Inquiries (Japanese only)
1. What is National Health Insurance (NHI)?
In Japan, all residents are required to enroll in a public medical insurance program. National Health Insurance (NHI) is one such public medical insurance program, administered by prefectures and municipalities. It is a mutual support system under which every member contributes money to allow them to receive medical treatment in the event of illness or injury with peace of mind. NHI members can receive medical care at a medical institution with a small co-payment. However, they are obliged to pay insurance premiums.
Foreign nationals must enroll in NHI in any of the following cases. An application needs to be filed to join NHI.
- Persons aged 74 years or younger who are registered as residents of Sakai City
- Persons who live in Sakai City and whose status of residence is “Entertainer,” “Technical Intern Training,” “Dependent,” or “Designated Activities” with a period of stay of 3 months or less, but who are permitted to stay longer than 3 months by an employment agreement, etc.
However, the following cases are excluded.
Persons who are ineligible for NHI
- Persons who are enrolled in employees’ health insurance (including those who are dependents of such persons)
- Persons who are enrolled in the Latter-Stage Elderly Healthcare Insurance System
- Persons who are receiving public assistance
- Persons whose status of residence is “Designated Activities” and whose activities are specified as follows:
(1) Receiving medical treatment
(2) Taking care of persons stated in (1) in daily life
(3) Sightseeing, recreation, or other similar activities
(4) Spouses accompanying persons stated in (3)
If you fall under any of the above after enrolling in NHI, you will lose your eligibility for NHI, so please be sure to promptly submit a notification. If the notification is delayed, you may not be able to receive a refund even if you have overpaid your insurance premiums. After losing your eligibility, you cannot use your National Health Insurance card. If you receive medical care using the NHI card, you must return the medical expenses borne by NHI.
2. Benefits Available
If you present your health insurance card at a medical institution when you are sick or injured, you can receive medical examinations or treatments and be given prescription drugs by paying only part of the medical expenses. The proportion of medical expenses you need to pay at a medical institution is as follows.
From age 0 up to the end of the school year in which the person turns 6*: 20%
* The first March 31 after the person’s 6th birthday. For those born on April 1, the day before their 6th birthday.
From the beginning of the school year in which the person turns 7** up to age 69: 30%
** The first April 1 after the person’s 6th birthday. For those born on April 1, their 6th birthday.
From age 70*** up to 74: 20% or 30% (determined according to income)
*** The first day of the month following the month in which the person turns 70. For those born on the first day of each month, their 70th birthday.
Dental treatment, outpatient treatment, and hospitalization are all covered by the insurance. However, some medical treatments are not covered by the insurance. Please check with the medical institution at the time of your visit to see if the treatment is covered.
In Japan, it is not necessary to register in advance the medical institution you plan to visit in order to be covered by the insurance. Insurance coverage is available regardless of which medical institution you visit in Japan.
There is no deductible (which would require full payment up to a certain amount). You can receive a medical examination at the above co-payment rate from the time of your first visit.
If the monthly medical expenses paid by the same person to the same medical institution exceed the prescribed amount, the excess amount will be reimbursed.
A lump sum payment will be provided when an insured person gives birth or dies.
Medical examinations by NHI
In Sakai City, the following two types of medical examination are conducted at medical institutions designated by the City in order to help NHI members manage their health and prevent disease. Either medical examination can be undertaken once a year, subsidized by Sakai City.
●
“
Specific health checkup” with no co-payment required (Japanese)
Eligible persons: Those aged between 40 and 74 years
●
“
Complete physical examination” for which Sakai City subsidizes 70% of the fee (Japanese)
Eligible persons: Those aged between 30 and 74 years. There are requirements for payment of insurance premiums.
Subsidization of medical expenses for children
Sakai City subsidizes part of the medical expenses paid when children up to the age of 18 (up to the first March 31 after the date when they turn 18) who are registered as residents of the City and who are enrolled in a public medical insurance program such as NHI visit a medical institution to seek treatment for illness or injury.
Subsidization of medical expenses for children (Japanese)
3. Insurance Premiums
Insurance premiums are a valuable source of revenue for the NHI system, in order to pay for the medical expenses of insured persons. Please be sure to pay your insurance premiums by the due date. You are required to pay your insurance premiums even if you do not visit a medical institution. Also, your insurance premiums will not increase, regardless of the number of times you visit a medical institution.
(1) Determination and payment of insurance premiums
The amount to be paid as insurance premiums is determined based on your income from the previous year and other factors. A notification for insurance premiums will be sent in June each year. If you enroll in NHI in the middle of the year or if your insurance premiums are changed, you will be notified as necessary after the amount is decided.
The head of the household is responsible for paying the insurance premiums for all NHI members in the household.
The insurance premiums for one year should be paid in a total of 10 monthly installments from June to March of the following year.
As a general rule, the insurance premiums should be paid by direct debit. The payment due date (direct debit date) is the last day of each month from June to March (the 25th for December, or the next business day if December 25 or the last day of the month falls on a weekend or a holiday). The insurance premiums will be automatically deducted on the debit date. Please ensure prior to the debit date that the account balance is sufficient to cover the amount to be deducted. If you have not completed the direct debit application procedures, please apply at the ward office, bank, or post office.
Payment by direct debit (Japanese)
If you have difficulty paying the insurance premiums due to a disaster or unemployment, please consult with us as soon as possible, as you may be eligible for a premium reduction or exemption.
(2) What happens if you fail to pay by the due date?
You will be required to pay a delinquent charge.
A reminder or demand letter will be sent to you. If you receive a reminder or a demand letter, please pay your insurance premiums immediately with the enclosed payment form.
Reminder/Demand
If you continue to fail to pay your insurance premiums even after receipt of the reminder, your salary or savings may be subject to seizure. The seized property will be unable to be freely disposed of (for example, you will not be able to withdraw money from your bank account). If payment is still not made after that, the City will collect the seized property to be used to cover the delinquent insurance premiums.
A health insurance card with a shorter validity period will be issued in place of the regular health insurance card. If you continue to fail to pay your insurance premiums thereafter, you must return your health insurance card and will be issued a National Health Insurance Eligibility Certificate instead. Those who are issued an Eligibility Certificate must temporarily pay the full amount of medical expenses when they receive treatment at a medical institution.
4. Inquiries (Japanese only)
Please contact the Health Insurance and Pension Division of the ward office in the ward where you currently live (or the ward where you previously lived if you have moved).

更新日：2026年9月28日
マイナ保険証について
令和6年12月2日以降、マイナ保険証（健康保険証の利用登録がされたマイナンバーカード）を基本とする仕組みに移行し、従来の被保険者証は発行されなくなりました。
マイナ保険証のメリット
過去のお薬・診療データに基づく、より良い医療が受けられます。
突然の手術・入院でも高額支払いが不要になります。（保険料を滞納等されている場合を除く）
救急現場で、救急搬送中の適切な応急処置や病院の選定、搬送先の病院で活用されます。
マイナ保険証を利用するには登録が必要です
次のいずれかの方法で登録してください。
医療機関・薬局の受付（顔認証付きカードリーダー）
マイナポータル（パソコン・スマートフォンから）
セブン銀行ATM端末
マイナ保険証について、詳しくは以下のサイトを確認してください。
【厚生労働省HP】マイナンバーカードの健康保険証利用（マイナ保険証）について
資格確認書について
マイナ保険証をお持ちではない方には資格確認書を送付します。
保険医療機関等を受診する際には、資格確認書を提示してください。
資格確認書の有効期限は毎年7月31日です。
ただし、以下の場合、通常の有効期限より短い有効期限が記載されています。
(1)7月31日までに75歳になる方
75歳の誕生日に、後期高齢者医療制度の被保険者になります。そのため、有効期限は「75歳の誕生日の前日」になります。
(2)7月31日までに70歳になる方
有効期限は70歳の誕生月の月末まで（1日生まれの方は誕生月の前月末）です。
有効期限が切れるまでに、負担割合、発効期日が記載された資格確認書を別途送付します。
(3)7月31日までに在留期間が切れる外国籍の方
有効期限は在留期間の翌日までです。
(4)就学のため他市町村へ転出し、学生特例の申請をした方で7月31日までに卒業予定の方
有効期限は卒業予定日までです。
資格情報のお知らせについて
マイナ保険証をお持ちの方には資格情報のお知らせを送付します。
保険医療機関等を受診する際には、マイナ保険証で電子資格確認を受けてください。
資格情報のお知らせだけでは保険医療機関等を受診できません。顔認証付きカードリーダーの不具合など、何らかの事情で保険医療機関等でマイナ保険証が使えない時に、資格情報のお知らせや、マイナポータルの資格情報画面をダウンロードしたPDFファイルや、それを印刷したものをマイナンバーカードと一緒に提示することで、保険診療が受けられます。
なお、新たに国保へ加入したり、住所、氏名、世帯主などの変更の届出をした場合、マイナポータル等で確認できる資格情報が切り替わるまでに日数がかかる場合があります。
また、70歳以上の方の資格情報のお知らせには有効期限が記載されています。
有効期限は毎年7月31日です。
ただし、以下の場合、通常の有効期限より短い有効期限が記載されています。
(1)7月31日までに75歳になる方
75歳の誕生日に、後期高齢者医療制度の被保険者になります。そのため、有効期限は「75歳の誕生日の前日」になります。
(2)7月31日までに在留期間が切れる外国籍の方（70歳以上の方）
有効期限は在留期間の翌日までです。
なお、69歳以下の方の資格情報のお知らせには有効期限の記載がありません。毎年の更新による送付は無いため、大切に保管してください。
マイナ保険証利用時には電子証明書の有効期限をご確認ください
マイナンバーカードの電子証明書の有効期限が切れてから3 か月経過後は、マイナ保険証としての利用ができなくなります。
マイナンバーカードの更新や電子証明書についてご不明な点は、所管の区役所市民課へお問合せください。
詳しくは下記をご覧ください。
マイナンバーカードと電子証明書の更新について
資格確認書交付申請について
マイナ保険証がある⼈のうち、マイナンバーカードを紛失したり、⾼齢者や障害者などで、マイナ保険証での受診が困難な場合、申請により資格確認書の交付を受けることができます。
詳しくは下記をご覧ください。
資格確認書交付申請について（国民健康保険）
マイナンバーカードの健康保険証利用登録の解除について
マイナ保険証を持っている方が、健康保険証利用登録の解除を希望する場合は登録解除の申出ができます。
詳しくは下記をご覧ください。
マイナンバーカードの健康保険証利用登録の解除について（堺市国民健康保険及び後期高齢者医療制度）
70歳から74歳までの方の医療（資格確認書等と高齢受給者証の一体化）
堺市国民健康保険では、令和8年5月に資格確認書等と高齢受給者証が一体化され、70歳から74歳までの方へ交付していた高齢受給者証に記載していた情報が、資格確認書や資格情報のお知らせに併記されるようになりました。
70歳以上の方には負担割合、発効期日が記載された資格確認書又は資格情報のお知らせを交付します。
保険医療機関等を受診される際には、資格確認書又はマイナ保険証で受診してください。
一部負担金の割合　【70歳から74歳までの方】
70歳以上の方は一部負担金の割合が「2割」となります。ただし、現役並み所得者の方は、「3割」となります。
一部負担金の割合は、資格確認書又は資格情報のお知らせの負担割合欄でご確認ください。
一部負担金の割合が 「3割」の方で、70歳から74歳までの国保被保険者の合計収入額が特定の条件を満たす場合は、申請により一部負担金の割合が2割になります。また、自己負担限度額は「一般」区分が適用されます。
詳しくは下記をご覧ください。
一部負担金の割合　【70歳から74歳までの方】
在留期間を延長された外国籍の方の資格確認書等について
在留期間が切れた外国籍の方は、国民健康保険で保険医療機関等を受診できなくなります。
在留期間が切れる前に在留期間を延長した場合は、引き続き国民健康保険で保険医療機関等を受診できます。また、有効期限を更新した資格確認書等を送付します。
在留期間の延長手続き中に資格確認書等の有効期限が切れそうな場合は、次のものを持って所管の区役所保険年金課へ来てください。
必要なもの
在留期間の延長手続き中であることを証明するスタンプが押された在留カード又はオンラインで在留期間の延長を申請したことがわかる受付完了メール
資格確認書又は資格情報のお知らせ
資格確認書等は正しく使い、大切に保管しましょう
交付されたら、記載内容に間違いがないか確認してください
間違いがあった場合は、自分で書き直さずに所管の区役所保険年金課に届け出てください。
国民健康保険の資格（適用）がなくなった日以降は、使えません
堺市以外の市区町村へ転出した場合は転出日以降、会社など他の健康保険に加入した場合は加入日以降、または生活保護を受けるようになった場合は生活保護の開始日以降において、堺市国保の資格確認書等は使えません。堺市国保の資格確認書等を使って受診した場合は、堺市が負担した医療費を返していただくことになります。
資格確認書等を紛失したり汚したりした場合は、再発行ができます
再発行は、所管の区役所保険年金課に届け出てください。
なお、外出先での紛失や盗難にあった場合は、犯罪に使われるおそれもありますので、区役所への再発行の届出とは別に、警察署に紛失の届出をしてください。
資格確認書等の表記変更申出について
外国籍の方の氏名表記は、本名または住民基本台帳に登録されている通称名のいずれかを選択できます。また性同一性障害の方については、表面に記載している戸籍上の氏名・性別を、申出により記載変更できる場合があります。詳しくは、

Life in Japan
Insurance
HOME
Life in Japan
Insurance
National Health Insurance (NHI)
In Japan, a national health insurance system is available to reduce medical costs.
Foreign residents who will be staying in Japan for three months or more have to subscribe to the National Health Insurance program (NHI; also known as "Kokuho").
Registration Procedures
Register for the National Health Insurance at the municipal office after completing resident registration in your local municipal office.
Health Insurance Premium
Health insurance premium is calculated according to your previous year's income (including part-time jobs). Please be sure to report your income at the municipal office, as correct premium calculations cannot be made if income is not declared.
Reduction of Health Insurance Premium
Premiums are reduced if your previous year's income is below a certain threshold. However, your income must be declared in order to qualify for the reduction. Even if you had no or little income, you still need to declare your income, so don't forget to do so.
Coverage
When receiving treatment for injuries or illnesses, you have to present your insurance card to be eligible for the discounted payment. Since 70% of the total medical cost is covered by the National Health Insurance, you will need to pay 30% of the total medical bill. However, all medical expenses not covered by insurance are to be paid in full.
The National Health Insurance program has a system for refunding medical expenses that exceed your individual limit if your medical costs in a single month are high. In addition, if you need to be hospitalized, etc., you can apply for and receive an eligibility certificate that entitles you to receive the ceiling amount in advance. This will allow you to keep the amount you pay at the hospital to your individual limit.
Accident/Property Insurance and Mutual Aid (Kyosai)
To cover expenses incurred by an unexpected accident, etc. that is not covered by National Health Insurance, there are casualty insurance plans and personal liability insurance plans that international students can register for.
For example, the following cases would be covered:
If the oil you are using to deep-fry food catches fire and burns your kitchen, requiring the walls to be redone.
If you ride a bicycle and injure someone else, and must pay for their medical expenses.
If your room is burglarized while you are not there, and items, such as your personal computer or camera, are stolen.
Your school will provide you with information on various types of insurance to consider.
Personal Accident Insurance for Students Pursuing Education and Research ("Gakkensai")
This insurance is adopted by the majority of schools in Japan (universities, graduate schools, junior colleges and colleges of technology). Coverage is provided for injuries sustained during classes, commuting to and from school and other instances. Also available is insurance known as "Inbound Futai-Gakuso" as a means of supplementing coverage for international students who belong to the Gakkensai plan. Both of these insurance plans are offered by Japan Educational Exchanges and Services (a public interest incorporated foundation).
Note: Because these insurance plans are not available at certain schools, applicants are advised to contact the specific school to confirm.
University CO-OP's Kyosai
This is a university co-op insurance system you can enroll in while attending university.

Enroll in Pension System
All residents of Japan between age 20 and 59, regardless of nationality, must be covered by National Pension by law. There are three types of insured persons of National Pension according to their status as follows:
Category Ⅰ insured persons (self-employed persons, students, agricultural, forestry and fishery workers, unemployed persons)
Category Ⅱ insured persons (company workers and public sector workers)
Category Ⅲ insured persons (economically-dependent spouses of category Ⅱ insured persons)
Category Ⅰ Insured Persons
All residents of Japan between age 20 and 59 who are not Category Ⅱ or Ⅲ insured persons (e.g. self-employed persons, students, agricultural, forestry and fishery workers, unemployed persons.)
When you become subject to Category Ⅰ insured person, you need to submit, by yourself, application to enroll in as Category I insured person to the municipal office of your place of residence within 14 days.
Enrollment in National Pension
Note:Foreign nationals with specific visa (i.e. medical stay/long stay for sightseeing) are not subject to coverage of National Pension as Category Ⅰ insured persons.
Category Ⅱ Insured Persons
Company workers and public sector workers under 70 who are covered in Employees’ Pension Insurance  (except for persons age 65 or older who are eligible for old-age pension.)
When you become subject to the Category Ⅱ insured person, your employer needs to submit “Application to Enroll in EPI / EHI.”
Enrollment in Employees' Pension Insurance
Notes:
You must be covered as Category Ⅰ insured person for the period from your entry to Japan until you become Category Ⅱ insured person.
Mariners shall be covered by Seamen’s Insurance system.
Enrollment in Seamen's Insurance
Category Ⅲ Insured Persons
Category Ⅱ insured persons’ economically-dependent spouses between age 20 and 59, residing in Japan (excluding spouse of Category Ⅱ insured person who reached age 65 and eligible for Old-age Basic Pension.)
When you become subject to the Category Ⅲ insured person, employer of your spouse needs to submit “National Pension: Application to Enroll in as Category Ⅲ Insured Person.”
Report of Dependents
Notes:
You must be covered as Category Ⅰ insured person for the period from your entry to Japan until you become Category Ⅲ insured person.
Foreign nationals with specific visa (i.e. medical stay/long stay for sightseeing) are not subject to coverage of National Pension as the Category Ⅲ insured person.

Exemption of National Pension Contributions
Page ID：150010-891-528-929
Last updated date：4 1 2026
Print
You may apply for exemption or postponement of contribution payments if you have temporarily financial difficulties. Student may apply for "Special Payment system for Students“ (payment postponement.)
Your future Old-age Basic Pension amount will be, however, lower than that with fully paid periods, if you have such contribution-exempted or postponed period. To avoid that, you may make retroactive payments to recover the past contribution-exempted periods for up to the past 10 years.
Index
Special Payment System for Students
Exemption / Postponement of the Contributions by Application
Statutory Exemption (e.g. beneficiary of Disability Basic Pension)
Recovery of the Past Exempted-Contribution
Special Payment System for Students
If you are a student and your income is less than a certain amount, you may be allowed to postpone contribution payments if your application is approved.
The period which the postponement was granted is considered as valid periods, not as non-payment period. So, if you become disabled or die during such periods, Disability / Survivors' Basic Pensions will be provided if you meet the following conditions;
(1) By the second month preceding the month of incident causing disability or death, you have filled at least two-thirds of your insured periods (months) with contribution paid periods and contribution-exempted periods.
(2) You have paid your contributions or you were exempted from contribution payments for the last 12 months up to the second month preceding the month of incident causing disability or death.
The granted periods count as qualifying periods for Old-age Basic Pension, however, unless you recover contribution payments afterwards, the periods will not be reflected to the amount of old-age benefits.
How to apply
You need to apply for it at the municipal office of your place of residence. One application covers up to one year, so you need to apply for it every year, if needed.
Exemption / Postponement of the Contributions by Application
Contribution Exemption
You may be exempt from contribution payments if the previous year's income of you, your spouse, or head of your household is limited, and if your application for exemption is granted.
The type of exemption and monthly contribution amount for the fiscal year 2026 are as follows;
full-amount-exemption
3/4-amount-exemption (you pay remaining \4,480)
half-amount-exemption (you pay remaining \8,960)
1/4-amount-exemption (you pay remaining \13,440)
If you fail to pay the due remaining contribution amount during the granted period, however, it will be considered to be non-payment rather than partial exemption.
For the purpose of calculation of your pension benefits, your periods of full-amount-exemption for March 2009 and earlier will count as one-third of full-contribution-paid periods (the 3/4-amount-exemption periods will count as half, the half-amount-exemption periods as two-thirds and the 1/4-amount-exemption periods as five-sixths.) Your periods of full-amount-exemption for April 2009 and later will count as half of full-contribution-paid periods (the 3/4-amount-exemption periods will count as five-eighths, the half-amount exemption periods as six-eighths and the 1/4-amount-exemption periods as seven-eighths.)
How to apply
You need to apply for it at the municipal office of your place of residence. One application covers up to one year, so you need to apply for it every year, if needed.
Statutory Exemption (e.g. beneficiary of Disability Basic Pension)
If you meet certain conditions specified by National Pension Act, e.g. beneficiary of the Disability Basic Pension, your contribution shall be exempted.
How to report
To establish exemption, you must report at the municipal office of your place of residence.
Recovery of the Past Exempted-Contribution
You may retroactively make payments to recover past contribution-exempted periods for up to the past 10 years. In that case, a specific index shall be imposed on your past contribution amount when you recover the old payments. That is, if you were granted the contribution exemption in a certain fiscal year (April to March) and if you wish to recover the contribution three or more fiscal years later, your old contribution amount is indexed by certain rate according to the age of the due contribution.
Note: Apply for the retroactive payments well in advance. If applied just before the deadline, your payments may not be technically accepted in time.
How to pay for exempted / postponed contribution in the past
For retroactive payments, contact your
nearest JPS branch office.

Information for those who are　　　　　 bringing medicines for personal use　　　 into Japan
Information for those who are　　　　　 bringing medicines for personal use　　　 into Japan
To import medicines from overseas is subject to control by the Pharmaceutical Affairs Law and the
Customs Law to prevent health hazard caused by defective products.
Therefore, when you enter Japan, procedures should be done depending on your bringing medicines even if you have medicines for personal use.
1. Drugs, Quasi drugs
You can bring medicines for personal use into Japan once certain procedures are completed.
This is because there are patients who need continuous medication and travelers who need
medicines as belongings, however, when you bring narcotics and Stimulants' Raw Materials described in 4, please note that importing them from overseas is subject to control by other laws and rules.
To be more specific, when you bring medicines for personal use into Japan, you have to apply for
Import Confirmation, and receive it before you leave home, and show it to the officer at customs.
When you bring medicines for personal use into Japan up to the amount described below, you do not have to apply for Import Confirmation.
◆　Poison, Deadly poison, Prescription drug : Up to 1 month supply
◆　Drug for external use (excluding Poison, Deadly poison, Prescription drug) : Up to 24 per one item
◆　Injectable drug and Syringe for the drug: Up to 1 month supply
* Only "Pre-filled Syringe" or "Self-injection Kit"
◆　Other Drugs, Quasi drugs : Up to 2 month supply
In addition, no product containing
the designated pharmaceutical ingredients (see linked table)［116KB］
, which is sold in foreign countries/regions with advertisement on enhancing cerebral function and other mental effects, shall be imported, unless use of such a product is complying with doctor’s prescription or instruction.
However, it would be permissible for you to bring such a medicinal product into Japan by yourself,
in the purpose of self-medication during your stay.
Regardless of the description above, you cannot bring prohibited drugs and controlled drugs into
Japan.
Regarding details about application for Import Confirmation, please check
"Q&A for those who are importing medicines into Japan"
.

◆　Up to 24 per one item
(e.g. If you want to bring your lip sticks into Japan , you can have up to 24 regardless of brand or color)
3. Medical devices
Basically, the procedures are the same as in the case of drugs and quasi drugs.
When you bring medical devices for personal use into Japan up to the amount described below, you do not have to apply for Import Confirmation.
◆　Medical device for household use (e.g. electric massaging tools): 1 set
◆　Disposable contact lens: Up to 2 month supply
4. Narcotics (e.g. Morphine, Fentanyl), Stimulants' 　Raw Materials (e.g. Lisdexamfetamine)
It is strictly prohibited to import narcotics and Stimulants' Raw Materials into Japan except in the
case of prescribed narcotics and Stimulants' Raw Materials for a specific patient bringing them with
permission before you enter Japan.
When you bring prescribed narcotics and Stimulants' Raw Materials for personal use into Japan, you have to apply for permission by the Japanese Government   (the directors of the Regional Bureaus of Health and Welfare) and receive it before you leave home.
Regardless of the description above, you cannot bring prohibited or controlled narcotics, Stimulants' Raw Materials into Japan.

In case of bringing medicines, please read the following from Q1 to Q8, Q10 and

In case of sending medicines, please read the following Q1,3,4, Q7 to Q11. 
 
Q1. Can I bring /send general prescription medicine into Japan from overseas? 
 
A1. You can bring /send general prescription medicine into Japan without any special 
procedures on condition that  
(1)  you bring/send it only for personal use  
    (2)  it is not any prohibited drug in Japan such as Methamphetamine,  
(3)  it is not any especially controlled drug in Japan such as Narcotics 
(e.g.Morphine) and Stimulants' Raw Materials (e.g. Lisdexamfetamine),  
(4)  quantity is up to one month supply.  
(5)  it is not permitted to SEND Psychotropics, Narcotics and Stimulants' Raw 
Materials. 
 
Q2. How can I bring more than one month supply of general prescription medicine 
only for personal use into Japan?  
 
A2. You need to apply for Import Confirmation before entering Japan.  
 
Q3. How can I bring/send injection and injector only for personal use into Japan?  
 
A3. If you bring/send medicines with syringes for them (permissive self-injection like 
insulin) at the same time for less than 1 month supply, Certificate for Import 
Confirmation is not required. (Regarding to efficacy and dosage)  
However, if you import syringe only (without medicines), you need to apply for 
Import Confirmation as medical devices even if you import 1 piece.

 You have to take care never to correct the Certificate for Import Confirmation, or it

A7. It will be normally issued in a few business days (not including Saturday, Sunday

※I-wing なかもずから森之宮キャンパスまでの所要時間は約 1 時間です。

履修 ※現時点の情報であり内容は変更になる場合があります。

成績証明書 
成績証明書（英文）は受入期間終了後に大学担当者宛に PDF を送付します。 
※1 年間の受入の場合、半期ごとの成績証明書は発行されません。  
半期ごとの成績は本人が在籍中に学生ポータルにて確認できます。 
 
在留資格認定証明書（以下、COE） 
・COE の取得については、 申請時に申告された内容に基づき、大阪公立大学が出入国在留管理庁へ代理で申請します。  
※申請に必要な書類については大学担当者宛に別途案内します。 
※COE の発行は出入国在留管理庁の審査によるものです。大阪公立大学では、 COE の発行および発行時期について保証
できません。出入国在留管理庁の COE 発行に係る審査が⾧引いた場合は、送付が遅れる場合があります。  
・日本国籍をお持ちの方（二重国籍を含む）は、日本国籍で入国いただくため COE 申請の対象外となります。入国後の手
続きに関しては、別途案内します。 
 
受入許可証（Letter of Acceptance）の発行 
本学での受入許可の準備ができ次第、受入許可証（PDF）を発行します。 
なお、選考内容に関するお問い合わせにはお答えできませんので、ご了承ください。  
※受入許可証発行後であっても、申請内容の虚偽が発覚した場合、受け入れを取り消すことがあります。  
 
査証（ビザ）申請 
受入許可証（Letter of Acceptance）を印刷の上、電子在留資格認定証明書（COE）とともに在外公館へ査証申請をしてく
ださい。 
※ 査証（ビザ）申請に時間を要する場合がありますので、余裕を持って申請してください。 
※ 在外公館によっては、査証申請に予約が必要な場合がありますので、ご自身でご確認ください。 
※ 査証（ビザ）を取得した後に、航空券を購入してください。

*As a rule, the deposit is applied to the payment of the final month's dormitory fees if there is no outstanding

【重要】授業再開と履修手続についてのお知らせ / [Important]Resumption of Classes and Class Registration Procedures
​
*English follows below.
学生のみなさんへ
このたびのシステム障害により、学生のみなさんには、授業の休講や各種システムの利用停止など、多大なご不便とご心配をおかけしております。
10月9日（金）より授業を再開します。授業の受講や履修手続に必要な情報を以下のとおりお知らせします。\
1　授業の再開と受講時の確認事項
​
授業の実施方法と時間割・教室
​
対面授業だけでなく、オンライン授業についても受講環境の整備を進めています。各授業の実施方法は、担当教員から臨時Moodleのアナウンスメント等でお知らせします。
自身の時間割・教室は、臨時Moodleで確認してください。教室変更も確認できますので、授業前に最新の情報を確認してください。
教務日程
​
教務日程
（
英語版
はこちら）を更新しました。授業実施日、補講日等が変更になっていますので、ご確認をお願いします。
なお、10月12日（月・祝）の授業は月曜日の授業として、予定どおり実施します。
出席登録
​
10月9日（金）から、OMU＋（大学アプリ）でQRコードによる出席登録を利用できます。学生証をタッチする固定型出席登録端末は利用できません。

臨時Moodle

My Number (Individual Number)
What is the My Number (Individual Number)
The My Number is a 12‑digit number assigned to everyone registered as a resident in Japan, and is used for procedures such as taxes and social security. Your My Number is notified to you by the “Individual Number Notification” sent when you first register your residence in Japan.
What is the My Number Card (Individual Number Card)
The My Number Card is a photo ID card that contains your My Number (cards issued to applicants under one year of age do not include a photo). The My Number Card can be used not only for identity verification but also for certificate issuance at convenience‑store multifunction machines and as a health insurance card. Integration with residence cards is planned in the near future.
Applying for issuance of the My Number Card
You can apply for a card by using the methods below. About one month after application, an issuance notification (postcard) will be sent; bring the notification and your identity document(s) (e.g., a residence card) to your ward office to receive the card.
Application Method
How to apply
Online application
Scan the 2D code printed on the Individual Number Notification.
Postal application
Complete the issuance application form enclosed with the Individual Number Notification, attach a passport‑style photo, and mail it in the enclosed return envelope.
Application via a photo‑booth (ID‑photo kiosk)
Read the 2D code on the Individual Number Notification at an ID photo‑booth and apply there.
If you wish to obtain a My Number Card quickly, you can apply for expedited issuance at your ward office counter (issued in about one week). For details, see the Osaka City website page “About Expedited Issuance of the My Number Card.”

資格確認書等について　堺市
堺市ホームページではJavaScriptを使用しています。JavaScriptの使用を有効にしていない場合は、一部の機能が正確に動作しない恐れがあります。
お手数ですがJavaScriptの使用を有効にしてください。
このページの先頭です
このページの本文へ移動
資格確認書等について
更新日：2026年9月28日
マイナ保険証について
令和6年12月2日以降、マイナ保険証（健康保険証の利用登録がされたマイナンバーカード）を基本とする仕組みに移行し、従来の被保険者証は発行されなくなりました。
マイナ保険証のメリット
過去のお薬・診療データに基づく、より良い医療が受けられます。
突然の手術・入院でも高額支払いが不要になります。（保険料を滞納等されている場合を除く）
救急現場で、救急搬送中の適切な応急処置や病院の選定、搬送先の病院で活用されます。
マイナ保険証を利用するには登録が必要です
次のいずれかの方法で登録してください。
医療機関・薬局の受付（顔認証付きカードリーダー）
マイナポータル（パソコン・スマートフォンから）
セブン銀行ATM端末
マイナ保険証について、詳しくは以下のサイトを確認してください。
【厚生労働省HP】マイナンバーカードの健康保険証利用（マイナ保険証）について
資格確認書について
マイナ保険証をお持ちではない方には資格確認書を送付します。
保険医療機関等を受診する際には、資格確認書を提示してください。
資格確認書の有効期限は毎年7月31日です。
ただし、以下の場合、通常の有効期限より短い有効期限が記載されています。
(1)7月31日までに75歳になる方
75歳の誕生日に、後期高齢者医療制度の被保険者になります。そのため、有効期限は「75歳の誕生日の前日」になります。
(2)7月31日までに70歳になる方
有効期限は70歳の誕生月の月末まで（1日生まれの方は誕生月の前月末）です。
有効期限が切れるまでに、負担割合、発効期日が記載された資格確認書を別途送付します。
(3)7月31日までに在留期間が切れる外国籍の方
有効期限は在留期間の翌日までです。
(4)就学のため他市町村へ転出し、学生特例の申請をした方で7月31日までに卒業予定の方
有効期限は卒業予定日までです。
資格情報のお知らせについて
マイナ保険証をお持ちの方には資格情報のお知らせを送付します。
保険医療機関等を受診する際には、マイナ保険証で電子資格確認を受けてください。
資格情報のお知らせだけでは保険医療機関等を受診できません。顔認証付きカードリーダーの不具合など、何らかの事情で保険医療機関等でマイナ保険証が使えない時に、資格情報のお知らせや、マイナポータルの資格情報画面をダウンロードしたPDFファイルや、それを印刷したものをマイナンバーカードと一緒に提示することで、保険診療が受けられます。
なお、新たに国保へ加入したり、住所、氏名、世帯主などの変更の届出をした場合、マイナポータル等で確認できる資格情報が切り替わるまでに日数がかかる場合があります。
また、70歳以上の方の資格情報のお知らせには有効期限が記載されています。
有効期限は毎年7月31日です。
ただし、以下の場合、通常の有効期限より短い有効期限が記載されています。
(1)7月31日までに75歳になる方
75歳の誕生日に、後期高齢者医療制度の被保険者になります。そのため、有効期限は「75歳の誕生日の前日」になります。
(2)7月31日までに在留期間が切れる外国籍の方（70歳以上の方）
有効期限は在留期間の翌日までです。
なお、69歳以下の方の資格情報のお知らせには有効期限の記載がありません。毎年の更新による送付は無いため、大切に保管してください。
マイナ保険証利用時には電子証明書の有効期限をご確認ください
マイナンバーカードの電子証明書の有効期限が切れてから3 か月経過後は、マイナ保険証としての利用ができなくなります。
マイナンバーカードの更新や電子証明書についてご不明な点は、所管の区役所市民課へお問合せください。
詳しくは下記をご覧ください。
マイナンバーカードと電子証明書の更新について
資格確認書交付申請について
マイナ保険証がある⼈のうち、マイナンバーカードを紛失したり、⾼齢者や障害者などで、マイナ保険証での受診が困難な場合、申請により資格確認書の交付を受けることができます。
詳しくは下記をご覧ください。
資格確認書交付申請について（国民健康保険）
マイナンバーカードの健康保険証利用登録の解除について
マイナ保険証を持っている方が、健康保険証利用登録の解除を希望する場合は登録解除の申出ができます。
詳しくは下記をご覧ください。
マイナンバーカードの健康保険証利用登録の解除について（堺市国民健康保険及び後期高齢者医療制度）
70歳から74歳までの方の医療（資格確認書等と高齢受給者証の一体化）
堺市国民健康保険では、令和8年5月に資格確認書等と高齢受給者証が一体化され、70歳から74歳までの方へ交付していた高齢受給者証に記載していた情報が、資格確認書や資格情報のお知らせに併記されるようになりました。
70歳以上の方には負担割合、発効期日が記載された資格確認書又は資格情報のお知らせを交付します。
保険医療機関等を受診される際には、資格確認書又はマイナ保険証で受診してください。
一部負担金の割合　【70歳から74歳までの方】
70歳以上の方は一部負担金の割合が「2割」となります。ただし、現役並み所得者の方は、「3割」となります。
一部負担金の割合は、資格確認書又は資格情報のお知らせの負担割合欄でご確認ください。
一部負担金の割合が 「3割」の方で、70歳から74歳までの国保被保険者の合計収入額が特定の条件を満たす場合は、申請により一部負担金の割合が2割になります。また、自己負担限度額は「一般」区分が適用されます。
詳しくは下記をご覧ください。
一部負担金の割合　【70歳から74歳までの方】
在留期間を延長された外国籍の方の資格確認書等について
在留期間が切れた外国籍の方は、国民健康保険で保険医療機関等を受診できなくなります。
在留期間が切れる前に在留期間を延長した場合は、引き続き国民健康保険で保険医療機関等を受診できます。また、有効期限を更新した資格確認書等を送付します。
在留期間の延長手続き中に資格確認書等の有効期限が切れそうな場合は、次のものを持って所管の区役所保険年金課へ来てください。
必要なもの
在留期間の延長手続き中であることを証明するスタンプが押された在留カード又はオンラインで在留期間の延長を申請したことがわかる受付完了メール
資格確認書又は資格情報のお知らせ
資格確認書等は正しく使い、大切に保管しましょう
交付されたら、記載内容に間違いがないか確認してください
間違いがあった場合は、自分で書き直さずに所管の区役所保険年金課に届け出てください。
国民健康保険の資格（適用）がなくなった日以降は、使えません
堺市以外の市区町村へ転出した場合は転出日以降、会社など他の健康保険に加入した場合は加入日以降、または生活保護を受けるようになった場合は生活保護の開始日以降において、堺市国保の資格確認書等は使えません。堺市国保の資格確認書等を使って受診した場合は、堺市が負担した医療費を返していただくことになります。
資格確認書等を紛失したり汚したりした場合は、再発行ができます
再発行は、所管の区役所保険年金課に届け出てください。
なお、外出先での紛失や盗難にあった場合は、犯罪に使われるおそれもありますので、区役所への再発行の届出とは別に、警察署に紛失の届出をしてください。
資格確認書等の表記変更申出について
外国籍の方の氏名表記は、本名または住民基本台帳に登録されている通称名のいずれかを選択できます。また性同一性障害の方については、表面に記載している戸籍上の氏名・性別を、申出により記載変更できる場合があります。詳しくは、
こちら
をご覧ください。
禁止!!　他人との貸し借りは犯罪です
資格確認書等を他人に貸したり、また、他人から借りたりして不正に使用した場合は、刑法上の詐欺罪にあたり、貸した人も借りた人も罰せられます。

Enroll in Pension System
All residents of Japan between age 20 and 59, regardless of nationality, must be covered by National Pension by law. There are three types of insured persons of National Pension according to their status as follows:
Category Ⅰ insured persons (self-employed persons, students, agricultural, forestry and fishery workers, unemployed persons)
Category Ⅱ insured persons (company workers and public sector workers)
Category Ⅲ insured persons (economically-dependent spouses of category Ⅱ insured persons)
Category Ⅰ Insured Persons
All residents of Japan between age 20 and 59 who are not Category Ⅱ or Ⅲ insured persons (e.g. self-employed persons, students, agricultural, forestry and fishery workers, unemployed persons.)
When you become subject to Category Ⅰ insured person, you need to submit, by yourself, application to enroll in as Category I insured person to the municipal office of your place of residence within 14 days.
Enrollment in National Pension
Note:Foreign nationals with specific visa (i.e. medical stay/long stay for sightseeing) are not subject to coverage of National Pension as Category Ⅰ insured persons.
Category Ⅱ Insured Persons
Company workers and public sector workers under 70 who are covered in Employees’ Pension Insurance  (except for persons age 65 or older who are eligible for old-age pension.)
When you become subject to the Category Ⅱ insured person, your employer needs to submit “Application to Enroll in EPI / EHI.”
Enrollment in Employees' Pension Insurance
Notes:
You must be covered as Category Ⅰ insured person for the period from your entry to Japan until you become Category Ⅱ insured person.
Mariners shall be covered by Seamen’s Insurance system.
Enrollment in Seamen's Insurance
Category Ⅲ Insured Persons
Category Ⅱ insured persons’ economically-dependent spouses between age 20 and 59, residing in Japan (excluding spouse of Category Ⅱ insured person who reached age 65 and eligible for Old-age Basic Pension.)
When you become subject to the Category Ⅲ insured person, employer of your spouse needs to submit “National Pension: Application to Enroll in as Category Ⅲ Insured Person.”
Report of Dependents
Notes:
You must be covered as Category Ⅰ insured person for the period from your entry to Japan until you become Category Ⅲ insured person.
Foreign nationals with specific visa (i.e. medical stay/long stay for sightseeing) are not subject to coverage of National Pension as the Category Ⅲ insured person.

original_evidence.text:
Exemption of National Pension Contributions
Page ID：150010-891-528-929
Last updated date：4 1 2026
Print
You may apply for exemption or postponement of contribution payments if you have temporarily financial difficulties. Student may apply for "Special Payment system for Students“ (payment postponement.)
Your future Old-age Basic Pension amount will be, however, lower than that with fully paid periods, if you have such contribution-exempted or postponed period. To avoid that, you may make retroactive payments to recover the past contribution-exempted periods for up to the past 10 years.
Index
Special Payment System for Students
Exemption / Postponement of the Contributions by Application
Statutory Exemption (e.g. beneficiary of Disability Basic Pension)
Recovery of the Past Exempted-Contribution
Special Payment System for Students
If you are a student and your income is less than a certain amount, you may be allowed to postpone contribution payments if your application is approved.
The period which the postponement was granted is considered as valid periods, not as non-payment period. So, if you become disabled or die during such periods, Disability / Survivors' Basic Pensions will be provided if you meet the following conditions;
(1) By the second month preceding the month of incident causing disability or death, you have filled at least two-thirds of your insured periods (months) with contribution paid periods and contribution-exempted periods.
(2) You have paid your contributions or you were exempted from contribution payments for the last 12 months up to the second month preceding the month of incident causing disability or death.
The granted periods count as qualifying periods for Old-age Basic Pension, however, unless you recover contribution payments afterwards, the periods will not be reflected to the amount of old-age benefits.
How to apply
You need to apply for it at the municipal office of your place of residence. One application covers up to one year, so you need to apply for it every year, if needed.
Exemption / Postponement of the Contributions by Application
Contribution Exemption
You may be exempt from contribution payments if the previous year's income of you, your spouse, or head of your household is limited, and if your application for exemption is granted.
The type of exemption and monthly contribution amount for the fiscal year 2026 are as follows;
full-amount-exemption
3/4-amount-exemption (you pay remaining \4,480)
half-amount-exemption (you pay remaining \8,960)
1/4-amount-exemption (you pay remaining \13,440)
If you fail to pay the due remaining contribution amount during the granted period, however, it will be considered to be non-payment rather than partial exemption.
For the purpose of calculation of your pension benefits, your periods of full-amount-exemption for March 2009 and earlier will count as one-third of full-contribution-paid periods (the 3/4-amount-exemption periods will count as half, the half-amount-exemption periods as two-thirds and the 1/4-amount-exemption periods as five-sixths.) Your periods of full-amount-exemption for April 2009 and later will count as half of full-contribution-paid periods (the 3/4-amount-exemption periods will count as five-eighths, the half-amount exemption periods as six-eighths and the 1/4-amount-exemption periods as seven-eighths.)
How to apply
You need to apply for it at the municipal office of your place of residence. One application covers up to one year, so you need to apply for it every year, if needed.
Statutory Exemption (e.g. beneficiary of Disability Basic Pension)
If you meet certain conditions specified by National Pension Act, e.g. beneficiary of the Disability Basic Pension, your contribution shall be exempted.
How to report
To establish exemption, you must report at the municipal office of your place of residence.
Recovery of the Past Exempted-Contribution
You may retroactively make payments to recover past contribution-exempted periods for up to the past 10 years. In that case, a specific index shall be imposed on your past contribution amount when you recover the old payments. That is, if you were granted the contribution exemption in a certain fiscal year (April to March) and if you wish to recover the contribution three or more fiscal years later, your old contribution amount is indexed by certain rate according to the age of the due contribution.
Note: Apply for the retroactive payments well in advance. If applied just before the deadline, your payments may not be technically accepted in time.
How to pay for exempted / postponed contribution in the past
For retroactive payments, contact your
nearest JPS branch office.

Suzukakedai Campus renamed Yokohama Campus on April 1, 2026
April  1, 2026
Announcements
About Science Tokyo
Co-creating with society
Science Tokyo has changed the name of its Suzukakedai Campus to "Yokohama Campus," effective April 1, 2026.
Since its establishment in 1975, this campus has continued its educational and research activities for over half a century in northern Yokohama. Nestled in a lush green environment, it has produced numerous research achievements and progressed hand in hand with the local community.
The new campus name expresses Science Tokyo’s respect for the history of educational and research activities conducted in collaboration with the City of Yokohama, and the Institute’s determination to continue contributing to the development of the city.
The name "Suzukakedai" will continue to be used for certain facilities and events, such as Suzukakedai Library and Suzukake Science Day.
Having surpassed its 50th anniversary, Yokohama Campus is now taking a new step forward. While maintaining strong ties with the local community, it will fulfill its role as an important part of Science Tokyo as a University for International Research Excellence and return its achievements to society.

Overview
Under the Academic Course Access Program (ACAP), Science Tokyo waives the application, enrollment, and tuition fees of undergraduate (second-year or above) and graduate-level International Exchange Students from participating partner universities [
LIST of agreements
]. ACAP students are accepted for a period of one quarter to four quarters (a year) – for JASSO scholarship recipients, a period of two quarters (a semester) to four quarters (a year) – and are able to study alongside Science Tokyo students in regular courses offered on a quarter or semester basis.
*ACAP students are not permitted to take courses offered by the faculties/graduate schools of Medicine, Dentistry and Health Care Sciences.
Eligibility
Applicants must be enrolled at partner universities with which Science Tokyo has a tuition waiver agreement.
Those with student status at their home university, enrolled in the following programs at the time they start coursework at Science Tokyo:
・Doctoral program
・Master’s program
・Bachelor’s program (at least one year of study)*
*
Except for undergraduate students in their final year, an official Japanese Language Proficiency Test (JLPT N1) result or equivalent document is required as students are supposed to take courses conducted in Japanese.
Applicants must carefully consider what they wish to study at Science Tokyo and prepare an ACAP Course-Oriented Program Sheet, which will be submitted to Science Tokyo through the partner university at the time of nomination.

If you are undergraduate students other than those in their final year and your Japanese language ability is not sufficient to take courses in Japanese, please confirm well in advance if you can achieve your study plan by taking the 300-level.

Application Procedures
Once you have decided to apply
Step 1. Contact the Student Exchange Officer (or equivalent) at your home university
ACAP Course-Oriented Program Sheet
ACAP applicants must be officially nominated to Science Tokyo by their home university, and Science Tokyo must be informed of the nomination BEFORE applicants are invited to apply online. At the time of nomination, the "ACAP Course-Oriented Program Sheet" prepared by each applicant should be submitted to Science Tokyo by their home university.
After receiving the official nomination from your home university, Science Tokyo will directly send you the necessary information for logging in to the online application form via email to you.
Step 2. Be assigned an Academic Supervisor at Science Tokyo
Science Tokyo's Schools
For all applicants, the Global Education Division will assign an ACAP Specialized Faculty member, selected from the applicant's desired department based on the ACAP Course-Oriented Program Sheet, to serve as their academic supervisor, and will notify the applicants of the result by email before application deadline. Applicants are NOT required to contact any faculty members at Science Tokyo directly.
Applicants applying to the Department of Architecture and Building Engineering are required to submit their Curriculum Vitae (CV) and portfolio via the online application form.
Currently, no applicants are accepted to the Department of Innovation Sciences.
After the application deadline, applicants are required to contact the assigned ACAP Specialized faculty member to confirm their acceptance and for an initial greeting.
Note that some Departments may exceed their capacity due to a high number of applicants and will be unable to accept additional students. In such cases, Science Tokyo will request the applicant to change their desired Department.

*For example, a bank statement (which verifies the available balance in the account) for you or your financial supporter; or a scholarship certificate (if any). If there is not an English version of these documents, you should attach a certified English translation with a signature of the translator and the date of translation.
Course Information for International Exchange Students
ACAP participants are mandated to take 6 classes (600 minutes) or more per week to maintain student visa status. All participants are assigned to one of Science Tokyo's Schools or Departments. In principle, they should plan their course of study mainly around courses offered in the Department to which they are assigned. However, not all courses offered at Science Tokyo are available for International Exchange Students. Final-year undergraduate students should refer to previously approved 400-level courses and carefully consider the courses they can take while studying abroad at Science Tokyo. Please refer to the document “
Science Tokyo Course Information to Help Develop Your Study Plan
.”
Housing
For students who have submitted a request to move into a Science Tokyo dormitory through the online application, the Global Education Division will request that the department in charge of university dormitories will allocate a room for them. (Students are not required to apply for dormitories individually.) Students will be notified by email 1 to 1.5 months prior to enrollment whether or not they will be able to move into the dormitory. In that case, please follow the instructions in the email. We do not accept changes of dormitories assigned to applicants. Note that not all incoming students will be assigned a dormitory room as room availability is limited.

Young Science and Engineering Researchers Program (YSEP)
offers students from partner universities the opportunity to spend 5 months to 1 year at the Institute. Under the YSEP, Science Tokyo waives the application, enrollment, and tuition fees of undergraduate and graduate-level International Exchange Students from participating partner universities [

(a) Take at least one of the following courses.

original_evidence.text:
Frequently Asked Questions
Frequently asked questions about applying for a student dormitory and living in a dormitory are listed below. Please read them before you apply.
About dormitory applications
Expand all
Q
I'd like to enter Tokyo Tech next spring and stay in a student dormitory. When do applications open?
A
We start accepting online applications from mid-January.
Q
Can I apply before the release of the entrance exam results?
A
Yes. However, you’ll lose your eligibility if you fail the exam.
Q
I’d like to secure a room in a dormitory in February, before the entrance exam results in March. Is that possible if I pay rent?
A
Not allowed. You can move in after the move-in date.
Q
Can I apply for more than one dormitory and indicate my first choice, second choice, etc.?
A
Applications will only be accepted for one dormitory. However, if you are unable to move into the dormitory you have applied for, we may be able to offer you another dormitory if one is available.
Q
Could my application be rejected? What’s the ratio of applications for dormitories?
A
Selection will be by lottery if the number of applications exceeds capacity.
The ratio of applications differs every year, depending on the dormitory.
Q
If my application is successful, can I choose my room? Can I request a room change after moving in?
A
You can’t choose your room or roommates, and room change requests are not accepted.
Q
Is there a charge for cancellation?
A
No cancellation fee will be charged.
Q
Will the initial fee be refunded when I leave?
A
The initial fee is not refundable.
Q
Can I view rooms before applying?
A
A Yes. Please contact the Student Support Division.
(No viewing available for Suzukakedai House and Minami-Tsukushino House)
Q
Can I keep my room while on a leave of absence or studying abroad? If yes, will I be charged rent?
A
Please inquire separately as it depends on the period and circumstances.
Q
What is the “reservation number” printed on my application form?
A
It’s a number for students enrolling in certain specified programs.
About dormitory life
Expand all
Q
Is there a curfew?
A
No curfew.
Q
Can my friends visit me in my room?
A
In principle, only residents are allowed to enter private rooms. Access to common areas is handled differently in each dormitory, so please inquire for details.
Q
May friends stay overnight?
A
Non-residents are not allowed to stay overnight.
Q
Are meals provided?
A
No, the dormitories aren’t catered.
Q
Is there a TV in the dormitory? If not, can I bring my own?
A
Private rooms are not equipped with a TV, but some dormitories have common rooms with one. Please consult us if you would like to bring your own.
Q
Can I access the internet in my room?
A
Internet service is available in the dormitory. No application is required.
Q
Is bedding provided?
A
Those in other dormitories have only a mattress. Please bring your own bedding set and linen, or purchase them from our supplier at a discount rate. (No purchasing available for Suzukakedai House and Minami-Tsukushino House)
Q
How do I pay the rent?
A
Payment methods differ depending on the dormitory. We’ll explain the relevant procedure to each student well before their residency starts.
Minamishinagawa House
Expand all
Q
Is the Minami-Shinagawa House located within cycling distance of the campus?
A
Yes. Some residents commute by bicycle.
Q
What appliances are provided in residential units?
A
There is a refrigerator, microwave.
Senzokuike House
Expand all
Q
Can I have a specific address?
A
Only if you’ve been assigned a room. Please contact us if you would like to view the facility.
Q
Can my friends visit me in the house?
A
Female visitors are allowed to visit, but may only enter the dining room and lounge.
Q
I’d like to ask my father to help me move in/out. Can he enter the dormitory?
A
He’ll be allowed to enter the dining room and lounge on the first floor only. Please follow the rules about visitors.
Midorigaoka House
Expand all
Q
Are undergraduate students accepted?
A
No, the Midorigaoka House is exclusively for graduate students.
Nagatsuta House
Expand all
Q
Is there a shuttle bus to the campus?
A
Yes, there’s a free shuttle bus that for only Nagatsuta House residents  between the dormitory and Suzukakedai Campus — three times in the morning and evening. It takes about 10 minutes.
Unfortunately, Nagatsuta House residents are not allowed to ride bicycles to school.
Komaba Dormiory, Shofu  Dormiory and Umegaoka Dormiory
Expand all
Q
I’m a new international student. Can I apply for an international dormitory?
A
New international students and exchange students who have received an invitation to move in from the Student Support Division and have a reservation number may apply.
Q
How can I get a reservation number?
A
If you have a reservation number, yes. We send information about dormitories along with a reservation number to eligible international students.
Q
Can Japanese students reside in the dormitory?
A
Only those assigned as dormitory tutors will be permitted and may be able to move in when recruited.
Contact
Student Support Division (Dormitory)
Email
dormitory.se@adm.isct.ac.jp
Dormitories and other accommodation

International student guide
This guide compiles necessary and useful information for international students regarding life in Japan and studying at Science Tokyo. There are unique systems and procedures specifically for international students, so when you're in doubt or trouble, first use this guide to collect the information you need.
International student guide
This international student guide contains important information for your studies at Science Tokyo. Since there are certain systems and procedures specific to international students, please refer to it as needed.
The guide is only available in English.
Table of contents
1. Residence Status and Registration Procedures
2. Visa Consulting Service
3. Japanese Health and Social Insurance Systems
4．Student Insurance
5. Medical Checkup
6．Counseling and Support System
7．Certifications

9. Accommodations
10．Commuter Passes and Student Discounts
11．Inviting Family Members to Japan
12．Use of the Libraries
13. Career Support
14．Bulletin Boards
15．Application for Privately Funded Scholarships
16. Science Tokyo Tsubame Scholarship for Doctoral Students
17．Useful Information
1. Residence Status and Registration Procedures
1.1 Residence Card
1.2 Registration of Address Information
1.3 Change in Information on the Residence Card Other than Place of Residence
1.4 Social Security and Tax Number (Individual Number)
1.5 Procedures to Be Taken before Traveling Overseas from Japan
1.6 When Taking a Leave of Absence
1.7 When Studying Abroad
1.8 When Undertaking an Internship in/outside Japan
1.9 When Graduating from Science Tokyo/ Completing a Degree Program
1.10 When Withdrawing/ Being Expelled from Science Tokyo
1.11 Extension of Period of Stay
1.12 Applying for Permission to Engage in Activity Other than That Permitted under the Status of Residence Previously Granted
1.1 Residence Card
A residence card is issued at the port of entry to persons entering Japan who have been granted residence status with a period of stay of three or more months. Please carry your residence card with you at all times.
1.2 Registration of Address Information
(1) Notification of Place of Residence (registration of residence)
After entering Japan, international students are required to report their place of residence to local municipal offices without delay. Submit a Notification of Place of Residence to the office for registration of your residency within 14 days after moving in.
(2) Procedures to Be Taken When Changing Residence
a. Notify the local municipal or ward office
Whenever you move to a new residence, you are required to notify your local municipal or ward office of the change of address within 14 days after moving in.
b. Notify the Student Division and the Student Support Division
Science and engineering students
Bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral students:
Please change your address on the website (Web System for Students and Faculty).
Additionally, please bring your residence card with the new address to Student Support Division for scanning.
Research Students, International Exchange Students, International Visiting Students, Japanese Intensive Course Students:
Please bring your residence card with the new address to Student Support Division for scanning.
Medical and dental sciences students
Undergraduate, graduate, doctoral, and research students:
Please submit a copy of both sides of your updated residence card that lists the new address to the Student Support Division at Yushima Campus via the following link:
- Reporting Your Residence Status "Student"
c. Change the address registered on your National Health Insurance Card.
Once you have changed your address, you can no longer use the National Health Insurance Card issued with your former address. To change the address, complete the required procedures at the local municipal or ward office for your new address without delay. Please bring your old National Health Insurance Card with you.
d. Change the address registered on your bank account.
Please notify your bank of any change of address. Bring your bankbook to the bank where it was issued and have the address updated. If scholarship recipients fail to do so, their scholarships may not be credited appropriately.
e. Notify the post office.
To receive letters and mail addressed to your former address at your new place, request a mail forwarding service at a post office. Fill in and submit the prescribed form which is available at any post office, and mail will be forwarded to your new address for up to one year. Note that mail cannot be forwarded to overseas addresses; forwarding addresses must be in Japan. Please also note that forwarded mail will take longer to reach you than normal, since it takes some time to redirect mail to a different address.
1.3 Change in Information on the Residence Card Other than Place of Residence
If there is any change in the information on the residence card other than the address (e.g., name, date of birth, sex, nationality/region) or termination of the “Student” status of residence (e.g., graduation, withdrawal, etc.), mid-to-long-term residents must report it to the Regional Immigration Services Bureau within 14 days of the change. Bring your residence card to the nearest office and complete the necessary procedures. Failing to do so may result in penalties or revocation of status of residence. Once the necessary procedures are completed, a new residence card will be issued.
After receiving your new residence card with the updated information, please notify the Student Support Division.
1.4 Social Security and Tax Number (Individual Number)
In accordance with the Social Security and Tax Number System (My Number System), all registered residents of Japan are issued a twelve-digit individual number. This number will be required for various types of administrative procedures, including social security and tax procedures, as well as disaster countermeasures. This number is very important for managing personal information, so please do not throw it away or show it to other persons. It is valid for life. The same number will be issued when leaving and re-entering Japan.
1.5 Procedures to Be Taken before Traveling Overseas from Japan
Science and engineering students
Notify the Global Education Division.
Regular students
Please submit an “Overseas Travel Notice” via Rakrak WF II. For more information, please visit the following website.
Procedures for Study Abroad and Other Overseas Travel
Non-regular students
Please submit an “Overseas Travel Notice” via Microsoft Forms using the link below.
- International exchange students and international visiting students
- Non-regular students who are not international exchange or visiting students
Medical and dental sciences students
Notify the Student Support Division.
All students
Please submit a “Temporary Leave Notice” via Microsoft Forms using the link below here:
Temporary Leave Notice
Whenever you travel outside Japan (including travel for vacations and travel to your home country), please ensure that you have travel insurance.
1.6 When Taking a Leave of Absence
Consult with the Student Support Division before deciding to take a leave of absence.
If you take a leave of absence, you cannot remain in Japan under "Student" status, nor are you allowed to work part-time. You must leave Japan promptly or change to an appropriate residence status if you wish to stay.
If you are going to take a leave of absence for more than three months, your "Student" status will be revoked, even if your period of stay remains valid, as you will no longer be considered a student in Japan. When leaving Japan, please return your residence card at the airport. You will need to obtain a new Certificate of Eligibility (COE) to apply for a student visa in order to resume studying at Science Tokyo. The Student Support Division will assist you with the COE application, so please contact us at least three months before your planned date of re-entry to Japan.
1.7 When Studying Abroad
Consult with the Student Support Division before deciding to study abroad.
If you are going to study abroad for more than three months, your "Student" status will be revoked, even if your period of stay remains valid, as you will no longer be considered a student in Japan. When leaving Japan, please return your residence card at the airport.
You will need to obtain a new Certificate of Eligibility (COE) to apply for a student visa in order to re-enter Japan. The Student Support Division will assist you with the COE application, so please contact us at least three months before your planned date of re-entry to Japan.
1.8 When Undertaking an Internship in/outside Japan
Consult with the Student Support Division before deciding to undertake internships.
If you undertake an internship abroad for more than three months, your "Student" status will be revoked, even if your period of stay remains valid, as you will no longer be considered a student in Japan. When leaving Japan, please return your residence card at the airport.
You will need to obtain a new Certificate of Eligibility (COE) to apply for a student visa in order to re-enter Japan. The Student Support Division will assist you with the COE application, so please contact us at least three months before your planned date of re-entry to Japan.
If you are going to undertake an internship in Japan, see the Immigration Services Agency's website and apply for permission as necessary.
For those wishing to apply for an internship | Immigration Services Agency
1.9 When Graduating from Science Tokyo/ Completing a Degree Program
The "Student" status is only valid during your period of enrollment at Science Tokyo. After graduation or completion, you must leave Japan promptly, even if your period of stay still remains valid. When leaving Japan, please return your residence card at the airport.
If your period of stay includes extra time beyond your enrollment for departure preparation, (i.e., if your residence period is significantly longer than your period of enrollment), you cannot change to "Temporary visitor" status for the purpose of such preparation.
If you plan to stay in Japan after graduation/completion, you must change to an appropriate status (see below for examples) and submit a "Notification of Affiliation Change (Leave/Transfer)" to the Regional Immigration Services Bureau within 14 days of graduation/completion, unless you continue your studies at Science Tokyo.
Immigration Services Agency website for a "Notification of Affiliation Change (Leave/Transfer)"
If you are planning to start work: contact the company where you have received a job offer (Naitei) and change your status to "Working."
If you already have a job offer (Naitei) from a company and want to stay in Japan until your job starts: contact the company and change your status to "Designated Activities (Naitei Taiki)."
If you want to continue job hunting (regular students only): contact the Student Support Division and apply for a change of status to "Designated Activities (Job Hunting)."
If you have a letter of acceptance to a graduate school and want to stay until the date of enrollment: contact the Student Support Division and apply for a change of status to "Designated Activities (Shingaku Taiki)."
1.10 When Withdrawing/ Being Expelled from Science Tokyo
If you withdraw or are expelled from Science Tokyo, you cannot remain in Japan under "Student" status and must leave Japan promptly. When departing, please return your residence card at the airport.
If you plan to stay in Japan to enroll at another university or to work in Japan, please check your status with your new university or company. You must also submit a "Notification of Affiliation Change (Leave/Transfer)" to the Regional Immigration Services Bureau within 14 days of the date of withdrawal/expulsion.
Immigration Services Agency website for a "Notification of Affiliation Change (Leave/Transfer)"
1.11 Extension of Period of Stay
Undergraduate international students who have acquired less than 25 credits over the past year may not be granted permission to renew their period of stay. (For medical and dental science students, this applies to those who have not acquired the required credits for advancement to the next academic year.)
For details, refer to the Science Tokyo website
Find the application procedures and necessary documents for extending your stay or changing your status of residence. Please check the relevant contact points according to your field below.
