Visiting Students & Student Exchange Program
SMWU’s Semester Abroad Program offers a unique opportunity for university students currently enrolled in institutions outside of Korea. Both male and female students are eligible to apply. As a Study Abroad student, you can earn credits towards your home degree while immersing yourself in a valuable international and intercultural experience in Korea. Additionally, Exchange Students from Partner Institutions have the option to participate in this program, with the possibility of tuition waiver based on the exchange agreement. Participants in the program have the chance to enroll in SMWU’s undergraduate and graduate schools. Earned credits are recorded on an official SMWU transcript, which may be transferable to other universities.

Academic Calendar
Sookmyung Women’s University operates on a two-semester academic year. The spring semester runs from March to mid-June, while the fall semester takes place from September to mid-December. In addition to these regular semesters, Summer Sessions are offered prior to the fall semester.

Courses
We offer over 150 English-taught courses in various disciplines at both undergraduate and graduate levels. Students can choose from a range of subjects such as Korean language, International Studies, Korean Studies, Business and Economics and more. Additionally, there are numerous opportunities to engage in traditional Korean culture through lectures and field trips. For a complete course list and descriptions, please visit: [Click here-
http://e.sookmyung.ac.kr
>Academic>courses>Type of Lecture>Language:English- Search]
Costs
All students are required to complete their payments upon arrival. Exchange students from SMU’s partner institutions will have their tuition waived as part of the agreement.

How to apply
Entry Requilrements
All students including SMWU’s exchange students are required to complete their payments upon arrival.
Visiting Students
Students who are not from exchange universities or from SMWU’s partner institution who were not selected as exchange students.
Before applying directly, it is recommended that students contact the international office of their home university to verify the transferability of credits earned at SMWU.
Exchange Students
SMWU’s partner institution students must be nominated by their home university as exchange candidates. All application documents should be submitted to SMWU through the international office of their home university. Individual applications are not accepted.
The following documents are required to Apply:
Online Application Apply Now
Recent Official Academic Transcript
Copy of Passport
Copy of a recent photo
Health Insurance Verification Form or a copy of a Health Insurance Certificate that covers medical treatments and accidents in Korea.
Verification Form

All required documents should be uploaded through the online application system
Please ensure that you have all the necessary documents ready for a complete application.
Application Deadline
Spring Semester- November 30th, prior to the March start of the following year
Fall Semester - May 31st, prior to the September start of the same year
Benefits for International Students
Sookmyung Buddy Leadership Group, URINK
U.R.I. (United Relationship for Internationalization) is a student-led group at Sookmyung Women’s University. Local SMWU students volunteer as buddies to assist and support international students on campus. Each international student is paired with a student buddy who helps them with general matters in Korea and helps them adjust to university life. The program promotes cultural exchange, fosters lasting friendships, and offers opportunities for students to participate in various events and activities together.
Scholarship Offered Volunteer Programs
International students from around the world can volunteer in Sookmyung Women’s University’s English Speaking Spot (ESS) and Second Language Tutoring program (SLT). In this program, they have the opportunity to teach their native language to Sookmyung students and receive a scholarship of KRW 10,000 per hour throughout the semester. It is a great way for international students to share their language skills and earn a scholarship at the same time.

Sookmyung Buddy Leadership Group, URINK
U.R.I. (United Relationship for Internationalization) is a student-led group at Sookmyung Women’s University. Local SMWU students volunteer as buddies to assist and support international students on campus. Each international student is paired with a student buddy who helps them with general matters in Korea and helps them adjust to university life. The program promotes cultural exchange, fosters lasting friendships, and offers opportunities for students to participate in various events and activities together.
Scholarship Offered Volunteer Programs
International students from around the world can volunteer in Sookmyung Women’s University’s English Speaking Spot (ESS) and Second Language Tutoring program (SLT). In this program, they have the opportunity to teach their native language to Sookmyung students and receive a scholarship of KRW 10,000 per hour throughout the semester. It is a great way for international students to share their language skills and earn a scholarship at the same time.

Visiting Students & Student Exchange Program
SMWU’s Semester Abroad Program offers a unique opportunity for university students currently enrolled in institutions outside of Korea. Both male and female students are eligible to apply. As a Study Abroad student, you can earn credits towards your home degree while immersing yourself in a valuable international and intercultural experience in Korea. Additionally, Exchange Students from Partner Institutions have the option to participate in this program, with the possibility of tuition waiver based on the exchange agreement. Participants in the program have the chance to enroll in SMWU’s undergraduate and graduate schools. Earned credits are recorded on an official SMWU transcript, which may be transferable to other universities.

Sookmyung Women’s University operates on a two-semester academic year. The spring semester runs from March to mid-June, while the fall semester takes place from September to mid-December. In addition to these regular semesters, Summer Sessions are offered prior to the fall semester.

國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。

Visiting Students & Student Exchange Program
SMWU’s Semester Abroad Program offers a unique opportunity for university students currently enrolled in institutions outside of Korea. Both male and female students are eligible to apply. As a Study Abroad student, you can earn credits towards your home degree while immersing yourself in a valuable international and intercultural experience in Korea. Additionally, Exchange Students from Partner Institutions have the option to participate in this program, with the possibility of tuition waiver based on the exchange agreement. Participants in the program have the chance to enroll in SMWU’s undergraduate and graduate schools. Earned credits are recorded on an official SMWU transcript, which may be transferable to other universities.

Academic Calendar
Sookmyung Women’s University operates on a two-semester academic year. The spring semester runs from March to mid-June, while the fall semester takes place from September to mid-December. In addition to these regular semesters, Summer Sessions are offered prior to the fall semester.

Courses
We offer over 150 English-taught courses in various disciplines at both undergraduate and graduate levels. Students can choose from a range of subjects such as Korean language, International Studies, Korean Studies, Business and Economics and more. Additionally, there are numerous opportunities to engage in traditional Korean culture through lectures and field trips. For a complete course list and descriptions, please visit: [Click here-

All students are required to complete their payments upon arrival. Exchange students from SMU’s partner institutions will have their tuition waived as part of the agreement.

How to apply
Entry Requilrements
All students including SMWU’s exchange students are required to complete their payments upon arrival.
Visiting Students
Students who are not from exchange universities or from SMWU’s partner institution who were not selected as exchange students.
Before applying directly, it is recommended that students contact the international office of their home university to verify the transferability of credits earned at SMWU.
Exchange Students
SMWU’s partner institution students must be nominated by their home university as exchange candidates. All application documents should be submitted to SMWU through the international office of their home university. Individual applications are not accepted.
The following documents are required to Apply:
Online Application Apply Now
Recent Official Academic Transcript
Copy of Passport
Copy of a recent photo

Please ensure that you have all the necessary documents ready for a complete application.
Application Deadline
Spring Semester- November 30th, prior to the March start of the following year
Fall Semester - May 31st, prior to the September start of the same year
Benefits for International Students
Sookmyung Buddy Leadership Group, URINK
U.R.I. (United Relationship for Internationalization) is a student-led group at Sookmyung Women’s University. Local SMWU students volunteer as buddies to assist and support international students on campus. Each international student is paired with a student buddy who helps them with general matters in Korea and helps them adjust to university life. The program promotes cultural exchange, fosters lasting friendships, and offers opportunities for students to participate in various events and activities together.
Scholarship Offered Volunteer Programs
International students from around the world can volunteer in Sookmyung Women’s University’s English Speaking Spot (ESS) and Second Language Tutoring program (SLT). In this program, they have the opportunity to teach their native language to Sookmyung students and receive a scholarship of KRW 10,000 per hour throughout the semester. It is a great way for international students to share their language skills and earn a scholarship at the same time.

Visiting Students & Student Exchange Program
SMWU’s Semester Abroad Program offers a unique opportunity for university students currently enrolled in institutions outside of Korea. Both male and female students are eligible to apply. As a Study Abroad student, you can earn credits towards your home degree while immersing yourself in a valuable international and intercultural experience in Korea. Additionally, Exchange Students from Partner Institutions have the option to participate in this program, with the possibility of tuition waiver based on the exchange agreement. Participants in the program have the chance to enroll in SMWU’s undergraduate and graduate schools. Earned credits are recorded on an official SMWU transcript, which may be transferable to other universities.

Visiting Students & Student Exchange Program
SMWU’s Semester Abroad Program offers a unique opportunity for university students currently enrolled in institutions outside of Korea. Both male and female students are eligible to apply. As a Study Abroad student, you can earn credits towards your home degree while immersing yourself in a valuable international and intercultural experience in Korea. Additionally, Exchange Students from Partner Institutions have the option to participate in this program, with the possibility of tuition waiver based on the exchange agreement. Participants in the program have the chance to enroll in SMWU’s undergraduate and graduate schools. Earned credits are recorded on an official SMWU transcript, which may be transferable to other universities.
Academic Calendar
Courses
Costs
How to apply

Academic Calendar
Sookmyung Women’s University operates on a two-semester academic year. The spring semester runs from March to mid-June, while the fall semester takes place from September to mid-December. In addition to these regular semesters, Summer Sessions are offered prior to the fall semester.

Courses
We offer over 150 English-taught courses in various disciplines at both undergraduate and graduate levels. Students can choose from a range of subjects such as Korean language, International Studies, Korean Studies, Business and Economics and more. Additionally, there are numerous opportunities to engage in traditional Korean culture through lectures and field trips. For a complete course list and descriptions, please visit: [Click here-
http://e.sookmyung.ac.kr
>Academic>courses>Type of Lecture>Language:English- Search]
Costs
All students are required to complete their payments upon arrival. Exchange students from SMU’s partner institutions will have their tuition waived as part of the agreement.

Fees are subject to fluctuation based on the exchange rate. Please provide fees in Korean currency (KRW).
Kindly note that the cost is subject to annual changes.
How to apply
Entry Requilrements
All students including SMWU’s exchange students are required to complete their payments upon arrival.
Visiting Students
Students who are not from exchange universities or from SMWU’s partner institution who were not selected as exchange students.
Before applying directly, it is recommended that students contact the international office of their home university to verify the transferability of credits earned at SMWU.
Exchange Students
SMWU’s partner institution students must be nominated by their home university as exchange candidates. All application documents should be submitted to SMWU through the international office of their home university. Individual applications are not accepted.
The following documents are required to Apply:
Online Application Apply Now
Recent Official Academic Transcript
Copy of Passport
Copy of a recent photo
Health Insurance Verification Form or a copy of a Health Insurance Certificate that covers medical treatments and accidents in Korea.
Verification Form

Original Bank Statement showing minimum amount of US $5,000 per semester
All required documents should be uploaded through the online application system
Please ensure that you have all the necessary documents ready for a complete application.
Application Deadline
Spring Semester- November 30th, prior to the March start of the following year
Fall Semester - May 31st, prior to the September start of the same year
Benefits for International Students
Sookmyung Buddy Leadership Group, URINK
U.R.I. (United Relationship for Internationalization) is a student-led group at Sookmyung Women’s University. Local SMWU students volunteer as buddies to assist and support international students on campus. Each international student is paired with a student buddy who helps them with general matters in Korea and helps them adjust to university life. The program promotes cultural exchange, fosters lasting friendships, and offers opportunities for students to participate in various events and activities together.
Scholarship Offered Volunteer Programs
International students from around the world can volunteer in Sookmyung Women’s University’s English Speaking Spot (ESS) and Second Language Tutoring program (SLT). In this program, they have the opportunity to teach their native language to Sookmyung students and receive a scholarship of KRW 10,000 per hour throughout the semester. It is a great way for international students to share their language skills and earn a scholarship at the same time.

Visiting Students & Student Exchange Program
SMWU’s Semester Abroad Program offers a unique opportunity for university students currently enrolled in institutions outside of Korea. Both male and female students are eligible to apply. As a Study Abroad student, you can earn credits towards your home degree while immersing yourself in a valuable international and intercultural experience in Korea. Additionally, Exchange Students from Partner Institutions have the option to participate in this program, with the possibility of tuition waiver based on the exchange agreement. Participants in the program have the chance to enroll in SMWU’s undergraduate and graduate schools. Earned credits are recorded on an official SMWU transcript, which may be transferable to other universities.

Academic Calendar
Sookmyung Women’s University operates on a two-semester academic year. The spring semester runs from March to mid-June, while the fall semester takes place from September to mid-December. In addition to these regular semesters, Summer Sessions are offered prior to the fall semester.

Courses
We offer over 150 English-taught courses in various disciplines at both undergraduate and graduate levels. Students can choose from a range of subjects such as Korean language, International Studies, Korean Studies, Business and Economics and more. Additionally, there are numerous opportunities to engage in traditional Korean culture through lectures and field trips. For a complete course list and descriptions, please visit: [Click here-
http://e.sookmyung.ac.kr

Costs
All students are required to complete their payments upon arrival. Exchange students from SMU’s partner institutions will have their tuition waived as part of the agreement.

How to apply
Entry Requilrements
All students including SMWU’s exchange students are required to complete their payments upon arrival.
Visiting Students
Students who are not from exchange universities or from SMWU’s partner institution who were not selected as exchange students.
Before applying directly, it is recommended that students contact the international office of their home university to verify the transferability of credits earned at SMWU.
Exchange Students
SMWU’s partner institution students must be nominated by their home university as exchange candidates. All application documents should be submitted to SMWU through the international office of their home university. Individual applications are not accepted.

Benefits for International Students
Sookmyung Buddy Leadership Group, URINK
U.R.I. (United Relationship for Internationalization) is a student-led group at Sookmyung Women’s University. Local SMWU students volunteer as buddies to assist and support international students on campus. Each international student is paired with a student buddy who helps them with general matters in Korea and helps them adjust to university life. The program promotes cultural exchange, fosters lasting friendships, and offers opportunities for students to participate in various events and activities together.
Scholarship Offered Volunteer Programs
International students from around the world can volunteer in Sookmyung Women’s University’s English Speaking Spot (ESS) and Second Language Tutoring program (SLT). In this program, they have the opportunity to teach their native language to Sookmyung students and receive a scholarship of KRW 10,000 per hour throughout the semester. It is a great way for international students to share their language skills and earn a scholarship at the same time.

Health Insurance
Sookmyung Women’s University requires all full-time international students, including exchange students, to have hospital/accident insurance or other healthcare coverage for the entire year.
Please check the link below for the information on Korea's National Health Care mandatory requirement (since May 2021):
https://www.sookmyung.ac.kr/en/university-life/notice.do?mode=view&articleNo=83797
Students with sufficient insurance coverage that fulfills the health insurance waiver conditions must submit a copy of their insurance policy to the staff at Global Lounge. Please be aware that students without adequate health insurance will not be eligible for benefits available to International Students, including scholarships and other services (such as Cultural Activities) provided by SMU.
International Students' Indemnity Health Insurance
Sookmyung Women’s University requires all full-time international students to purchases the International Students’ Indemnity Medical Expenses Insurance.(March 2024). It covers deaths and diseases, etc, not covered by the national health insurance of Korea. For those who have not yet purchased adequate health insurance for their study at SMU in Korea, we would like to provide a brief information on the health insurance policy program offered by DB Insurance, one of the major local insurance companies in Korea.

Visiting Students & Student Exchange Program
SMWU’s Semester Abroad Program offers a unique opportunity for university students currently enrolled in institutions outside of Korea. Both male and female students are eligible to apply. As a Study Abroad student, you can earn credits towards your home degree while immersing yourself in a valuable international and intercultural experience in Korea. Additionally, Exchange Students from Partner Institutions have the option to participate in this program, with the possibility of tuition waiver based on the exchange agreement. Participants in the program have the chance to enroll in SMWU’s undergraduate and graduate schools. Earned credits are recorded on an official SMWU transcript, which may be transferable to other universities.

Academic Calendar
Sookmyung Women’s University operates on a two-semester academic year. The spring semester runs from March to mid-June, while the fall semester takes place from September to mid-December. In addition to these regular semesters, Summer Sessions are offered prior to the fall semester.

Courses
We offer over 150 English-taught courses in various disciplines at both undergraduate and graduate levels. Students can choose from a range of subjects such as Korean language, International Studies, Korean Studies, Business and Economics and more. Additionally, there are numerous opportunities to engage in traditional Korean culture through lectures and field trips. For a complete course list and descriptions, please visit: [Click here-
http://e.sookmyung.ac.kr

How to apply
Entry Requilrements
All students including SMWU’s exchange students are required to complete their payments upon arrival.
Visiting Students
Students who are not from exchange universities or from SMWU’s partner institution who were not selected as exchange students.
Before applying directly, it is recommended that students contact the international office of their home university to verify the transferability of credits earned at SMWU.
Exchange Students
SMWU’s partner institution students must be nominated by their home university as exchange candidates. All application documents should be submitted to SMWU through the international office of their home university. Individual applications are not accepted.

Benefits for International Students
Sookmyung Buddy Leadership Group, URINK
U.R.I. (United Relationship for Internationalization) is a student-led group at Sookmyung Women’s University. Local SMWU students volunteer as buddies to assist and support international students on campus. Each international student is paired with a student buddy who helps them with general matters in Korea and helps them adjust to university life. The program promotes cultural exchange, fosters lasting friendships, and offers opportunities for students to participate in various events and activities together.
Scholarship Offered Volunteer Programs
International students from around the world can volunteer in Sookmyung Women’s University’s English Speaking Spot (ESS) and Second Language Tutoring program (SLT). In this program, they have the opportunity to teach their native language to Sookmyung students and receive a scholarship of KRW 10,000 per hour throughout the semester. It is a great way for international students to share their language skills and earn a scholarship at the same time.

National Central University

國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。

5. Student Life at Sungshin
Home University Coordinator.  Please note that original hard copies will 
not be provided.
Health Insurance 
Private Health Insurance (Mandatory)
Ÿ As required by the Korean Ministry of Education, you are required to be 
covered by Korean private health insurance.
Ÿ For a one-time payment of around KRW 80,000, coverage is provided for 
six months (one semester).
Ÿ The purpose of this private insurance is to cover medical gaps that may 
arise from the time you enter the country until your National Health 
Insurance coverage begins, which can take several months.
Ÿ The Certificate of Admission will be issued only after the payment has 
been confirmed.  Further details will be provided to students who have 
completed the application.
 National Health Insurance (Mandatory)
Ÿ National Health Insurance is mandated by the law.
Ÿ National Health Insurance is applied upon the issuance of the Residence Card.
Ÿ Details about registration and fees are TBA.
Ÿ Fees must be paid on a monthly basis. (₩80,000‒100,000 per month)
Ÿ Students with Japanese or French nationality are eligible to apply for 
the exemption. (Students must apply for the exemption individually)
Student Visa
(D-2)
All incoming international students at Sungshin must obtain a D-2 student visa.
Ÿ Required documents provided by Sungshin Women's University:
  1. Certificate of Admission
  2. Business Registration Certificate of Sungshin Women’s University
Ÿ Documents Sending Date:
 - Spring semester: End of Dec ember
 - Fall semester: End of June
u Note
 - After receiving the Certificate of Admission and the Business Registration 
Certificate from us via email, you can apply for a D-2 student visa at the 
Korean Embassy in your home country. Please contact the relevant 
diplomatic mission for specific procedures, required forms, and 
processing time, as they may vary by country.
 - The D-2 student visa is valid for a single entry to Korea. Without an 
ARC, you cannot re-enter Korea on the same student visa. Be sure to 
obtain your ARC before departure during your exchange period.
 - Please note that your D-2 visa will be used upon your first entry into 
Korea and will be invalidated when you depart from Korea in the 
absence of a valid Registration Card. Should you wish to go ahead with 
the above planned itinerary, you will need to apply for D-2 visa again 
for your exchange program.
Housing
Ÿ Dormitory Accommodation : Dormitory housing is available for 
international students.
Ÿ Room Type: Double Room / Triple Room / Quadruple Room (Room 
assignments may vary depending on the university’s circumstances.)

original_evidence.text:
National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。 
 
 
 
□我已閱讀並同意上述所有內容。 
申請人簽名:___________________ 
簽名日期:_____________________

Q
[Academic Records] Grading
A.
Students will receive a letter grade
ranging from A+ to F. The grade of “A” is given for excellent performance; “B”
for above average; “C” for average; “D” for minimally passing performance; and
“F” for failure. In addition, “+” and “0“ are used for further differentiation.
A student’s performance with “+” indicates a superior performance in that
letter grade, and “0“ indicates a slightly weaker performance in that letter
grade. Other grades include “P” (pass) and “F” (fail). The grade will become a
part of permanent record at CUK.
9
Q
[Courses Registration] Is there any other information that I should know?
A.
Students
cannot drop any official grades including classes that received an ‘F.’
Therefore, make sure to attend all classes on the first week of school and if
there are any courses you would like to drop, you may add or drop courses
during the “C
lass Schedule Change Period”.
8
Q
[Courses Registration] Can I withdrawal the courses after the “Class Schedule Change Period”?
A.
Students
may withdrawal from enrolled courses during the given period, by the 4
th
of week of September without penalty. However, please keep in mind that course
addition is not allowed during this period.
The
students are required to have their withdrawn courses approved by the course
professor for the process to be completed. In addition, the “Class Schedule
Change Form” must be submitted to the department you belong to, during this
period. If not, students may face academic penalty such as receiving an “F”
grade for the course.
7
Q
[Courses Registration] Can I change the courses after registration on orientation?
A.
Students
may add or drop courses during the “C
lass Schedule Change Period”
(the first week of the semester), by
logging in to the school website called Trinity System.
6
Q
[Courses Registration] Is there a maximum of credits I can register for?
A.
Students
can take almost all courses offered at undergraduate level from 9 credits up to
a maximum of 19 credits per semester. If you register less than 9 credits you
must submit an statement of reasons to Office of International Affairs.
5
Q
[Courses Registration] When and how do I register?
A.
In
the third week of August (around Aug 10~14), there will be a course
registration date, in that period, most students will self-quarantine.
4

Q
[Academic Records] Grading
A.
Students will receive a letter grade
ranging from A+ to F. The grade of “A” is given for excellent performance; “B”
for above average; “C” for average; “D” for minimally passing performance; and
“F” for failure. In addition, “+” and “0“ are used for further differentiation.
A student’s performance with “+” indicates a superior performance in that
letter grade, and “0“ indicates a slightly weaker performance in that letter
grade. Other grades include “P” (pass) and “F” (fail). The grade will become a
part of permanent record at CUK.
9
Q
[Courses Registration] Is there any other information that I should know?
A.
Students
cannot drop any official grades including classes that received an ‘F.’
Therefore, make sure to attend all classes on the first week of school and if
there are any courses you would like to drop, you may add or drop courses
during the “C
lass Schedule Change Period”.
8
Q
[Courses Registration] Can I withdrawal the courses after the “Class Schedule Change Period”?
A.
Students
may withdrawal from enrolled courses during the given period, by the 4
th
of week of September without penalty. However, please keep in mind that course
addition is not allowed during this period.
The
students are required to have their withdrawn courses approved by the course
professor for the process to be completed. In addition, the “Class Schedule
Change Form” must be submitted to the department you belong to, during this
period. If not, students may face academic penalty such as receiving an “F”
grade for the course.
7
Q
[Courses Registration] Can I change the courses after registration on orientation?
A.
Students
may add or drop courses during the “C
lass Schedule Change Period”
(the first week of the semester), by
logging in to the school website called Trinity System.
6
Q
[Courses Registration] Is there a maximum of credits I can register for?
A.
Students
can take almost all courses offered at undergraduate level from 9 credits up to
a maximum of 19 credits per semester. If you register less than 9 credits you
must submit an statement of reasons to Office of International Affairs.
5
Q
[Courses Registration] When and how do I register?
A.
In
the third week of August (around Aug 10~14), there will be a course
registration date, in that period, most students will self-quarantine.
4

There are 3 campuses so choose Songsim. Check your google map and choose the
best option to come to the campus depending on each other's budget. (Taxi or

Taking
a taxi is the fastest way to get to CUK. It takes about 50 ~ 60 minutes and

All the transportation is not allowed for all overseas arrivals after the corona pandemic so all the incoming students are expected to take a designated taxi in the Incheon airport. You will be guided by an airport staff when you ask for help. The designated taxis are ready for COVID-19 prevention so it could be more expensive than regular taxi (about 70,000~90,000 won).

Yes there is, the pick up service is offered
only once
so the students who want this service have to arrive in the Incheon airport on the informed day & time from CUK OIA.
1) Where is meeting point?
Students
should be at Incheon International Airport, Terminal 1, Arrival Hall(1F), GATE
D. There are two terminals(Terminal1 and Terminal2) at the airport. Please do
not confused.
1)-3. How can I find you?
We
will be holding a sign that says “The Catholic University of Korea.”
1)-4. How much is it?
It
is offered for free.
-> The pick up service is not offered until the social ending of coronavirus.

FAQ
Student Exchange Program
CUK offers a coeducational international program and welcomes students to study for one or two semesters as an exchange student at CUK. This program is open to undergraduate students enrolled as full-time students at our partner institutions. During the program, students will have opportunities to experience Korean culture, and develop "global competence" through the multicultural environment that CUK offers.
Exchange students are those nominated by partner institutions which have formal exchange agreements with CUK. Therefore, before applying for the CUK Student Exchange Program, students are asked to contact the related office of their home institutions in advance. Students are required to follow the process mentioned below.
Application Procedures for Spring 2025
Application Procedures for Spring 2022
Nomination
Period
26 August ~ 25 October 2024
Procedure
It must be completed by a staff who in charge of student exchange program
Application
Period
30 October ~ 17 November 2024
Procedure
Students need to complete the online application and also post documents to CUK OIA
*Link for online application will be accessable from 17 November 2024
*Hard copies of all application document must arrive to CUK no later than 27 December 2024
Admission
Period
First week of January 2025
Procedure
Certificate of Admission(CoA) will be issued and sent to student by email
*Hard copies(original documents) must be submitted before issuing the CoA
Important Dates for Spring 2025
Important Dates for Spring 2022
Course Registration
Course Registration: February 2025
Course Change Period: 1st week of the semester
Dormitory Move-in
A week before the semester begins
Orientation
A week before the semester begins
Spring Semester Starts
4 March 2025(*estimated)
Spring Semester Ends
Mid June 2025
Official Transcript Issuance
Early July 2025
Academic year
Spring semester
begins in the early March
Fall semester
begins in the late August
Duration of classes
16 weeks per semester
Duration of exchange
One semester or two semesters (one full year)
Language of instruction
Exchange students can study either 100% in English, 100% in Korean or mixing classes in both languages if their level is good enough
Grading
Students will receive a letter grade ranging from A+ to F. The grade of “A” is given for excellent performance; “B” for above average; “C” for average; “D” for minimally passing performance; and “F” for failure. In addition, “+” and “0“ are used for further differentiation. A student’s performance with “+” indicates a superior performance in that letter grade, and “0“ indicates a slightly weaker performance in that letter grade. Other grades include “P” (pass) and “F” (fail). The grade will become a part of permanent record at CUK.
Transcripts
Credits earned at CUK can be transferred. Please consult with your study abroad advisor or academic advisor at your home institution for regulations concerning credit transfer. The official transcript will be sent to the home institution of an exchange student automatically. If you request more copies, you should pay for the transcript issuance fee and delivery fee.

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。

CUK offers a coeducational international program and welcomes students to study for one or two semesters as an exchange student at CUK. This program is open to undergraduate students enrolled as full-time students at our partner institutions. During the program, students will have opportunities to experience Korean culture, and develop "global competence" through the multicultural environment that CUK offers.
Exchange students are those nominated by partner institutions which have formal exchange agreements with CUK. Therefore, before applying for the CUK Student Exchange Program, students are asked to contact the related office of their home institutions in advance. Students are required to follow the process mentioned below.

Duration of classes

Duration of exchange
One semester or two semesters (one full year)
Language of instruction
Exchange students can study either 100% in English, 100% in Korean or mixing classes in both languages if their level is good enough
Grading
Students will receive a letter grade ranging from A+ to F. The grade of “A” is given for excellent performance; “B” for above average; “C” for average; “D” for minimally passing performance; and “F” for failure. In addition, “+” and “0“ are used for further differentiation. A student’s performance with “+” indicates a superior performance in that letter grade, and “0“ indicates a slightly weaker performance in that letter grade. Other grades include “P” (pass) and “F” (fail). The grade will become a part of permanent record at CUK.
Transcripts
Credits earned at CUK can be transferred. Please consult with your study abroad advisor or academic advisor at your home institution for regulations concerning credit transfer. The official transcript will be sent to the home institution of an exchange student automatically. If you request more copies, you should pay for the transcript issuance fee and delivery fee.

B형(영) | M10: This course serves as an introductory major course in Spatial Design, offering fundamental practical experience in English.

The primary objective of this course is to comprehensively understand various spatial environments where life occurs and to enhance the necessary perspectives, theoretical knowledge, and spatial design expression skills needed to create them. We aim to broaden our perspective on how we perceive spatial environments in our daily lives, foster creative thinking, interdisciplinary abilities, and expressive skills to create improved spaces.

Throughout this course, students will practice exercises that involve expressing spaces using architectural elements, with the goal of developing perceptual and creative potential in relation to spaces. Students will gain experience in the basic architectural language of form required to create spaces accommodating human behavior, analyze spatial meanings, and cultivate spatial expression abilities during the design process. Additionally, the course aims to enhance conceptual idea development, visual communication skills, and provide fundamental practice in spatial design, ultimately contributing to a broader understanding of architecture and interior design as a whole.

● to observe and gain an understanding of the physical characteristics of the spatial environments in which we reside
● to understand architects’ philosophy, design concepts, and spatial drawings through the examination of global architectural works
● to understand spatial scale and design elements while acquiring the skills necessary for architectural representation techniques and 3D model making (including sketching, drawing, diagrams, photography, collage, 3D study models, etc.).
● to foster the design development of spatial concept ideas and enhance visual communication skills
● to Acquire knowledge of spatial design methods, fundamental components, and the overall design process.

B형(영) | M11: 
This course focuses on acquiring the fundamental and essential mathematical tools required for specialized studies in Biologics Engineering. Moving beyond general mathematical concepts, it specifically educates students on the core principles of differential equations, linear algebra, and basic statistics necessary for solving practical engineering problems such as bioreactor modeling, pharmacokinetic analysis, and biological system data processing. Students will strengthen their quantitative reasoning skills through this course, enabling them to analytically model and predict complex bioengineering phenomena using real-world examples from the biologics field.

B형(영) | M12: This course is designed for students who have selected or are considering Biologics Engineering as their major. It aims to enhance their understanding of biomedical polymers, which serve as the fundamental basis for the delivery of biopharmaceutical raw materials. By taking this course, students will be provided with opportunities for proper academic exploration and informed major selection. Furthermore, it will establish a solid foundation in drug delivery systems (DDS), ensuring sufficient comprehension for future advanced coursework related to biopharmaceuticals.

Q
[Academic Records] Grading
A.
Students will receive a letter grade
ranging from A+ to F. The grade of “A” is given for excellent performance; “B”
for above average; “C” for average; “D” for minimally passing performance; and
“F” for failure. In addition, “+” and “0“ are used for further differentiation.
A student’s performance with “+” indicates a superior performance in that
letter grade, and “0“ indicates a slightly weaker performance in that letter
grade. Other grades include “P” (pass) and “F” (fail). The grade will become a
part of permanent record at CUK.
9
Q
[Courses Registration] Is there any other information that I should know?
A.
Students
cannot drop any official grades including classes that received an ‘F.’
Therefore, make sure to attend all classes on the first week of school and if
there are any courses you would like to drop, you may add or drop courses
during the “C
lass Schedule Change Period”.
8
Q
[Courses Registration] Can I withdrawal the courses after the “Class Schedule Change Period”?
A.
Students
may withdrawal from enrolled courses during the given period, by the 4
th
of week of September without penalty. However, please keep in mind that course
addition is not allowed during this period.
The
students are required to have their withdrawn courses approved by the course
professor for the process to be completed. In addition, the “Class Schedule
Change Form” must be submitted to the department you belong to, during this
period. If not, students may face academic penalty such as receiving an “F”
grade for the course.
7
Q
[Courses Registration] Can I change the courses after registration on orientation?
A.
Students
may add or drop courses during the “C
lass Schedule Change Period”
(the first week of the semester), by
logging in to the school website called Trinity System.
6
Q
[Courses Registration] Is there a maximum of credits I can register for?
A.
Students
can take almost all courses offered at undergraduate level from 9 credits up to
a maximum of 19 credits per semester. If you register less than 9 credits you
must submit an statement of reasons to Office of International Affairs.
5
Q
[Courses Registration] When and how do I register?
A.
In
the third week of August (around Aug 10~14), there will be a course
registration date, in that period, most students will self-quarantine.
4

【同頁視覺核對選定原文；非全文轉錄】
APPLICATION DOCUMENTS: 1. Copy of Passport. 2. Certificate of Enrollment (issued by Home University): Apostille OR Notarization from the Embassy/Consulate of Korea required for students from Non-OECD countries. 3. Academic Transcript: Issued in English (if not, please submit translation with the document). 4. Bank Statement of Deposit Balance: USD 3,400 (1-semester) / USD 8,453 (2-semester); Bank statement officially issued from the bank; If submitting account of parents, should submit the document proving family relationship. 5. Letter of Recommendation from Home University. 6. Essays (2 questions): [Q1] What is the main reason for choosing Exchange student program in Korea? Explain your Study plan. [Q2] With the experience of studying in Korea, What would you like to do in the future? 7. Official Language Proficiency Test Result (ENG/KOR): If applicable. 8. Personal Information Collection & Usage Agreement: CUK template. FEES: Balanced Exchange Program: NONE. Korean Language Class: FREE (Spring/Fall term); During vacation Summer/Winter: KRW 1,015,000 (30% discount). Dormitory, 16 weeks: Stephan Hall 2-bed KRW 1,308,000; 3-bed KRW 1,040,000; 4-bed KRW 790,000. Andrea Hall 2-bed A type KRW 1,680,000, B type KRW 1,508,000; A type space separated. International students are assigned to dormitories with priority. Korean language classes: 200 hours per term, Level 1 to 6. Office of International Affairs: 43 Jibong-ro, Bucheon-si, Gyeonggi-do, Korea.

Q
[Dormitory] Toiletries
A.
Toiletries can be purchased at the
nearest convenience store or market here.
19
Q
[Dormitory] What do I need when moving into the dorm?
A.
Students will need to bring their own
pillow, linens, blankets, towels, and toiletries.
18
Q
[Dormitory] When can I move in and move out?
A.
It is available from 9AM to 10PM at
the end of the August (the exact date will be notice). Please be sure to keep
your time, as it may not be possible to move into in other times.
Students who chose a 16-weeks plan,
have to move out by 14th December 2019. Students, chose a 24-weeks plan, have
to move out by the mid of February. If students chose a 16-week plan at first and
changed to a 24-week plan after arriving in Korea, students should leave the
dormitory for 7 to 10 days, dormitory cleaning period, right after the fall
semester. Please choose carefully.
17
Q
[Korean Language Class] How much is the tuition fee?
A.
Students from our partner universities
could receive a 30% discount. So, the tuition is KRW 910,000.
However, Korean language courses are
offered free of charge to every partner university which offers free language
courses to CUK students, following the reciprocity principle. In this case, Tuition
exemption applies only to Spring and Fall semesters. For summer and winter
semester, KRW 910,000 is required.
16
Q
[Korean Language Class] How does Korean language class work?
A.
Our Korean Language Education Center(KLEC)
offers Korean language classes at several different levels from beginner(level
1) to advance(level 6). Students will be assigned in accordance with their
placement test results. The placement test includes writing and an interview.
Beginners with no Korean background are also required to take the test. Korean
classes are offered 4 hours a day, from 9:00 am to 1:00 pm, Monday through
Friday. A total of 10 weeks and 200 hours of classes are offered.
15
Q
[Attendance] Regarding Absence Waivers for a menstrual period
A.
Female
students may use an absence waiver once a month
, by logging in to the school website called Trinity
System.
14
Q
[Attendance] Regarding Attendance for the Korean Language Education Center
A.
Korean language classes are 200 hours
in total for 10 weeks. If you miss more than 20 hours, you will not be able to
pass.
13
Q
[Attendance] Attendance for Regular Courses
A.
It is
an automatic F, when students are absent more than 1/4 of the classes. If students
suddenly become sick and cannot attend classes, it is needed to tell the course
professor. In addition, students should bring medical records and other
documents to discuss with the course professor whether there is any way that it
will not be treated as absent.
12
Q
[Academic Records] How many credits can I transfer?
A.
Credits earned at CUK can be
transferred. Please consult with your study abroad advisor or academic advisor
at your home institution for regulations concerning credit transfer.
11
Q
[Academic Records] How can I get my transcript?
A.
Transcripts will be sent to the
International Affairs of your school after the end of the semester. Students
who are enrolled for one year will have transcripts sent at the end of the
second semester. If you request more copies, you should pay for the transcript
issuance fee and delivery fee.

【同頁視覺核對選定原文；非全文轉錄】
APPLICATION DOCUMENTS: 1. Copy of Passport. 2. Certificate of Enrollment (issued by Home University): Apostille OR Notarization from the Embassy/Consulate of Korea required for students from Non-OECD countries. 3. Academic Transcript: Issued in English (if not, please submit translation with the document). 4. Bank Statement of Deposit Balance: USD 3,400 (1-semester) / USD 8,453 (2-semester); Bank statement officially issued from the bank; If submitting account of parents, should submit the document proving family relationship. 5. Letter of Recommendation from Home University. 6. Essays (2 questions): [Q1] What is the main reason for choosing Exchange student program in Korea? Explain your Study plan. [Q2] With the experience of studying in Korea, What would you like to do in the future? 7. Official Language Proficiency Test Result (ENG/KOR): If applicable. 8. Personal Information Collection & Usage Agreement: CUK template. FEES: Balanced Exchange Program: NONE. Korean Language Class: FREE (Spring/Fall term); During vacation Summer/Winter: KRW 1,015,000 (30% discount). Dormitory, 16 weeks: Stephan Hall 2-bed KRW 1,308,000; 3-bed KRW 1,040,000; 4-bed KRW 790,000. Andrea Hall 2-bed A type KRW 1,680,000, B type KRW 1,508,000; A type space separated. International students are assigned to dormitories with priority. Korean language classes: 200 hours per term, Level 1 to 6. Office of International Affairs: 43 Jibong-ro, Bucheon-si, Gyeonggi-do, Korea.

Q
[Dormitory] When can I make the payment for dormitory fee?
A.
The dormitory office will inform you the
specific payment schedule and method after you arrive. It is acceptable only by
domestic wire transfer. Please bring cash or withdraw KRW from ATM and visit
Woori Bank, located in the 1st floor of the International Hub Building, makes the
payment.
Please check the dormitory fee below;
General residents (16 weeks)
Long-term residents (24 weeks)
Double
KRW 1,248,000
KRW 1,835,000
3-Bed
KWR 1,040,000
KRW 1,529,000
4-Bed
KRW 790,000
KRW 1,161,000
Before
leaving your country, please be sure to check whether you can withdraw money
from Korea ATMs and withdrawal limit in a day.
31
Q
[Dormitory]  Cleaning Period
A.
The dorm cleaning period is for about 7-10
days right after the end of the fall semester and just before the start of the
spring semester. If you selected a 16-weeks plan at first and changed to a 24-weeks
plan after arrival at CUK, you must leave out the dorm for this period. The
dormitory office will offer temporary accommodation on campus during this
period at a reasonable price.
If you selected a 24-weeks plan from
the start, you don't have to leave at this time. However, you have to leave the
dormitory during the cleaning period just before the spring semester starts.
The dormitory will offer temporary accommodation at reasonable prices.

Q
[Dormitory] WIFI
A.
Free WIFI is available on campus
including dormitory. Look for the “Catholic_Univ” signal. The password is
1234567890.
29
Q
[Dormitory] Dormitory Rules & Regulations or any other dormitory information
A.
It is for a student who use a room for
4 students(4-bed room). If you use the top of a double deck bed, you are
supposed use the desk close to the window. If you use the bottom of a double
deck bed, you are supposed to use the desk near the door.
※
If there are two foreign students in a
quad room (a room for 4 students), the two foreign students should use only one
side only (bed 1,3 or bed 2,4)
28
Q
[Dormitory] Curfew
A.
From 1.am to 5.am.
27
Q
[Dormitory] Prohibition
A.
It is not allowed to drink alcohol and
smoke. Anybody caught breaking this rule will be out of the dormitory right
away.
26
Q
[Dormitory] Can I send my luggage to the dormitory?
A.
You can send your luggage to the
address below. When you have a room number after entering our school, you must write
the room number and your name to reduce the risk of losing it.
(English)
Cardinal
Kim Sou Hwan Building (Dormitory Stephen)
The
Catholic University of Korea
43,
Jibong-ro, Bucheon-si, Gyeonggi-do, Republic of Korea
Zip
code : 14662

code : 14662

Q
[Dormitory] Forbidden Stuff
A.
Possession or use of personal electric
heating appliances, boilers, irons, microwaves, any flammable and hazardous
materials are forbidden.
24
Q
[Dormitory] Personal belongings
A.
Desk lamp is mandatory for students
who are living in 3 beds room. You can bring hair dryers, laptops, clothes,
book etc.
23
Q
[Dormitory] Power Plug Adapters
A.
The standard voltage in Korea is 220
volts. If you do not have a multi-voltage travel adapter, please make sure to
purchase one before arrival.
22
Q
[Dormitory] Thick bed cover
A.
You must bring or purchase your own
ONE THICK BED COVER to prevent mattress contamination.
21
Q
[Dormitory] Linen & Bedding
A.
You can either purchase your linens in
Korea or bedding rental is provided by the Dormitory with a KRW 50,000 charge
in cash. (Includes pillow, pillowcase, bed sheet, blanket).

【同頁視覺核對選定原文；非全文轉錄】
APPLICATION DOCUMENTS: 1. Copy of Passport. 2. Certificate of Enrollment (issued by Home University): Apostille OR Notarization from the Embassy/Consulate of Korea required for students from Non-OECD countries. 3. Academic Transcript: Issued in English (if not, please submit translation with the document). 4. Bank Statement of Deposit Balance: USD 3,400 (1-semester) / USD 8,453 (2-semester); Bank statement officially issued from the bank; If submitting account of parents, should submit the document proving family relationship. 5. Letter of Recommendation from Home University. 6. Essays (2 questions): [Q1] What is the main reason for choosing Exchange student program in Korea? Explain your Study plan. [Q2] With the experience of studying in Korea, What would you like to do in the future? 7. Official Language Proficiency Test Result (ENG/KOR): If applicable. 8. Personal Information Collection & Usage Agreement: CUK template. FEES: Balanced Exchange Program: NONE. Korean Language Class: FREE (Spring/Fall term); During vacation Summer/Winter: KRW 1,015,000 (30% discount). Dormitory, 16 weeks: Stephan Hall 2-bed KRW 1,308,000; 3-bed KRW 1,040,000; 4-bed KRW 790,000. Andrea Hall 2-bed A type KRW 1,680,000, B type KRW 1,508,000; A type space separated. International students are assigned to dormitories with priority. Korean language classes: 200 hours per term, Level 1 to 6. Office of International Affairs: 43 Jibong-ro, Bucheon-si, Gyeonggi-do, Korea.

Q
[Academic Records] Grading
A.
Students will receive a letter grade
ranging from A+ to F. The grade of “A” is given for excellent performance; “B”
for above average; “C” for average; “D” for minimally passing performance; and
“F” for failure. In addition, “+” and “0“ are used for further differentiation.
A student’s performance with “+” indicates a superior performance in that
letter grade, and “0“ indicates a slightly weaker performance in that letter
grade. Other grades include “P” (pass) and “F” (fail). The grade will become a
part of permanent record at CUK.
9
Q
[Courses Registration] Is there any other information that I should know?
A.
Students
cannot drop any official grades including classes that received an ‘F.’
Therefore, make sure to attend all classes on the first week of school and if
there are any courses you would like to drop, you may add or drop courses
during the “C
lass Schedule Change Period”.
8
Q
[Courses Registration] Can I withdrawal the courses after the “Class Schedule Change Period”?
A.
Students
may withdrawal from enrolled courses during the given period, by the 4
th
of week of September without penalty. However, please keep in mind that course
addition is not allowed during this period.
The
students are required to have their withdrawn courses approved by the course
professor for the process to be completed. In addition, the “Class Schedule
Change Form” must be submitted to the department you belong to, during this
period. If not, students may face academic penalty such as receiving an “F”
grade for the course.
7
Q
[Courses Registration] Can I change the courses after registration on orientation?
A.
Students
may add or drop courses during the “C
lass Schedule Change Period”
(the first week of the semester), by
logging in to the school website called Trinity System.
6
Q
[Courses Registration] Is there a maximum of credits I can register for?
A.
Students
can take almost all courses offered at undergraduate level from 9 credits up to
a maximum of 19 credits per semester. If you register less than 9 credits you
must submit an statement of reasons to Office of International Affairs.
5
Q
[Courses Registration] When and how do I register?
A.
In
the third week of August (around Aug 10~14), there will be a course
registration date, in that period, most students will self-quarantine.
4

Yes there is, the pick up service is offered
only once
so the students who want this service have to arrive in the Incheon airport on the informed day & time from CUK OIA.

original_evidence.text:
Pre-Arrival Information
Course Registration
Once you are admitted to the University of Seoul as an exchange student, the coordinators of the OIA office will contact you directly and assist you with your course registration. You may register a course or drop a course online during the course change period, the first week of each semester. Normally, course registration and changes are done through the website at
http://wise.uos.ac.kr.
Unfortunately, since all the instructions are in Korean, you are advised to ask for your UOS Buddy’s help.
Notice
You must print out your confirmed course registration results shown on the computer screen of the online registration and submit it to your coordinator after the course change period ends.
Please check if your name is on the final class rosters.
If you do not follow the academic regulations and fail to confirm your online registration during this period, you will be responsible for any failure in taking a course and acquiring credits or dropping a course.
Courses Only for Exchange Students Offered by OIA office
All of the exchange students are strongly recommended to take Korean language courses and at least one course in Asian studies. You will be arranged to the Korean language courses on the basis of your Korean language proficiency. Asian Studies courses will be taught in English. Korean Language Courses cannot be registered by students online. OIA office will register your Korean Language courses collectively within the online course change period.
Notice
Please make sure that other courses registered do not coincide with Korean Language courses when you make any changes. In case you took Korean language level test, your schedule could be changed according to the result of the test.
Graduates students are not able to do the online course registration with these courses offered by OIA office. Please let your coordinator know if you take these courses.
Regular Courses Offered in English and in Korean
Some of the regular courses are offered in English, but many of them are in Korean. Some classes cannot be accessed because of academic regulations or class size. If this happens to you, you will need permission from the professor of the course. Please contact your coordinator at the OIA office for assistance concerning these matters. You can ask your UOS buddy where your classrooms are.
Transportation to UOS
1
Incheon International Airport
By Limousine Bus from Incheon International Airport
You are advised to find the bus stop "5B” at the exit of Incheon International Airport Terminal 1 and the bus stop “No.34” of Terminal 2.
The limousine, #6002, will take you to Cheongryangni, the bus's final destination. The fare of limousine is 17,000 KRW. You may
1) Get off at the Cheongryangni stop and take a taxi or take a bus to the University of Seoul, or 2) Wait a little while until the bus heads to the next stop and the next stop will be University of Seoul.
By Taxi/Call Van from Incheon International Airport
From the airport, it costs approximately 80,000 - 90,000 KRW by taxi up for 4 people to the University of Seoul. The fare of regular taxi starts from 4,800 KRW, while deluxe taxis start from 6,500 KRW.
By Subway from Incheon International Airport
You will have to make a transfer at Seoul station (line1).
Incheon International Airport Public Transportation Guide
2
Kimpo International Airport
By Subway from Kimpo International Airport
If your flight arrives at Kimpo International Airport you are advised to use subway (Line 5). Get off at Dapsimni station which is the closest station from University of Seoul and take a taxi to the University of Seoul at Exit 3 or 4. The taxi fare from Dapsimni station to the University of Seoul (pronounced 'Seoul Sirip Dae-hak-kyo', 서울시립대학교 in Korean) is around 7,000 KRW.
Gimpo International Airport Subway Usage Guide
By Taxi/Call Van from Kimpo International Airport시
From the airport, it costs approximately 40,000 - 50,000 KRW by taxi up for 4 people to the University of Seoul. The fare of regular taxi starts from 4,800 KRW, while deluxe taxis start from 6,500 KRW.
Gimpo International Airport Taxi/Call Van Usage Guide

Changing and Dropping Courses
답변
To change or drop your courses, you need to know how to access the WISE system (
http://wise.uos.ac.kr), not the UOSCRS website.
Usually, we provide a student handbook and hold orientation sessions a week before the semester starts, which include information on changing and dropping courses.
No
24
Category
Academic
Subject
Does UOS provide assistance to exchange students with course registration?
답변
As each exchange student does the course registration themselves, there is nothing UOS OIA can do for you.
Check the system often during the Course Registration Period to see if there are any available seats to register for the courses you want to take.
No
23
Category
Nomination&Application
Subject
What are the minimum and maximum credits an exchange student can enroll in per semester?
답변
A student should take at least 6 credits and can take up to 20 credits a semester.
This is a rule of our university, and you must check your home university's regulations to transfer your grades without any problems.
We hope you can check it well through your home university.
No
22
Category
Nomination&Application
Subject
Can Korean students also apply?  Is it possible for Korean nationals studying at overseas institutions to apply as well?
답변
The exchange student program is open to all students, regardless of nationality.
The exchange student program allows for the exchange and reception of students between the University of Seoul and institutions with which we have a student exchange agreement.
You will need to check whether student exchanges are currently possible with your university.
If participation through the exchange student program is not feasible, you may still join the program as a visiting student (limited to partner institutions).
No
21
Category
Academic
Subject
When will the university transcript be available?
답변
The transcript will be released around the end of January for the Fall Semester and the end of July for the Spring Semester.
No
20
Category
Nomination&Application
Subject
Are there any fees that students have to pay or do they need to submit proof of financial support?
답변
While there are no additional fees, students from non-OECD countries must provide proof of financial support, as required by the guidelines set by the Korean Immigration Office.
No
19
Category
Academic
Subject
Are there special requirements for our students (e.g., certain TOEFL/IELTS scores, GPA requirements, etc.)?
답변
Although there are no specific requirements, it is recommended that students have a good proficiency in English or Korean.
In addition, UOS will prefer to accept students with a GPA above 2.5/4.0 (equivalent to a 'B' or higher).
If a nominated student does not meet the grade requirements, they must provide a recommendation letter indicating their ability to perform well academically.
No
18
Category
Academic
Subject
Are there restricted subject areas that our students are not allowed to take?
답변
For STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics), architecture, economics, and design courses, it is not guaranteed that exchange students from different majors will be able to enroll.
Acceptance may be determined on a case-by-case basis, as professors and other reviewers thoroughly examine the applicants' majors and grades from their home universities.
It is preferable for students to enroll in courses related or relevant to their degree program at their home universities.

Please tell us about the bus route to the University of Seoul from Incheon Airport
답변
Please refer to the link below for your reference:
https://airportlimousine.co.kr/en/sub/sub01.php?cat_no=5
The 6002 limousine bus's last stop is Cheongnyangni Station, but it will proceed to the University of Seoul as the next stop once it departs for Incheon International Airport.
However, please inform the bus driver of your destination when you board the 6002 limousine bus.

What do Semester 1 (Spring) and Semester 2 (Fall) mean?
답변
Semester 1 means Spring Semester, 2024.
Semester 2 means Fall Semester, 2024.
Course Enrollment is done one semester at a time.

What Exchange Students Should Know About Course Registration
답변
For STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics), Architecture, Economics, and Design courses, enrollment is not guaranteed for exchange students whose majors are different.
Admission to these courses is reviewed case by case. Professors and academic staff will consider your major and academic record from your home university before approving enrollment.
Please note that some courses may not be offered every semester. The availability of English-taught courses depends on faculty decisions, so courses listed now may become unavailable in future semesters.
In addition, some courses are restricted to specific majors only, such as:
- Electrical and Computer Engineering majors only
- Architecture majors only
- Materials Science and Engineering majors only
- Business majors only
During the course registration period, courses have a limited number of seats for exchange students. If a course is already full, you may only register if a seat becomes available during the first week of the semester.
Updated syllabi will be provided during the course registration period.

[On-Campus Dormitory Only] What Documents Are Required Before Check-In?
답변
Certificate of MMR (Measles, Mumps, and Rubella)
To meet the requirements, your Certificate of MMR must include two clearly visible dates for your MMR vaccinations.
The certificate must be written in English, and your name, along with the two vaccination dates, should be clearly visible on a single page.
(If the original documents are not in English, a seal from a qualified translator is sufficient for translated documents.)
If your local health department or hospital is unable to issue this certificate, you will need to consult with a doctor.
The doctor must provide a statement confirming that you have antibodies or clear indications of immunity from two MMR vaccinations.
If provided by a doctor, the medical certificate must include a statement confirming that you possess immunity antibodies from the second dose of the MMR vaccine.
(If the original documents are not in English, a seal from a qualified translator is sufficient for translated documents.)
Generally, as long as you have received two doses of the measles vaccination, it will be sufficient!
If you can provide your vaccination certificate, it will help expedite the verification process. (Highly recommended.)
Certificate of Health (Chest X-Ray Result or TB Test Result)
You will also need to provide a document from a hospital or clinic pertaining to a chest X-ray result or a TB (Tuberculosis) test result.
(If the original documents are not in English, a seal from a qualified translator is sufficient for translated documents.)
Please note that final approval is at the discretion of the dormitory team, so it is essential that all information, including the two vaccination dates, is clearly legible from their perspective.

National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) Enrollment and Important Information for International Students
답변
National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) Enrollment and Important Information for International Students
1. Automatic Enrollment
Starting March 2021, all non-Korean international students, including exchange and visiting students, are mandatory and automatically enrolled in Korea’s National Health Insurance upon the date of alien registration.
2. Consequences of Non-Payment
Restrictions on Health Insurance Benefits
Health insurance benefits at medical institutions will be unavailable starting from the first day of the month following the payment deadline until the outstanding contributions are fully paid.
Restrictions on Visa Extension
Non-payment may result in the denial of visa extensions by the Korean Immigration Office.
Compulsory Collection
If the insurance contributions are not paid by the specified deadline, the NHIS may initiate compulsory collection procedures.
This may include seizing assets such as real estate, vehicles, bank deposits, etc.
3. Important Note
For all insurance-related inquiries, please contact the NHIS directly. Our office cannot assist with these matters.
NHIS Contact Information
For appointments or other inquiries before visiting the NHIS Seoul Center, please contact their English Call Center at
033-811-2000
.
Visit Preparation
After making your inquiry by phone, refer to the attached image for directions to the NHIS Seoul Center. Additionally, please review the attached documents to ensure you have the necessary paperwork prepared.
If you have insurance documents issued overseas, please bring them with you when visiting the NHIS. Additionally, please review the
Exclusion from National Health Insurance
form (English instructions can be found on the second page).
I have attached the necessary documents for your review and understanding.

National Central University 
 
 
 
 
 
桃園市中壢區中大路 300 號 300,Jhongda Rd., Jhongli Dist., Taoyuan City, Taiwan 320 
Tel: +886-3-4207107 / +886-3-4207094 / Fax: +886-3-4203384  
 www.ncu.edu.tw / ncuoia@ncu.edu.tw 
國立中央大學國際事務處 
學生個人資料提供同意書 
 
國立中央大學國際事務處為辦理各項出國計畫之申請、審查、校內程序作業、向國外各
地區姐妹校薦送及補助金撥款與核銷，在中華民國『個人資料保護法』與相關法令之規
範下，蒐集，處理及利用申請人的個人資料。國立中央大學國際事務處蒐集個人資料，
包括申請人之姓名，出生日期，性別，身份證字號，就讀學校系所，年級，語言考試成
績，聯絡電話，e-mail 等相關於申請表上所有資訊。前述個資之處理方式會以 EMAIL
或紙本方式傳遞。 
 
若申請人未提供或所提供之資料錯誤或不完整 ， 將導致國際處無法正確審查申請人之申
請案，造成申請人相關權益之損失如審查不通過等。而申請人依中華民國『個人資料保
護法』得行使相關權利 ： 請求刪除或閱讀，製作複本，停止蒐集，處理，利用。國際
資料傳輸等權利，若申請人欲行使上述權利，請與國際處聯繫。但因行使上述相關權利
而導致申請人權益受損，國際處將不負相關賠償責任。 
 
校內初審錄取後，國際處將提供個人聯絡資料(姓名、性別、系所名稱、年級、手機、
E-mail)予國際處製作通訊錄予同行同學，以互相聯絡行前相關細節。 
 
申請人勾選『我同意』並簽屬本同意書時，即表示已閱讀，瞭解並同意本同意書之所有
內容。 
個資保存五年後(自簽名日期算起)即消毀。

Changing and Dropping Courses
답변
To change or drop your courses, you need to know how to access the WISE system (
http://wise.uos.ac.kr), not the UOSCRS website.
Usually, we provide a student handbook and hold orientation sessions a week before the semester starts, which include information on changing and dropping courses.

Subject
Does UOS provide assistance to exchange students with course registration?
답변
As each exchange student does the course registration themselves, there is nothing UOS OIA can do for you.
Check the system often during the Course Registration Period to see if there are any available seats to register for the courses you want to take.

Subject
What are the minimum and maximum credits an exchange student can enroll in per semester?
답변
A student should take at least 6 credits and can take up to 20 credits a semester.
This is a rule of our university, and you must check your home university's regulations to transfer your grades without any problems.
We hope you can check it well through your home university.

Subject
Can Korean students also apply?  Is it possible for Korean nationals studying at overseas institutions to apply as well?
답변
The exchange student program is open to all students, regardless of nationality.
The exchange student program allows for the exchange and reception of students between the University of Seoul and institutions with which we have a student exchange agreement.
You will need to check whether student exchanges are currently possible with your university.
If participation through the exchange student program is not feasible, you may still join the program as a visiting student (limited to partner institutions).

When will the university transcript be available?

Are there any fees that students have to pay or do they need to submit proof of financial support?

Are there special requirements for our students (e.g., certain TOEFL/IELTS scores, GPA requirements, etc.)?
답변
Although there are no specific requirements, it is recommended that students have a good proficiency in English or Korean.
In addition, UOS will prefer to accept students with a GPA above 2.5/4.0 (equivalent to a 'B' or higher).
If a nominated student does not meet the grade requirements, they must provide a recommendation letter indicating their ability to perform well academically.

Acceptance may be determined on a case-by-case basis, as professors and other reviewers thoroughly examine the applicants' majors and grades from their home universities.
It is preferable for students to enroll in courses related or relevant to their degree program at their home universities.

What Exchange Students Should Know About Course Registration
답변
For STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics), Architecture, Economics, and Design courses, enrollment is not guaranteed for exchange students whose majors are different.
Admission to these courses is reviewed case by case. Professors and academic staff will consider your major and academic record from your home university before approving enrollment.
Please note that some courses may not be offered every semester. The availability of English-taught courses depends on faculty decisions, so courses listed now may become unavailable in future semesters.
In addition, some courses are restricted to specific majors only, such as:
- Electrical and Computer Engineering majors only
- Architecture majors only
- Materials Science and Engineering majors only
- Business majors only
During the course registration period, courses have a limited number of seats for exchange students. If a course is already full, you may only register if a seat becomes available during the first week of the semester.
Updated syllabi will be provided during the course registration period.

[On-Campus Dormitory Only] What Documents Are Required Before Check-In?
답변
Certificate of MMR (Measles, Mumps, and Rubella)
To meet the requirements, your Certificate of MMR must include two clearly visible dates for your MMR vaccinations.
The certificate must be written in English, and your name, along with the two vaccination dates, should be clearly visible on a single page.
(If the original documents are not in English, a seal from a qualified translator is sufficient for translated documents.)
If your local health department or hospital is unable to issue this certificate, you will need to consult with a doctor.
The doctor must provide a statement confirming that you have antibodies or clear indications of immunity from two MMR vaccinations.
If provided by a doctor, the medical certificate must include a statement confirming that you possess immunity antibodies from the second dose of the MMR vaccine.
(If the original documents are not in English, a seal from a qualified translator is sufficient for translated documents.)
Generally, as long as you have received two doses of the measles vaccination, it will be sufficient!
If you can provide your vaccination certificate, it will help expedite the verification process. (Highly recommended.)
Certificate of Health (Chest X-Ray Result or TB Test Result)
You will also need to provide a document from a hospital or clinic pertaining to a chest X-ray result or a TB (Tuberculosis) test result.
(If the original documents are not in English, a seal from a qualified translator is sufficient for translated documents.)
Please note that final approval is at the discretion of the dormitory team, so it is essential that all information, including the two vaccination dates, is clearly legible from their perspective.
